quiz.q: What is odd about K.'s 'old assistants'?
o: They know nothing about surveying and have no instruments
quiz.why_uz: Ular yer o'lchashni bilmaydi va asboblari yo'q.

quiz.q: Who signs the letter Barnabas brings?
quiz.why_uz: Imzo o'qilmaydi; Barnabas uni Klamm deb aytadi.

quiz.q: What does K. decide after reading the letter?
o: To become a village worker to reach the Castle
quiz.why_uz: Faqat qishloq ishchisi sifatida Qasrda biror narsaga erisha oladi, deb o'ylaydi.

chapters.title: 3. Frieda
chapters.recap_uz: K. Barnabasning qo'lidan ushlab, Qasrga ketyapmiz, deb o'ylaydi, lekin u uni o'z uyiga — ota-onasi va singillari Olga va Amaliya oldiga olib boradi. Olga bilan K. «Herrenhof» mehmonxonasiga boradi: u yerda faqat Qasr janoblari tunaydi, Klamm ham shu yerda. Bufetchi Frida K.ga tirqishdan uxlab o'tirgan Klammni ko'rsatadi va o'zini uning ma'shuqasi deb ataydi. Frida Klammning xizmatkorlarini qamchi bilan otxonaga haydaydi.

paras.en: 'Barnabas,' said K., unable to master a tremor in his voice, 'there was something else I wanted to tell you. I notice it is really very badly arranged that I should depend only on your chance visits when I need something from the Castle. If I hadn't happened to catch you just now — how you fly! I thought you were still in the house — who knows how long I would have had to wait for your next appearance.' 'You can ask the head of department,' said Barnabas, 'to have me come always at fixed times that you name.' — 'Even that wouldn't be enough,' said K. 'Perhaps for a whole year I won't want to send any message, and then, just a quarter of an hour after you've gone, something that can't wait.' — 'Then shall I report to the head of department,' said Barnabas, 'that some other connection between him and you should be set up, instead of through me?' — 'No, no,' said K., 'not at all. I only mentioned it in passing; this time, luckily, I did catch you.' — 'Shall we go back to the inn,' said Barnabas, 'so that you can give me the new message there?' He had already taken a step towards the house. 'Barnabas,' said K., 'there's no need. I'll walk a little way with you.' — 'Why don't you want to go into the inn?' asked Barnabas. 'The people there disturb me,' said K. 'You saw for yourself how pushy the peasants are.' — 'We could go to your room,' said Barnabas. 'It's the maids' room,' said K., 'dirty and stuffy. It was so as not to have to stay there that I wanted to walk with you a little. Only,' K. added, to overcome his hesitation once and for all, 'you must let me take your arm, because you walk more surely.' And K. hung on his arm. It was quite dark; K. could not see his face at all, his figure only dimly; he had already been groping for the arm a little while before.
paras.uz: — Barnabas, — dedi K. va ovozidagi titroqni yenga olmadi, — senga yana bir narsani aytmoqchi edim. Qasrdan biror narsa kerak bo'lganda faqat sening tasodifiy kelishingga bog'liq bo'lishim juda yomon tashkil etilganini payqayapman. Agar hozir seni tasodifan quvib yetmaganimda — qanday uchib ketasan, men seni hali uydasan deb o'ylagan edim — keyingi kelishingni qancha kutishimga to'g'ri kelardi, kim bilsin. — Sen boshliqdan, — dedi Barnabas, — men doim sen belgilagan aniq vaqtlarda kelishimni so'rashing mumkin. — Bu ham yetarli bo'lmasdi, — dedi K., — balki men bir yil davomida hech qanday xabar yubormoqchi bo'lmayman, lekin aynan sen ketganingdan chorak soat o'tib, kechiktirib bo'lmaydigan biror narsa bo'lib qoladi. — Unda boshliqqa, — dedi Barnabas, — u bilan sen o'rtasida men orqali emas, boshqa aloqa o'rnatilishi kerakligini xabar qilaymi? — Yo'q, yo'q, — dedi K., — mutlaqo yo'q, men bu masalani shunchaki yo'l-yo'lakay aytdim, bu safar seni baxtimga quvib yetdim-ku. — Mehmonxonaga qaytamizmi, — dedi Barnabas, — u yerda menga yangi topshiriq bera olasan? — U allaqachon uy tomon bir qadam tashlagan edi. — Barnabas, — dedi K., — kerak emas, men sen bilan biroz yo'l yuraman. — Nega mehmonxonaga kirishni istamaysan? — so'radi Barnabas. — U yerdagi odamlar menga xalaqit beradi, — dedi K., — dehqonlarning surbetligini o'zing ko'rding. — Sening xonangga borishimiz mumkin, — dedi Barnabas. — Bu xizmatkor qizlarning xonasi, — dedi K., — iflos va dim; u yerda qolmaslik uchun sen bilan biroz yurmoqchi edim; faqat, — deb qo'shdi K. ikkilanishini uzil-kesil yengish uchun, — qo'lingdan ushlab olishimga ruxsat ber, chunki sen ishonchliroq yurasan. — Va K. uning qo'liga osildi. Butunlay qorong'i edi, K. uning yuzini umuman ko'rmas, qomati noaniq edi, qo'lini esa allaqachon bir muddat oldin paypaslab topishga uringan edi.

paras.en: Barnabas gave in, and they moved away from the inn. K. felt, of course, that despite the greatest effort he could not keep step with Barnabas, that he was hindering his free movement, and that under ordinary circumstances everything would come to grief over this trifle alone — especially in side lanes like the one where K. had sunk in the snow that morning and from which he could only have got out if Barnabas had carried him. But he kept such worries away from him now; and it comforted him too that Barnabas was silent. If they walked in silence, then for Barnabas as well the walking itself could be the only purpose of their being together.
paras.uz: Barnabas ko'ndi, ular mehmonxonadan uzoqlashishdi. Albatta, K. eng katta urinishga qaramay Barnabas bilan bir xil qadam tashlay olmayotganini, uning erkin harakatiga xalaqit berayotganini va oddiy sharoitda hamma narsa aynan shu arzimas narsaga borib barbod bo'lishi kerakligini his qildi — ayniqsa K. ertalab qorga botib qolgan va undan faqat Barnabas ko'tarib chiqsagina chiqa oladigan o'sha kabi chetki ko'chalarda. Lekin u endi bunday xavotirlarni o'zidan uzoq tutdi; buning ustiga Barnabasning jim turgani ham uni yupatdi: agar ular jim yurishsa, demak, Barnabas uchun ham birga bo'lishlarining maqsadi faqat yurishning o'zi bo'lishi mumkin edi.

paras.en: They walked, but K. did not know where to; he could make out nothing. He did not even know whether they had already passed the church. Because of the effort that the mere walking cost him, he could not control his thoughts. Instead of staying fixed on the goal, they grew confused. Again and again his home town rose up, and memories of it filled him. There too a church stood in the main square, partly surrounded by an old graveyard, which in turn was surrounded by a high wall. Only very few boys had climbed that wall, and K. had not yet managed it. It was not curiosity that drove them; the graveyard held no more secrets for them. They had often got in through its little iron gate; it was only the smooth, high wall they wanted to conquer. One morning — the quiet, empty square was flooded with light; when had K. ever seen it like that, before or since? — he managed it surprisingly easily. At a spot where he had often been beaten back, with a little flag between his teeth, he climbed the wall at the first attempt. Loose stones were still trickling down below him, and already he was on top. He rammed in the flag, the wind stretched the cloth, he looked down and round about, and over his shoulder too, at the crosses sinking into the earth; no one here and now was greater than he. Then the teacher happened to come by and with an angry look drove K. down. In jumping K. hurt his knee and only got home with difficulty, but he had been on the wall all the same. The feeling of that victory had seemed to him then to give him something to hold on to for a long life — which had not been entirely foolish, for now, after many years, in the snowy night on Barnabas's arm, it came to his aid.
paras.uz: Ular yurishardi, lekin K. qayerga ekanini bilmasdi; hech narsani ajrata olmasdi. Hatto ular cherkov yonidan o'tib ketishganmi, yo'qmi — buni ham bilmasdi. Shunchaki yurishning o'zi unga qanchalik qiyinchilik tug'dirgani sababli, u fikrlarini boshqara olmay qoldi. Maqsadga qaratilgan bo'lib qolish o'rniga ular chalkashib ketardi. Qayta-qayta ona yurti ko'z oldida paydo bo'lar va u haqidagi xotiralar uni to'ldirardi. U yerda ham bosh maydonda cherkov turardi, uni qisman eski qabriston, qabristonni esa baland devor o'rab olgan edi. Bu devorga faqat juda kam bolalar chiqa olgan edi, K. ham hali uddalay olmagan edi. Ularni bunga qiziqish undamasdi, qabristonning ular uchun boshqa siri qolmagan edi. Ular uning kichkina panjarali eshigidan ko'p marta kirishgan edi, faqat silliq, baland devorni zabt etishni istashardi. Bir kuni ertalab — sokin, bo'sh maydon nurga cho'mgan edi, K. uni ilgari yoki keyin qachon shunday ko'rgan edi? — bu unga kutilmaganda oson bo'ldi; ko'p marta qaytarilgan bir joyda, tishlari orasida kichkina bayroqcha bilan, u devorga birinchi urinishdayoq chiqdi. Ostidan hali mayda toshlar to'kilib turardi, u esa allaqachon tepada edi. U bayroqni qadadi, shamol matoni tortib yoydi, u pastga va atrofga, yelkasi osha yerga botib borayotgan xochlarga qaradi; hozir va bu yerda hech kim undan ulug'roq emas edi. Keyin tasodifan o'qituvchi o'tib qoldi va g'azabli nigoh bilan K.ni pastga haydadi. Sakrayotganda K. tizzasini shikastladi, uyga zo'rg'a yetib bordi, lekin baribir devorda bo'lgan edi. Bu g'alaba hissi o'shanda unga uzoq umr uchun tayanch bo'ladigandek tuyulgan edi va bu butunlay ahmoqona emas edi, chunki endi, ko'p yillardan keyin, qorli tunda Barnabasning qo'lida u unga yordamga keldi.

paras.en: He clung on more tightly; Barnabas was almost dragging him; the silence was not broken. Of the way K. knew only that, judging by the state of the road, they had not yet turned into any side lane. He vowed to himself that no difficulty of the way, nor even worry about the way back, would stop him going on. His strength would surely be enough at least to be dragged along. And could the way be endless? By day the Castle had lain before him like an easy goal, and the messenger surely knew the shortest way.
paras.uz: U mahkamroq osildi, Barnabas uni deyarli sudrab borardi, sukut buzilmadi. Yo'l haqida K. faqat bir narsani bilardi: ko'chaning holatiga qaraganda, ular hali hech qanday chetki ko'chaga burilmagan edilar. U o'ziga yo'lning hech qanday qiyinchiligi, hatto orqaga qaytish tashvishi ham uni yurishdan to'xtatmasligiga qasam ichdi. Oxir-oqibat sudralib borish uchun kuchi yetar. Axir yo'l cheksiz bo'lishi mumkinmi? Kunduzi Qasr uning oldida oson maqsaddek turgan edi, xabarchi esa, albatta, eng qisqa yo'lni bilardi.

paras.en: Then Barnabas stopped. Where were they? Could they go no further? Would Barnabas send K. away? He would not succeed. K. held Barnabas's arm so tightly that it almost hurt him himself. Or had the incredible happened, and they were already in the Castle or before its gates? But as far as K. knew, they had not climbed at all. Or had Barnabas led him along a path that rose so imperceptibly? 'Where are we?' K. asked quietly, more of himself than of him. 'At home,' said Barnabas in the same tone. 'At home?' — 'But now take care, sir, that you don't slip. The path goes downhill.' — 'Downhill?' — 'It's only a few steps,' he added, and was already knocking at a door.
paras.uz: Shunda Barnabas to'xtadi. Ular qayerda edi? Boshqa yo'l yo'qmi? Barnabas K. bilan xayrlashadimi? Buni uddalay olmaydi. K. Barnabasning qo'lini shunchalik mahkam ushladiki, o'zi ham deyarli og'riq his qildi. Yoki aql bovar qilmaydigan narsa sodir bo'lib, ular allaqachon Qasrda yoki uning darvozasi oldidamidilar? Lekin K. bilishicha, ular umuman yuqoriga ko'tarilmagan edilar. Yoki Barnabas uni shunchalik sezilmas ko'tariladigan yo'ldan olib keldimi? «Qayerdamiz?» — so'radi K. sekin, undan ko'ra ko'proq o'zidan. «Uydamiz», dedi Barnabas xuddi shunday. «Uydamiz?» — «Endi ehtiyot bo'ling, taqsir, sirpanib ketmang. Yo'l pastga tushadi.» — «Pastgami?» — «Faqat bir necha qadam», deb qo'shdi u va allaqachon bir eshikni taqillatayotgan edi.

paras.en: A girl opened it. They were standing on the threshold of a large room, almost in darkness, for only a tiny oil lamp hung over a table on the left at the back. 'Who's that with you, Barnabas?' asked the girl. 'The land surveyor,' he said. 'The land surveyor,' the girl repeated more loudly towards the table. At that two old people stood up there, a man and a woman, and another girl. They greeted K. Barnabas introduced them all: they were his parents and his sisters, Olga and Amalia. K. hardly looked at them; they took off his wet coat to dry it by the stove. K. let them.
paras.uz: Bir qiz ochdi; ular deyarli qorong'i katta xonaning ostonasida turishardi, chunki faqat chap tomonda, orqadagi stol tepasida kichkina moy chiroq osilib turardi. «Sen bilan kim keldi, Barnabas?» — so'radi qiz. «Yer o'lchovchi», dedi u. «Yer o'lchovchi», takrorladi qiz stol tomonga balandroq ovozda. Shunda u yerda ikki keksa odam — er va xotin, yana bir qiz o'rnidan turishdi. K. bilan salomlashishdi. Barnabas hammasini tanishtirdi: bular uning ota-onasi va singillari Olga va Amaliya edi. K. ularga deyarli qaramadi, ho'l kamzulini pechka yonida quritish uchun yechib olishdi. K. bunga yo'l qo'ydi.

paras.en: So it was not they who were at home — only Barnabas was at home. But why were they here? K. took Barnabas aside and asked: 'Why have you gone home? Or do you already live within the bounds of the Castle?' — 'Within the bounds of the Castle?' Barnabas repeated, as though he did not understand K. 'Barnabas,' said K., 'you meant to go from the inn to the Castle.' — 'No, sir,' said Barnabas, 'I meant to go home. I don't go to the Castle until early morning; I never sleep there.' — 'So,' said K., 'you didn't mean to go to the Castle, only here.' His smile seemed duller to him, Barnabas himself more insignificant. 'Why didn't you tell me?' — 'You didn't ask me, sir,' said Barnabas. 'You only wanted to give me another message, but neither in the taproom nor in your room, so I thought you could give me the message undisturbed here with my parents. They will all go away at once if you order it; and if you like it better with us, you could spend the night here. Haven't I done right?' K. could not answer. It had been a misunderstanding, then, a common, low misunderstanding, and K. had surrendered himself to it completely. He had let himself be enchanted by Barnabas's tight, silk-sheened jacket, which Barnabas was now unbuttoning, and under which there appeared a coarse, grey-dirty, much-patched shirt over the mighty, square chest of a farmhand.
paras.uz: Demak, uyda ular emas, faqat Barnabas uyda edi. Lekin ular nega bu yerda edi? K. Barnabasni chetga tortib so'radi: «Nega uyingga kelding? Yoki sizlar allaqachon Qasr hududida yashaysizlarmi?» — «Qasr hududidami?» — deb takrorladi Barnabas, go'yo K.ni tushunmayotgandek. «Barnabas, — dedi K., — axir sen mehmonxonadan Qasrga bormoqchi eding-ku.» — «Yo'q, taqsir, — dedi Barnabas, — men uyga bormoqchi edim; Qasrga faqat erta tongda boraman, u yerda hech qachon uxlamayman.» — «Shunday, — dedi K., — sen Qasrga emas, faqat shu yerga bormoqchi bo'lgan ekansan.» — Uning jilmayishi unga xiraroq, o'zi esa ko'rimsizroq tuyuldi. — «Nega buni menga aytmading?» — «Siz so'ramadingiz, taqsir, — dedi Barnabas, — siz menga faqat yana bir topshiriq bermoqchi edingiz, lekin na umumiy zalda, na xonangizda; shunda o'yladimki, topshiriqni shu yerda, ota-onamnikida xalaqitsiz bera olasiz. Agar buyursangiz, ularning hammasi darhol chiqib ketishadi; agar bizda sizga ko'proq yoqsa, shu yerda tunashingiz ham mumkin. To'g'ri qilmadimmi?» K. javob bera olmadi. Demak, bu anglashilmovchilik ekan, past, tuban anglashilmovchilik, K. esa unga butunlay berilib ketgan ekan. U Barnabasning tor, ipakdek yaltiroq kamzuliga maftun bo'lgan edi; Barnabas endi uning tugmalarini yechayotgan edi va uning ostidan qishloq malayining kuchli, burchakli ko'kragi ustida dag'al, kulrang-iflos, ko'p yamalgan ko'ylak ko'rindi.

paras.en: And everything round about not only matched this but outdid it: the old, gouty father, who moved forward more with the help of his groping hands than of his stiff, slowly shuffling legs; the mother, with her hands folded on her breast, who because of her stoutness could take only the tiniest steps. Both father and mother had been coming towards him from their corner ever since K. came in, and were still far from reaching him. The sisters, both fair, like each other and like Barnabas but with harder features than his, big strong girls, stood round the newcomers and waited for some word of greeting from K. But he could say nothing. He had believed that here in the village everyone mattered to him, and that was probably so; only these people here did not concern him at all. Had he been able to manage the way back to the inn alone, he would have left at once. The possibility of going to the Castle early in the morning with Barnabas did not tempt him at all. Now, at night, unnoticed, he would have liked to press into the Castle, led by Barnabas — but by Barnabas as he had appeared to him until now, a man closer to him than all those he had seen here so far, and of whom he had at the same time believed that he was closely connected with the Castle, far beyond his visible rank.
paras.uz: Va atrofdagi hamma narsa bunga nafaqat mos kelar, balki undan ham oshib tushardi: sekin suriladigan qotgan oyoqlari emas, ko'proq paypaslovchi qo'llari yordamida oldinga siljiydigan keksa, podagrali ota; qo'llarini ko'kragida qovushtirib olgan, semizligi tufayli faqat eng mayda qadamlar tashlay oladigan ona. Ikkalasi — ota ham, ona ham — K. kirganidan beri o'z burchaklaridan unga qarab yurishar va hali unga yetib kelishdan juda uzoq edi. Singillar — ikkalasi ham sarg'ish sochli, bir-biriga va Barnabasga o'xshash, lekin Barnabasnikidan qattiqroq chehrali, katta, baquvvat qizlar — kelganlar atrofida turib, K.dan qandaydir salom so'zini kutishardi. Lekin u hech narsa ayta olmadi; u bu yerda, qishloqda har kim uning uchun ahamiyatga ega, deb ishongan edi va, ehtimol, shunday ham edi, faqat aynan bu yerdagi odamlar uni umuman qiziqtirmasdi. Agar mehmonxonagacha yo'lni yolg'iz bosib o'ta olsa, darhol ketib qolardi. Erta tongda Barnabas bilan Qasrga borish imkoniyati uni umuman jalb qilmasdi. Hozir, tunda, hech kimga sezdirmay, u Barnabas boshchiligida Qasrga kirib bormoqchi edi — lekin hozirgacha unga ko'ringan o'sha Barnabas boshchiligida: bu yerda hozirgacha ko'rganlarining hammasidan unga yaqinroq bo'lgan va ayni paytda ko'rinadigan martabasidan ancha yuqori darajada Qasr bilan chambarchas bog'liq, deb ishongan odam boshchiligida.

paras.en: But to go into the Castle in broad daylight on the arm of the son of this family — to which he wholly belonged and with which he was already sitting at table — with a man who, significantly, was not even allowed to sleep in the Castle: that was impossible, a ridiculously hopeless attempt.
paras.uz: Lekin u butunlay tegishli bo'lgan, u bilan allaqachon bir stolda o'tirgan bu oilaning o'g'li bilan — xarakterli tarzda Qasrda hatto uxlashga ham ruxsati bo'lmagan odam bilan — uning qo'lida kunduzi Qasrga borish imkonsiz edi, kulgili darajada umidsiz urinish edi.

paras.en: K. sat down on a window seat, determined to spend the night there too and not to accept any other service from the family. The people from the village who sent him away or who were afraid of him seemed less dangerous to him, for basically they referred him back to himself and helped him keep his strength gathered together. But such apparent helpers, who instead of leading him to the Castle led him, thanks to a little masquerade, into their families, distracted him whether they meant to or not, and worked at destroying his strength. He paid no attention whatever to an inviting call from the family table, and stayed on his seat with his head lowered.
paras.uz: K. deraza tokchasiga o'tirdi, tunni ham shu yerda o'tkazishga va oiladan boshqa hech qanday xizmat olmaslikka qaror qilib. Uni haydagan yoki undan qo'rqqan qishloq odamlari unga xavfsizroq tuyulardi, chunki ular aslida uni o'ziga qaytarar, kuchlarini to'plangan holda saqlashga yordam berardi; lekin uni Qasrga emas, kichik bir niqoblanish tufayli o'z oilalariga olib kelgan bunday zohiriy yordamchilar, xohlasalar ham, xohlamasalar ham, uni chalg'itar, kuchlarini yo'q qilish ustida ishlardi. Oila stolidan kelgan taklifli chaqiruvga u umuman e'tibor bermadi, boshini egib, o'rindig'ida qolaverdi.

paras.en: Then Olga, the gentler of the sisters, stood up — she showed a trace of girlish embarrassment too — came over to K. and asked him to come to the table. Bread and bacon were ready there, and she would fetch some beer. 'From where?' asked K. 'From the inn,' she said. That was very welcome to K. He asked her not to fetch any beer but to take him with her to the inn; he had important work still waiting there. But it now turned out that she did not mean to go so far, not to his inn, but to another one much nearer, the Herrenhof. Even so K. asked to be allowed to go with her; perhaps, he thought, he would find somewhere to sleep there; whatever it was like, he would have preferred it to the best bed here in the house. Olga did not answer at once but looked round at the table. There the brother had stood up; he nodded readily and said: 'If the gentleman wishes.' This consent almost moved K. to withdraw his request — that man could consent only to worthless things. But when the question was now discussed whether K. would be let into the inn, and everyone doubted it, he still insisted urgently on going, without taking the trouble to invent an understandable reason for his request. This family had to take him as he was; in a sense he felt no shame before it. Only Amalia unsettled him a little in this, with her serious, direct, unmovable, perhaps rather dull gaze.
paras.uz: Shunda singillarning muloyimrog'i Olga o'rnidan turdi — unda qizlarcha xijolatning izi ham ko'rinardi — K.ning oldiga kelib, uni stolga kelishga taklif qildi. U yerda non va cho'chqa yog'i tayyor, pivoni u hozir olib keladi. «Qayerdan?» — so'radi K. «Mehmonxonadan», dedi u. Bu K.ga juda ma'qul bo'ldi. U undan pivo olib kelmaslikni, balki o'zini mehmonxonaga kuzatib qo'yishni so'radi, u yerda hali muhim ishlari bor. Lekin endi ma'lum bo'ldiki, u bunchalik uzoqqa, uning mehmonxonasiga emas, balki boshqa, ancha yaqinroq mehmonxonaga — «Herrenhof»ga (janoblar mehmonxonasiga) bormoqchi ekan. Shunga qaramay K. unga hamroh bo'lishga ruxsat so'radi; balki, deb o'yladi u, u yerda tunash uchun joy topilar; qanday bo'lmasin, u uni bu uydagi eng yaxshi to'shakdan afzal ko'rgan bo'lardi. Olga darhol javob bermadi, stol tomonga qaradi. U yerda akasi o'rnidan turib, tayyorlik bilan bosh irg'adi va dedi: «Agar janob xohlasa.» Bu rozilik K.ni iltimosini qaytarib olishga undashiga oz qoldi — u faqat qadrsiz narsalarga rozi bo'la olardi. Lekin endi K.ni mehmonxonaga kiritisharmikan, degan masala muhokama qilinib, hammasi bunga shubha qilganida, u baribir iltimosiga qandaydir tushunarli sabab o'ylab topishga urinmasdan, borishni qat'iy talab qildi; bu oila uni qanday bo'lsa, shunday qabul qilishi kerak edi, u bir ma'noda uning oldida hech qanday uyat hissini sezmasdi. Bunda uni faqat Amaliya o'zining jiddiy, to'g'ri, qimirlamas, balki biroz to'mtoq nigohi bilan biroz sarosimaga soldi.

paras.en: On the short way to the inn — K. had taken Olga's arm and was being pulled along by her, he could not help it, almost as he had been by her brother earlier — he learned that this inn was really meant only for gentlemen from the Castle, who ate there when they had business in the village and sometimes even spent the night. Olga spoke to K. quietly and as if they were close; it was pleasant to walk with her, almost as with her brother. K. resisted the feeling of comfort, but it was there.
paras.uz: Mehmonxonagacha qisqa yo'lda — K. Olganing qo'lidan ushlab olgan va, boshqa ilojini topa olmay, xuddi avval akasi sudragandek deyarli u tomonidan sudralib borardi — u bu mehmonxona aslida faqat Qasr janoblari uchun mo'ljallanganini bildi: ular qishloqda biror ishlari bo'lganda u yerda ovqatlanishar va hatto ba'zan tunashardi. Olga K. bilan sekin va go'yo yaqin odamdek gaplashardi; u bilan yurish yoqimli edi, deyarli akasi bilan yurgandek. K. bu yoqimli hissga qarshilik qildi, lekin u bor edi.

paras.en: From outside, the inn looked very like the inn where K. was staying. There were probably no great outward differences in the village at all, yet small differences could be noticed at once: the front steps had a railing, and a handsome lantern was fixed above the door. As they went in, a cloth fluttered over their heads — a flag in the Count's colours. In the hall they at once met the landlord, evidently on a round of inspection; with small eyes, searching or sleepy, he looked at K. in passing and said: 'The land surveyor may go only as far as the bar.' 'Of course,' said Olga, immediately taking K.'s part, 'he is only seeing me there.' But K., ungratefully, freed himself from Olga and took the landlord aside. Olga meanwhile waited patiently at the end of the hall. 'I'd like to spend the night here,' said K. 'That is unfortunately impossible,' said the landlord. 'You don't seem to know yet.
paras.uz: Tashqi ko'rinishdan mehmonxona K. yashayotgan mehmonxonaga juda o'xshardi. Qishloqda umuman katta tashqi farqlar bo'lmasa kerak, lekin kichik farqlar darhol ko'zga tashlanardi: old zinaning panjarasi bor edi, eshik tepasiga chiroyli fonus o'rnatilgan edi. Ular kirishganda, boshlari ustida mato hilpiradi — bu graflik ranglaridagi bayroq edi. Dahlizda ularni darhol, aftidan nazorat aylanishida yurgan mehmonxona egasi uchratdi; kichkina, sinchkov yoki uyqusiragan ko'zlari bilan u o'tib ketayotib K.ga qaradi va dedi: «Janob yer o'lchovchi faqat bufetgacha kira oladi.» «Albatta, — dedi K.ni darhol o'z himoyasiga olgan Olga, — u meni faqat kuzatib keldi.» Lekin K. noshukurlik bilan Olgadan ajralib, mehmonxona egasini chetga tortdi. Olga bu orada dahlizning oxirida sabr bilan kutib turdi. «Men shu yerda tunamoqchiman», dedi K. «Afsuski, bu mumkin emas, — dedi mehmonxona egasi. — Siz hali bilmasangiz kerak.

paras.en: This house is meant exclusively for the gentlemen from the Castle.' — 'That may be the rule,' said K., 'but surely it is possible to let me sleep somewhere in a corner.' — 'I should be exceedingly glad to oblige you,' said the landlord, 'but quite apart from the strictness of the rule, which you speak of as strangers do, it is also impracticable because the gentlemen are extremely sensitive. I am convinced that they are incapable, at least unprepared, of bearing the sight of a stranger. So if I let you spend the night here and you were discovered by some chance — and chance is always on the gentlemen's side — not only I would be lost but you yourself as well. It sounds ridiculous, but it is true.' This tall, tightly buttoned gentleman, who spoke to K. confidentially, one hand pressed against the wall, the other on his hip, his legs crossed, bending down a little towards K., hardly seemed to belong to the village any more, even if his dark clothes still looked only like a peasant's Sunday best. 'I believe you completely,' said K., 'and I don't underestimate the importance of the rule at all, even if I expressed myself clumsily.
paras.uz: Bu uy faqat Qasr janoblari uchun mo'ljallangan.» — «Bu qoida bo'lishi mumkin, — dedi K., — lekin meni qayerdadir bir burchakda uxlatish, albatta, mumkin.» — «Sizga juda bajonidil yon bosgan bo'lardim, — dedi mehmonxona egasi, — lekin siz begonalarga xos tarzda gapirayotgan qoidaning qattiqligidan tashqari ham, buni amalga oshirib bo'lmaydi, chunki janoblar nihoyatda nozik; ishonamanki, ular, hech bo'lmaganda tayyorgarliksiz, begona odamni ko'rishga chiday olmaydilar; agar sizni shu yerda tunatsam va siz tasodifan — tasodiflar esa doim janoblar tomonida — topilib qolsangiz, nafaqat men, balki o'zingiz ham halok bo'lasiz. Kulgili eshitiladi, lekin bu haqiqat.» Bir qo'lini devorga tirab, ikkinchisini beliga qo'yib, oyoqlarini chalishtirib, K.ga biroz egilib, u bilan samimiy gaplashayotgan bu baland bo'yli, tugmalarini mahkam qadagan janob qorong'i kiyimi hali faqat dehqoncha bayramona ko'rinsa ham, endi qishloqqa deyarli tegishli emasdek tuyulardi. «Sizga to'liq ishonaman, — dedi K., — va qoidaning ahamiyatini ham umuman kam baholamayman, garchi o'zimni noqulay ifodalagan bo'lsam ham.

paras.en: Only one thing I'd like to point out to you: I have valuable connections at the Castle and shall get even more valuable ones; they protect you against any danger that might arise from my spending the night here, and they guarantee that I am in a position to repay a small favour in full.' — 'I know,' said the landlord, and repeated once more: 'I know that.' Now K. could have pressed his demand, but precisely this answer of the landlord's distracted him, so he only asked: 'Are many gentlemen from the Castle spending the night here today?' — 'In that respect today is favourable,' said the landlord, almost temptingly. 'Only one gentleman has stayed.' Still K. could not bring himself to insist, and was already hoping he had almost been taken in; so he merely asked the gentleman's name. 'Klamm,' said the landlord casually, as he turned round to his wife, who came rustling up in strangely worn, old-fashioned town clothes overloaded with ruffles and pleats, but fine ones. She had come to fetch the landlord: the head of department had some wish. But before the landlord went, he turned to K. once more, as though it were no longer he himself but K. who had to decide about the night's lodging. K., however, could say nothing; it was especially the fact that his own superior was here that dumbfounded him.
paras.uz: Faqat bir narsaga e'tiboringizni qaratmoqchiman: Qasrda qimmatli aloqalarim bor va bundan ham qimmatlirog'ini olaman, ular sizni mening bu yerda tunashim tufayli yuzaga kelishi mumkin bo'lgan har qanday xavfdan himoya qiladi va kichik bir iltifot uchun to'liq minnatdorchilik bildira olishimga kafolat beradi.» — «Bilaman», dedi mehmonxona egasi va yana takrorladi: «Buni bilaman.» Endi K. talabini qat'iy qo'yishi mumkin edi, lekin aynan mehmonxona egasining bu javobi uni chalg'itdi, shuning uchun faqat so'radi: «Bugun bu yerda Qasrdan ko'p janoblar tunayaptimi?» — «Bu jihatdan bugun qulay, — dedi mehmonxona egasi go'yo vasvasaga solgandek. — Faqat bitta janob qoldi.» K. hamon talab qila olmadi, endi deyarli qabul qilinganiga umid ham qilayotgan edi; shuning uchun faqat janobning ismini so'radi. «Klamm», dedi mehmonxona egasi yo'l-yo'lakay va g'alati eskirgan, modadan qolgan, burma va jiyaklar bilan haddan tashqari bezatilgan, lekin nafis shaharcha kiyimlarda shitirlab kelayotgan xotiniga o'girildi. U mehmonxona egasini chaqirgani kelgan edi: janob boshliqning qandaydir istagi bor ekan. Lekin mehmonxona egasi ketishdan oldin yana K.ga o'girildi, go'yo tunash masalasini endi u o'zi emas, K. hal qilishi kerakdek. Lekin K. hech narsa ayta olmadi; ayniqsa aynan uning boshlig'i shu yerda ekani uni lol qoldirdi.

paras.en: Without being quite able to explain it to himself, he did not feel as free towards Klamm as he otherwise did towards the Castle. To be caught here by him would not have been a horror for K. in the landlord's sense, but it would have been an embarrassing impropriety, rather as if he were thoughtlessly to cause pain to someone to whom he owed gratitude. At the same time it weighed on him heavily to see that in such scruples the dreaded consequences of being a subordinate, of being a worker, were evidently already showing, and that he could not fight them down even here, where they appeared so plainly. So he stood there, biting his lips, and said nothing. Once more, before the landlord disappeared through a door, he looked back at K. K. looked after him and did not move from the spot until Olga came and drew him away. 'What did you want from the landlord?' asked Olga. 'I wanted to spend the night here,' said K. 'But you'll spend the night with us,' said Olga in surprise. 'Yes, of course,' said K., and left the interpretation of his words to her. In the bar, a large room completely empty in the middle, some peasants were sitting along the walls by the barrels and on top of them — but they looked different from the people at K.'s inn. They were cleaner and more uniformly dressed in coarse greyish-yellow cloth, with baggy jackets and tight trousers. They were small men, at first sight very like one another, with flat, bony and yet round-cheeked faces.
paras.uz: O'zi ham buni to'liq tushuntira olmagan holda, u Klammga nisbatan odatda Qasrga nisbatan bo'lganidek erkin his qilmasdi; uning tomonidan shu yerda tutib olinish K. uchun mehmonxona egasi aytgan ma'nodagi dahshat bo'lmasa-da, baribir noqulay nojo'ya ish bo'lardi — taxminan minnatdor bo'lishi kerak bo'lgan odamga o'ylamasdan og'riq yetkazgandek; shu bilan birga, bunday ikkilanishlarda bo'ysunuvchi bo'lishning, ishchi bo'lishning qo'rqinchli oqibatlari, aftidan, allaqachon namoyon bo'layotganini va ular aniq ko'ringan shu yerda ham ularni yenga olmayotganini ko'rish uni og'ir ezardi. Shunday qilib u turdi, lablarini tishladi va hech narsa demadi. Mehmonxona egasi bir eshik ortida g'oyib bo'lishdan oldin yana bir bor K.ga qaradi. K. uning ortidan qarab qoldi va Olga kelib, uni olib ketguncha joyidan qimirlamadi. «Mehmonxona egasidan nima istading?» — so'radi Olga. «Shu yerda tunamoqchi edim», dedi K. «Axir sen bizda tunaysan-ku», dedi Olga hayron bo'lib. «Ha, albatta», dedi K. va so'zlarning talqinini unga qoldirdi. O'rtasi butunlay bo'm-bo'sh katta xona bo'lgan bufetda devorlar bo'ylab bochkalar yonida va ularning ustida bir necha dehqon o'tirardi, lekin ular K.ning mehmonxonasidagi odamlardan boshqacha ko'rinardi. Ular ozodaroq va bir xilroq — kulrang-sarg'ish, dag'al matoga kiyingan edilar, kamzullari keng, shimlari tor edi. Ular kichkina, birinchi qarashda bir-biriga juda o'xshash, yassi, suyakdor, lekin dumaloq yonoqli erkaklar edi.

paras.en: All were quiet and hardly moved; they followed the newcomers only with their eyes, and even that slowly and indifferently. Even so, because there were so many of them and because it was so quiet, they had a certain effect on K. He took Olga's arm again, so as to explain to these people why he was there. In one corner a man stood up, an acquaintance of Olga's, and was about to come over to her, but K. turned her away in another direction with the arm he held. No one but she could notice it; she put up with it with a smiling sidelong glance.
paras.uz: Hammasi jim edi va deyarli qimirlamasdi, kirganlarni faqat nigohlari bilan kuzatishardi, lekin sekin va befarq. Shunga qaramay, ular shunchalik ko'p bo'lgani va shunchalik jimjit bo'lgani uchun K.ga qandaydir ta'sir qilardi. U odamlarga bu yerda bo'lishini tushuntirish uchun yana Olganing qo'lidan ushladi. Bir burchakda Olganing tanishi bo'lgan bir erkak o'rnidan turib, unga yaqinlashmoqchi bo'ldi, lekin K. ushlab turgan qo'li bilan uni boshqa tomonga burib yubordi. Buni undan boshqa hech kim payqay olmasdi; u bunga jilmayib, yonlama qarash bilan chidadi.

paras.en: The beer was served by a young girl called Frieda — an inconspicuous, small, fair girl with sad eyes and thin cheeks, but who surprised one by her look, a look of particular superiority. When this look fell on K., it seemed to him that it had already settled matters concerning K. whose very existence he himself did not yet know of, but of whose existence the look convinced him. K. did not stop looking at Frieda from the side, even when she was already talking to Olga. Olga and Frieda did not seem to be friends; they exchanged only a few cold words. K. wanted to help things along and so asked abruptly: 'Do you know Herr Klamm?' Olga burst out laughing. 'Why are you laughing?' asked K. crossly. 'I'm not laughing,' she said, but went on laughing. 'Olga is still a rather childish girl,' said K., and leaned far over the counter so as to draw Frieda's gaze firmly to himself once more. But she kept it lowered and said quietly: 'Would you like to see Herr Klamm?' K. said he would. She pointed to a door just to her left. 'There's a little peephole here; you can look through it.' — 'And the people here?' asked K. She pushed out her lower lip and drew K. to the door with an extraordinarily soft hand. Through the little peephole, which had evidently been bored for purposes of observation, he could see almost the whole of the next room.
paras.uz: Pivoni Frida ismli yosh qiz quyib berardi. Ko'rimsiz, kichkina, sarg'ish sochli, g'amgin ko'zli va ozg'in yuzli qiz, lekin u nigohi bilan hayratga solardi — o'ziga xos ustunlik nigohi bilan. Bu nigoh K.ga tushganida, unga bu nigoh K.ga tegishli, uning o'zi hali mavjudligini ham bilmagan, lekin nigoh mavjudligiga uni ishontirgan ishlarni allaqachon hal qilib qo'ygandek tuyuldi. K. Frida Olga bilan gaplasha boshlaganida ham unga yonlama qarashdan to'xtamadi. Olga va Frida dugona emasdek edi, ular faqat bir-ikki sovuq so'z almashishdi. K. yordam bermoqchi bo'lib, kutilmaganda so'radi: «Siz janob Klammni taniysizmi?» Olga qah-qah urib kuldi. «Nega kulyapsan?» — so'radi K. achchiqlanib. «Kulayotganim yo'q-ku», dedi u, lekin kulishda davom etdi. «Olga hali ancha bolalarcha qiz», dedi K. va Fridaning nigohini yana bir bor o'ziga qattiq tortish uchun peshtaxta ustiga ancha engashdi. Lekin u nigohini pastga qaratib turdi va sekin dedi: «Janob Klammni ko'rmoqchimisiz?» K. iltimos qildi. U o'zining shundoqqina chap tomonidagi eshikni ko'rsatdi. «Mana bu yerda kichkina tirqish bor, shundan qarashingiz mumkin.» — «Bu yerdagi odamlar-chi?» — so'radi K. U pastki labini burdi va g'ayrioddiy yumshoq qo'li bilan K.ni eshik tomon tortdi. Aftidan kuzatish maqsadida teshilgan kichkina tirqish orqali u qo'shni xonaning deyarli hammasini ko'ra oldi.

paras.en: At a desk in the middle of the room, in a comfortable round-backed armchair, harshly lit by an electric bulb hanging down in front of him, sat Herr Klamm: a middle-sized, fat, ponderous gentleman. His face was still smooth, but his cheeks were already sagging a little with the weight of age. His black moustache was drawn out long. A pince-nez, set on askew and reflecting the light, hid his eyes. Had Herr Klamm been sitting squarely at the table, K. would have seen only his profile; but as Klamm was turned well towards him, he saw him full face. Klamm had his left elbow on the table; his right hand, holding a Virginia cigar, rested on his knee. On the table stood a beer glass. Because the rim of the table was high, K. could not see exactly whether any papers were lying there, but it seemed to him that it was empty. To be sure, he asked Frieda to look through the hole and tell him. But since she had been in the room a little while ago, she could confirm without further ado that no papers lay there. K. asked Frieda whether he had to go away now, but she said he could look through as long as he liked. K. was now alone with Frieda. Olga, as he noted in passing, had found her way to her acquaintance after all; she was sitting high up on a barrel, kicking her feet. 'Frieda,' said K. in a whisper, 'do you know Herr Klamm very well?' — 'Oh yes,' she said.
paras.uz: Xonaning o'rtasidagi yozuv stoli oldida, qulay dumaloq suyanchiqli kresloda, oldida osilib turgan elektr lampochka bilan o'tkir yoritilgan holda janob Klamm o'tirardi. O'rta bo'yli, semiz, og'ir harakatli janob. Yuzi hali silliq edi, lekin yonoqlari yosh og'irligi bilan biroz osilib qolgan edi. Qora mo'ylovi uzun tortib qo'yilgan edi. Qiyshiq taqilgan, yaltirab turgan pensne ko'zlarini to'sib turardi. Agar janob Klamm stolga to'g'ri o'tirganida, K. faqat uning profilini ko'rgan bo'lardi; lekin Klamm unga ancha o'girilib o'tirgani uchun, uning yuziga to'g'ri qaradi. Klamm chap tirsagini stolga qo'ygan, Virjiniya sigarasini ushlab turgan o'ng qo'li tizzasida yotardi. Stolda pivo stakani turardi; stolning chekka hoshiyasi baland bo'lgani uchun K. u yerda qandaydir qog'ozlar yotganini aniq ko'ra olmadi, lekin unga stol bo'shdek tuyuldi. Ishonch hosil qilish uchun u Fridadan tirqishdan qarab, unga bu haqda aytib berishni so'radi. Lekin u yaqinda xonada bo'lgani uchun K.ga u yerda hech qanday qog'oz yo'qligini darhol tasdiqladi. K. Fridadan endi ketishi kerakmi, deb so'radi, lekin u istaganicha qarab turishi mumkinligini aytdi. K. endi Frida bilan yolg'iz edi; Olga, u bir zum payqaganidek, baribir tanishining oldiga yo'l topgan, bochka ustida baland o'tirib, oyoqlarini silkitardi. «Frida, — dedi K. pichirlab, — siz janob Klammni juda yaxshi taniysizmi?» — «Ha, albatta», dedi u.

paras.en: 'Very well.' She was leaning beside K. and, playfully, as K. only now noticed, adjusting her light, low-cut, cream-coloured blouse, which lay on her poor body as though it belonged to someone else. Then she said: 'Don't you remember Olga's laughing?' — 'Yes, the naughty girl,' said K. 'Well,' she said, conciliatingly, 'there was reason to laugh. You asked whether I know Klamm, and I am' — here she involuntarily drew herself up a little, and again her triumphant look, quite unconnected with what was being said, passed over K. — 'I am his mistress.' — 'Klamm's mistress,' said K. She nodded. 'Then you are,' said K., smiling, so as not to let too much seriousness come between them, 'a person to be respected, so far as I'm concerned.' — 'Not only so far as you are concerned,' said Frieda kindly, but without taking up his smile. K. had a remedy for her arrogance, and he applied it; he asked: 'Have you ever been to the Castle?' But it did not work, for she answered: 'No, but isn't it enough that I am here in the bar?' Her ambition was evidently wild, and it was on K., it seemed, that she wanted to satisfy it. 'Certainly,' said K., 'here in the bar — after all, you understand the landlord's work.' — 'That's right,' she said, 'and I started as a stable girl at the Bridge Inn.' — 'With those delicate hands?' said K., half asking, and did not himself know whether he was only flattering or had really been conquered by her.
paras.uz: «Juda yaxshi.» U K.ning yonida suyanib turardi va o'ynoqi tarzda, K. endigina payqaganidek, bechora tanasida begonanikidek turgan yengil, ochiq yoqali, krem rangli bluzkasini to'g'rilardi. Keyin dedi: «Olganing kulgisi esingizdami?» — «Ha, odobsiz qiz», dedi K. «Xo'sh, — dedi u yarashuvchan ohangda, — kulishga sabab bor edi. Siz Klammni taniysizmi, deb so'radingiz, axir men… — shu yerda u beixtiyor biroz qad rostladi va yana uning aytilayotgan gapga umuman aloqasi yo'q g'olibona nigohi K. ustidan o'tdi, — axir men uning ma'shuqasiman.» — «Klammning ma'shuqasi», dedi K. U bosh irg'adi. «Unda siz, — dedi K. jilmayib, ular o'rtasida haddan tashqari jiddiylik paydo bo'lmasligi uchun, — men uchun hurmatga sazovor shaxssiz.» — «Faqat siz uchun emas», dedi Frida mehribonlik bilan, lekin uning jilmayishini qabul qilmay. K.da uning takabburligiga qarshi bir vosita bor edi va u uni qo'lladi; u so'radi: «Qasrda bo'lganmisiz?» Lekin bu ta'sir qilmadi, chunki u javob berdi: «Yo'q, lekin men bu yerda, bufetda ekanim yetarli emasmi?» Uning shuhratparastligi, aftidan, telbalarcha edi va uni aynan K. hisobiga qondirmoqchidek tuyulardi. «Albatta, — dedi K., — bu yerda, bufetda, axir siz mehmonxona egasining ishini tushunasiz.» — «Shunday, — dedi u, — boshlanishda men «Ko'prik yonidagi» mehmonxonada otxona xizmatkori edim.» — «Shu nozik qo'llar bilanmi?» — dedi K. yarim so'roq ohangida va o'zi ham faqat xushomad qilayaptimi yoki haqiqatan ham u tomonidan zabt etilganmi, bilmasdi.

paras.en: Her hands were indeed small and delicate; but one could also have called them weak and expressionless. 'Nobody paid any attention to that then,' she said, 'and even now —' K. looked at her questioningly. She shook her head and would not go on. 'Of course you have your secrets,' said K., 'and you won't speak of them to someone you have known for half an hour and who hasn't yet had a chance to tell you how matters really stand with him.' But this, as it turned out, was an unfortunate remark; it was as if he had woken Frieda from a slumber that had been favourable to him. She took a little wooden peg out of the leather bag that hung at her belt, stopped up the peephole with it, and said to K., visibly controlling herself so that he should not notice the change in her feelings: 'As far as you are concerned, I know everything; you are the land surveyor.' Then she added: 'But now I must get to work,' and went to her place behind the bar, while here and there one of the men stood up to have his empty glass filled by her. K. wanted to speak to her once more unobtrusively, so he took an empty glass from a rack and went over to her. 'Just one more thing, Fräulein Frieda,' he said. 'It is extraordinary, and it takes exceptional strength, to work one's way up from stable girl to barmaid. But for such a person, is that the final goal?
paras.uz: Uning qo'llari, albatta, kichkina va nozik edi; lekin ularni zaif va ifodasiz deb ham atash mumkin edi. «O'shanda bunga hech kim e'tibor bermagan, — dedi u, — hatto hozir ham…» K. unga so'roq nazari bilan qaradi. U boshini chayqadi va boshqa gapirishni istamadi. «Albatta, — dedi K., — sizning o'z sirlaringiz bor va siz ular haqida yarim soatdan beri taniydigan, hali sizga o'zi haqida aslida qanday ekanini aytib berishga imkoni bo'lmagan odam bilan gaplashmaysiz.» Lekin bu, ma'lum bo'lishicha, nojo'ya gap bo'ldi; go'yo u Fridani o'zi uchun qulay bo'lgan mudroqdan uyg'otib yuborgandek bo'ldi. U kamaridagi charm sumkadan kichkina yog'och tiqin olib, tirqishni tiqib qo'ydi va kayfiyati o'zgarganini K. payqamasligi uchun ko'rinib turibdiki o'zini tutib, K.ga dedi: «Sizga kelsak, men hammasini bilaman, siz yer o'lchovchisiz», keyin qo'shib qo'ydi: «Endi esa ishga kirishim kerak», va bufet peshtaxtasi ortidagi joyiga ketdi; bu orada odamlardan biri u yerda, biri bu yerda bo'sh stakanini to'ldirish uchun o'rnidan turardi. K. u bilan yana bir bor sezdirmay gaplashmoqchi edi, shuning uchun tokchadan bo'sh stakan olib, uning oldiga bordi. «Yana faqat bir narsa, Frida xonim, — dedi u, — otxona xizmatkoridan bufetchi qizgacha ko'tarilish g'ayrioddiy ish va buning uchun alohida kuch kerak, lekin bunday odam uchun bu bilan yakuniy maqsadga erishildimi?

paras.en: A senseless question. From your eyes — don't laugh at me, Fräulein Frieda — it is not so much past struggle that speaks as struggle to come. But the resistance of the world is great; it grows with greater goals; and it is no disgrace to secure the help even of a small man without influence, but one who is fighting just as hard. Perhaps we could talk together in peace some time, without so many eyes staring at us.' — 'I don't know what you want,' she said, and this time there seemed to sound in her voice, against her will, not the victories of her life but its endless disappointments. 'Do you perhaps want to take me away from Klamm? Good heavens!' And she clapped her hands together. 'You've seen through me,' said K., as though tired of so much mistrust. 'That was precisely my most secret intention. You were to leave Klamm and become my mistress. And now I can go. Olga!' called K. 'We're going home.' Obediently Olga slid down from the barrel, but could not get free at once of the friends crowding round her. Then Frieda said quietly, looking at K. threateningly: 'When can I talk to you?' — 'Can I spend the night here?' asked K. 'Yes,' said Frieda. 'Can I stay right now?' — 'Go off with Olga, so that I can get rid of the people here. Then you can come back in a little while.' — 'Good,' said K., and waited impatiently for Olga.
paras.uz: Bema'ni savol. Sizning ko'zlaringizdan — mendan kulmang, Frida xonim — o'tgan kurashdan ko'ra ko'proq kelajakdagi kurash gapirib turibdi. Lekin dunyoning qarshiligi katta, u katta maqsadlar bilan kattalashadi va hatto kichik, ta'sirsiz, lekin xuddi shunday kurashayotgan odamning yordamini ta'minlash uyat emas. Balki biz bir kun tinchgina, shuncha ko'p ko'zlar tikilmagan holda gaplasharmiz.» — «Nima istayotganingizni bilmayman», dedi u va bu safar uning ohangida, irodasiga qarshi, hayotining g'alabalari emas, balki cheksiz ko'ngil qolishlari jaranglagandek tuyuldi. «Balki meni Klammdan ajratib olmoqchidirsiz? Voy Xudoyim!» — va u qo'llarini bir-biriga urdi. «Meni fosh qildingiz, — dedi K. go'yo shuncha ishonchsizlikdan charchagandek, — aynan shu mening eng yashirin niyatim edi. Siz Klammni tashlab, mening ma'shuqam bo'lishingiz kerak edi. Endi esa ketishim mumkin. Olga! — chaqirdi K. — Uyga ketamiz.» Olga itoatkorona bochkadan sirpanib tushdi, lekin uni o'rab olgan do'stlaridan darhol qutula olmadi. Shunda Frida K.ga tahdidli qarab, sekin dedi: «Siz bilan qachon gaplasha olaman?» — «Shu yerda tunashim mumkinmi?» — so'radi K. «Ha», dedi Frida. «Hozir qolsam bo'ladimi?» — «Olga bilan chiqib keting, men bu yerdagi odamlarni chiqarib yuboray. Biroz o'tib kelishingiz mumkin.» — «Yaxshi», dedi K. va Olgani toqatsizlik bilan kutdi.

paras.en: But the peasants would not let her go. They had invented a dance with Olga at its centre; they danced round her in a ring, and every time they all shouted together, one of them stepped up to Olga, seized her firmly round the waist with one hand and whirled her round several times. The ring went faster and faster, and the shouts, hungry and rasping, gradually became almost a single one. Olga, who earlier had tried laughing to break out of the circle, now only reeled from one to another with her hair coming loose. 'These are the people they send me,' said Frieda, biting her thin lips in anger. 'Who are they?' asked K. 'Klamm's servants,' said Frieda. 'He always brings this lot with him, and their presence wrecks me. I hardly know what I have said to you today, land surveyor; if it was anything bad, forgive me; the presence of these people is to blame. They are the most contemptible and disgusting creatures I know, and I have to pour the beer into their glasses. How often I have asked Klamm to leave them at home. If I have to put up with the servants of other gentlemen, he at least could show me some consideration; but all my begging is in vain. An hour before he arrives they always come storming in, like cattle into the stable. But now they really shall go into the stable, where they belong.
paras.uz: Lekin dehqonlar uni qo'yib yuborishmadi, ular Olga markazida bo'lgan bir raqs o'ylab topishgan edi: davra bo'lib uning atrofida aylanib raqsga tushishar va har safar birgalikda qichqirganlarida, ulardan biri Olgaga yaqinlashib, uni bir qo'li bilan belidan mahkam ushlab, bir necha marta aylantirardi; davra tobora tezlashar, och, xirillagan qichqiriqlar asta-sekin deyarli bitta bo'lib qolardi. Avval davrani kulib yorib chiqmoqchi bo'lgan Olga endi sochi to'zg'igan holda faqat biridan ikkinchisiga gandiraklab borardi. «Menga mana shunday odamlarni yuborishadi», dedi Frida va jahl bilan ingichka lablarini tishladi. «Ular kim?» — so'radi K. «Klammning xizmatkorlari, — dedi Frida. — U doim bu xalqni o'zi bilan olib keladi, ularning borligi meni ado qiladi. Bugun siz bilan, janob yer o'lchovchi, nima gaplashganimni zo'rg'a bilaman; agar biror yomon gap bo'lsa, kechiring, bunga bu odamlarning borligi aybdor, ular men biladigan eng jirkanch va eng manfur mavjudotlar, men esa ularning stakanlariga pivo quyishim kerak. Klammdan ularni uyda qoldirishni necha marta so'raganman; agar boshqa janoblarning xizmatkorlariga chidashim kerak bo'lsa, hech bo'lmaganda u meni hisobga olishi mumkin edi, lekin barcha iltimoslar behuda, u kelishidan bir soat oldin ular doim go'yo mollar otxonaga yopirilgandek bostirib kirishadi. Lekin endi ular haqiqatan ham o'zlari tegishli bo'lgan otxonaga borishsin.

paras.en: If you weren't here I would tear this door open, and Klamm himself would have to drive them out.' — 'Doesn't he hear them, then?' asked K. 'No,' said Frieda. 'He's asleep.' — 'What!' cried K. 'Asleep? When I looked into the room he was still awake, sitting at the table.' 'He's still sitting like that,' said Frieda. 'Even when you saw him he was already asleep. Would I have let you look in otherwise? That was his sleeping position. The gentlemen sleep a great deal; one can hardly understand it. Besides, if he didn't sleep so much, how could he bear these people? But now I shall have to drive them out myself.' She took a whip from the corner and, with a single high, not quite steady leap — rather as a lamb leaps — sprang towards the dancers. At first they turned towards her as though a new dancer had arrived, and indeed for a moment it looked as though Frieda would let the whip fall; but then she raised it again. 'In Klamm's name,' she cried, 'into the stable! All of you into the stable!' Now they saw she was in earnest. In a terror incomprehensible to K. they began to crowd towards the back; under the push of the first of them a door there flew open, the night air blew in, and they all disappeared with Frieda, who was evidently driving them across the yard into the stable.
paras.uz: Agar siz bu yerda bo'lmaganingizda, men mana bu eshikni yulqib ochardim va Klammning o'zi ularni haydab chiqarishi kerak bo'lardi.» — «U ularni eshitmaydimi?» — so'radi K. «Yo'q, — dedi Frida. — U uxlayapti.» — «Qanday? — qichqirdi K. — Uxlayaptimi? Men xonaga qaraganimda u hali uyg'oq edi va stol yonida o'tirardi.» «U hamon shunday o'tiribdi, — dedi Frida, — siz uni ko'rganingizda ham u allaqachon uxlayotgan edi. Aks holda sizga qarashga ruxsat berarmidim? Bu uning uxlash holati edi, janoblar juda ko'p uxlaydi, buni tushunish qiyin. Aytgancha, agar u shunchalik ko'p uxlamaganida, bu odamlarga qanday chidardi? Endi esa ularni o'zim haydab chiqarishimga to'g'ri keladi.» U burchakdan qamchi oldi va qo'zichoq sakraganidek, bitta baland, unchalik ishonchli bo'lmagan sakrash bilan raqs tushayotganlar tomon otildi. Avvaliga ular go'yo yangi raqqosa kelgandek unga qarab o'girilishdi va haqiqatan ham bir lahza Frida qamchini tushirib yubormoqchidek ko'rindi, lekin keyin uni yana ko'tardi. «Klamm nomidan, — qichqirdi u, — otxonaga! Hammang otxonaga!» Endi ular bu jiddiy ekanini ko'rishdi; K.ga tushunarsiz qo'rquv bilan ular orqa tomonga yopirila boshlashdi, birinchilarining turtkisidan u yerdagi eshik ochildi, ichkariga tungi havo esdi va hammasi Frida bilan birga g'oyib bo'lishdi — u, aftidan, ularni hovli orqali otxonaga haydab borayotgan edi.
