chapters.title: 9. The record
chapters.recap_uz: K. bo'sh hovlida o'zini erkin, ammo bu erkinlik ma'nosiz ekanini his qiladi. Bufetda yosh janob o'zini Momus — Klammning qishloq kotibi deb tanishtiradi va K.dan bayonnoma uchun savollarga javob berishni talab qiladi. Beka bu bayonnoma K. uchun Klammga olib boradigan yagona yo'l ekanini aytadi, ammo Momus Klamm bayonnomalarni o'qimasligini tan oladi. K. so'roqdan bosh tortib ketadi. Yo'lda Barnabas Klammdan xat olib keladi: Klamm K.ning qilmagan o'lchash ishlarini maqtaydi. K. bu tushunmovchilik ekanini aytadi va Barnabas uning oldingi xabarini hali yetkazmaganini bilib, jahli chiqadi.

paras.en: Perhaps he did have this power, but it could have been of no use to him; to call the sledge back would have meant driving himself away. So he stayed still, the only one holding his ground — but it was a victory that gave no joy. He looked alternately after the gentleman and the coachman. The gentleman had already reached the door through which K. had first entered the yard; once more he looked back — K. thought he saw him shake his head at so much obstinacy — then turned with a resolute, short, final movement and entered the hall, where he disappeared at once. The coachman stayed longer in the yard; he had a lot of work with the sledge: he had to open the heavy stable door, back the sledge into its place, unharness the horses, lead them to their manger. He did all this seriously, completely withdrawn into himself, without any hope of an early drive; this silent handling, without a single sidelong glance at K., seemed to K. a much harsher reproach than the gentleman's behaviour.
paras.uz: Balki unda bu qudrat bor edi, lekin u unga hech qanday foyda keltira olmasdi; chanani qaytarib chaqirish o'zini haydash degani edi. Shunday qilib, u joyini saqlab qolgan yagona odam sifatida jim qoldi, lekin bu quvonch keltirmaydigan g'alaba edi. U navbatma-navbat janob va aravakashning ortidan qaradi. Janob allaqachon K. hovliga birinchi kirgan eshikka yetib borgan edi, u yana bir bor orqasiga qaradi — K.ga u shunchalik qaysarlik ustidan bosh chayqayotgandek tuyuldi — keyin qat'iy, qisqa, yakuniy harakat bilan o'girilib, dahlizga kirdi va u yerda darhol g'oyib bo'ldi. Aravakash hovlida uzoqroq qoldi, chana bilan ishi ko'p edi: og'ir otxona eshigini ochishi, chanani orqaga yurgizib joyiga qo'yishi, otlarni chiqarib, oxuriga olib borishi kerak edi; bularning hammasini u jiddiy, butunlay o'ziga cho'mib, tez orada yo'lga chiqishga hech qanday umidsiz qilardi; K.ga birorta ham yonlama qaramay qilinayotgan bu jim ish K.ga janobning xatti-harakatidan ancha qattiqroq ta'nadek tuyuldi.

paras.en: And when, his work in the stable finished, the coachman crossed the yard with his slow, rocking walk, shut the big gate, then came back, everything slowly and as if only contemplating his own track in the snow, then shut himself into the stable, and now switched off all the electric light too — for whom should it shine? — and only the slit in the wooden gallery up above stayed bright and held the wandering eye a little: then it seemed to K. as though all connection with him had now been broken off, and as though he were now, of course, freer than ever, and could wait here, in this place otherwise forbidden to him, as long as he liked, and had fought for this freedom as hardly anyone else could, and nobody might touch him or drive him away, indeed hardly speak to him; but — and this conviction was at least as strong — as though at the same time there were nothing more senseless, nothing more desperate, than this freedom, this waiting, this inviolability.
paras.uz: Va otxonadagi ish tugagach, aravakash sekin, chayqaluvchan yurishi bilan hovlini kesib o'tib, katta darvozani yopdi, keyin qaytib keldi — hammasini sekin va go'yo faqat qordagi o'z iziga qarab — keyin otxonaga o'zini qulflab oldi va endi barcha elektr chiroqlarini ham o'chirdi — ular kimga yorug'lik berishi kerak edi? — va faqat tepada, yog'och ayvondagi tirqish yorug' qolib, adashgan nigohni biroz ushlab turganida, K.ga go'yo endi u bilan barcha aloqa uzilgandek, go'yo u endi, albatta, har qachongidan erkinroqdek va bu yerda, unga aks holda taqiqlangan joyda xohlaganicha kuta oladigandek, bu erkinlikni boshqa hech kim qila olmaydigan darajada kurashib qo'lga kiritgandek, hech kim unga tega olmaydi, haydab yubora olmaydi, hatto gapira olmaydigandek tuyuldi; lekin — bu ishonch hech bo'lmaganda xuddi shunchalik kuchli edi — go'yo ayni paytda bu erkinlikdan, bu kutishdan, bu daxlsizlikdan ko'ra ma'nosizroq, umidsizroq narsa yo'qdek.

paras.en: And he tore himself away and went back into the house, this time not along the wall but straight through the snow. In the hall he met the landlord, who greeted him silently and pointed to the door of the bar. He followed the hint, because he was cold and because he wanted to see people, but was very disappointed when he saw there, at a little table that had probably been set up specially — for otherwise people made do with barrels there — the young gentleman sitting, and standing in front of him — a depressing sight for K. — the landlady of the Bridge Inn. Pepi, proud, her head thrown back, with her eternally identical smile, irrefutably conscious of her dignity, swinging her braid at every turn, hurried to and fro, brought beer and then ink and pen, for the gentleman had papers spread out in front of him, was comparing data that he found now in one paper, now in another at the other end of the table, and now wanted to write. The landlady, from her height, quietly surveyed the gentleman and the papers, her lips pushed out a little, as if resting, as though she had already said everything necessary and it had been well received. 'The land surveyor, at last,' said the gentleman as K. came in, looking up briefly; then he became absorbed in his papers again. The landlady too merely brushed K. with an indifferent, not at all surprised look. But Pepi seemed to notice K. at all only when he stepped up to the counter and ordered a brandy.
paras.uz: Va u o'zini yulib oldi va uyga qaytdi, bu safar devor bo'ylab emas, to'g'ri qor o'rtasidan; dahlizda mehmonxona egasini uchratdi, u indamay salom berib, bufet eshigini ko'rsatdi; K. sovqotgani va odamlarni ko'rishni istagani uchun ishoraga amal qildi, lekin u yerda, ehtimol, ataylab qo'yilgan kichkina stol yonida — chunki aks holda u yerda bochkalar bilan qanoatlanishardi — yosh janob o'tirganini va uning oldida — K. uchun og'ir manzara — «Ko'prik yonidagi» mehmonxonaning bekasi turganini ko'rib, juda ko'ngli qoldi. Pepi mag'rur, boshini orqaga tashlab, doim bir xil jilmayish bilan, o'z obro'sini inkor etib bo'lmas darajada anglab, har burilishda o'rimini silkitib, u yoqdan-bu yoqqa shoshilar, pivo, keyin siyoh va qalam olib kelardi, chunki janob oldiga qog'ozlarni yoyib qo'ygan, goh bu qog'ozda, goh stolning narigi chetidagi boshqa qog'ozda topgan ma'lumotlarni solishtirar va endi yozmoqchi edi. Beka o'z balandligidan, lablarini biroz bo'rtirib, go'yo dam olayotgandek, janob va qog'ozlarni jim kuzatardi, go'yo u barcha zarur gaplarni allaqachon aytgan va ular yaxshi qabul qilingandek. «Janob yer o'lchovchi, nihoyat», dedi janob K. kirganida bir zum boshini ko'tarib, keyin yana qog'ozlariga cho'mdi. Beka ham K.ga faqat befarq, umuman hayron bo'lmagan nigoh tashladi. Pepi esa K.ni faqat u bufet peshtaxtasiga kelib, konyak buyurgandagina payqagandek bo'ldi.

paras.en: K. leaned there, pressed his hand to his eyes and paid no attention to anything. Then he sipped the brandy and pushed it back because it was undrinkable. 'All the gentlemen drink it,' said Pepi curtly, poured away the rest, washed the little glass and put it on the shelf. 'The gentlemen have better as well,' said K. 'Possibly,' said Pepi, 'but I don't.' With that she had finished with K. and was again at the service of the gentleman, who needed nothing, however, and behind whom she kept walking up and down in an arc, with respectful attempts to glance at the papers over his shoulders; but it was only empty curiosity and showing off, which the landlady too disapproved of with knitted brows.
paras.uz: K. u yerga suyanib, qo'lini ko'zlariga bosdi va hech narsa bilan qiziqmadi. Keyin konyakdan ho'pladi va uni ichib bo'lmasligi uchun orqaga surdi. «Hamma janoblar uni ichishadi», dedi Pepi qisqagina, qolganini to'kib tashladi, qadahchani yuvib, javonga qo'ydi. «Janoblarda yaxshirog'i ham bor», dedi K. «Bo'lishi mumkin, — dedi Pepi, — lekin menda yo'q.» Shu bilan u K. bilan ishini tugatdi va yana janobning xizmatiga o'tdi; lekin unga hech narsa kerak emas edi, Pepi esa uning orqasida doim yoy bo'ylab u yoqdan-bu yoqqa yurib, uning yelkasi osha qog'ozlarga hurmat bilan ko'z tashlashga urinardi; lekin bu faqat ma'nosiz qiziqish va kerilish edi, beka ham buni qoshlarini chimirib ma'qullamadi.

paras.en: Suddenly, however, the landlady listened intently and stared into space, wholly given up to listening. K. turned round; he heard nothing special, and the others did not seem to hear anything either; but the landlady ran on tiptoe with long strides to the door at the back that led into the yard, looked through the keyhole, then turned to the others with eyes wide open and a flushed face, beckoned them to her with her finger, and now they took turns looking through. The landlady kept the largest share, but Pepi too was always given a turn; the gentleman was relatively the most indifferent. Pepi and the gentleman soon came back, only the landlady still looked through strenuously, deeply bent, almost kneeling; one almost had the impression that she was now only imploring the keyhole to let her through, for there had long been nothing more to see. When at last she did get up, passed her hands over her face, tidied her hair, took a deep breath and seemed to have to get her eyes used again to the room and the people here — and did so reluctantly — K. said, not to have something he knew confirmed, but to forestall an attack he almost feared, so vulnerable was he now: 'So Klamm has already driven off?' The landlady walked past him in silence, but the gentleman said from his little table: 'Yes, certainly. Since you had given up your sentry post, Klamm was able to leave.
paras.uz: Lekin birdan beka quloq soldi va butunlay tinglashga berilib, bo'shliqqa tikilib qoldi. K. o'girildi, u hech qanday alohida narsa eshitmadi, boshqalar ham hech narsa eshitmayotgandek edi, lekin beka oyoq uchida katta qadamlar bilan orqadagi hovliga olib chiqadigan eshik tomon yugurdi, kalit teshigidan qaradi, keyin ko'zlarini katta ochib, yuzi qizargan holda boshqalarga o'girildi, barmog'i bilan ularni o'ziga chaqirdi va endi ular navbatma-navbat qarashdi; bekaga, to'g'ri, eng katta ulush tegdi, lekin Pepi ham doim hisobga olinardi, janob esa nisbatan eng befarq edi. Pepi va janob tez orada qaytib kelishdi, faqat beka hamon zo'r berib, chuqur egilib, deyarli tiz cho'kib qarab turardi; go'yo u endi faqat kalit teshigidan o'zini o'tkazishni yolvorayotgandek taassurot paydo bo'lardi, chunki ko'radigan narsa allaqachon qolmagan bo'lsa kerak. U nihoyat baribir o'rnidan turib, qo'llari bilan yuzini silab, sochini tuzatib, chuqur nafas olib, ko'zlarini go'yo xonaga va bu yerdagi odamlarga yana ko'niktirishi kerakdek va buni istamaygina qilganida, K. — bilgan narsasini tasdiqlatish uchun emas, balki deyarli qo'rqayotgan hujumning oldini olish uchun, chunki u hozir shunchalik zaif edi — dedi: «Demak, Klamm allaqachon jo'nab ketdimi?» Beka indamay uning yonidan o'tib ketdi, lekin janob kichkina stolidan dedi: «Ha, albatta. Siz qorovullik joyingizni tashlab ketganingiz uchun Klamm jo'nab keta oldi.

paras.en: But it is wonderful how sensitive the gentleman is. Did you notice, Frau Landlady, how uneasily Klamm looked all round?' The landlady seemed not to have noticed that, but the gentleman went on: 'Well, fortunately there was nothing more to be seen; the coachman had swept away the footprints in the snow too.' — 'The landlady didn't notice anything,' said K., but he said it not from any hope, only irritated by the gentleman's assertion, which had meant to sound so final and beyond appeal. 'Perhaps I wasn't at the keyhole just then,' said the landlady, at first to take the gentleman's part; but then she wanted to give Klamm his due as well and added: 'Though I don't believe in such great sensitivity on Klamm's part. We, of course, are afraid for him and try to protect him, and in doing so we start from the assumption that Klamm is extremely sensitive. That is as it should be, and certainly Klamm's will. But how it is in reality, we don't know. Certainly, Klamm will never speak to someone he doesn't want to speak to, however much trouble this someone takes and however unbearably he pushes forward; but this fact alone, that Klamm will never speak to him, never let him come before his face, is enough — why should he in reality be unable to bear the sight of anyone? At least it cannot be proved, since it will never come to the test.' The gentleman nodded eagerly.
paras.uz: Lekin janobning qanchalik sezgir ekani ajoyib. Payqadingizmi, bekam, Klamm atrofga qanchalik bezovta qaradi?» Beka buni payqamaganga o'xshardi, lekin janob davom etdi: «Xo'sh, baxtimizga, endi hech narsa ko'rinmasdi, aravakash qordagi izlarni ham supurib tekislab qo'ygan edi.» — «Beka hech narsa payqamadi», dedi K., lekin buni qandaydir umid bilan emas, faqat janobning shunchalik yakuniy va e'tiroz bildirib bo'lmaydigandek eshitilishini istagan da'vosidan g'ashlanib aytdi. «Balki men o'sha paytda kalit teshigi oldida bo'lmagandirman», dedi beka avval janobni himoya qilish uchun, lekin keyin Klammga ham haqqini bermoqchi bo'lib qo'shib qo'ydi: «To'g'ri, men Klammning bunchalik katta sezgirligiga ishonmayman. Biz, albatta, u uchun qo'rqamiz va uni himoya qilishga urinamiz, bunda Klammning nihoyatda sezgirligi haqidagi farazdan kelib chiqamiz. Bu yaxshi va, albatta, Klammning irodasi. Lekin haqiqatda qanday ekanini bilmaymiz. Albatta, Klamm gaplashishni istamagan odam bilan, bu odam qanchalik harakat qilmasin va qanchalik chidab bo'lmas darajada oldinga intilmasin, hech qachon gaplashmaydi; lekin Klamm u bilan hech qachon gaplashmasligi, uni hech qachon o'z huzuriga kiritmasligi faktining o'zi yetarli — nega u haqiqatda biror kishini ko'rishga chiday olmasligi kerak? Hech bo'lmaganda buni isbotlab bo'lmaydi, chunki bu hech qachon sinovga kelmaydi.» Janob g'ayrat bilan bosh irg'adi.

paras.en: 'That is of course basically my opinion too,' he said. 'If I expressed myself a little differently, it was in order to be understood by the land surveyor. But it is true that when Klamm stepped outside he looked round several times in a semicircle.' — 'Perhaps he was looking for me,' said K. 'Possibly,' said the gentleman, 'that hadn't occurred to me.' Everyone laughed — Pepi, who understood hardly anything of the whole matter, loudest of all.
paras.uz: «Bu, albatta, aslida mening ham fikrim, — dedi u, — agar o'zimni biroz boshqacha ifodalagan bo'lsam, bu janob yer o'lchovchiga tushunarli bo'lish uchun edi. Lekin to'g'ri, Klamm ochiq havoga chiqqanida bir necha marta yarim doira bo'ylab atrofga qaradi.» — «Balki u meni izlagandir», dedi K. «Bo'lishi mumkin, — dedi janob, — bu xayolimga kelmagan edi.» Hamma kuldi, butun ishdan deyarli hech narsa tushunmagan Pepi eng baland ovozda.

paras.en: 'Since we are all so cheerful together now,' the gentleman then said, 'I would very much ask you, land surveyor, to complete my files with a few particulars.' — 'There is a great deal of writing here,' said K., looking at the files from a distance. 'Yes, a bad habit,' said the gentleman, and laughed again. 'But perhaps you don't even know who I am. I am Momus, Klamm's village secretary.' At these words the whole room became serious; although the landlady and Pepi of course knew the gentleman, they were as if struck by the mention of the name and the dignity. And even the gentleman himself, as if he had said too much for his own capacity to take it in, and as if he wanted at least to flee from any after-solemnity inherent in his own words, became absorbed in the files and began to write, so that nothing could be heard in the room but the pen. 'What is that, then — a village secretary?' asked K. after a little while. For Momus, who, having introduced himself, no longer thought it fitting to give such explanations himself, the landlady said: 'Herr Momus is Klamm's secretary, like any of Klamm's secretaries, but his official seat and, if I'm not mistaken, his official sphere too —' Momus, without stopping writing, shook his head vigorously, and the landlady corrected herself — 'well, only his official seat, not his official sphere, is limited to the village.
paras.uz: «Endi biz shunchalik quvnoq birga bo'lganimizdan keyin, — dedi keyin janob, — sizdan, janob yer o'lchovchi, hujjatlarimni bir nechta ma'lumot bilan to'ldirishingizni juda iltimos qilardim.» — «Bu yerda ko'p yoziladi», dedi K. va hujjatlarga uzoqdan qaradi. «Ha, yomon odat, — dedi janob va yana kuldi, — lekin balki siz hali mening kimligimni ham bilmassiz. Men Momus, Klammning qishloq kotibiman.» Bu so'zlardan keyin butun xonada jiddiylik cho'kdi; beka va Pepi janobni, albatta, tanisalar ham, ism va mansabning aytilishidan go'yo larzaga kelishdi. Hatto janobning o'zi ham, go'yo o'z qabul qilish qobiliyati uchun haddan ortiq gapirib yuborgandek va hech bo'lmaganda o'z so'zlariga xos har qanday keyingi tantanavorlikdan qochmoqchidek, hujjatlarga cho'mdi va yoza boshladi, shuning uchun xonada qalamdan boshqa hech narsa eshitilmasdi. «Qishloq kotibi degani nima?» — so'radi K. biroz o'tgach. O'zini tanishtirgandan keyin bunday tushuntirishlarni o'zi berishni endi munosib deb hisoblamagan Momus uchun beka dedi: «Janob Momus — Klammning kotibi, Klammning har qanday kotibi kabi, lekin uning ish joyi va, agar adashmasam, ish doirasi ham…» — Momus yozishdan to'xtamay qattiq bosh chayqadi, beka esa o'zini tuzatdi, — «ya'ni faqat ish joyi, ish doirasi emas, qishloq bilan cheklangan.

paras.en: Herr Momus attends to the written work of Klamm's that becomes necessary in the village, and is the first to receive all requests to Klamm that come from the village.' When K., still little moved by these things, looked at the landlady with empty eyes, she added, half embarrassed: 'That's how it's arranged; all the gentlemen from the Castle have their village secretaries.' Momus, who had listened much more attentively than K., said, supplementing the landlady: 'Most village secretaries work for only one gentleman, but I work for two, for Klamm and for Vallabene.' — 'Yes,' said the landlady, now remembering it in her turn, and turned to K. 'Herr Momus works for two gentlemen, for Klamm and for Vallabene, so he is a double village secretary.' — 'Double, even,' said K., and nodded to Momus — who now, almost leaning forward, was looking up at him full face — as one nods to a child one has just heard praised. If there was a certain contempt in it, it was either not noticed or positively demanded. Precisely before K., who was not even worthy enough to be seen by Klamm even by chance, the merits of a man from Klamm's closest circle were presented at length, with the undisguised intention of provoking K.'s recognition and praise.
paras.uz: Janob Momus Klammning qishloqda zarur bo'lib qoladigan yozma ishlarini bajaradi va qishloqdan Klammga keladigan barcha arizalarni birinchi bo'lib qabul qiladi.» K. bu narsalardan hali unchalik ta'sirlanmagan holda bekaga bo'sh ko'zlar bilan qaraganida, u yarim xijolat bilan qo'shib qo'ydi: «Shunday tartib, Qasrning barcha janoblarining qishloq kotiblari bor.» K.dan ancha diqqat bilan tinglagan Momus bekani to'ldirib dedi: «Ko'pchilik qishloq kotiblari faqat bitta janob uchun ishlaydi, men esa ikkita uchun — Klamm va Vallabene uchun.» — «Ha», dedi beka endi o'zi ham eslab va K.ga o'girildi: «Janob Momus ikki janob uchun — Klamm va Vallabene uchun ishlaydi, demak, u ikki karra qishloq kotibi.» — «Hatto ikki karra», dedi K. va endi deyarli oldinga engashib, unga tik qarab turgan Momusga, xuddi hozirgina maqtovini eshitgan bolaga bosh irg'aganidek, bosh irg'adi. Agar bunda qandaydir nafrat bo'lgan bo'lsa, u yo payqalmadi, yo rosmana talab qilindi. Aynan Klamm tomonidan hatto tasodifan ko'rilishga ham loyiq bo'lmagan K.ning oldida Klammning eng yaqin davrasidan bo'lgan odamning xizmatlari K.ning tan olishi va maqtovini qo'zg'atish niyatini yashirmagan holda batafsil bayon qilinardi.

paras.en: And yet K. had no real sense for it. He, who was striving with all his strength for a glance from Klamm, did not, for example, value highly the position of a Momus, who was allowed to live under Klamm's eyes; admiration, let alone envy, was far from him, for it was not Klamm's nearness in itself that he found worth striving for, but that he, K., only he and nobody else, should come to Klamm with his wishes and no one else's — and come to him not in order to rest with him, but in order to get past him, further into the Castle.
paras.uz: Shunga qaramay, K.da bunga to'g'ri munosabat yo'q edi; butun kuchi bilan Klammning bir nigohiga intilayotgan u, masalan, Klammning ko'z o'ngida yashashga ruxsat berilgan Momus kabi odamning mavqeini yuqori baholamasdi; hayrat, hatto hasad undan uzoq edi, chunki unga intilishga arziydigan narsa Klammning yaqinligining o'zi emas, balki uning — K.ning, faqat uning, boshqa hech kimning emas, o'z istaklari bilan, boshqa hech kimning istaklari bilan emas, Klammga yetib borishi edi — u bilan dam olish uchun emas, balki undan o'tib, Qasrga yanada ichkariroq kirish uchun.

paras.en: And he looked at his watch and said: 'But now I must go home.' At once the relationship changed in Momus's favour. 'Yes, of course,' he said, 'the caretaker's duties are calling. But you must give me a moment more. Only a few short questions.' — 'I don't feel like it,' said K., and made to go to the door. Momus struck a file against the table and stood up: 'In Klamm's name I call on you to answer my questions.' — 'In Klamm's name?' K. repeated. 'Do my affairs concern him, then?' — 'On that,' said Momus, 'I have no judgement, and you surely much less; so let us both confidently leave that to him.
paras.uz: Va u soatiga qarab dedi: «Endi esa uyga ketishim kerak.» Darhol munosabat Momusning foydasiga o'zgardi. «Ha, albatta, — dedi u, — maktab qorovulining burchlari chaqiryapti. Lekin menga yana bir lahza ajratishingiz kerak. Faqat bir nechta qisqa savol.» — «Xohishim yo'q», dedi K. va eshik tomon yurmoqchi bo'ldi. Momus bir hujjatni stolga urdi va o'rnidan turdi: «Klamm nomidan sizni savollarimga javob berishga chaqiraman.» — «Klamm nomidanmi? — takrorladi K. — Uni mening ishlarim qiziqtiradimi?» — «Bu haqda, — dedi Momus, — mening hukmim yo'q, siznikida esa undan ham kamroq, shuning uchun buni ikkalamiz ham ishonch bilan unga qoldiraylik.

paras.en: But in my position, conferred on me by Klamm, I do call on you to stay and answer.' — 'Land surveyor,' the landlady interposed, 'I shall take care not to advise you any further. I have been rebuffed by you in an unheard-of way with my advice so far — the most well-meant there could be — and I have come here to the secretary — I have nothing to hide — only to inform the authorities properly of your behaviour and your intentions, and to protect myself for all time against your being quartered on me again. That is how we stand towards each other, and nothing is likely to change that now; and so if I now give my opinion, I do it not to help you but to lighten a little the heavy task the secretary has in dealing with a man like you. Nevertheless, precisely because of my complete frankness — I cannot deal with you other than frankly, and even so I do it reluctantly — you too can draw some benefit from my words, if only you want to. In that case I would point out to you that the only path that leads, for you, to Klamm goes here, through the secretary's records.
paras.uz: Lekin Klamm menga bergan lavozimimda sizni qolishga va javob berishga chaqiraman.» — «Janob yer o'lchovchi, — gapga aralashdi beka, — men sizga boshqa maslahat berishdan saqlanaman; axir men hozirgacha bergan maslahatlarim bilan — eng xayrixoh maslahatlar bilan — siz tomonidan misli ko'rilmagan tarzda rad etildim; bu yerga, janob kotibning oldiga — yashiradigan hech narsam yo'q — men faqat idorani xatti-harakatingiz va niyatlaringiz haqida munosib tarzda xabardor qilish va sizning yana menikiga joylashtirilishingizdan o'zimni abadiy himoya qilish uchun keldim; biz bir-birimizga shunday munosabatdamiz va buni endi hech narsa o'zgartirmasa kerak; shuning uchun agar hozir fikrimni aytsam, buni sizga yordam berish uchun emas, balki janob kotibga siz kabi odam bilan muzokara olib borishning og'ir vazifasini biroz yengillashtirish uchun qilaman. Shunga qaramay, aynan mening to'liq ochiqligim tufayli — siz bilan ochiqdan boshqacha muomala qila olmayman, shunda ham istamaygina — agar xohlasangiz, so'zlarimdan o'zingiz uchun ham foyda olishingiz mumkin. Shu holat uchun sizning e'tiboringizni shunga qarataman: siz uchun Klammga olib boradigan yagona yo'l shu yerda, janob kotibning bayonnomalari orqali o'tadi.

paras.en: But I don't want to exaggerate; perhaps the path doesn't lead as far as Klamm, perhaps it stops far short of him; that is for the secretary's discretion to decide. But in any case it is the only path that leads, for you, at least in the direction of Klamm. And you want to give up this only path for no other reason than defiance?' — 'Oh, Frau Landlady,' said K., 'it is neither the only path to Klamm, nor is it worth more than the others. And you, secretary, decide whether what I might say here may reach Klamm or not?' 'Certainly,' said Momus, looking with proudly lowered eyes to right and left, where there was nothing to be seen, 'what else would I be secretary for?' — 'There, you see, Frau Landlady,' said K., 'it's not to Klamm that I need a path, but first to the secretary.' — 'That's the path I wanted to open for you,' said the landlady. 'Didn't I offer this morning to pass your request on to Klamm? That would have been done through the secretary. But you refused, and yet now nothing will remain for you but this path. Of course, after your conduct today, after your attempted ambush of Klamm, with even less prospect of success.
paras.uz: Lekin mubolag'a qilmoqchi emasman, balki yo'l Klammgacha olib bormas, balki undan ancha oldin tugar, bunda janob kotibning ixtiyori hal qiladi. Har holda bu siz uchun hech bo'lmaganda Klamm tomon olib boradigan yagona yo'l. Va siz bu yagona yo'ldan faqat qaysarlik tufayli voz kechmoqchimisiz?» — «Eh, bekam, — dedi K., — bu na Klammga yagona yo'l, na boshqalaridan qimmatroq. Siz-chi, janob kotib, bu yerda aytadigan gapim Klammgacha yetib borishi mumkinmi-yo'qmi, shuni hal qilasizmi?» «Albatta, — dedi Momus va mag'rur ko'zlarini pastga qaratib, hech narsa ko'rinmaydigan o'ngga va chapga qaradi, — aks holda nega kotib bo'lardim.» — «Mana, ko'ryapsizmi, bekam, — dedi K., — menga Klammgacha emas, avval janob kotibgacha yo'l kerak.» — «Men sizga aynan shu yo'lni ochmoqchi edim, — dedi beka. — Ertalab men sizga iltimosingizni Klammga yetkazishni taklif qilmaganmidim? Bu janob kotib orqali bo'lardi. Lekin siz rad etdingiz, shunga qaramay endi sizga shu yo'ldan boshqa hech narsa qolmaydi. Albatta, bugungi xatti-harakatingizdan keyin, Klammga qilingan hujum urinishidan keyin muvaffaqiyatga yanada kamroq umid bilan.

paras.en: But this last, smallest, vanishing, really non-existent hope is still your only one.' — 'How is it, Frau Landlady,' said K., 'that at first you tried so hard to keep me from pressing on to Klamm, and now you take my request so very seriously and seem to consider me lost, in a sense, if my plans fail? If someone could advise me from a sincere heart not to strive for Klamm at all, how is it possible that the same person now, apparently just as sincerely, positively drives me forward on the path to Klamm, even though admittedly it may not lead to him at all?' — 'Am I driving you forward?' said the landlady. 'Is it driving forward when I say your attempts are hopeless? It would truly be the height of audacity if you wanted to shift responsibility for yourself onto me like that. Is it perhaps the presence of the secretary that gives you the desire? No, land surveyor, I'm driving you to nothing. I can only admit this one thing: that when I first saw you, I perhaps overestimated you a little. Your quick victory over Frieda frightened me; I didn't know what else you might be capable of; I wanted to prevent further mischief and thought I could achieve that only by trying to shake you with pleas and threats. In the meantime I have learned to think about the whole thing more calmly. Do what you like.
paras.uz: Lekin bu so'nggi, eng kichik, yo'qolib borayotgan, aslida umuman mavjud bo'lmagan umid baribir sizning yagona umidingiz.» — «Bekam, qanday qilib, — dedi K., — avvaliga siz meni Klammga yetib borishdan shunchalik qattiq qaytarishga urindingiz, endi esa iltimosimga shunchalik jiddiy qarayapsiz va rejalarim barbod bo'lsa, meni go'yo halok bo'lgan deb hisoblayotgandek ko'rinasiz? Agar meni bir marta chin yurakdan umuman Klammga intilmaslikka undash mumkin bo'lgan bo'lsa, qanday qilib endi meni go'yo xuddi shunchalik samimiy ravishda Klammga — tan olish kerakki, umuman unga olib bormasligi mumkin bo'lsa ham — olib boradigan yo'lda rosmana oldinga haydash mumkin?» — «Men sizni oldinga haydayapmanmi? — dedi beka. — Urinishlaringiz umidsiz deyishim oldinga haydash bo'ladimi? Agar shu tarzda o'zingiz uchun mas'uliyatni mening zimmamga ag'darmoqchi bo'lsangiz, bu haqiqatan jasoratning eng yuqori cho'qqisi bo'lardi. Balki janob kotibning borligi sizni bunga undayotgandir? Yo'q, janob yer o'lchovchi, men sizni hech narsaga undamayman. Faqat bir narsani tan olishim mumkin: sizni birinchi marta ko'rganimda, balki sizni biroz ortiqcha baholagandirman. Fridani tez zabt etganingiz meni qo'rqitdi, yana nimalarga qodir bo'lishingizni bilmasdim, yangi baxtsizlikning oldini olmoqchi edim va bunga faqat sizni iltimoslar va tahdidlar bilan larzaga solishga urinish orqali erishish mumkin, deb o'yladim. Bu orada men butun ish haqida xotirjamroq o'ylashni o'rgandim. Xohlaganingizni qiling.

paras.en: Your deeds will perhaps leave deep footprints out there in the snow in the yard, but nothing more.' — 'The contradiction doesn't seem to me entirely cleared up,' said K., 'but I'm content to have drawn attention to it. Now, though, I ask you, secretary, to tell me whether the landlady's opinion is right — namely, that the record you want to take with me could, in its consequences, lead to my being allowed to appear before Klamm. If that's the case, I'm ready to answer all the questions at once. In that respect I'm ready for anything at all.' — 'No,' said Momus, 'no such connections exist. It's only a matter of obtaining, for Klamm's village registry, an exact description of this afternoon. The description is already finished; you are only to fill in two or three gaps, for the sake of order; there is no other purpose, nor can any other be achieved.' K. looked at the landlady in silence. 'Why are you looking at me?' asked the landlady. 'Did I perhaps say anything different? That's how he always is, secretary, that's how he always is. He falsifies the information he's given and then claims he was given false information. I've always told him — yesterday, today, and always — that he hasn't the slightest prospect of being received by Klamm; well, if there's no prospect, he won't get one through this record either. Can anything be clearer?
paras.uz: Qilmishlaringiz, ehtimol, tashqarida, hovlidagi qorda chuqur izlar qoldirar, lekin undan ortiq emas.» — «Qarama-qarshilik menga butunlay oydinlashmagandek tuyuladi, — dedi K., — lekin unga e'tibor qaratganim bilan qanoatlanaman. Endi esa sizdan, janob kotib, ayting: bekaning fikri to'g'rimi — ya'ni siz men bilan tuzmoqchi bo'lgan bayonnoma oqibatda Klammning huzuriga chiqishimga ruxsat berilishiga olib kelishi mumkinmi? Agar shunday bo'lsa, barcha savollarga darhol javob berishga tayyorman. Bu borada men umuman hamma narsaga tayyorman.» — «Yo'q, — dedi Momus, — bunday bog'liqliklar yo'q. Gap faqat Klammning qishloq qayd idorasi uchun bugungi tushdan keyingi vaqtning aniq tavsifini olish haqida. Tavsif allaqachon tayyor, siz faqat ikki-uchta bo'shliqni to'ldirishingiz kerak, tartib uchun; boshqa maqsad yo'q va unga erishib ham bo'lmaydi.» K. bekaga indamay qaradi. «Nega menga qarayapsiz? — so'radi beka. — Balki men boshqa narsa degandirman? U doim shunday, janob kotib, doim shunday. Unga berilgan ma'lumotlarni soxtalashtiradi, keyin noto'g'ri ma'lumot olganini da'vo qiladi. Men unga azaldan, bugun ham, har doim ham Klamm tomonidan qabul qilinishiga zarracha ham imkoniyati yo'qligini aytib kelganman; xo'sh, agar imkoniyat yo'q bo'lsa, u uni bu bayonnoma orqali ham olmaydi. Bundan aniqroq narsa bo'lishi mumkinmi?

paras.en: I say further that this record is the only real official connection he can have with Klamm; that too is surely clear enough and beyond doubt. But if he doesn't believe me, and keeps hoping — I don't know why or what for — that he can get through to Klamm, then, if one follows his line of thought, the only thing that can help him is the only real official connection he has with Klamm — that is, this record. That's all I said, and whoever claims anything else is maliciously twisting my words.' — 'If that's how it is, Frau Landlady,' said K., 'then I beg your pardon, then I misunderstood you; for I thought — wrongly, as it now turns out — that I heard in your earlier words that there was, after all, some very smallest hope for me.' — 'Certainly,' said the landlady, 'that is indeed my opinion. You're twisting my words again, only this time in the opposite direction. Such a hope exists for you, in my opinion, and it rests, admittedly, only on this record. But it isn't the case that you can simply pounce on the secretary with the question: "Will I be allowed to see Klamm if I answer the questions?" When a child asks like that, people laugh; when a grown man does it, it's an insult to the authorities; the secretary only graciously covered it up through the delicacy of his answer.
paras.uz: Yana aytamanki, bu bayonnoma uning Klamm bilan bo'lishi mumkin bo'lgan yagona haqiqiy rasmiy aloqasi; bu ham yetarlicha aniq va shubhasiz-ku. Lekin agar u menga ishonmasa, doim — nega va nima uchun, bilmayman — Klammga yetib borishga umid qilsa, unda, uning fikr yo'nalishida qolinsa, unga faqat Klamm bilan bo'lgan yagona haqiqiy rasmiy aloqasi — ya'ni shu bayonnoma — yordam berishi mumkin. Men faqat shuni aytdim, kim boshqa narsani da'vo qilsa, so'zlarni yomon niyat bilan buzib talqin qiladi.» — «Agar shunday bo'lsa, bekam, — dedi K., — unda sizdan uzr so'rayman, unda sizni noto'g'ri tushunibman; chunki men — endi ma'lum bo'lishicha, adashib — oldingi so'zlaringizdan men uchun baribir qandaydir eng kichik umid bor, deb eshitgandek bo'ldim.» — «Albatta, — dedi beka, — bu, to'g'ri, mening fikrim, siz yana so'zlarimni buzyapsiz, faqat bu safar teskari yo'nalishda. Mening fikrimcha, siz uchun shunday umid bor va u, to'g'ri, faqat shu bayonnomaga asoslanadi. Lekin bu shunday emaski, siz janob kotibga shunchaki: «Savollarga javob bersam, Klammning huzuriga kirishga ruxsat berilarmikan?» degan savol bilan tashlana olsangiz. Bola shunday so'rasa, ustidan kulishadi, katta odam qilsa, bu idoraga haqorat; janob kotib buni faqat javobining nozikligi bilan muruvvat ko'rsatib yashirdi.

paras.en: But the hope I mean consists precisely in this: that through the record you have a kind of connection, perhaps a kind of connection, with Klamm. Isn't that hope enough? If you were asked about the merits that make you worthy of the gift of such a hope, could you put forward the least thing? Of course nothing more precise can be said about this hope, and the secretary in particular, in his official capacity, will never be able to make even the slightest hint about it. For him it's only a matter, as he says, of a description of this afternoon, for the sake of order; he won't say more, even if you ask him right now with reference to my words.' — 'Will Klamm read this record, then, secretary?' asked K. — 'No,' said Momus, 'why should he? Klamm can't read all the records; in fact he reads none at all. "Keep away from me with your records!" he usually says.' — 'Land surveyor,' complained the landlady, 'you exhaust me with such questions. Is it necessary, or even desirable, that Klamm should read this record and learn word for word of the trivialities of your life? Wouldn't you rather beg most humbly that the record be hidden from Klamm — a request, by the way, that would be just as unreasonable as the earlier one, for who can hide anything from Klamm? — but which would at least show a more likeable character. And is it even necessary for what you call your hope?
paras.uz: Men nazarda tutgan umid esa aynan shundaki, siz bayonnoma orqali qandaydir aloqaga, balki Klamm bilan qandaydir aloqaga egasiz. Bu yetarlicha umid emasmi? Agar sizdan bunday umid in'omiga loyiq qiladigan xizmatlaringiz haqida so'rashsa, eng kichik narsani bo'lsa ham ko'rsata olasizmi? Albatta, bu umid haqida aniqroq hech narsa aytib bo'lmaydi va ayniqsa janob kotib o'z rasmiy maqomida bu haqda hech qachon zarracha ishora ham qila olmaydi. U uchun, o'zi aytganidek, gap faqat bugungi tushdan keyingi vaqtning tavsifi haqida, tartib uchun; hozir mening so'zlarimga tayanib undan so'rasangiz ham, u bundan ortiq hech narsa demaydi.» — «Janob kotib, — so'radi K., — Klamm bu bayonnomani o'qiydimi?» — «Yo'q, — dedi Momus, — nega o'qisin? Klamm hamma bayonnomalarni o'qiy olmaydi-ku, u hatto umuman birortasini ham o'qimaydi. «Bayonnomalaringiz bilan mendan uzoqroq yuring!» — deydi u odatda.» — «Janob yer o'lchovchi, — nolidi beka, — siz meni bunday savollar bilan holdan toydiryapsiz. Klamm bu bayonnomani o'qishi va hayotingizdagi arzimas narsalardan so'zma-so'z xabardor bo'lishi zarurmi yoki hatto istalganmi? Bayonnomani Klammdan yashirishlarini eng kamtarlik bilan iltimos qilganingiz ma'qul emasmi — aytgancha, bu iltimos ham oldingisi kabi aqlsiz bo'lardi — axir kim Klammdan biror narsani yashira oladi? — lekin hech bo'lmaganda yoqimliroq xarakterni ko'rsatardi. Bu siz umidingiz deb atagan narsa uchun zarurmi o'zi?

paras.en: Didn't you yourself declare that you'd be satisfied if only you had the opportunity to speak in front of Klamm, even if he didn't look at you and didn't listen to you? And don't you achieve at least that through this record — perhaps much more?' 'Much more?' asked K. 'In what way?' — 'If only you didn't always,' cried the landlady, 'like a child, want everything served up at once in edible form! Who can give an answer to such questions? The record goes into Klamm's village registry — you heard that; nothing more can be said about it with certainty. But do you then already know the whole significance of the record, of the secretary, of the village registry? Do you know what it means when the secretary questions you? Perhaps — or probably — he doesn't know himself. He sits here calmly and does his duty, for the sake of order, as he said. But consider that Klamm appointed him, that he works in Klamm's name, that what he does, even if it never reaches Klamm, has Klamm's approval from the start. And how can something have Klamm's approval that is not filled with his spirit?
paras.uz: Klamm sizga qaramasa va sizni tinglamasa ham, faqat uning oldida gapirish imkoniyati bo'lsa, mamnun bo'lishingizni o'zingiz aytmaganmidingiz? Bu bayonnoma orqali hech bo'lmaganda shunga, balki undan ham ko'proqqa erishmaysizmi?» «Ancha ko'proqqa? — so'radi K. — Qanday qilib?» — «Qaniydi siz doim, — qichqirdi beka, — bola kabi hamma narsani darhol yeyiladigan shaklda taqdim etilishini istamasangiz! Bunday savollarga kim javob bera oladi? Bayonnoma Klammning qishloq qayd idorasiga boradi, buni eshitdingiz, bu haqda aniq qilib bundan ortiq hech narsa aytib bo'lmaydi. Lekin siz bayonnomaning, janob kotibning, qishloq qayd idorasining butun ahamiyatini allaqachon bilasizmi? Janob kotib sizni so'roq qilsa, bu nimani anglatishini bilasizmi? Balki yoki ehtimol, buni uning o'zi ham bilmas. U bu yerda xotirjam o'tirib, o'z burchini bajaradi, o'zi aytganidek, tartib uchun. Lekin o'ylab ko'ring: uni Klamm tayinlagan, u Klamm nomidan ishlaydi, uning qilayotgan ishi hech qachon Klammgacha yetib bormasa ham, boshidanoq Klammning roziligiga ega. Uning ruhi bilan to'lmagan narsa qanday qilib Klammning roziligiga ega bo'lishi mumkin?

paras.en: Far be it from me to flatter the secretary crudely by this — he himself would firmly forbid it — but I'm not speaking of his independent personality, but of what he is when he has Klamm's approval, as he has right now: then he is a tool on which Klamm's hand rests, and woe to anyone who does not submit to it.'
paras.uz: Bu bilan janob kotibga qo'pol xushomad qilish mendan yiroq bo'lsin, uning o'zi ham buni qat'iyan man qilardi, lekin men uning mustaqil shaxsiyati haqida emas, balki u Klammning roziligiga ega bo'lganda — xuddi hozirgidek — nima ekanligi haqida gapiryapman: unda u Klammning qo'li yotgan quroldir va unga bo'ysunmaganning holiga voy.»

paras.en: K. did not fear the landlady's threats, and he was tired of the hopes with which she tried to catch him. Klamm was far away. Once the landlady had compared Klamm to an eagle, and that had seemed ridiculous to K.; but not any more. He thought of his remoteness, of his impregnable dwelling, of his silence, broken perhaps only by cries such as K. had never yet heard, of his downward-piercing gaze, which could never be proved, never refuted, of the circles he drew up above according to incomprehensible laws, indestructible from K.'s depth below, visible only for moments — all this Klamm and the eagle had in common. But certainly this record had nothing to do with any of it — this record over which Momus was just now breaking apart a salt pretzel, which he was enjoying with his beer and with which he was strewing all the papers with salt and caraway.
paras.uz: K. bekaning tahdidlaridan qo'rqmasdi, u o'zini tutib olishga uringan umidlardan esa charchagan edi. Klamm uzoqda edi. Bir paytlar beka Klammni burgutga qiyoslagan edi va bu K.ga kulgili tuyulgandi, endi esa yo'q; u uning uzoqligini, egallab bo'lmas qarorgohini, balki faqat K. hali hech qachon eshitmagan qichqiriqlar bilangina buziladigan sukutini, hech qachon isbotlab ham, rad etib ham bo'lmaydigan pastga sanchiladigan nigohini, tepada tushunarsiz qonunlarga ko'ra chizadigan, K.ning pastdagi chuqurligidan buzib bo'lmaydigan, faqat lahzalargagina ko'rinadigan doiralarini o'yladi — bularning hammasi Klamm va burgutga umumiy edi. Lekin, albatta, bularning hech biriga bu bayonnomaning aloqasi yo'q edi — uning ustida Momus hozirgina sho'r kulchani sindirib, uni pivoga gazak qilib yeyar va u bilan barcha qog'ozlarga tuz va zira sepib yuborardi.

paras.en: 'Good night,' said K., 'I have an aversion to every interrogation,' and now he really did go to the door. 'So he's going after all,' said Momus almost anxiously to the landlady. 'He won't dare,' she said; K. heard no more, he was already in the hall. It was cold and a strong wind was blowing. From a door opposite came the landlord; he seemed to have been keeping the hall under watch from behind a peephole there. He had to wrap the skirts of his coat round his body, the wind tore at them so even here in the hall. 'You're going already, land surveyor?' he said. 'Does that surprise you?' asked K. 'Yes,' said the landlord. 'Aren't you being questioned, then?' — 'No,' said K. 'I didn't let myself be questioned.' — 'Why not?' asked the landlord. 'I don't know,' said K., 'why I should let myself be questioned, why I should give in to a joke or an official whim. Perhaps another time I'd have done it, also as a joke or a whim, but not today.' — 'Well, yes, certainly,' said the landlord, but it was only polite agreement, not convinced. 'I must let the servants into the bar now,' he said then; 'it's long been their hour. I just didn't want to disturb the interrogation.' — 'You thought it so important?' asked K. 'Oh yes,' said the landlord. 'So I shouldn't have refused it,' said K.
paras.uz: «Xayrli tun, — dedi K., — menda har qanday so'roqqa nisbatan jirkanish bor», va endi u rostdan ham eshik tomon yurdi. «Demak, baribir ketyapti», dedi Momus bekaga deyarli xavotir bilan. «Jur'at etmaydi», dedi beka; K. boshqa hech narsa eshitmadi, u allaqachon dahlizda edi. Sovuq edi va kuchli shamol esardi. Ro'paradagi eshikdan mehmonxona egasi chiqdi, u, aftidan, o'sha yerda tuynukcha orqasidan dahlizni kuzatib turgan edi. U kamzulining etaklarini tanasiga o'rab olishga majbur bo'ldi — shamol ularni hatto bu yerda, dahlizda ham shunchalik yulqirdi. «Ketyapsizmi, janob yer o'lchovchi?» — dedi u. «Bunga hayronmisiz?» — so'radi K. «Ha, — dedi egasi. — Sizni so'roq qilishmayaptimi?» — «Yo'q, — dedi K. — Men o'zimni so'roq qildirmadim.» — «Nega?» — so'radi egasi. «Bilmayman, — dedi K., — nega o'zimni so'roq qildirishim kerak, nega hazilga yoki idoraning injiqligiga bo'ysunishim kerak. Balki boshqa safar men ham buni hazil yoki injiqlik tufayli qilgan bo'lardim, lekin bugun emas.» — «Xo'sh, ha, albatta», dedi egasi, lekin bu ishonch bilan emas, faqat xushmuomalalik bilan bildirilgan rozilik edi. «Endi xizmatkorlarni bufetga kiritishim kerak, — dedi keyin u, — ularning soati allaqachon kelgan. Men faqat so'roqqa xalaqit bermoqchi emas edim.» — «Uni shunchalik muhim deb hisoblaganmidingiz?» — so'radi K. «Ha, albatta», dedi egasi. «Demak, uni rad etmasligim kerak edi», dedi K.

paras.en: 'No,' said the landlord, 'you shouldn't have done that.' As K. said nothing, he added, whether to comfort K. or to get away faster: 'Well, well, it doesn't mean brimstone has to rain from heaven straight away.' — 'No,' said K., 'the weather doesn't look like that.' And they parted laughing. K. stepped out onto the wildly wind-swept front steps and looked into the darkness. Wicked, wicked weather. Somehow in connection with this it occurred to him how the landlady had tried to make him submit to the record, and how he had held out. Of course it hadn't been an open effort; secretly she had at the same time been dragging him away from the record; in the end one didn't know whether one had held out or given in. An intriguing nature, working apparently senselessly like the wind, on distant, alien commissions one never got any insight into.
paras.uz: «Yo'q, — dedi egasi, — buni qilmasligingiz kerak edi.» K. jim bo'lgani uchun u — yo K.ni yupatish uchun, yo tezroq ketish uchun — qo'shib qo'ydi: «Xo'sh, xo'sh, lekin shuning uchun darhol osmondan oltingugurt yog'ishi shart emas.» — «Yo'q, — dedi K., — ob-havo bunga o'xshamaydi.» Va ular kulib ajralishdi. K. shamol vahshiyona esayotgan ayvon zinasiga chiqdi va zulmatga qaradi. Yomon, yomon ob-havo. Qandaydir tarzda shu bilan bog'liq holda uning xayoliga beka uni bayonnomaga bo'ysundirishga qanday urinib, u esa qanday qarshilik ko'rsatgani keldi. Albatta, bu ochiq urinish emas edi, yashirincha u bir vaqtning o'zida uni bayonnomadan uzoqqa sudrab ketgan edi; oxir-oqibat qarshilik ko'rsatdingmi yoki yon berdingmi — bilib bo'lmasdi. Hiyla-nayrangga moyil tabiat, shamol kabi go'yo ma'nosiz ishlaydi, uzoq, begona topshiriqlarga ko'ra — ularning mohiyatiga hech qachon ko'z yetkazib bo'lmaydi.

paras.en: He had hardly taken a few steps on the high road when he saw two swaying lights in the distance; this sign of life pleased him, and he hurried towards them, and they for their part floated towards him. He did not know why he was so disappointed when he recognised the assistants. They were coming to meet him, probably sent by Frieda, and the lanterns that freed him from the darkness, in which everything round about was roaring against him, were probably his own property; nevertheless he was disappointed. He had expected strangers, not these old acquaintances who were a burden to him. But it was not only the assistants: out of the darkness between them stepped Barnabas. 'Barnabas!' cried K., holding out his hand to him. 'Are you coming to me?' The surprise of seeing him again at first made him forget all the annoyance Barnabas had once caused him. 'To you,' said Barnabas, as unchangingly friendly as before. 'With a letter from Klamm!' 'A letter from Klamm!' said K., throwing his head back, and took it hastily from Barnabas's hand. 'Light!' he said to the assistants, who pressed close against him on the right and left and raised the lanterns. To read it, K. had to fold the large sheet very small to protect it from the wind. Then he read: 'To the land surveyor at the Bridge Inn. The surveying work you have carried out so far has my approval. The work of the assistants too is praiseworthy; you know how to keep them at their work well.
paras.uz: U katta yo'lda bir necha qadam tashlashi bilan uzoqda ikkita tebranib turgan chiroqni ko'rdi; hayotning bu belgisi uni quvontirdi va u ular tomon shoshildi, ular ham o'z navbatida unga qarab suzib kelardi. Yordamchilarni tanigach, nega bunchalik ko'ngli qolganini u bilmadi. Ular, ehtimol, Frida yuborgani uchun uni kutib olishga kelishardi, atrofda unga qarshi shovqin solayotgan zulmatdan uni xalos qilgan fonuslar esa, ehtimol, o'zining mulki edi; shunga qaramay, u hafsalasi pir bo'ldi, u begonalarni kutgan edi, unga yuk bo'lgan bu eski tanishlarni emas. Lekin bular faqat yordamchilar emas edi, ularning o'rtasidagi qorong'ilikdan Barnabas chiqib keldi. «Barnabas! — qichqirdi K. va unga qo'lini cho'zdi. — Menga kelyapsanmi?» Qayta ko'rishish hayratidan u avvaliga Barnabas bir paytlar unga keltirgan barcha g'ashlikni unutdi. «Senga, — dedi Barnabas avvalgidek o'zgarmas do'stona. — Klammdan xat bilan!» «Klammdan xat!» — dedi K. boshini orqaga tashlab va uni Barnabasning qo'lidan shoshib oldi. «Yoritinglar!» — dedi u o'ng va chapdan unga zich yopishib, fonuslarni ko'targan yordamchilarga. K. o'qish uchun katta xat varag'ini shamoldan himoya qilish maqsadida juda kichik qilib buklashga majbur bo'ldi. Keyin u o'qidi: ««Ko'prik yonidagi» mehmonxonadagi janob yer o'lchovchiga. Siz hozirgacha bajargan yer o'lchash ishlari mening tahsinimga sazovor. Yordamchilarning ishlari ham maqtovga loyiq, siz ularni ishga yaxshi undashni bilasiz.

paras.en: Do not slacken in your zeal! Bring the work to a good end. An interruption would embitter me. For the rest, be reassured: the question of payment will be decided shortly. I am keeping you in view.' K. looked up from the letter only when the assistants, who read much more slowly than he did, cried 'Hurrah!' loudly three times in celebration of the good news and swung the lanterns. 'Be quiet,' he said, and to Barnabas: 'It's a misunderstanding.' Barnabas did not understand him. 'It's a misunderstanding,' K. repeated, and the tiredness of the afternoon came back; the way to the schoolhouse still seemed so far to him, and behind Barnabas his whole family rose up, and the assistants were still pressing against him, so that he pushed them away with his elbow. How could Frieda have sent them out to meet him, when he had ordered that they were to stay with her? He would have found his way home alone, and more easily alone than in this company. On top of that, one of them had wound a scarf round his neck whose loose ends fluttered in the wind and had several times struck K. in the face; the other assistant, admittedly, had always immediately removed the scarf from K.'s face with a long, pointed, constantly playing finger, but that hadn't made things any better. Both even seemed to have taken pleasure in the to and fro, just as the wind and the restlessness of the night excited them generally. 'Away!' shouted K.
paras.uz: G'ayratingizni susaytirmang! Ishlarni yaxshi yakunga yetkazing. Uzilish meni g'azablantirgan bo'lardi. Qolgan masalada xotirjam bo'ling, haq to'lash masalasi yaqin orada hal qilinadi. Sizni ko'zdan qochirmayman.» K. xatdan faqat undan ancha sekin o'qiydigan yordamchilar yaxshi xabarlar sharafiga uch marta baland ovozda «Ura!» deb qichqirib, fonuslarni silkitganlaridagina boshini ko'tardi. «Jim bo'linglar», dedi u va Barnabasga: «Bu tushunmovchilik.» Barnabas uni tushunmadi. «Bu tushunmovchilik», takrorladi K. va tushdan keyingi charchoq yana qaytdi; maktab binosigacha bo'lgan yo'l unga hali juda uzoq tuyuldi, Barnabasning orqasida esa uning butun oilasi qad ko'tardi, yordamchilar esa hamon unga yopishib turishardi, shuning uchun u ularni tirsagi bilan itarib yubordi; Frida ularni qanday qilib uni kutib olishga yubora oldi, axir u ular uning yonida qolishsin, deb buyurgan edi-ku. Uyga yo'lni u yolg'iz ham topgan bo'lardi, bu hamrohlik bilan emas, yolg'iz osonroq. Buning ustiga, ulardan biri bo'yniga ro'mol o'rab olgan edi, uning bo'sh uchlari shamolda hilpirab, bir necha marta K.ning yuziga urilgan edi; ikkinchi yordamchi, to'g'ri, ro'molni K.ning yuzidan doim darhol uzun, o'tkir, to'xtovsiz o'ynayotgan barmog'i bilan olib qo'yardi, lekin bu bilan ishni yaxshilamagan edi. Ikkalasi ham, aftidan, bu u yoq-bu yoqdan zavq olishardi, umuman shamol va tunning notinchligi ularni hayajonga solgan edi. «Yo'qolinglar!» — baqirdi K.

paras.en: 'If you've come to meet me, why didn't you bring my stick? What am I to drive you home with?' They ducked behind Barnabas, but they weren't so frightened that they didn't set their lanterns right and left on their protector's shoulders; he shook them off at once, of course. 'Barnabas,' said K., and it weighed heavily on his heart that Barnabas plainly didn't understand him; that in quiet times his jacket shone beautifully, but when things became serious there was no help to be found, only mute resistance — resistance one couldn't fight against, for he himself was defenceless, only his smile shone, but it helped just as little as the stars up there against the storm wind down here. 'Look what the gentleman writes to me,' said K., holding the letter in front of his face. 'The gentleman is wrongly informed. I'm not doing any surveying work, and what the assistants are worth you can see for yourself. And of course I can't interrupt the work I'm not doing either; I can't even arouse the gentleman's bitterness — how could I earn his approval! And I can never be reassured.' 'I'll pass it on,' said Barnabas, who all the while had been reading past the letter — which, admittedly, he couldn't have read at all, for he had it right in front of his face. 'Oh,' said K., 'you promise me you'll pass it on, but can I really believe you?
paras.uz: «Agar meni kutib olishga kelgan bo'lsangiz, nega tayog'imni olib kelmadingiz? Sizlarni uyga nima bilan haydayman?» Ular Barnabasning orqasiga bukilishdi, lekin shunchalik qo'rqib ketmagandilarki, fonuslarini o'z himoyachilarining o'ng va chap yelkalariga qo'ymaslik darajada; u, albatta, ularni darhol silkitib tashladi. «Barnabas», dedi K. va Barnabas uni ochiqdan-ochiq tushunmayotgani, osoyishta paytlarda uning kamzuli chiroyli yaltirashi, lekin ish jiddiylashganda hech qanday yordam emas, faqat jim qarshilik topilishi uning yuragiga og'ir botdi — qarshilikki, unga qarshi kurashib bo'lmasdi, chunki uning o'zi himoyasiz edi, faqat jilmayishi porlardi, lekin u tepadagi yulduzlar pastdagi bo'ronli shamolga qarshi qanchalik yordam bersa, shunchalik yordam berardi. «Qara, janob menga nima yozyapti», dedi K. va xatni uning yuziga tutdi. «Janobga noto'g'ri ma'lumot berilgan. Men axir hech qanday o'lchash ishini qilmayapman, yordamchilar nimaga arzishini esa o'zing ko'rib turibsan. Qilmayotgan ishimni, albatta, uzib ham qo'ya olmayman, hatto janobning g'azabini ham qo'zg'ata olmayman — uning tahsiniga qanday loyiq bo'laman! Xotirjam esa hech qachon bo'la olmayman.» «Men buni yetkazaman», dedi butun vaqt davomida xatning yonidan o'qib turgan Barnabas — u, to'g'ri, uni umuman o'qiy olmasdi ham, chunki xat yuzining oldida, juda yaqin edi. «Eh, — dedi K., — sen menga buni yetkazishga va'da beryapsan, lekin senga rostdan ham ishonsam bo'ladimi?

paras.en: I need a trustworthy messenger so badly, now more than ever.' K. bit his lips with impatience. 'Sir,' said Barnabas, with a soft inclination of his neck — K. almost let himself be seduced by it again into believing Barnabas — 'I'll certainly pass it on; and what you entrusted to me last time I'll certainly pass on too.' 'What!' cried K. 'Haven't you passed that on yet? Weren't you at the Castle the next day?' 'No,' said Barnabas. 'My good father is old, you saw that yourself, and there happened to be a lot of work, I had to help him; but now I'll soon go to the Castle again.' 'But what are you doing, you incomprehensible man!' cried K., striking his forehead. 'Don't Klamm's affairs come before everything else? You have the high office of a messenger, and you administer it so shamefully? Who cares about your father's work? Klamm is waiting for the news, and you, instead of tumbling head over heels in your hurry, prefer to cart the dung out of the stable.' 'My father is a shoemaker,' said Barnabas, unperturbed; 'he had orders from Brunswick, and after all I'm my father's journeyman.' 'Shoemaker — orders — Brunswick,' cried K. grimly, as though he were making each of the words useless for ever. 'And who needs boots here anyway, on these eternally empty roads?
paras.uz: Menga ishonchli chopar shunchalik kerak, hozir har qachongidan ham ko'proq.» K. sabrsizlikdan lablarini tishladi. «Janob, — dedi Barnabas bo'ynini muloyim egib — K. yana deyarli bunga aldanib, Barnabasga ishonib yuboray dedi, — men buni albatta yetkazaman; sen menga oxirgi marta topshirgan narsani ham albatta yetkazaman.» «Qanday! — qichqirdi K. — Sen uni hali yetkazmadingmi? Ertasi kuni Qasrda bo'lmadingmi?» «Yo'q, — dedi Barnabas. — Mehribon otam qari, o'zing ko'rding, ayni paytda ish ko'p edi, unga yordam berishim kerak edi, lekin endi tez orada yana Qasrga boraman.» «Lekin sen nima qilyapsan, tushunib bo'lmas odam! — qichqirdi K. va peshonasiga urdi. — Klammning ishlari hamma narsadan ustun emasmi? Senda chopar degan yuksak lavozim bor, sen esa uni shunchalik sharmandalarcha boshqaryapsanmi? Otangning ishi kimga kerak? Klamm xabarlarni kutyapti, sen esa yugurib, boshing bilan yiqilib-turib shoshilish o'rniga otxonadan go'ng tashishni afzal ko'rasan.» «Otam etikdo'z, — dedi Barnabas ikkilanmay, — unga Brunsvikdan buyurtmalar bor edi, men esa axir otamning shogirdiman.» «Etikdo'z — buyurtmalar — Brunsvik», qichqirdi K. alam bilan, go'yo har bir so'zni abadiy yaroqsiz qilayotgandek. «Bu yerda, abadiy bo'm-bo'sh yo'llarda kimga etik kerak o'zi?

paras.en: And what do I care about all this shoemaking? I entrusted a message to you not so that you'd forget it and muddle it on the cobbler's bench, but so that you'd carry it at once to the gentleman.' K. calmed down a little here when it occurred to him that Klamm had probably not been at the Castle all this time anyway, but at the Herrenhof; but Barnabas irritated him again when he began to recite K.'s first message, to prove he had kept it well. 'Enough, I don't want to know,' said K. 'Don't be angry with me, sir,' said Barnabas, and, as though he unconsciously wanted to punish K., he withdrew his gaze from him and lowered his eyes; but it was probably dismay at K.'s shouting. 'I'm not angry with you,' said K., and his restlessness now turned against himself. 'Not with you; but it's very bad for me to have only such a messenger for the most important things.'
paras.uz: Bu butun etikdo'zlik menga nima? Men senga xabarni etikdo'z kursisida unutib, chalkashtirib yuborishing uchun emas, balki uni darhol janobga olib borishing uchun ishonib topshirganman.» K. bu yerda Klamm, ehtimol, butun vaqt davomida Qasrda emas, balki Herrenhofda bo'lganini eslab, biroz tinchlandi, lekin Barnabas uni yaxshi eslab qolganini isbotlash uchun K.ning birinchi xabarini yoddan aytib bera boshlaganida, uni yana g'ashlantirdi. «Yetar, bilishni istamayman», dedi K. «Mendan xafa bo'lma, janob», dedi Barnabas va go'yo beixtiyor K.ni jazolamoqchidek, undan nigohini olib, ko'zlarini pastga tushirdi, lekin bu, ehtimol, K.ning qichqirig'idan kelgan sarosima edi. «Men sendan xafa emasman», dedi K. va uning bezovtaligi endi o'ziga qarshi burildi. «Sendan emas, lekin eng muhim ishlar uchun faqat shunday chopar borligi men uchun juda yomon.»
