chapters.title: 11. Frieda and Hans
chapters.recap_uz: K. yordamchilarni haydaydi; ular panjara ortidan iltijo qilishadi. Frida charchagan, so'lib borayotgandek. U K. bilan boshqa yurtga ketishni taklif qiladi, ammo K. bu yerda qolishini aytadi. Frida yordamchilarni Klammning elchilari bo'lishi mumkin, deb o'ylaydi. Shunda kichkina Hans Brunsvik kirib keladi va K.ga yordam bermoqchi bo'ladi. K. undan oilasi haqida so'raydi: onasi kasalmand va hech kim bilan uchrashmaydi. K. Hans orqali uning onasi bilan gaplashish yo'lini izlaydi.

paras.en: Hardly had everyone gone when K. said to the assistants: 'Go out!' Taken aback by this unexpected order, they obeyed; but when K. locked the door behind them, they wanted to come back, whimpered outside and knocked on the door. 'You're dismissed!' cried K. 'I'll never take you into my service again.' This, of course, they wouldn't put up with, and they hammered on the door with their hands and feet. 'Back to you, master!' they cried, as though K. were dry land and they were about to sink in the flood. But K. had no pity; he waited impatiently until the unbearable noise should force the teacher to intervene. It soon happened. 'Let your cursed assistants in!' he shouted. 'I've dismissed them!' K. shouted back. This had the unintended side effect of showing the teacher how it looked when someone was strong enough not only to give notice but also to carry it out. The teacher now tried to calm the assistants kindly: they should only wait here quietly; in the end K. would have to let them in again. Then he left. And it might now have stayed quiet if K. had not started calling to them again that they were now finally dismissed and had not the slightest hope of being taken back. At that they started making a noise again as before. Again the teacher came, but now he no longer negotiated with them; he drove them out of the house, evidently with the dreaded cane.
paras.uz: Hamma ketishi bilan K. yordamchilarga dedi: «Chiqinglar!» Bu kutilmagan buyruqdan dovdirab qolgan yordamchilar bo'ysunishdi, lekin K. ularning orqasidan eshikni qulflaganida, qaytib kirmoqchi bo'lishdi, tashqarida ingrab, eshikni taqillatishdi. «Sizlar bo'shatildingiz! — qichqirdi K. — Sizlarni hech qachon xizmatimga olmayman.» Bunga ular, albatta, chidashni istamadilar va eshikka qo'llari va oyoqlari bilan urishdi. «Senga qaytamiz, janob!» — qichqirishdi ular, go'yo K. quruqlik, ular esa toshqinda cho'kib ketay deb turgandek. Lekin K.ning rahmi kelmadi, u chidab bo'lmas shovqin o'qituvchini aralashishga majbur qilishini sabrsizlik bilan kutdi. Bu tez orada sodir bo'ldi. «La'nati yordamchilaringizni kiriting!» — baqirdi u. «Men ularni bo'shatdim!» — javoban baqirdi K.; bu o'qituvchiga kimdir nafaqat bo'shatishga, balki bo'shatishni amalga oshirishga ham yetarlicha kuchli bo'lsa, bu qanchalik ko'zga tashlanishini ko'rsatish kabi kutilmagan natija berdi. Endi o'qituvchi yordamchilarni muloyimlik bilan tinchlantirishga urindi: ular shu yerda faqat jim kutib turishsin, oxir-oqibat K. ularni baribir yana kiritishga majbur bo'ladi. Keyin u ketdi. Va agar K. ularga endi butunlay bo'shatilganliklarini va qayta olinishga zarracha ham umidlari yo'qligini yana qichqira boshlamaganida, balki jimlik saqlanib qolardi. Shundan keyin ular yana avvalgidek shovqin ko'tarishdi. O'qituvchi yana keldi, lekin endi ular bilan muzokara qilmadi, balki, aftidan, o'sha qo'rqinchli tayoq bilan ularni uydan haydab chiqardi.

paras.en: Soon they appeared in front of the windows of the gymnasium, knocked on the panes and shouted; but the words could no longer be understood. They didn't stay there long either, though; in the deep snow they couldn't jump about as their restlessness demanded. So they hurried to the railings of the school garden and jumped up onto the stone base, from where they also had a better view into the room, if only from a distance. They ran up and down there, holding on to the railings, then stood still again and stretched out their clasped hands imploringly towards K. They kept this up for a long time, regardless of the uselessness of their efforts; they were as if blinded, and they probably didn't stop even when K. let down the window curtains to free himself from the sight of them.
paras.uz: Tez orada ular gimnastika xonasining derazalari oldida paydo bo'lib, oynalarni taqillatib qichqirishdi; lekin so'zlarni endi tushunib bo'lmasdi. Biroq ular u yerda ham uzoq qolishmadi — chuqur qorda notinchliklari talab qilganidek sakrab yura olmasdilar. Shuning uchun ular maktab bog'ining panjarasiga shoshilishdi, tosh poydevorga sakrab chiqishdi — u yerdan ular, to'g'ri, faqat uzoqdan bo'lsa ham, xonani yaxshiroq ko'rishardi; ular panjaraga yopishib, u yoqdan-bu yoqqa yugurishar, keyin yana to'xtab, kaftlarini juftlab, K.ga yolvorib cho'zishardi. Ular buni urinishlarining befoydaligiga qaramay uzoq davom ettirishdi; ular go'yo ko'r bo'lib qolgandek edilar, ehtimol, K. ularni ko'rishdan qutulish uchun deraza pardalarini tushirganida ham to'xtamagandirlar.

paras.en: In the now dim room K. went to the parallel bars to see to Frieda. Under his gaze she got up, tidied her hair, dried her face and set about making coffee in silence. Although she knew everything, K. nevertheless informed her formally that he had dismissed the assistants. She only nodded. K. sat on a school bench and watched her tired movements. It had always been her freshness and resolve that had made her insignificant body beautiful; now this beauty was gone. A few days of living with K. had been enough to bring this about. The work in the bar had not been easy, but it had probably suited her better. Or was her separation from Klamm the real cause of her decline? Klamm's nearness had made her so absurdly alluring; in this allure she had seized K. for herself, and now she was withering in his arms.
paras.uz: Endi g'ira-shira bo'lib qolgan xonada K. Fridaning holidan xabar olish uchun brus yoniga bordi. Uning nigohi ostida Frida o'rnidan turdi, sochini tuzatdi, yuzini artdi va indamay qahva qaynatishga kirishdi. U hamma narsani bilsa ham, K. unga yordamchilarni bo'shatganini rasman ma'lum qildi. U faqat bosh irg'adi. K. maktab partasida o'tirib, uning charchagan harakatlarini kuzatdi. Uning arzimas tanasini doim tetiklik va qat'iyat go'zal qilib kelgan edi; endi bu go'zallik yo'qolgan edi. K. bilan birga yashashning bir necha kuni bunga erishish uchun yetarli bo'lgan edi. Bufetdagi ish oson emas edi, lekin, ehtimol, unga baribir ko'proq mos edi. Yoki Klammdan uzoqlashish uning so'lishining asl sababimidi? Klammning yaqinligi uni shunchalik bema'ni darajada jozibali qilgan edi, bu jozibada u K.ni o'ziga tortib olgan edi, endi esa uning quchog'ida so'lib borardi.

paras.en: 'Frieda,' said K. She put the coffee grinder aside at once and came to K. on the bench. 'Are you angry with me?' she asked. 'No,' said K. 'I think you can't do otherwise. You lived contentedly at the Herrenhof. I should have left you there.' 'Yes,' said Frieda, looking sadly in front of her, 'you should have left me there. I'm not worthy of living with you. Freed of me, you could perhaps achieve everything you want. Out of consideration for me you submit to the tyrannical teacher, take on this miserable post, strive laboriously for an interview with Klamm. All for me, and I repay you badly.' 'No,' said K., putting his arm round her comfortingly. 'All those are trifles that don't hurt me, and I don't want to go to Klamm only for your sake. And think of all you've done for me! Before I knew you, I was wandering completely astray here. Nobody took me in, and whoever I forced myself on quickly sent me away. And if there was anyone with whom I might have found rest, they were people from whom I in turn fled — Barnabas's family, for instance.' 'You fled from them? Didn't you? Dearest!' Frieda broke in eagerly, and then, after a hesitant 'Yes' from K., sank back into her tiredness.
paras.uz: «Frida», dedi K. U darhol qahva tegirmonchasini chetga qo'yib, partaga, K.ning yoniga keldi. «Mendan xafamisan?» — so'radi u. «Yo'q, — dedi K. — Menimcha, sen boshqacha qila olmaysan. Sen Herrenhofda mamnun yashading. Seni o'sha yerda qoldirishim kerak edi.» «Ha, — dedi Frida va g'amgin oldiga qaradi, — meni o'sha yerda qoldirishing kerak edi. Men sen bilan yashashga loyiq emasman. Mendan qutulsang, balki xohlagan hamma narsangga erisharding. Men uchun sen zolim o'qituvchiga bo'ysunasan, bu achinarli lavozimni olasan, Klamm bilan suhbat uchun mashaqqat bilan harakat qilasan. Hammasi men uchun, men esa senga yomon qaytaraman.» «Yo'q, — dedi K. va uni yupatib quchoqladi. — Bularning hammasi menga og'riq bermaydigan mayda narsalar, Klammning oldiga esa faqat sen uchun bormoqchi emasman. Sen men uchun nimalar qilmading! Seni tanishimdan oldin men bu yerda butunlay adashib yurardim. Hech kim meni qabul qilmasdi, kimga yopishsam, meni tezda jo'natib yuborardi. Agar birortasining yonida tinchlik topa olganimda ham, ular yana men o'zim qochgan odamlar edi — masalan, Barnabasning oilasi.» «Ulardan qochding-a? Shundaymi? Jonim!» — gapga qizg'in aralashdi Frida va K.ning ikkilanib aytgan «Ha»sidan keyin yana charchog'iga cho'kdi.

paras.en: But K. too no longer had the resolve to explain in what way everything had turned out for the good for him through his union with Frieda. He slowly withdrew his arm from her and sat in silence for a little while, until Frieda — as though K.'s arm had given her a warmth she could no longer do without — said: 'I won't be able to bear this life here. If you want to keep me, we must emigrate, somewhere — to the south of France, to Spain.' 'I can't emigrate,' said K. 'I came here to stay here. I shall stay here.' And in a contradiction that he made no effort at all to explain, he added, as if talking to himself: 'What could have lured me to this desolate country, if not the desire to stay here?' Then he said: 'But you want to stay here too; after all, it's your country. It's only Klamm you miss, and that gives you desperate ideas.' 'I should miss Klamm?' said Frieda. 'There's a superabundance of Klamm here, too much Klamm; I want to go away to escape him. It's not Klamm I miss, it's you; I want to go away because of you, because I can't have enough of you here, where everyone is tugging at me. If only the pretty mask were torn off me, if only my body became wretched, so that I could live in peace with you!' K. heard only one thing in this. 'Is Klamm still in touch with you?' he asked at once. 'Does he call you?'
paras.uz: Lekin K.da ham Frida bilan bog'lanish tufayli hamma narsa uning uchun qanday qilib yaxshilikka burilganini tushuntirishga endi qat'iyat qolmagan edi. U qo'lini sekin undan olib, biroz jim o'tirdi, toki Frida — go'yo K.ning qo'li unga endi usiz yashay olmaydigan iliqlik bergandek — dedi: «Men bu yerdagi bu hayotga chiday olmayman. Agar meni saqlab qolmoqchi bo'lsang, ko'chib ketishimiz kerak, qayergadir — Fransiyaning janubiga, Ispaniyaga.» «Ko'chib keta olmayman, — dedi K., — men bu yerga shu yerda qolish uchun kelganman. Men shu yerda qolaman.» Va tushuntirishga umuman urinmagan bir qarama-qarshilik bilan go'yo o'zi bilan gaplashayotgandek qo'shib qo'ydi: «Bu yerda qolish istagidan boshqa nima meni bu huvillagan yurtga jalb qila olardi?» Keyin dedi: «Lekin sen ham bu yerda qolishni istaysan, axir bu sening yurting. Senga faqat Klamm yetishmaydi, bu esa seni umidsiz fikrlarga olib keladi.» «Menga Klamm yetishmasmish? — dedi Frida. — Bu yerda Klamm haddan ziyod ko'p, Klamm juda ko'p; undan qochish uchun ketmoqchiman. Menga Klamm emas, sen yetishmaysan; sen uchun ketmoqchiman; chunki hamma meni tortqilayotgan bu yerda sendan to'ya olmayman. Qaniydi bu chiroyli niqobni yulib olishsa, qaniydi tanam xunuk bo'lsa, toki sen bilan tinchlikda yashay olsam.» K. bundan faqat bir narsani eshitdi. «Klamm hali ham sen bilan aloqadami? — so'radi u darhol. — U seni chaqiradimi?»

paras.en: 'I know nothing of Klamm,' said Frieda. 'I'm talking now about others — the assistants, for instance.' 'Ah, the assistants!' said K., surprised. 'Are they pursuing you?' 'Haven't you noticed, then?' asked Frieda. 'No,' said K., trying in vain to remember details. 'They're pushy and lecherous lads, certainly, but I didn't notice that they'd dared to approach you.' 'No?' said Frieda. 'You didn't notice how they couldn't be got out of our room at the Bridge Inn, how they jealously watched over our relations, how one of them lay down in my place on the straw mattress the other night, how they've now testified against you in order to drive you away, to ruin you, so as to be alone with me? You didn't notice any of that?' K. looked at Frieda without answering. These accusations against the assistants were probably correct, but they could all be interpreted much more innocently too, from the whole ridiculous, childish, scatterbrained, uncontrolled nature of the two. And didn't it also speak against the accusation that they had always striven to go everywhere with K. and not to stay behind with Frieda? K. said something to this effect. 'Hypocrisy,' said Frieda, 'didn't you see through that? Then why did you drive them away, if not for these reasons?' And she went to the window, moved the curtain aside a little, looked out and then called K. over.
paras.uz: «Klamm haqida hech narsa bilmayman, — dedi Frida, — men hozir boshqalar haqida gapiryapman, masalan, yordamchilar haqida.» «A, yordamchilar! — dedi K. hayron bo'lib. — Ular seni ta'qib qilishadimi?» «Nahotki payqamagan bo'lsang?» — so'radi Frida. «Yo'q, — dedi K. va tafsilotlarni eslashga behuda urindi, — ular, to'g'ri, surbet va shahvatparast bolalar, lekin senga yaqinlashishga jur'at etganlarini payqamadim.» «Payqamadingmi? — dedi Frida. — Ularni «Ko'prik yonidagi» mehmonxonadagi xonamizdan qanday chiqarib bo'lmaganini, munosabatlarimizni qanday rashk bilan kuzatganlarini, birortasi yaqinda somon to'shakda mening joyimga qanday yotib olganini, endi seni haydash, halok qilish, men bilan yolg'iz qolish uchun qanday qilib senga qarshi guvohlik berganlarini payqamadingmi? Bularning hech birini payqamadingmi?» K. javob bermay Fridaga qaradi. Yordamchilarga qarshi bu ayblovlar, ehtimol, to'g'ri edi, lekin ularning hammasini ikkalasining butun kulgili, bolalarcha, parishon, o'zini tuta olmaydigan tabiatidan kelib chiqib, ancha beg'uborroq talqin qilish ham mumkin edi. Ular doim K. bilan hamma joyga borishga intilganlari va Frida yonida qolmaganlari ham ayblovga qarshi gapirmasmidi? K. shunga o'xshash bir narsani aytdi. «Ikkiyuzlamachilik, — dedi Frida, — buni anglamadingmi? Unda nega ularni haydading, agar shu sabablar tufayli bo'lmasa?» Va u derazaga borib, pardani biroz surib, tashqariga qaradi, keyin K.ni yoniga chaqirdi.

paras.en: The assistants were still outside at the railings; tired as they evidently already were, they still from time to time, summoning all their strength, stretched out their arms imploringly towards the school. One of them, so as not to have to keep holding on, had hooked the back of his coat on one of the railing spikes.
paras.uz: Yordamchilar hamon tashqarida, panjara yonida edi; ular ko'rinib turganidek, allaqachon qanchalik charchagan bo'lishsa ham, vaqti-vaqti bilan bor kuchlarini yig'ib, qo'llarini maktab tomon iltijo bilan cho'zishardi. Ulardan biri doim ushlab turmaslik uchun kamzulining orqa etagini panjara nayzasiga ilib qo'ygan edi.

paras.en: 'The poor things! The poor things!' said Frieda.
paras.uz: «Bechoralar! Bechoralar!» — dedi Frida.

paras.en: 'Why did I drive them away?' cried K. 'The immediate cause of it was you.' 'I?' asked Frieda, without turning her eyes from outside. 'Your all too friendly treatment of the assistants,' said K., 'forgiving their bad behaviour, laughing at them, stroking their hair, your constant pity for them — "the poor things, the poor things", you're saying it again — and finally the latest incident, when I wasn't too high a price for you to buy the assistants off from a beating.' 'But that's just it,' said Frieda, 'that's what I'm talking about, that's what makes me unhappy, what keeps me from you, while I know no greater happiness for myself than to be with you, constantly, without interruption, without end; while I dream that here on earth there is no quiet place for our love, not in the village and not elsewhere, and so I imagine a grave, deep and narrow; there we hold each other embraced as if with tongs, I hide my face against you, you yours against me, and nobody will ever see us again. But here — look at the assistants! It's not you they mean when they clasp their hands, it's me.' 'And it's not I,' said K., 'who am looking at them, it's you.' 'Certainly, I,' said Frieda, almost angrily, 'that's what I keep talking about. Otherwise what would it matter that the assistants are after me — even if they are Klamm's emissaries.'
paras.uz: «Nega ularni haydaganimmi? — qichqirdi K. — Buning bevosita sababi sen bo'lding.» «Menmi?» — so'radi Frida tashqaridan nigohini uzmay. «Yordamchilarga haddan tashqari do'stona muomalang, — dedi K., — odobsizliklarini kechirishing, ularning ustidan kulishing, sochlarini silashing, ularga doimiy achinishing — «bechoralar, bechoralar» deb yana aytyapsan — va nihoyat oxirgi voqea: yordamchilarni kaltakdan qutqarib olish uchun men senga juda yuqori narx bo'lmadim.» «Gap ham shunda-da, — dedi Frida, — men shu haqda gapiryapman-ku, aynan shu meni baxtsiz qiladi, meni sendan uzoqlashtiradi, holbuki men o'zim uchun sen bilan doim, uzluksiz, cheksiz birga bo'lishdan kattaroq baxtni bilmayman; holbuki men bu yerda, yer yuzida sevgimiz uchun na qishloqda, na boshqa joyda tinch joy yo'qligini orzu qilaman va shuning uchun chuqur va tor qabrni tasavvur qilaman; u yerda biz bir-birimizni go'yo qisqich bilan qisgandek quchoqlab yotamiz, men yuzimni senga, sen yuzingni menga yashirasan va bizni hech kim boshqa hech qachon ko'rmaydi. Bu yerda esa yordamchilarga qara! Ular kaftlarini juftlaganida, bu senga emas, menga qaratilgan.» «Va ularga men emas, — dedi K., — sen qarayapsan.» «Albatta, men, — dedi Frida deyarli jahl bilan, — men doim shu haqda gapiryapman-ku. Aks holda yordamchilarning ortimdan yurishi nimani anglatardi — ular Klammning elchilari bo'lsa ham.»

paras.en: 'Klamm's emissaries,' said K., who was very surprised by this description, however natural it seemed to him at once. 'Klamm's emissaries, certainly,' said Frieda. 'Even if they are, they are at the same time silly boys who still need beatings for their upbringing. What ugly, dark boys they are! And how repulsive is the contrast between their faces, which suggest grown men, almost students, and their childish, foolish behaviour! Do you think I don't see that? I'm ashamed of them. But that's just it: they don't repel me, rather I'm ashamed of them. I always have to look over at them. When one ought to be annoyed with them, I have to laugh. When one ought to hit them, I have to stroke their hair. And when I lie beside you at night I can't sleep, and have to watch, over you, how one of them sleeps rolled tightly in the blanket and the other kneels in front of the open stove door stoking, and I have to lean forward so that I almost wake you. And it isn't the cat that frightens me — oh, I know cats, and I also know the restless, constantly disturbed dozing in the bar — it isn't the cat that frightens me, I frighten myself. And there's no need at all for that monster of a cat; I start at the slightest sound.
paras.uz: «Klammning elchilari», dedi K. — bu atama unga darhol qanchalik tabiiy tuyulsa ham, uni juda hayron qoldirdi. «Klammning elchilari, albatta, — dedi Frida, — ular shunday bo'lishsa ham, ayni paytda tarbiyasi uchun hali kaltak kerak bo'lgan bema'ni bolalar. Qanday xunuk, qora bolalar ular! Ularning katta yoshli odamlarni, hatto deyarli talabalarni eslatadigan yuzlari bilan bolalarcha-telbalarcha xatti-harakatlari o'rtasidagi zidlik qanchalik jirkanch! Buni ko'rmayman deb o'ylaysanmi? Men ulardan uyalaman. Lekin gap ham shunda: ular meni jirkantirmaydi, balki men ulardan uyalaman. Men doim ularga qarashga majburman. Ulardan g'ashlanish kerak bo'lganda, kulishga majburman. Ularni urish kerak bo'lganda, sochlarini silashga majburman. Tunda yoningda yotganimda uxlay olmayman va sening ustingdan birining adyolga mahkam o'ranib uxlayotganini, ikkinchisining esa pechning ochiq eshigi oldida tiz cho'kib olov yoqayotganini kuzatishga majburman va seni deyarli uyg'otib yuboradigan darajada oldinga engashishga majburman. Meni mushuk qo'rqitmaydi — eh, men mushuklarni bilaman, bufetdagi notinch, doim buziladigan mudroqni ham bilaman — meni mushuk qo'rqitmaydi, men o'zimni o'zim qo'rqitaman. Buning uchun o'sha mushuk degan maxluqning ham keragi yo'q, eng kichik shovqindan seskanib tushaman.

paras.en: At one moment I'm afraid that you'll wake up and everything will be over, and then again I jump up and light the candle so that you'll wake quickly and can protect me.' 'I knew nothing of all this,' said K., 'I drove them away only from a presentiment of it; but now they're gone, now perhaps everything is all right.' 'Yes, at last they're gone,' said Frieda, but her face was tormented, not joyful, 'only we don't know who they are. Klamm's emissaries — I call them that in my thoughts, as a game, but perhaps they really are. Their eyes, those simple and yet sparkling eyes, somehow remind me of Klamm's eyes; yes, that's it: it's Klamm's gaze that sometimes pierces me from their eyes. And so it isn't right when I said I was ashamed of them. I only wish it were so. I know, of course, that elsewhere and with other people the same behaviour would be stupid and offensive; with them it isn't so. I watch their foolishness with respect and admiration. But if they are Klamm's emissaries, who will free us from them? And would it then be good at all to be freed from them? Wouldn't you then have to fetch them in quickly and be happy if they still came?' 'You want me to let them in again?' asked K. 'No, no,' said Frieda, 'there's nothing I want less.
paras.uz: Goh sen uyg'onib qolasan va hammasi tugaydi, deb qo'rqaman, goh yana sakrab turib, sen tezroq uyg'onib, meni himoya qila olishing uchun sham yoqaman.» «Bularning hech biridan xabarim yo'q edi, — dedi K., — men ularni faqat shuni sezib haydadim; endi esa ular ketdi, endi, balki, hammasi yaxshidir.» «Ha, nihoyat ketishdi, — dedi Frida, lekin uning yuzi quvonchli emas, iztirobli edi, — faqat ular kimligini bilmaymiz. Klammning elchilari — men ularni xayolimda, o'yin tariqasida shunday atayman, lekin balki ular rostdan ham shundaydir. Ularning ko'zlari, o'sha sodda, lekin chaqnab turgan ko'zlari menga qandaydir Klammning ko'zlarini eslatadi; ha, gap shunda: ba'zan ularning ko'zlaridan meni Klammning nigohi teshib o'tadi. Shuning uchun ulardan uyalaman deganim noto'g'ri. Qaniydi shunday bo'lsa. Bilaman, boshqa joyda va boshqa odamlarda xuddi shu xatti-harakat ahmoqona va uyatli bo'lardi, ularda esa bunday emas. Men ularning ahmoqliklarini hurmat va hayrat bilan kuzataman. Lekin agar ular Klammning elchilari bo'lsa, bizni ulardan kim xalos qiladi; unda ulardan xalos bo'lish umuman yaxshi bo'larmidi? Unda sen ularni tezroq ichkariga olib kirishing va ular hali kelishsa, baxtiyor bo'lishing kerak emasmidi?» «Ularni yana kiritishimni xohlaysanmi?» — so'radi K. «Yo'q, yo'q, — dedi Frida, — bundan kamroq xohlaydigan narsam yo'q.

paras.en: The sight of them, if they now stormed in, their joy at seeing me again, their hopping about like children and their stretching out their arms like men — perhaps I wouldn't be able to bear any of it. But then, when I consider again that if you stay hard towards them, you may thereby be refusing Klamm himself access to you, I want to save you from the consequences of that by every means. Then I want you to let them come in. Then, K., in with them quickly! Have no regard for me — what do I matter! I'll defend myself as long as I can; but if I should lose, well, then I'll lose, but then with the knowledge that this too has happened for you.' 'You only strengthen me in my judgement about the assistants,' said K. 'They'll never come in with my consent. That I got them out proves, surely, that in certain circumstances they can be mastered, and further, that they have nothing essential to do with Klamm. Only yesterday evening I got a letter from Klamm from which it's clear that Klamm is quite wrongly informed about the assistants, from which again it must be concluded that they are completely indifferent to him, for if they weren't, he could certainly have got exact information about them. But that you see Klamm in them proves nothing, for you are still, unfortunately, influenced by the landlady and see Klamm everywhere.
paras.uz: Ular hozir bostirib kirsalar, ularning qiyofasi, meni yana ko'rganlaridan quvonishlari, bolalardek sakrab yurishlari va erkaklardek qo'l cho'zishlari — bularning hech biriga, balki, umuman chiday olmasdim. Lekin keyin yana o'ylasamki, agar sen ularga qattiqqo'l bo'lib qolsang, balki bu bilan Klammning o'ziga ham sening yoningga yo'lni yopasan — unda seni buning oqibatlaridan har qanday yo'l bilan saqlab qolishni istayman. Unda ularni ichkariga kiritishingni istayman. Unda, K., ularni tezroq ichkariga kirit! Meni o'ylama, men nima edim! Qo'limdan kelguncha o'zimni himoya qilaman; agar yutqazsam, xo'sh, yutqazaman, lekin bu ham sen uchun bo'lganini anglagan holda.» «Sen meni yordamchilar haqidagi fikrimda faqat mustahkamlayapsan, — dedi K. — Ular hech qachon mening roziligim bilan ichkariga kirmaydi. Ularni chiqarib yuborganim axir ularni ba'zi sharoitlarda jilovlash mumkinligini, demak, ularning Klamm bilan hech qanday muhim aloqasi yo'qligini isbotlaydi. Kecha kechqurungina men Klammdan xat oldim, undan Klammga yordamchilar haqida butunlay noto'g'ri ma'lumot berilgani ko'rinib turibdi, bundan esa ular unga mutlaqo befarq ekani degan xulosa kelib chiqadi, chunki aks holda u ular haqida, albatta, aniq ma'lumot olishi mumkin edi. Sening ularda Klammni ko'rishing esa hech narsani isbotlamaydi, chunki sen hamon, afsuski, bekaning ta'siridasan va hamma joyda Klammni ko'rasan.

paras.en: You are still Klamm's mistress, not yet by a long way my wife. Sometimes that makes me quite gloomy; then I feel as if I'd lost everything, I have the feeling that I've only just come to the village — but not full of hope, as I really was then, but knowing that only disappointments await me and that I'll have to taste them one after another, down to the last dregs. But that's only sometimes,' K. added with a smile, when he saw how Frieda sank down under his words, 'and basically it proves something good: namely, what you mean to me. And if you now ask me to choose between you and the assistants, then the assistants have already lost. What an idea, to choose between you and the assistants! But now I want to be rid of them for good, in words and thoughts. Besides, who knows whether the weakness that has come over us both doesn't come from our still not having had breakfast?' 'Possibly,' said Frieda, smiling tiredly, and went to work. K. too took up the broom again. After a little while there was a soft knock. 'Barnabas!' cried K., threw down the broom and was at the door in a few bounds. Frightened by the name more than by anything else, Frieda looked at him. With his unsteady hands K. couldn't open the old lock at once. 'I'm opening it,' he kept repeating, instead of asking who was actually knocking.
paras.uz: Sen hali ham Klammning ma'shuqasisan, mening xotinim bo'lishingga esa hali ancha bor. Ba'zan bu meni butunlay g'amgin qiladi, o'shanda go'yo hamma narsani yo'qotgandek bo'laman, go'yo qishloqqa endigina kelgandek his qilaman — lekin o'sha paytda aslida bo'lganimdek umid bilan emas, balki meni faqat hafsalasizliklar kutayotganini va ularni birin-ketin so'nggi quyqasigacha totib ko'rishim kerakligini anglagan holda. Lekin bu faqat ba'zan bo'ladi, — deb qo'shib qo'ydi K. jilmayib, uning so'zlaridan Frida qanday cho'kib ketganini ko'rib, — va aslida yaxshi narsani isbotlaydi: ya'ni sen men uchun nimani anglatishingni. Agar sen meni hozir sen bilan yordamchilar o'rtasida tanlashga chaqirsang, yordamchilar allaqachon yutqazgan. Sen bilan yordamchilar o'rtasida tanlash — bu qanday fikr! Endi esa ulardan so'zda ham, fikrda ham butunlay qutulmoqchiman. Aytgancha, kim biladi, ikkalamizni bosgan bu holsizlik hali ham nonushta qilmaganimizdan emasmikan?» «Bo'lishi mumkin», dedi Frida charchoq bilan jilmayib va ishga kirishdi. K. ham yana supurgini oldi. Biroz o'tgach, eshik sekin taqilladi. «Barnabas!» — qichqirdi K., supurgini tashlab, bir necha sakrashda eshik oldida bo'ldi. Bu ismdan boshqa hamma narsadan ko'ra ko'proq qo'rqib ketgan Frida unga qaradi. Titroq qo'llari bilan K. eski qulfni darhol ocha olmadi. «Hozir ochaman», deb takrorlardi u to'xtovsiz, aslida kim taqillatayotganini so'rash o'rniga.

paras.en: And then he had to watch as through the wide-flung door it was not Barnabas who came in, but the little boy who had once before wanted to speak to K. But K. had no wish to remember him. 'What do you want here?' he said. 'Lessons are next door.' 'I've come from there,' said the boy, and looked up at K. calmly with his big brown eyes, standing upright, his arms close to his body. 'What do you want, then? Quickly!' said K., bending down a little, for the boy spoke quietly. 'Can I help you?' asked the boy. 'He wants to help us,' K. said to Frieda, and then to the boy: 'What's your name, then?' 'Hans Brunswick,' said the boy, 'pupil in the fourth class, son of Otto Brunswick, master shoemaker in Madeleine Lane.' 'Well, well — your name is Brunswick,' said K., and was now friendlier to him. It turned out that Hans had been so upset by the bloody weals the schoolmistress had scratched into K.'s hand that he had decided then and there to stand by K. On his own authority, at the risk of severe punishment, he had now slipped away from the classroom next door like a deserter. It was probably above all boyish notions of this kind that governed him. The seriousness that spoke from everything he did matched them.
paras.uz: Keyin esa lang ochilgan eshikdan Barnabas emas, balki avval ham bir marta K. bilan gaplashmoqchi bo'lgan kichkina bola kirib kelganini ko'rishga majbur bo'ldi. Lekin K.ning uni eslashga xohishi yo'q edi. «Bu yerda nima qilyapsan? — dedi u. — Dars qo'shni xonada.» «Men o'sha yerdan keldim», dedi bola va katta jigarrang ko'zlari bilan K.ga xotirjam tikilib, qo'llarini tanasiga yopishtirib, tik turdi. «Xo'sh, nima istaysan? Tezroq!» — dedi K. va biroz engashdi, chunki bola sekin gapirardi. «Senga yordam bera olamanmi?» — so'radi bola. «U bizga yordam bermoqchi», dedi K. Fridaga, keyin bolaga: «Isming nima?» «Hans Brunsvik, — dedi bola, — to'rtinchi sinf o'quvchisi, Madlen ko'chasidagi etikdo'z usta Otto Brunsvikning o'g'li.» «Qara-ya, sening isming Brunsvik ekan», dedi K. va endi unga do'stonaroq bo'ldi. Ma'lum bo'lishicha, o'qituvchi qiz K.ning qo'lida tirnab qoldirgan qonli izlar Hansni shunchalik hayajonga solgan ekanki, u o'sha zahoti K.ni qo'llab-quvvatlashga qaror qilgan. Endi u katta jazo xavfiga qaramay, o'z boshimchaligi bilan qo'shni sinf xonasidan qochoq askardek sirg'alib chiqib kelgan edi. Uni, ehtimol, birinchi navbatda shunday bolalarcha tasavvurlar boshqarardi. Uning har bir qilmishidan sezilib turgan jiddiylik ham ularga mos edi.

paras.en: Only at first had shyness held him back; but he soon got used to K. and Frieda, and when he had been given hot, good coffee to drink he became lively and trusting, and his questions were eager and insistent, as though he wanted to learn the most important things as quickly as possible so as to be able to take decisions for K. and Frieda on his own. There was also something commanding in his nature; but it was so mixed with childish innocence that one gladly submitted to him, half sincerely, half in jest. At any rate he claimed all the attention for himself; all work had stopped, and breakfast dragged on a long time. Although he was sitting on the school bench, K. up on the teacher's desk and Frieda on a chair beside him, it looked as though Hans were the teacher, as though he were examining and judging the answers. A slight smile round his soft mouth seemed to suggest that he knew very well it was only a game, but for that very reason he was all the more serious about the rest of it; perhaps, too, it wasn't a smile at all but the happiness of childhood playing about his lips. Strikingly late he admitted that he had known K. ever since K. had once stopped at Lasemann's. K. was glad of this. 'You were playing at the woman's feet then?' asked K. 'Yes,' said Hans, 'that was my mother.'
paras.uz: Faqat dastlab uni uyatchanlik to'sib turdi, lekin tez orada u K. va Fridaga o'rganib qoldi, keyin issiq, yaxshi qahva ichgach, jonlanib, ishonuvchan bo'lib qoldi, savollari esa g'ayratli va qat'iy edi — go'yo u eng muhim narsalarni iloji boricha tezroq bilib olib, keyin K. va Frida uchun mustaqil qarorlar qabul qilmoqchidek. Uning tabiatida qandaydir buyruq beruvchilik ham bor edi; lekin u bolalarcha beg'uborlik bilan shunchalik aralashgan ediki, unga yarim chin, yarim hazil bilan bajonidil bo'ysunarding. Har holda u butun e'tiborni o'ziga tortdi, hamma ish to'xtadi, nonushta juda cho'zilib ketdi. U maktab partasida, K. tepada o'qituvchi stolida, Frida esa yonidagi kursida o'tirgan bo'lsa ham, go'yo Hans o'qituvchidek, go'yo u imtihon qilib, javoblarga baho berayotgandek ko'rinardi; uning yumshoq og'zi atrofidagi yengil tabassum u bu faqat o'yin ekanini yaxshi bilishini bildirayotgandek edi, lekin qolgan jihatdan u ishga shunchalik jiddiyroq yondashardi; balki bu umuman tabassum emas, balki lablari atrofida o'ynayotgan bolalik baxti edi. U K.ni bir marta Lazemannikiga kirganidan beri tanishini hayratlanarli darajada kech tan oldi. K. bundan xursand bo'ldi. «O'shanda sen ayolning oyoqlari ostida o'ynab o'tirganmiding?» — so'radi K. «Ha, — dedi Hans, — u mening onam edi.»

paras.en: And now he had to talk about his mother, but he did so only hesitantly and only after repeated prompting. It now turned out after all that he was a little boy. At times, it was true — especially in his questions, perhaps in a premonition of the future, perhaps only through an illusion of the restless, tense listener — an energetic, clever, far-sighted man almost seemed to speak from him; but then immediately afterwards, without any transition, he was only a schoolboy who didn't understand some questions at all, misinterpreted others, spoke too quietly with childish thoughtlessness although the fault had often been pointed out to him, and who finally, as if out of defiance, fell completely silent in the face of some urgent questions — and quite without embarrassment, as an adult never could. It was altogether as though, in his opinion, only he was allowed to ask questions, while the others' asking broke some rule and wasted time. He could then sit still for a long time with his body upright, head lowered, lower lip pushed out. Frieda liked this so much that she often put questions to him which she hoped would silence him in this way; and sometimes she succeeded, but it annoyed K. On the whole they learned little.
paras.uz: Endi u onasi haqida gapirib berishga majbur bo'ldi, lekin buni faqat ikkilanib va qayta-qayta undashlardan keyingina qildi; endi u baribir kichkina bola ekani ma'lum bo'ldi: ba'zan, ayniqsa savollarida — balki kelajakni oldindan sezib, balki faqat bezovta-zo'riqqan tinglovchining ko'z adashishi tufayli — undan deyarli g'ayratli, aqlli, uzoqni ko'ra oladigan erkak gapirayotgandek tuyulardi; lekin keyin darhol, hech qanday o'tishsiz, u faqat ba'zi savollarni umuman tushunmaydigan, boshqalarini noto'g'ri talqin qiladigan, bu xato unga ko'p marta ko'rsatilgan bo'lsa ham bolalarcha beparvolik bilan juda sekin gapiradigan va nihoyat ba'zi shoshilinch savollar oldida go'yo qaysarlikdan butunlay jim bo'lib qoladigan maktab o'quvchisi edi — buni u hech qanday xijolatsiz qilardi, katta odam hech qachon bunday qila olmasdi. Umuman, go'yo uning fikricha, faqat unga savol berishga ruxsat berilgandek, boshqalarning savol berishi bilan esa qandaydir qoida buzilib, vaqt behuda ketgandek edi. Shunda u tanasini tik tutib, boshini egib, pastki labini bo'rtirib, uzoq vaqt jim o'tira olardi. Bu Fridaga shunchalik yoqdiki, u unga tez-tez uni shu tarzda jim qildirishiga umid qilgan savollar berardi; bu unga ba'zan muyassar ham bo'lardi, lekin K.ning g'ashini keltirardi. Umuman olganda, oz narsa bilib olindi.

paras.en: His mother was a little sickly, but what illness it was remained undetermined. The child Frau Brunswick had had on her lap was Hans's sister and was called Frieda (Hans took the identity of name with the woman questioning him in an unfriendly way). They all lived in the village, but not at Lasemann's; they had only been there on a visit to be bathed, because Lasemann had the big tub, in which bathing and romping about gave special pleasure to the little children — to whom, however, Hans did not belong. Of his father Hans spoke reverently or fearfully, but only when there was not at the same time any talk of his mother; compared with his mother, his father's worth was evidently small. All questions about family life, by the way, however one tried to approach them, remained unanswered. About his father's trade one learned that he was the greatest shoemaker in the place, none was his equal — as was repeated more than once, even in reply to quite different questions; he even gave work to the other shoemakers, for instance to Barnabas's father too; in this last case Brunswick probably did it only as a special favour — at least that was what Hans's proud turn of the head suggested, which made Frieda jump down to him and give him a kiss. The question whether he had ever been to the Castle he answered only after many repetitions, and then with 'No'; the same question about his mother he didn't answer at all.
paras.uz: Onasi biroz kasalmand edi, lekin qanday kasallik ekani noaniq qoldi; Brunsvik xonim tizzasida tutgan bola Hansning singlisi edi va uning ismi Frida edi (o'zini so'roqqa tutayotgan ayol bilan ismlarining bir xilligini Hans yoqtirmay qabul qildi); ularning hammasi qishloqda yashardi, lekin Lazemannikida emas, ular u yerga faqat cho'milish uchun mehmonga borishgan edi, chunki Lazemannda katta tog'ora bor edi, unda cho'milish va o'ynab yurish kichkina bolalarga alohida zavq berardi — lekin Hans ular qatoriga kirmasdi. Otasi haqida Hans ehtirom bilan yoki qo'rquv bilan gapirardi, lekin faqat ayni paytda onasi haqida gap bo'lmagandagina; onasiga nisbatan otasining qadri, aftidan, kichik edi; aytgancha, oilaviy hayot haqidagi barcha savollar, qanday yondashishga urinilmasin, javobsiz qoldi. Otasining kasbi haqida uning qishloqdagi eng katta etikdo'z ekani, hech kim unga teng emasligi — bu butunlay boshqa savollarga javoban ham bir necha bor takrorlandi — bilib olindi; u hatto boshqa etikdo'zlarga, masalan, Barnabasning otasiga ham ish berardi; bu oxirgi holatda Brunsvik buni, ehtimol, faqat alohida marhamat bilan qilardi — hech bo'lmaganda Hansning mag'rur bosh burishi shunga ishora qildi va bu Fridani uning yoniga sakrab tushib, uni o'pishga undadi. Qasrda bo'lganmi degan savolga u faqat ko'p takrorlashlardan keyin, shunda ham «Yo'q» deb javob berdi; onasi haqidagi xuddi shu savolga esa umuman javob bermadi.

paras.en: Finally K. grew tired; he too thought the questioning useless — in that he agreed with the boy — and there was also something shameful in wanting to search out family secrets by way of an innocent child; doubly shameful, of course, was that even here one learned nothing. And when K., to finish, asked the boy what he was offering to help with, he was no longer surprised to hear that Hans only wanted to help with the work here, so that the teacher and schoolmistress wouldn't scold K. so much any more. K. explained to Hans that such help was not necessary. Scolding was probably part of the teacher's nature, and one could hardly protect oneself from it even with the most exact work; the work itself wasn't hard, and it was only because of chance circumstances that he was behind with it today. Besides, this scolding didn't affect K. as it did a pupil; he shook it off, it was almost a matter of indifference to him, and he hoped very soon to be able to escape the teacher entirely. So since it had only been a matter of help against the teacher, he thanked him very much, and Hans could go back again; he hoped he wouldn't be punished.
paras.uz: Nihoyat K. charchadi; unga ham so'roq qilish befoyda tuyuldi, bunda u bolaga haq berdi; beg'ubor bola orqali aylanma yo'l bilan oila sirlarini o'rganishga urinishda ham qandaydir uyatli narsa bor edi, to'g'ri, bu yerda ham hech narsa bilib olinmagani ikki baravar uyatli edi. Keyin K. yakunida boladan nimada yordam berishni taklif qilayotganini so'raganida, Hans faqat bu yerda ishga yordam bermoqchi, toki o'qituvchi va o'qituvchi qiz K. bilan boshqa bunchalik janjallashmasin, degan javobni eshitib, endi hayron bo'lmadi. K. Hansga bunday yordam kerak emasligini tushuntirdi: janjallashish o'qituvchining tabiatiga xos bo'lsa kerak, eng aniq ish bilan ham undan himoyalanish qiyin; ishning o'zi og'ir emas, u bugun faqat tasodifiy sharoitlar tufayli ishdan orqada qolgan; aytgancha, bu janjal K.ga o'quvchiga ta'sir qilgandek ta'sir qilmaydi, u uni silkitib tashlaydi, bu unga deyarli farqi yo'q, u tez orada o'qituvchidan butunlay qutulishga ham umid qiladi. Demak, gap faqat o'qituvchiga qarshi yordam haqida bo'lgani uchun, u buning uchun chin dildan minnatdor va Hans yana qaytib ketishi mumkin, umid qilamanki, uni jazolashmaydi.

paras.en: Although K. didn't stress it at all and only implied it involuntarily — that it was only help against the teacher he didn't need, while he left open the question of other help — Hans nevertheless heard it clearly and asked whether K. perhaps needed other help; he would very gladly help him, and if he weren't able to himself, he would ask his mother, and then it would certainly succeed. When his father had worries, too, he asked his mother for help. And his mother had once asked about K.; she herself hardly ever left the house, she had been at Lasemann's that time only as an exception; but he, Hans, often went there to play with Lasemann's children, and once his mother had asked him whether the land surveyor had perhaps been there again. Now his mother, being so weak and tired, mustn't be excited unnecessarily, and so he had simply said he hadn't seen the land surveyor there, and nothing more had been said about it; but now that he had found him here at the school, he had had to speak to him, so that he could report to his mother. For what his mother liked best was when one fulfilled her wishes without an express order.
paras.uz: K. buni umuman ta'kidlamagan va faqat beixtiyor ishora qilgan bo'lsa ham — ya'ni unga faqat o'qituvchiga qarshi yordam kerak emas, boshqa yordam haqidagi savolni esa ochiq qoldirgan — Hans buni baribir aniq eshitdi va K.ga balki boshqa yordam kerakdir, deb so'radi; u unga juda bajonidil yordam bergan bo'lardi, agar o'zi qodir bo'lmasa, onasidan so'rardi, shunda albatta muvaffaqiyatli bo'lardi. Otasi tashvishda bo'lganda ham onasidan yordam so'raydi. Onasi ham bir marta K. haqida so'ragan edi; uning o'zi uydan deyarli chiqmaydi, o'shanda Lazemannikida faqat istisno tariqasida bo'lgan; u — Hans esa Lazemannning bolalari bilan o'ynash uchun u yerga tez-tez boradi va bir marta onasi undan yer o'lchovchi yana u yerda bo'lganmi, deb so'ragan. Onasi shunchalik zaif va charchagan bo'lgani uchun uni behuda hayajonlantirish mumkin emas, shuning uchun u shunchaki yer o'lchovchini u yerda ko'rmaganini aytgan va bu haqda boshqa gap bo'lmagan; lekin endi uni shu yerda, maktabda topgach, onasiga xabar bera olishi uchun u bilan gaplashishi kerak edi. Chunki onasi eng ko'p shuni yoqtiradi: aniq buyruqsiz uning istaklarini bajarishsa.

paras.en: At this K. said, after brief reflection, that he needed no help, he had everything he required, but it was very kind of Hans to want to help him, and he thanked him for his good intention; it was possible that he would need something later, and then he would turn to him — he had his address, after all. On the other hand, perhaps he, K., could help a little this time; he was sorry that Hans's mother was ailing and that evidently nobody here understood her trouble; in such a neglected case a serious worsening of what was in itself a slight trouble could often set in. Now he, K., had some medical knowledge and, what was worth even more, experience in treating the sick. A good deal that doctors hadn't managed had succeeded for him. At home, because of his healing powers, he had always been called 'the bitter herb'. At any rate he would gladly see Hans's mother and speak to her. Perhaps he could give some good advice; he would gladly do it if only for Hans's sake. At first Hans's eyes lit up at this offer, which tempted K. to become more insistent; but the result was unsatisfactory, for in answer to various questions Hans said — and he wasn't even very sad about it — that no stranger might visit his mother, because she needed great care; although K. had hardly spoken to her that time, she had lain in bed for some days afterwards — which, admittedly, often happened.
paras.uz: Shunda K. biroz o'ylab, unga hech qanday yordam kerak emasligini, unda zarur bo'lgan hamma narsa borligini, lekin Hans unga yordam bermoqchi bo'lgani juda yoqimli ekanini va yaxshi niyati uchun minnatdorligini aytdi; balki keyinroq unga biror narsa kerak bo'lib qolar, shunda unga murojaat qiladi, manzili axir bor. Aksincha, balki bu safar u — K. biroz yordam bera olar; Hansning onasi kasal ekani va, aftidan, bu yerda hech kim bu dardni tushunmasligidan afsusda; bunday e'tiborsiz qolgan holatda o'z-o'zidan yengil bo'lgan dard ko'pincha jiddiy og'irlashishi mumkin. U — K.da esa ba'zi tibbiy bilimlar va, undan ham qimmatlirog'i, bemorlarni davolash tajribasi bor. Shifokorlar uddalay olmagan ko'p narsa unga muyassar bo'lgan. Uyida uni shifobaxsh ta'siri uchun doim «achchiq o't» deb atashardi. Har holda u Hansning onasini ko'rib, u bilan gaplashishni bajonidil istardi. Balki yaxshi maslahat bera olardi, buni faqat Hans uchun ham bajonidil qilardi. Bu taklifdan Hansning ko'zlari avvaliga chaqnab ketdi va bu K.ni yanada qat'iyroq bo'lishga undadi, lekin natija qoniqarsiz bo'ldi, chunki Hans turli savollarga — bundan unchalik xafa ham bo'lmay — onasining yoniga begona mehmon kelishi mumkin emas, chunki u juda ehtiyotga muhtoj, deb javob berdi; o'shanda K. u bilan deyarli gaplashmagan bo'lsa ham, u keyin bir necha kun to'shakda yotgan, bu, to'g'ri, tez-tez bo'lib turadi.

paras.en: His father, though, had been very annoyed with K. that time, and he would certainly never allow K. to come to his mother; indeed, he had wanted to seek K. out then to punish him for his behaviour; only his mother had held him back. But above all his mother herself generally didn't want to speak to anyone, and her question about K. was no exception to the rule; on the contrary, precisely when he was mentioned she could have expressed the wish to see him, but she hadn't done so, and had thereby clearly expressed her will. She only wanted to hear about K., but she didn't want to speak to him. Besides, it wasn't really an illness at all that she suffered from; she knew very well the cause of her condition, and sometimes she hinted at it too: it was probably the air here that she couldn't bear; but then again she didn't want to leave the place either, because of his father and the children; and besides, it was already better than it had been before. That was roughly what K. learned. Hans's powers of thought visibly increased now that he had to protect his mother from K. — from K., whom he had supposedly wanted to help; indeed, for the good purpose of keeping K. away from his mother, he even contradicted his own earlier statements in some things, for instance as regards the illness.
paras.uz: Lekin o'shanda otasi K.dan juda jahli chiqqan va u K.ning onasi yoniga kelishiga, albatta, hech qachon ruxsat bermaydi; ha, o'shanda u K.ni xatti-harakati uchun jazolash maqsadida izlab topmoqchi bo'lgan, faqat onasi uni bundan to'xtatgan. Lekin eng asosiysi, onasining o'zi umuman hech kim bilan gaplashishni istamaydi va uning K. haqidagi savoli qoidadan istisno emas edi; aksincha, aynan u eslatilganda uni ko'rish istagini bildirishi mumkin edi, lekin u bunday qilmadi va shu bilan o'z irodasini aniq ifoda etdi. U K. haqida faqat eshitishni istaydi, lekin u bilan gaplashishni istamaydi. Aytgancha, u chekayotgan narsa umuman haqiqiy kasallik emas, u o'z holatining sababini juda yaxshi biladi va ba'zan unga ishora ham qiladi: ehtimol, bu u chiday olmaydigan bu yerning havosi; lekin u otasi va bolalari tufayli bu joyni tark etishni ham istamaydi, bundan tashqari, avvalgidan allaqachon yaxshiroq. K. bilib olgani taxminan shular edi; Hans onasini K.dan — go'yo yordam bermoqchi bo'lgan K.dan himoya qilishi kerak bo'lgani uchun uning fikrlash qobiliyati ko'rinib turganidek kuchaydi; ha, K.ni onasidan uzoq tutishdek yaxshi maqsad uchun u ba'zi narsalarda, masalan, kasallik borasida, hatto o'zining oldingi gaplariga ham zid gapirdi.

paras.en: Nevertheless K. noticed even now that Hans was still well-disposed towards him; only, over his mother he forgot everything else. Whoever one set up against his mother was at once in the wrong — now it had been K., but it could also be his father, for instance. K. wanted to try this last and said that it was certainly very sensible of the father to guard the mother so from every disturbance, and if he, K., had had even an inkling of anything like that then, he would certainly not have dared to speak to the mother, and he asked now, belatedly, to have his apologies conveyed at home. On the other hand, he couldn't quite understand why the father, if the cause of the trouble was as clearly established as Hans said, held the mother back from recovering in other air; one had to say he held her back, for she wasn't going away only because of the children and him; but she could take the children with her; she wouldn't have to go away for long, nor very far; even up on the Castle hill the air was quite different. The father needn't fear the cost of such a trip; after all, he was the greatest shoemaker in the place, and surely he or the mother had relatives or acquaintances at the Castle who would gladly take her in. Why didn't he let her go?
paras.uz: Shunga qaramay, K. hozir ham Hans unga hali ham xayrixoh ekanini payqadi, faqat onasi tufayli u hamma narsani unutardi; onasiga qarshi kimni qo'ymasang, u darhol nohaq bo'lib qolardi; hozir bu K. edi, lekin bu, masalan, otasi ham bo'lishi mumkin edi. K. bu oxirgisini sinab ko'rmoqchi bo'ldi va otasi onasini har qanday bezovtalikdan shunchalik ehtiyot qilishi, albatta, juda oqilona ekanini, agar u — K. o'shanda shunga o'xshash narsani sezganida, onasiga gapirishga albatta jur'at etmasligini aytdi va hozir, kechikib bo'lsa ham, uyda uzr so'rashlarini iltimos qildi. Aksincha, agar dardning sababi Hans aytganidek shunchalik aniq bo'lsa, nega otasi onasini boshqa havoda dam olishdan ushlab turishini u unchalik tushuna olmasdi; ushlab turadi deyish kerak, chunki u faqat bolalari va u tufayli ketmayapti, bolalarni esa o'zi bilan olib ketishi mumkin edi; u uzoq muddatga ham, juda uzoqqa ham ketishi shart emas edi, Qasr tepaligining o'zida ham havo butunlay boshqacha. Otasi bunday sayohatning xarajatlaridan qo'rqmasligi kerak, axir u qishloqdagi eng katta etikdo'z, albatta, unda yoki onasida ham Qasrda uni bajonidil qabul qiladigan qarindoshlar yoki tanishlar bor. Nega uni qo'yib yubormaydi?

paras.en: He shouldn't underestimate such a trouble. K. had seen the mother only fleetingly, but it was precisely her striking pallor and weakness that had moved him to speak to her; even then he had wondered that the father had left the sick woman in the bad air of the common bathing and washing room and had also put no restraint on himself in his loud talk. The father probably didn't know what was at stake; even if the trouble had perhaps improved lately, such a trouble has its whims, but in the end, if one doesn't fight it, it comes back with gathered strength, and then nothing can help any more. If K. couldn't speak to the mother, it might still be good if he spoke to the father and drew his attention to all this.
paras.uz: U bunday dardni yengil baholamasligi kerak; K. onasini faqat bir zum ko'rgan, lekin aynan uning ko'zga tashlanadigan rangparligi va holsizligi uni u bilan gaplashishga undagan edi; o'shandayoq u otasi bemor ayolni umumiy cho'milish va yuvinish xonasining yomon havosida qoldirgani va baland ovozdagi gaplarida ham o'zini hech tiymagani uchun hayron bo'lgan edi. Otasi, ehtimol, gap nima haqida ekanini bilmaydi; dard so'nggi paytlarda, balki, yengillashgandir, bunday dardning injiqliklari bor, lekin oxir-oqibat, agar unga qarshi kurashilmasa, u to'plangan kuch bilan qaytadi va shunda endi hech narsa yordam bera olmaydi. Agar K. onasi bilan gaplasha olmasa, balki otasi bilan gaplashib, uning e'tiborini bularning hammasiga qaratsa, yaxshi bo'lardi.
