chapters.title: 12. The landlady's warning
chapters.recap_uz: Hans K.ni otasi yo'qligida, indinga onasining oldiga olib borishga rozi bo'ladi; K. Brunsvik bilan ham gaplashmoqchi. Hans katta bo'lsa, K.ga o'xshamoqchi. O'qituvchi K.ni ish bilan quvlaydi. Frida bekaning ogohlantirishini aytib beradi: K. uni faqat Klammga yetish uchun garov sifatida olgan, Hans bilan ham shunday hiyla ishlatyapti. K. bu dushman fikri ekanini aytadi va Brunsvik xonim Qasrdan kelganini, u yo'lni bilishi mumkinligini tushuntiradi. Kechqurun K. yo'lni tozalab, Giza va Shvarserning jim sevgisini kuzatadi.

paras.en: Hans had listened intently, had understood most of it and had keenly felt the threat of the incomprehensible remainder. Nevertheless he said K. couldn't speak to his father; his father had an aversion to him and would probably treat him as the teacher did. He said this smiling and shyly when he spoke of K., and grimly and sadly when he mentioned his father. But he added that K. might perhaps speak to his mother after all — though only without his father's knowledge. Then Hans thought for a while with a fixed stare, just like a woman who wants to do something forbidden and is looking for a way of doing it unpunished, and said that the day after tomorrow it might perhaps be possible: his father was going to the Herrenhof in the evening, he had meetings there; then he, Hans, would come in the evening and take K. to his mother — provided, of course, that his mother agreed, which was still very unlikely. Above all, she did nothing against his father's will; she submitted to him in everything, even in things whose unreasonableness even he, Hans, clearly saw. Hans was now really seeking help from K. against his father; it was as though he had deceived himself in thinking he wanted to help K., while in reality he had wanted to find out whether, since nobody from his old surroundings had been able to help, this stranger who had suddenly appeared, and whom his mother had even mentioned, might be able to. How unconsciously reserved, almost sly, the boy was!
paras.uz: Hans zo'r qiziqish bilan tingladi, ko'p narsani tushundi, tushunarsiz qolgan qismning tahdidini esa kuchli his qildi. Shunga qaramay, u K. otasi bilan gaplasha olmasligini aytdi: otasi undan jirkanadi va, ehtimol, unga o'qituvchidek muomala qiladi. U buni K. haqida gapirganda jilmayib va uyalib, otasini tilga olganda esa alam va g'am bilan aytdi. Lekin u K., balki, baribir onasi bilan gaplasha olishini qo'shib qo'ydi — faqat otasidan bexabar. Keyin Hans qotib qolgan nigoh bilan biroz o'yladi — xuddi taqiqlangan ish qilmoqchi bo'lib, uni jazosiz bajarish yo'lini izlayotgan ayoldek — va indinga, balki, mumkin bo'lar, dedi: otasi kechqurun Herrenhofga boradi, u yerda uning majlislari bor; shunda u — Hans kechqurun kelib, K.ni onasining oldiga olib boradi, faqat, albatta, onasi rozi bo'lsa — bu esa hali juda dargumon. Eng avvalo, u otasining irodasiga qarshi hech narsa qilmaydi, hamma narsada unga bo'ysunadi, hatto u — Hans ham aqlsizligini aniq ko'radigan narsalarda ham. Endi Hans haqiqatan ham K.dan otasiga qarshi yordam izlayotgan edi; go'yo u K.ga yordam bermoqchiman deb o'ylab, o'zini aldagandek edi, holbuki aslida u eski muhitidan hech kim yordam bera olmagani uchun, to'satdan paydo bo'lgan va hatto onasi ham tilga olgan bu begona yordam bera olarmikan, shuni bilib olmoqchi bo'lgan edi. Bola beixtiyor qanchalik ichimdan pishgan, deyarli makkor edi!

paras.en: Up to now it had hardly been possible to gather it from his appearance and his words; only from the confessions extracted, as it were, after the event, by chance and design, did one notice it. And now in long conversations with K. he considered what difficulties would have to be overcome. With the best will in the world on Hans's part, they were almost insurmountable difficulties; wholly lost in thought and yet seeking help, he kept looking at K. with restlessly blinking eyes. Before his father left he mustn't tell his mother anything, otherwise his father would find out and everything would be made impossible; so he could mention it only later; but even then, out of consideration for his mother, not suddenly and quickly but slowly and at a suitable opportunity; only then could he ask for his mother's consent, only then could he fetch K. But wouldn't it then already be too late — wouldn't his father's return already be threatening? No, it was impossible after all. K., on the other hand, proved that it was not impossible. There was no need to fear that the time wouldn't be enough; a short conversation, a short meeting, would be enough, and Hans needn't fetch K. K. would wait hidden somewhere near the house and come at once at a sign from Hans.
paras.uz: Buni hozirgacha uning qiyofasi va so'zlaridan deyarli sezib bo'lmasdi; faqat tasodif va niyat bilan go'yo keyinchalik sug'urib olingan iqrorlaridangina buni payqash mumkin edi. Endi esa u K. bilan uzoq suhbatlarda qanday qiyinchiliklarni yengish kerakligini o'ylardi. Hans qanchalik chin dildan istamasin, bu deyarli yengib bo'lmas qiyinchiliklar edi; butunlay xayolga cho'mgan, lekin baribir yordam izlab, u bezovta pirpirayotgan ko'zlari bilan to'xtovsiz K.ga qarardi. Otasi ketmasidan oldin onasiga hech narsa aytmasligi kerak, aks holda otasi bilib qoladi va hammasi imkonsiz bo'ladi, demak, buni faqat keyin aytishi mumkin; lekin o'shanda ham, onasini o'ylab, to'satdan va tez emas, balki sekin va qulay fursatda; faqat shundan keyin onasidan rozilik so'rashi, faqat shundan keyin K.ni olib kelishi mumkin; lekin unda allaqachon kech bo'lmaydimi, otasining qaytishi tahdid solmaydimi? Yo'q, bu baribir imkonsiz. K. esa aksincha, bu imkonsiz emasligini isbotladi. Vaqt yetmasligidan qo'rqmaslik kerak, qisqa suhbat, qisqa uchrashuv yetarli, Hans esa K.ni olib kelishi shart emas. K. uyning yaqinida qayerdadir yashirinib kutadi va Hansning ishorasi bilan darhol keladi.

paras.en: No, said Hans, K. mustn't wait near the house — again it was his sensitivity about his mother that governed him — K. mustn't set out without his mother's knowledge; Hans mustn't enter into such an understanding with K. kept secret from his mother; he must fetch K. from the school, and not before his mother knew and allowed it. Very well, said K., then it was really dangerous, and it was then possible that the father would catch him in the house; and even if that didn't happen, the mother, for fear of it, wouldn't let K. come at all, and so everything would founder on the father after all. Hans again defended himself against this, and so the argument went back and forth. K. had long since called Hans from the bench to the teacher's desk, had drawn him between his knees and now and then stroked him soothingly. This closeness, too, helped to bring about an agreement, despite Hans's occasional resistance. In the end they agreed on the following: Hans would first tell his mother the whole truth; but, to make her consent easier, he would add that K. also wanted to speak to Brunswick himself — not, however, about his mother, but about his own affairs.
paras.uz: Yo'q, dedi Hans, K. uy yonida kutmasligi kerak — uni yana onasi borasidagi sezgirlik boshqarayotgan edi — K. onasidan bexabar yo'lga chiqmasligi kerak, Hans K. bilan onasidan yashirin bunday kelishuvga kirmasligi kerak; u K.ni maktabdan olib ketishi kerak, shunda ham onasi bilmaguncha va ruxsat bermaguncha emas. Yaxshi, dedi K., unda bu rostdan ham xavfli, unda otasi uni uyda tutib olishi mumkin; agar bu sodir bo'lmasa ham, onasi bundan qo'rqib, K.ni umuman kelishiga yo'l qo'ymaydi va shunday qilib, hammasi baribir otasi tufayli barbod bo'ladi. Hans bunga yana qarshilik ko'rsatdi va shunday qilib bahs u yoqdan-bu yoqqa davom etdi. K. allaqachon Hansni partadan o'qituvchi stoliga chaqirib, uni tizzalari orasiga tortgan va vaqti-vaqti bilan tinchlantirib silab qo'yardi. Bu yaqinlik ham Hansning vaqti-vaqti bilan qarshilik ko'rsatishiga qaramay, kelishuvga erishishga yordam berdi. Nihoyat quyidagicha kelishildi: Hans avval onasiga butun haqiqatni aytadi; lekin unga rozilik berishni yengillashtirish uchun K. Brunsvikning o'zi bilan ham gaplashmoqchi ekanini qo'shib qo'yadi — to'g'ri, onasi haqida emas, balki o'z ishlari haqida.

paras.en: This was true, too. In the course of the conversation it had occurred to K. that Brunswick, however dangerous and wicked a man he might otherwise be, couldn't really be his opponent any more; after all, at least according to the mayor's account, he had been the leader of those who — even if for political reasons — had demanded that a land surveyor be appointed. K.'s arrival in the village must therefore have been welcome to Brunswick; in that case, admittedly, the angry greeting on the first day and the aversion Hans spoke of were almost incomprehensible; but perhaps Brunswick was offended precisely because K. hadn't turned to him first for help; perhaps there was some other misunderstanding that could be cleared up with a few words.
paras.uz: Bu to'g'ri ham edi: suhbat davomida K.ning xayoliga kelgan ediki, Brunsvik, boshqa jihatdan qanchalik xavfli va yovuz odam bo'lmasin, aslida endi uning raqibi bo'la olmaydi, axir u, hech bo'lmaganda oqsoqolning hikoyasiga ko'ra, — garchi siyosiy sabablarga ko'ra bo'lsa ham — yer o'lchovchini chaqirishni talab qilganlarning yetakchisi bo'lgan. Demak, K.ning qishloqqa kelishi Brunsvik uchun xushxabar bo'lishi kerak edi; unda, to'g'ri, birinchi kundagi g'azablangan qarshi olish va Hans aytgan jirkanish deyarli tushunarsiz edi; lekin balki Brunsvik aynan K. yordam so'rab avval unga murojaat qilmagani uchun xafa bo'lgandir, balki bir necha so'z bilan oydinlashtirish mumkin bo'lgan boshqa tushunmovchilik bordir.

paras.en: But once that had happened, K. might very well gain support in Brunswick against the teacher, indeed even against the mayor. The whole official deception — for what else was it? — by which the mayor and the teacher kept him away from the Castle authorities and forced him into the caretaker's post could be uncovered. If it came again to a struggle between Brunswick and the mayor over K., Brunswick would have to draw K. to his side; K. would become a guest in Brunswick's house, Brunswick's means of power would be put at his disposal in defiance of the mayor; who knew where that might lead him — and at any rate he would often be near the woman. So he played with his dreams, and they with him, while Hans, thinking only of his mother, anxiously watched K.'s silence, as one does with a doctor sunk in thought to find a remedy for a difficult case. Hans agreed to K.'s proposal that he should speak to Brunswick about the land surveyor's post, though only because his mother was thereby protected from his father, and besides, it was only an emergency that would, he hoped, not arise.
paras.uz: Agar bu amalga oshsa, K. Brunsvikda o'qituvchiga, hatto oqsoqolga qarshi ham yaxshi tayanch topishi mumkin edi; oqsoqol va o'qituvchi uni Qasr idoralaridan uzoq tutib, maktab qorovuli lavozimiga tiqib qo'ygan butun rasmiy aldov — bu boshqa nima edi? — fosh etilishi mumkin edi; agar Brunsvik bilan oqsoqol o'rtasida K. uchun yana kurash boshlansa, Brunsvik K.ni o'z tomoniga tortishi kerak bo'lardi, K. Brunsvikning uyida mehmon bo'lardi, Brunsvikning kuch-qudrat vositalari oqsoqolga qasddan uning ixtiyoriga berilardi; kim biladi, bu bilan u qayerga yetib borardi, har holda u o'sha ayolning yonida tez-tez bo'lardi — u orzular bilan, orzular esa u bilan shunday o'ynardi, Hans esa faqat onasini o'ylab, K.ning sukutini tashvish bilan kuzatardi — og'ir holat uchun davo topish maqsadida o'yga cho'mgan shifokorni kuzatgandek. K.ning Brunsvik bilan yer o'lchovchi lavozimi haqida gaplashmoqchi degan taklifiga Hans rozi bo'ldi, lekin faqat shu bilan onasi otasidan himoyalangani va bundan tashqari, bu faqat favqulodda holat bo'lib, umid qilamanki, yuz bermaydi, degani uchun.

paras.en: He only asked further how K. would explain the late hour of the visit to his father, and was finally satisfied — though with a somewhat darkened face — with K.'s saying that the unbearable caretaker's post and the treatment he got from the teacher had made him forget all consideration in a sudden fit of despair.
paras.uz: U faqat K. tashrifning kech soatini otasiga qanday tushuntirishini so'radi va nihoyat, biroz qorayib ketgan yuz bilan bo'lsa ham, K. chidab bo'lmas maktab qorovuli lavozimi va o'qituvchining unga mos muomalasi uni to'satdan umidsizlikka solib, barcha andishani unuttirib yubordi, deb aytishi bilan qanoatlandi.

paras.en: When in this way everything had been thought out, as far as one could see, and the possibility of success was at least no longer excluded, Hans, freed from the burden of reflection, grew merrier and chattered childishly for a little while, first with K. and then with Frieda too, who had long been sitting there as if lost in quite other thoughts and only now began to take part in the conversation again. Among other things she asked him what he wanted to be; he didn't think long and said he wanted to be a man like K. When he was then asked his reasons he didn't know how to answer, of course, and the question whether he wanted to become a caretaker, perhaps, he firmly denied. Only when they asked further did they see by what roundabout way he had come to his wish. K.'s present situation was by no means enviable, but sad and contemptible; Hans saw that clearly too, and he didn't need to watch other people to recognise it; he himself would have liked best to protect his mother from every look and word of K.'s. Nevertheless he came to K. and asked him for help and was happy when K. agreed; he believed he saw something similar in other people too, and above all his mother herself had mentioned K. Out of this contradiction arose in him the belief that, although K. was still lowly and off-putting now, in a future — admittedly almost unimaginably distant — he would surpass everyone.
paras.uz: Shu tarzda hamma narsa, ko'rish mumkin bo'lgan darajada, oldindan o'ylab chiqilgach va muvaffaqiyat imkoniyati hech bo'lmaganda endi istisno qilinmagach, o'ylash yukidan xalos bo'lgan Hans quvnoqroq bo'ldi, yana biroz bolalarcha gaplashdi — avval K. bilan, keyin Frida bilan ham; Frida uzoq vaqt go'yo butunlay boshqa xayollarga berilgandek o'tirgan va endigina yana suhbatga qo'shila boshlagan edi. Boshqa narsalar qatori u Hansdan kim bo'lmoqchi ekanini so'radi; u ko'p o'ylamay, K.ga o'xshagan odam bo'lmoqchi ekanini aytdi. Keyin undan sabablarini so'rashganida, u, albatta, javob bera olmadi, maktab qorovuli bo'lmoqchimisan degan savolni esa qat'iyan rad etdi. Faqat yana so'rab-surishtirilgandan keyingina u o'z istagiga qanday aylanma yo'l bilan kelgani ma'lum bo'ldi. K.ning hozirgi ahvoli hech qanday havas qilarli emas, balki achinarli va nafratli edi; buni Hans ham aniq ko'rardi va buni anglash uchun boshqa odamlarni kuzatishi ham shart emas edi, uning o'zi ham onasini K.ning har bir nigohi va so'zidan saqlashni istardi. Shunga qaramay, u K.ning oldiga kelib, undan yordam so'radi va K. rozi bo'lganida baxtiyor bo'ldi; boshqa odamlarda ham u shunga o'xshash narsani ko'rgandek bo'lardi, eng asosiysi esa onasining o'zi K.ni tilga olgan edi. Bu qarama-qarshilikdan unda shunday ishonch paydo bo'ldiki, K. hozir hali past va yoqimsiz bo'lsa ham, to'g'ri, deyarli tasavvur qilib bo'lmas darajada uzoq kelajakda u baribir hammadan o'zib ketadi.

paras.en: And it was precisely this positively foolish remoteness, and the proud development that was to lead into it, that attracted Hans; for this prize he was even willing to put up with the present K. The especially childish yet precocious thing about this wish was that Hans looked down on K. as on someone younger, whose future stretched further than his own — the future of a little boy. And it was also with an almost gloomy seriousness that he spoke of these things, compelled again and again by Frieda's questions. It was K. who cheered him up again, saying he knew what Hans envied him for: it was his fine knotted walking stick, which lay on the table and which Hans, distracted in the conversation, had been playing with. Well, K. knew how to make such sticks, and if their plan succeeded he would make Hans an even finer one. It was no longer quite clear now whether Hans hadn't really meant only the stick, so delighted was he with K.'s promise; and he took a cheerful leave, not without squeezing K.'s hand firmly and saying: 'The day after tomorrow, then.'
paras.uz: Aynan shu rosmana ahmoqona uzoqlik va unga olib borishi kerak bo'lgan mag'rur taraqqiyot Hansni o'ziga tortardi: bu narx uchun u hatto hozirgi K.ni ham qabul qilishga tayyor edi. Bu istakning ayniqsa bolalarcha-oqsoqollarcha tomoni shunda ediki, Hans K.ga o'zidan kichikka — kelajagi o'zinikidan, kichkina bolaning kelajagidan ham uzoqroqqa cho'zilgan odamga qaragandek yuqoridan qarardi. U bu narsalar haqida Fridaning savollari bilan qayta-qayta majburlanib, deyarli g'amgin jiddiylik bilan gapirardi. Faqat K. uni yana quvontirdi: u Hans unga nima uchun havas qilayotganini bilishini aytdi — bu stolda yotgan va Hans suhbat davomida parishonlik bilan o'ynab o'tirgan uning chiroyli tugunli hassasi edi. Xo'sh, K. bunday hassalarni yasashni biladi va agar rejalari muvaffaqiyatli bo'lsa, Hansga bundan ham chiroylirog'ini yasab beradi. Endi Hans haqiqatan ham faqat hassani nazarda tutmaganmi — bu unchalik aniq emas edi, u K.ning va'dasidan shunchalik quvondi va K.ning qo'lini mahkam siqib: «Demak, indinga», deb quvnoq xayrlashdi.

paras.en: It was high time that Hans had gone, for shortly afterwards the teacher flung the door open and, seeing K. and Frieda sitting quietly at the table, shouted: 'Excuse the disturbance! But tell me, when will this place finally be tidied? We have to sit crammed together over there, lessons are suffering, while you loll and stretch here in the big gymnasium, and to have even more room you've sent the assistants away as well! But now at least get up and get moving!' And to K. alone: 'You go and fetch me my mid-morning snack from the Bridge Inn!'
paras.uz: Hans ketgani ayni vaqtida bo'ldi, chunki ko'p o'tmay o'qituvchi eshikni lang ochib, K. va Fridaning stol yonida xotirjam o'tirganini ko'rib, qichqirdi: «Bezovta qilganim uchun kechiringlar! Lekin aytinglar-chi, bu yer qachon nihoyat yig'ishtiriladi? Biz u yoqda tiqilib o'tirishimiz kerak, dars zarar ko'ryapti, sizlar esa bu yerda, katta gimnastika xonasida cho'zilib-kerilib yotibsizlar, yana ko'proq joy bo'lsin deb yordamchilarni ham jo'natib yuboribsizlar! Endi esa hech bo'lmaganda turinglar va qimirlanglar!» Va faqat K.ga: «Sen hozir menga «Ko'prik yonidagi» mehmonxonadan nonushta gazagini olib kel!»

paras.en: All this was shouted furiously, but the words were relatively mild, even the 'you' — familiar and in itself rude. K. was ready to obey at once; only to sound the teacher out, he said: 'But I've been given notice.' 'Notice or no notice, fetch me my snack,' said the teacher. 'Notice or no notice — that's just what I want to know,' said K. 'What are you babbling about?' said the teacher. 'You didn't accept the notice, after all.' 'Is that enough to make it invalid?' asked K. 'Not for me,' said the teacher, 'you may believe me there; but for the mayor it is, incomprehensibly. But now run, or you really will be thrown out.' K. was satisfied: so the teacher had spoken to the mayor in the meantime, or perhaps not spoken to him at all but only worked out the mayor's probable opinion, and this was in K.'s favour. Now K. wanted to hurry off at once for the snack, but the teacher called him back again from the corridor — whether he had only wanted to test K.'s willingness to serve with this special order so as to be guided by it in future, or whether he now felt a fresh desire to command and enjoyed making K. run off in a hurry and then, at his order, turn round again just as hurriedly, like a waiter.
paras.uz: Bularning hammasi g'azab bilan baqirib aytildi, lekin so'zlar nisbatan yumshoq edi, hatto o'z-o'zidan qo'pol «sen» ham. K. darhol bo'ysunishga tayyor edi; faqat o'qituvchining fikrini bilib olish uchun dedi: «Axir men bo'shatilganman-ku.» «Bo'shatilgan-bo'shatilmagan, menga gazakni olib kel», dedi o'qituvchi. «Bo'shatilganmanmi-yo'qmi — men aynan shuni bilmoqchiman», dedi K. «Nima deb valdirayapsan? — dedi o'qituvchi. — Sen axir bo'shatishni qabul qilmading-ku.» «Uni kuchsiz qilish uchun shu yetarlimi?» — so'radi K. «Men uchun yetarli emas, — dedi o'qituvchi, — bunga ishonishing mumkin, lekin oqsoqol uchun yetarli, tushunib bo'lmaydigan tarzda. Endi esa yugur, aks holda rostdan ham haydalasan.» K. mamnun edi: demak, o'qituvchi bu orada oqsoqol bilan gaplashgan yoki balki umuman gaplashmagan, faqat oqsoqolning taxminiy fikrini o'zi uchun tuzib olgan va bu fikr K.ning foydasiga edi. Endi K. darhol gazak uchun shoshilmoqchi edi, lekin o'qituvchi uni yo'lakdan yana qaytarib chaqirdi — yo bu alohida buyruq bilan K.ning xizmatga tayyorligini sinab, keyinchalik shunga qarab ish tutmoqchi bo'lgani uchun, yo endi unda buyruq berishga yana yangi ishtiyoq paydo bo'lib, K.ni shoshib yugurtirib, keyin uning buyrug'i bilan ofitsiantdek xuddi shunday shoshib orqaga qaytarishdan zavqlangani uchun.

paras.en: K. for his part knew that by giving in too much he would make himself the teacher's slave and whipping boy; but up to a certain limit he was now willing to put up patiently with the teacher's whims, for even if, as had turned out, the teacher could not lawfully dismiss him, he could certainly make the post agonising to the point of being unbearable. But it was precisely this post that K. now cared about more than before. The conversation with Hans had given him new hopes — admittedly improbable, entirely groundless, but no longer to be forgotten; they almost overshadowed even Barnabas. If he pursued them — and he could not do otherwise — he would have to concentrate all his strength on them, worry about nothing else: not about food, lodging, the village authorities, indeed not even about Frieda; and at bottom it was all only about Frieda, for everything concerned him only in relation to her. So he had to try to keep this post, which gave Frieda some security, and he mustn't regret putting up with more from the teacher, with this aim in view, than he would otherwise have brought himself to endure. None of this was too painful; it belonged to the series of life's constant small sufferings; it was nothing compared with what K. was striving for, and he had not come here to lead a life of honour and peace.
paras.uz: K. o'z navbatida haddan tashqari yon bersa, o'zini o'qituvchining quli va kaltak yeydigan bolasiga aylantirishini bilardi, lekin ma'lum chegaragacha u endi o'qituvchining injiqliklarini sabr bilan qabul qilmoqchi edi, chunki o'qituvchi, ma'lum bo'lishicha, uni qonuniy ravishda bo'shata olmasa ham, lavozimni chidab bo'lmas darajada azobli qilishi, albatta, mumkin edi. Lekin aynan shu lavozim endi K. uchun avvalgidan ko'ra muhimroq edi. Hans bilan suhbat unda yangi — tan olish kerakki, ehtimoldan yiroq, butunlay asossiz, lekin endi unutib bo'lmaydigan — umidlar uyg'otgan edi; ular hatto Barnabasni ham deyarli to'sib qo'ygan edi. Agar ularning ortidan borsa — va u boshqacha qila olmasdi — butun kuchini shunga to'plashi, boshqa hech narsa haqida qayg'urmasligi kerak edi: na ovqat, na turar joy, na qishloq idoralari, hatto na Frida haqida; aslida esa gap faqat Frida haqida edi, chunki hamma narsa uni faqat unga bog'liq holda qiziqtirardi. Shuning uchun u Fridaga biroz xavfsizlik beradigan bu lavozimni saqlab qolishga harakat qilishi kerak edi va shu maqsadni ko'zlab, o'qituvchidan aks holda chidashga o'zini majbur qila olmaydiganidan ko'proq narsaga chidashdan afsuslanmasligi kerak edi. Bularning hammasi unchalik og'riqli emas edi, bu hayotning doimiy mayda azoblari qatoriga kirardi, bu K. intilayotgan narsaga nisbatan hech narsa emas edi va u bu yerga sharaf va tinchlikda hayot kechirish uchun kelmagan edi.

paras.en: And so, just as he had wanted to run to the inn at once, he was now, at the changed order, ready at once to tidy the room first, so that the schoolmistress could come back over with her class. But the tidying had to be done very fast, for afterwards K. was still to fetch the snack, and the teacher was already very hungry and thirsty. K. assured him that everything would be done as he wished. For a while the teacher watched K. hurrying — clearing away the sleeping place, pushing the gymnastic apparatus back into position, sweeping in a flash — while Frieda washed and scrubbed the platform. The zeal seemed to satisfy the teacher; he pointed out further that a pile of wood for heating had been prepared outside the door — he evidently didn't want to let K. near the shed any more — and then went over to the children, threatening to come back soon and check.
paras.uz: Shunday qilib, u darhol mehmonxonaga yugurmoqchi bo'lganidek, o'zgargan buyruqdan keyin ham darhol avval xonani tartibga keltirishga tayyor bo'ldi, toki o'qituvchi qiz o'z sinfi bilan yana bu yoqqa o'ta olsin. Lekin tartibni juda tez keltirish kerak edi, chunki keyin K. baribir gazakni olib kelishi kerak edi, o'qituvchi esa allaqachon qattiq och va chanqagan edi. K. hammasi xohlaganidek bo'lishiga ishontirdi; o'qituvchi biroz K.ning shoshilib yotoq joyini yig'ishtirayotganini, gimnastika jihozlarini joyiga surib qo'yayotganini, chaqqonlik bilan supurayotganini, Frida esa minbarni yuvib, ishqalayotganini kuzatib turdi. G'ayrat o'qituvchini qoniqtirganga o'xshardi; u yana eshik oldida isitish uchun bir uyum o'tin tayyorlab qo'yilganini eslatdi — shiyponga K.ni, ehtimol, endi yaqinlashtirmoqchi emas edi — va tez orada qaytib kelib tekshirishini tahdid qilib, bolalar oldiga o'tib ketdi.

paras.en: After a spell of silent work Frieda asked why K. was now submitting so much to the teacher. It was no doubt a compassionate, anxious question, but K., thinking how little Frieda had succeeded, according to her original promise, in protecting him from the teacher's orders and violence, merely said shortly that now that he had once become caretaker, he must fill the post. Then it was quiet again, until K. — reminded precisely by this short exchange that Frieda had for so long seemed lost in anxious thoughts, above all during almost the whole conversation with Hans — asked her openly, while he was carrying in the wood, what was occupying her. She answered, looking up at him slowly, that it was nothing definite; she was only thinking of the landlady and of the truth of some of her words. Only when K. pressed her did she answer more fully, after several refusals, without, however, stopping her work — which she did not out of diligence, for the work wasn't getting on at all, but only so as not to be forced to look at K.
paras.uz: Bir muddat jim ishlagandan keyin Frida nega K. endi o'qituvchiga bunchalik bo'ysunayotganini so'radi. Bu, ehtimol, achinish va tashvish bilan berilgan savol edi, lekin K. Frida dastlabki va'dasiga ko'ra uni o'qituvchining buyruqlari va zo'ravonliklaridan saqlashni qanchalik oz uddalaganini o'ylab, faqat qisqagina: endi bir marta maktab qorovuli bo'lgandan keyin lavozimni ham bajarishi kerak, dedi. Keyin yana jimlik cho'kdi, toki K. — aynan shu qisqa suhbat tufayli Frida allaqachon uzoq vaqtdan beri, ayniqsa Hans bilan bo'lgan deyarli butun suhbat davomida go'yo tashvishli o'ylarga cho'mib qolganini eslab — o'tinni ichkariga tashib yurgan holda undan ochiqchasiga nima uni band qilayotganini so'radi. U sekin unga ko'z tashlab, aniq hech narsa emasligini, faqat beka va uning ba'zi so'zlarining haqiqati haqida o'ylayotganini aytdi. Faqat K. qistaganidan keyingina u bir necha marta rad etgach, batafsilroq javob berdi, lekin bunda ishini to'xtatmadi — buni u tirishqoqlikdan qilmadi, chunki ish baribir umuman oldinga siljimayotgan edi, balki faqat K.ga qarashga majbur bo'lmaslik uchun qildi.

paras.en: And now she told how, during K.'s conversation with Hans, she had at first listened calmly; how then, startled by some of K.'s words, she had begun to grasp the meaning of the words more sharply; and how from then on she had been unable to stop hearing in K.'s words confirmations of a warning she owed to the landlady, but in whose justice she had never wanted to believe. K. — annoyed by the general phrases, and more irritated than moved even by the tearful, plaintive voice, above all because the landlady was now meddling in his life again, at least through memories, since in person she had so far had little success — threw down the wood he was carrying in his arms, sat on it and now demanded complete clarity in earnest words. 'Several times already,' Frieda began, 'right at the beginning, the landlady tried to make me doubt you. She didn't claim that you lie; on the contrary, she said you were childishly open, but that your nature was so different from ours that, even when you speak openly, we can hardly bring ourselves to believe you, and unless a good friend saves us first, we'll have to get used to believing you only through bitter experience. Even she, who has such a sharp eye for people, had fared hardly any differently.
paras.uz: Endi u K.ning Hans bilan suhbati paytida avval qanday xotirjam tinglaganini, keyin K.ning ba'zi so'zlaridan cho'chib, so'zlarning ma'nosini qanday o'tkirroq anglay boshlaganini va shundan buyon K.ning so'zlarida bekaga qarzdor bo'lgan, lekin haqligiga hech qachon ishonishni istamagan bir ogohlantirishning tasdiqlarini eshitishdan to'xtay olmaganini aytib berdi. K. umumiy iboralardan g'ashlanib, hatto ko'z yoshli, nolali ovozdan ta'sirlanishdan ko'ra ko'proq achchiqlanib — eng avvalo, beka endi yana uning hayotiga, hech bo'lmaganda xotiralar orqali aralashayotgani uchun, chunki shaxsan hozirgacha unchalik muvaffaqiyat qozonmagan edi — qo'lidagi o'tinni yerga tashladi, uning ustiga o'tirdi va endi jiddiy so'zlar bilan to'liq aniqlik talab qildi. «Bir necha marta, — deb boshladi Frida, — boshidanoq beka meni sendan shubhalanishga undashga urindi; u sen yolg'on gapirasan demadi, aksincha, sen bolalarcha ochiq ekansan, lekin tabiating biznikidan shunchalik farq qiladiki, sen ochiq gapirsang ham, senga ishonishga o'zimizni zo'rg'a majbur qilamiz va agar yaxshi dugona bizni avvalroq qutqarmasa, faqat achchiq tajriba orqali ishonishga o'rganishimiz kerak bo'ladi, dedi. Hatto odamlarni shunchalik o'tkir ko'radigan uning o'zi bilan ham deyarli boshqacha bo'lmagan ekan.

paras.en: But after the last conversation with you at the Bridge Inn she had — I'm only repeating her wicked words — seen through your tricks; now you couldn't deceive her any more, even if you made an effort to hide your intentions. But you don't hide anything, she said again and again, and then she said too: Just make an effort to really listen to him on any occasion — not just superficially, no, really listen. That was all she had done, and in doing so she had heard roughly the following about me: you made up to me — she used that disgraceful phrase only because I happened to come your way, didn't exactly displease you, and because you quite wrongly consider a barmaid the predestined victim of any guest who stretches out his hand. Besides, as the landlady learned from the landlord of the Herrenhof, for some reason you wanted to spend the night at the Herrenhof that time, and that could of course be achieved in no other way than through me. All that would have been reason enough to make you my lover for that night; but for more to come of it, more was needed, and this more was Klamm. The landlady claims she doesn't know what you want from Klamm; she only claims that before you knew me you strove for Klamm just as fiercely as afterwards. The only difference was that before you were hopeless, but now you believed you had in me a reliable means of really getting through to Klamm, soon, and even with the upper hand.
paras.uz: Lekin «Ko'prik yonidagi» mehmonxonada sen bilan bo'lgan so'nggi suhbatdan keyin u — men faqat uning yomon so'zlarini takrorlayapman — sening hiylalaringni fahmlab qolgan, endi sen niyatlaringni yashirishga urinsang ham, uni aldab bo'lmaysan. Lekin sen axir hech narsani yashirmaysan, buni u qayta-qayta aytdi, keyin yana dedi: Uni istalgan fursatda haqiqatan tinglashga harakat qil, yuzaki emas, yo'q, haqiqatan tingla. U shundan boshqa hech narsa qilmagan va bunda men haqimda taxminan quyidagilarni eshitgan: sen menga yopishib olgansan — u bu sharmandali so'zni faqat shuning uchun ishlatdiki, men tasodifan yo'lingga chiqib qoldim, senga unchalik yoqmagan ham emasdim va sen bufetchi qizni juda noto'g'ri ravishda qo'l cho'zgan har bir mehmonning oldindan belgilangan qurboni deb hisoblaysan. Bundan tashqari, bekaning Herrenhof egasidan bilishicha, sen o'shanda qandaydir sabablarga ko'ra Herrenhofda tunamoqchi bo'lgansan, bunga esa, albatta, mendan boshqa yo'l bilan erishib bo'lmasdi. Bularning hammasi seni o'sha tun uchun mening oshig'imga aylantirishga yetarli sabab bo'lardi; lekin bundan ko'prog'i chiqishi uchun ko'proq narsa kerak edi va bu ko'proq narsa Klamm edi. Beka sen Klammdan nima istashingni bilmasligini aytadi, u faqat sen meni tanishingdan oldin ham, keyin ham Klammga xuddi shunchalik shiddat bilan intilganingni ta'kidlaydi. Farq faqat shunda ekanki, avval sen umidsiz bo'lgansan, endi esa menda Klammga haqiqatan, tez va hatto ustunlik bilan yetib borishning ishonchli vositasini topgan deb o'ylagansan.

paras.en: But how frightened I was — though that was only fleeting, without deeper reason — when you said once today that before you knew me you had been wandering astray here. They may be the same words the landlady used; she too says that you have only become purposeful since you knew me. That, she says, came from your believing that in me you had conquered a mistress of Klamm's and so possessed a pledge that could only be redeemed at the highest price. To negotiate this price with Klamm is your only aim. Since I mean nothing to you and the price everything, you are ready to make any concession as regards me, but obstinate as regards the price. That's why it's a matter of indifference to you that I lose my place at the Herrenhof, indifferent that I have to leave the Bridge Inn too, indifferent that I'll have to do the heavy caretaker's work.
paras.uz: Lekin bugun bir marta meni tanishingdan oldin bu yerda adashib yurganingni aytganingda, qanchalik qo'rqib ketdim — bu faqat bir lahzalik edi, chuqurroq sababsiz. Bu, balki, beka ishlatgan o'sha so'zlardir; u ham sen faqat meni tanigandan keyingina maqsadli bo'lib qolganingni aytadi. Bu, uning aytishicha, sen menda Klammning ma'shuqasini zabt etdim va shu bilan faqat eng yuqori narxga qaytarib olinishi mumkin bo'lgan garovga ega bo'ldim, deb ishonganingdan kelib chiqqan. Bu narx haqida Klamm bilan savdolashish — sening yagona intilishing. Senga men hech narsa emasman, narx esa hamma narsa bo'lgani uchun, men borasida har qanday yon berishga tayyorsan, narx borasida esa qaysarsan. Shuning uchun Herrenhofdagi joyimni yo'qotishim ham, «Ko'prik yonidagi» mehmonxonani ham tark etishim kerakligi ham, og'ir maktab qorovuli ishini bajarishim kerakligi ham senga baribir.

paras.en: You have no tenderness, indeed no longer even time for me; you leave me to the assistants; you don't know jealousy; my only value for you is that I was Klamm's mistress. In your ignorance you strive not to let me forget Klamm, so that at the end I won't resist too much when the decisive moment has come; and yet you also fight against the landlady, the only one you believe capable of tearing me away from you; that's why you drove your quarrel with her to the limit, so as to have to leave the Bridge Inn with me. That I am, as far as it depends on me, your possession under all circumstances — of that you have no doubt. You imagine the interview with Klamm as a business deal, cash against cash.
paras.uz: Senda mehr yo'q, hatto men uchun vaqting ham yo'q; meni yordamchilarga tashlab qo'yasan, rashkni bilmaysan; sen uchun mening yagona qadrim — Klammning ma'shuqasi bo'lganim; nodonligingda sen meni Klammni unutmasligim uchun harakat qilasan, toki hal qiluvchi payt kelganda oxirida haddan tashqari qarshilik ko'rsatmayin; shunga qaramay, sen bekaga qarshi ham kurashasan — faqat uni meni sendan tortib ola oladi, deb hisoblaysan — shuning uchun men bilan «Ko'prik yonidagi» mehmonxonani tark etishga majbur bo'lish uchun u bilan janjalni avjiga chiqarding; men o'zimga bog'liq bo'lgan darajada har qanday holatda sening mulking ekanimga sen shubha qilmaysan. Klamm bilan suhbatni sen savdo bitimi sifatida — naqdga naqd — tasavvur qilasan.

paras.en: You reckon with all possibilities; provided you obtain the price, you are ready to do anything. If Klamm wants me, you'll give me to him; if he wants you to stay with me, you'll stay; if he wants you to cast me off, you'll cast me off; but you're also ready to play a comedy: if it's advantageous, you'll pretend to love me; you'll try to combat his indifference by emphasising your own insignificance and shaming him by the fact of being his successor, or by passing on to him my confessions of love for his person — which I did really make — and asking him to take me back, on payment of the price, of course; and if nothing else helps, you'll simply beg in the name of the married couple K. But then, the landlady concluded, when you see that you've been mistaken in everything — in your assumptions and in your hopes, in your idea of Klamm and of his relations with me — then my hell will begin; for then I'll be more than ever your only possession, on which you remain dependent, but at the same time a possession that has proved worthless, and that you'll treat accordingly, since you have no other feeling for me than that of an owner.'
paras.uz: Sen barcha imkoniyatlarni hisobga olasan; narxga erishsang, hamma narsani qilishga tayyorsan; Klamm meni istasa, meni unga berasan; u sening yonimda qolishingni istasa, qolasan; meni haydab yuborishingni istasa, haydab yuborasan; lekin sen komediya o'ynashga ham tayyorsan: agar foydali bo'lsa, meni sevgandek ko'rsatasan; uning befarqligiga qarshi o'z arzimasligingni ta'kidlab, uni o'rinbosari ekaning bilan uyaltirib kurashishga urinasan, yoki men uning shaxsiga nisbatan qilgan — rostdan ham qilgan — sevgi izhorlarimni unga yetkazib, meni yana qabul qilishini, albatta, narxni to'lab, so'raysan; agar boshqa hech narsa yordam bermasa, shunchaki K. er-xotin nomidan tilanchilik qilasan. Lekin keyin, — deb yakunladi beka, — hamma narsada — taxminlaringda ham, umidlaringda ham, Klamm va uning menga munosabati haqidagi tasavvuringda ham — adashganingni ko'rganingda, mening do'zaxim boshlanadi, chunki unda men senga qaram bo'lib qoladigan yagona mulking bo'laman, lekin ayni paytda qadrsiz bo'lib chiqqan mulk va sen unga shunga yarasha muomala qilasan, chunki menga nisbatan egalik hissidan boshqa hissing yo'q.»

paras.en: K. had listened intently, his mouth drawn tight; the wood under him had started to roll, he had almost slid onto the floor, he had paid no attention; only now did he get up, sit on the platform, take Frieda's hand, which weakly tried to withdraw from him, and say: 'In this account I haven't always been able to tell your opinion and the landlady's apart.' 'It was only the landlady's opinion,' said Frieda. 'I listened to all of it because I revere the landlady; but it was the first time in my life that I rejected her opinion completely. Everything she said seemed so miserable to me, so far from any understanding of how things stood between the two of us. Rather, the exact opposite of what she said seemed right to me. I thought of the dismal morning after our first night, how you knelt beside me with a look as though everything were lost. And how it then really turned out that, however hard I tried, I didn't help you but hindered you. Through me the landlady became your enemy, a powerful enemy whom you still underestimate; because of me, for whom you had such worries, you had to fight for your post, were at a disadvantage against the mayor, had to submit to the teacher, were at the mercy of the assistants — but worst of all: for my sake you had perhaps offended against Klamm.
paras.uz: K. lablarini qisib, zo'r diqqat bilan tingladi; ostidagi o'tin dumalay boshlagan, u deyarli yerga sirg'alib tushgan edi, lekin bunga e'tibor bermadi; faqat endi u o'rnidan turib, minbarga o'tirdi, Fridaning undan zaif tortib olishga urinayotgan qo'lini ushladi va dedi: «Bu hikoyada men har doim ham sening va bekaning fikrini bir-biridan ajrata olmadim.» «Bu faqat bekaning fikri edi, — dedi Frida. — Men hammasini tingladim, chunki bekani hurmat qilaman; lekin hayotimda birinchi marta uning fikrini butunlay rad etdim. U aytgan hamma narsa menga shunchalik ayanchli, ikkimizning o'rtamizdagi munosabatni tushunishdan shunchalik yiroq tuyuldi. Aksincha, uning aytganlarining mutlaqo teskarisi menga to'g'ri tuyuldi. Birinchi tunimizdan keyingi o'sha g'amgin tongni, sen go'yo hammasi yo'qolgandek nigoh bilan yonimda qanday tiz cho'kkaningni o'yladim. Keyin haqiqatan ham shunday bo'ldiki, men qanchalik urinmay, senga yordam bermadim, balki xalaqit berdim. Men tufayli beka sening dushmaning bo'ldi — sen hali ham yengil baholaydigan qudratli dushman; men uchun — men haqimda shunchalik qayg'urganing uchun — sen o'z lavozimingdan kurashishga majbur bo'lding, oqsoqol oldida noqulay ahvolga tushding, o'qituvchiga bo'ysunishga majbur bo'lding, yordamchilarga qaram bo'lib qolding; eng yomoni esa: men uchun sen, balki, Klammga qarshi gunoh qilgansan.

paras.en: That you now kept wanting to get to Klamm was surely only the powerless effort to placate him somehow. And I told myself that the landlady, who certainly knew all this much better than I, only wanted to save me from too terrible self-reproaches with her insinuations. A well-meant but superfluous effort. My love for you would have helped me over everything; in the end it would have carried you forward too, if not here in the village, then elsewhere; it had already given a proof of its strength — it saved you from Barnabas's family.' 'So that was your counter-opinion then,' said K. 'And what has changed since?' 'I don't know,' said Frieda, looking at K.'s hand, which was holding hers. 'Perhaps nothing has changed; when you're so close to me and ask so calmly, then I believe nothing has changed. But in reality —' she took her hand away from K., sat upright facing him and wept without covering her face; she held this tear-flooded face freely towards him, as though she weren't weeping over herself and so had nothing to hide, but were weeping over K.'s betrayal, and so the misery of the sight of her was his due as well — 'but in reality everything has changed since I heard you talking to the boy.
paras.uz: Endi to'xtovsiz Klammga yetib bormoqchi bo'lishing esa faqat uni qandaydir yo'l bilan yarashtirishga qilingan ojiz intilish edi. Va men o'zimga aytdimki, bularning hammasini mendan ancha yaxshi biladigan beka o'z shivirlari bilan meni faqat haddan tashqari og'ir o'z-o'zini ayblashdan saqlamoqchi. Yaxshi niyatli, lekin ortiqcha urinish. Senga bo'lgan sevgim meni hamma narsadan o'tkazib qo'ygan bo'lardi, oxir-oqibat seni ham oldinga olib borardi — bu yerda, qishloqda bo'lmasa, boshqa joyda; u o'z kuchining isbotini allaqachon bergan edi — seni Barnabasning oilasidan qutqardi.» «Demak, o'shanda sening qarshi fikring shu edi, — dedi K., — o'shandan beri nima o'zgardi?» «Bilmayman, — dedi Frida va K.ning o'z qo'lini ushlab turgan qo'liga qaradi, — balki hech narsa o'zgarmagandir; sen menga shunchalik yaqin bo'lsang va shunchalik xotirjam so'rasang, hech narsa o'zgarmagan deb ishonaman. Lekin aslida…» — u qo'lini K.dan tortib oldi, uning ro'parasida tik o'tirib, yuzini yopmay yig'ladi; u ko'z yoshiga to'lgan bu yuzni unga erkin tutib turardi, go'yo u o'zi uchun yig'lamayotgandek va shuning uchun yashiradigan hech narsasi yo'qdek, balki K.ning xiyonati uchun yig'layotgandek va shuning uchun uning qiyofasidagi alam ham K.ga tegishlidek, — «lekin aslida seni bola bilan gaplashayotganingni eshitganimdan beri hammasi o'zgardi.

paras.en: How innocently you began, asking about the household, about this and that; I felt as if you'd just come into the bar, friendly, open-hearted, looking for my eyes so eagerly, like a child. There was no difference from that time, and I only wished the landlady were here, listening to you, and then still trying to hold on to her opinion. But then, suddenly — I don't know how it happened — I noticed with what intention you were talking to the boy. With your sympathetic words you won his trust, which isn't easily won, in order then to go undisturbed for your goal, which I recognised more and more. That goal was the woman. From your speeches, apparently so concerned about her, nothing but regard for your own business spoke, quite undisguised. You were betraying the woman even before you had won her. Not only my past but my future too I heard in your words; it was as though the landlady were sitting beside me explaining everything to me, and I was trying with all my strength to push her away, yet seeing clearly the hopelessness of such an effort; and in fact it was no longer really I who was being betrayed — I wasn't even being betrayed any more — but the strange woman.
paras.uz: Qanchalik beg'ubor boshlading: uy sharoitlari, u-bu narsa haqida so'rading; menga go'yo sen endigina bufetga kirib kelgandek, iltifotli, ochiqko'ngil, nigohimni bolalarcha g'ayrat bilan izlayotgandek tuyuldi. O'sha paytdan hech qanday farq yo'q edi va men faqat beka shu yerda bo'lib, seni tinglab, keyin ham o'z fikrida turib olishga urinsa edi, deb istadim. Lekin keyin, to'satdan — bu qanday sodir bo'lganini bilmayman — bola bilan qanday niyatda gaplashayotganingni payqadim. Hamdardona so'zlar bilan sen uning oson qozonib bo'lmaydigan ishonchini qozonding, keyin xalaqitsiz o'z maqsadingga — men uni tobora ko'proq anglab borgan maqsadga — tashlanish uchun. Bu maqsad o'sha ayol edi. Uning uchun go'yo qayg'urayotgandek gaplaringdan butunlay yashirinmagan holda faqat o'z ishlaringni o'ylash gapirardi. Sen ayolni qozonishingdan oldinoq aldading. So'zlaringdan men faqat o'tmishimni emas, kelajagimni ham eshitdim; go'yo beka yonimda o'tirib, menga hammasini tushuntirayotgandek, men esa uni bor kuchim bilan itarib yuborishga urinayotgandek, lekin bunday urinishning umidsizligini aniq ko'rayotgandek edim; bunda esa aslida aldanayotgan endi men emas edim — hatto aldanmayotgan ham edim — balki o'sha begona ayol edi.

paras.en: And then, when I pulled myself together and asked Hans what he wanted to be, and he said he wanted to become like you — so he already belonged to you so completely — what great difference was there now between him, the good boy who was being misused here, and me, back then in the bar?'
paras.uz: Keyin men o'zimni qo'lga olib, Hansdan kim bo'lmoqchi ekanini so'raganimda va u senga o'xshagan bo'lmoqchi ekanini — demak, allaqachon butunlay seniki ekanini — aytganida, u yerda suiiste'mol qilinayotgan o'sha yaxshi bola bilan o'shanda bufetdagi men o'rtamizda endi qanday katta farq bor edi?»

paras.en: 'Everything,' said K. — through growing used to the reproach he had composed himself — 'everything you say is in a certain sense right; it isn't untrue, it's only hostile. They are the thoughts of the landlady, my enemy, even if you believe they're your own; that comforts me. But they're instructive; one can still learn a good deal from the landlady. She didn't say it to me herself, although otherwise she hasn't spared me; evidently she entrusted this weapon to you in the hope that you would use it at an hour that was especially bad or decisive for me. If I misuse you, she misuses you in a similar way. But now, Frieda, consider: even if everything were exactly as the landlady says, it would be very bad in one case only — namely, if you don't love me. Then, only then, would it really be the case that I won you with calculation and cunning in order to profiteer with this possession. Perhaps then it was even part of my plan that, to draw out your pity, I came before you arm in arm with Olga that time, and the landlady only forgot to mention this as well in her account of my guilt. But if it isn't the bad case, and it wasn't a cunning beast of prey that seized you that time, but you came to meet me just as I came to meet you, and we found each other, both forgetting ourselves — tell me, Frieda, how is it then?
paras.uz: «Hammasi, — dedi K. — ta'nalarga ko'nikib qolgani uchun u o'zini qo'lga olgan edi, — sen aytgan hamma narsa ma'lum ma'noda to'g'ri; u yolg'on emas, faqat dushmanona. Bular bekaning — mening dushmanimning fikrlari, ularni o'zingniki deb ishonsang ham; bu meni yupatadi. Lekin ular ibratli, bekadan hali ko'p narsani o'rganish mumkin. Menga u buni o'zi aytmadi, garchi boshqa paytlarda meni ayamagan bo'lsa ham; aftidan, u bu qurolni senga men uchun ayniqsa og'ir yoki hal qiluvchi soatda ishlatarsan, degan umidda ishonib topshirgan. Agar men seni suiiste'mol qilsam, u ham seni shunga o'xshab suiiste'mol qiladi. Lekin endi, Frida, o'ylab ko'r: hammasi beka aytganidek aynan shunday bo'lsa ham, bu faqat bir holatda juda yomon bo'lardi — ya'ni agar sen meni sevmasang. Shunda, faqat shunda, men haqiqatan ham bu mulk bilan foyda ko'rish uchun seni hisob-kitob va hiyla bilan qo'lga kiritgan bo'lardim. Balki unda o'shanda achinishingni uyg'otish uchun Olga bilan qo'ltiqlashib oldingga kelishim ham rejamning bir qismi bo'lgandir, beka esa buni ham aybnomamda eslatishni unutib qo'ygandir. Lekin agar bu yomon holat bo'lmasa va o'shanda seni qandaydir ayyor yirtqich tortib olmagan bo'lsa, balki men senga qarab kelganimdek, sen ham menga qarab kelgan bo'lsang va biz ikkalamiz ham o'zimizni unutib, bir-birimizni topgan bo'lsak — ayt, Frida, unda qanday bo'ladi?

paras.en: Then I'm pursuing my cause just as I pursue yours; there's no difference here, and only an enemy can separate them. That holds everywhere, including as regards Hans. In judging the conversation with Hans, by the way, you greatly exaggerate in your delicacy of feeling; for if Hans's intentions and mine don't entirely coincide, it doesn't go so far that there's any opposition between them; besides, our disagreement hasn't remained hidden from Hans — if you believe it has, you would very much underestimate that cautious little man — and even if it should all have remained hidden from him, nobody will come to any harm from it; I hope so.'
paras.uz: Unda men o'z ishimni xuddi sening ishingdek olib boraman; bu yerda farq yo'q, ularni faqat dushman ajrata oladi. Bu hamma joyda, Hans borasida ham to'g'ri. Aytgancha, Hans bilan suhbatga baho berishda sen nozik tuyg'ung bilan juda mubolag'a qilyapsan, chunki agar Hansning va mening niyatlarim to'liq mos kelmasa ham, bu ular o'rtasida qandaydir qarama-qarshilik bor darajasiga bormaydi; bundan tashqari, kelishmovchiligimiz Hansdan yashirin qolmagan — agar shunday deb o'ylasang, bu ehtiyotkor kichkina odamni juda yengil baholagan bo'larding — va hatto hammasi undan yashirin qolgan bo'lsa ham, bundan hech kimga zarar yetmaydi, umid qilaman.»

paras.en: 'It's so hard to find one's way, K.,' said Frieda, sighing. 'I've certainly had no mistrust of you, and if anything of the kind has passed from the landlady to me, I'll throw it off joyfully and beg your forgiveness on my knees, as I really do all the time, even when I say such wicked things. But it remains true that you keep a lot secret from me; you come and go, I don't know where from or where to. That time when Hans knocked, you even called out the name Barnabas. If only you'd once called me as lovingly as you called that hated name then, for a reason I can't understand. If you have no trust in me, how can mistrust not arise in me? Then I'm wholly abandoned to the landlady, whom you seem to confirm by your behaviour. Not in everything — I won't claim that you confirm her in everything; didn't you, after all, drive the assistants away for my sake? Oh, if only you knew with what longing I look, in everything you do and say, even when it torments me, for a kernel that is good for me.' 'First of all, Frieda,' said K., 'I'm not hiding the slightest thing from you. How the landlady hates me, and how she strives to tear you away from me, and with what contemptible means she does it, and how you give in to her, Frieda, how you give in to her! Tell me, in what do I hide anything from you?
paras.uz: «Yo'lni topish shunchalik qiyin, K.», dedi Frida va xo'rsindi. «Menda senga nisbatan albatta ishonchsizlik bo'lmagan, agar shunga o'xshash narsa bekadan menga o'tgan bo'lsa, uni baxtiyorlik bilan uloqtirib tashlayman va sendan tiz cho'kib kechirim so'rayman — aslida qanchalik yomon gaplar aytsam ham, butun vaqt davomida shuni qilayapman. Lekin sen mendan ko'p narsani yashirishing haqiqatligicha qoladi; kelasan va ketasan, qayerdan va qayerga — bilmayman. O'shanda, Hans taqillatganida, sen hatto Barnabasning ismini chaqirding. Qaniydi meni bir marta o'shanda men tushunmaydigan sabab bilan o'sha nafratli ismni chaqirganingdek mehr bilan chaqirsang. Agar menga ishonmasang, menda qanday qilib ishonchsizlik paydo bo'lmasin; unda men butunlay bekaga topshirilgan bo'laman, sen esa xatti-harakating bilan uni tasdiqlayotgandek ko'rinasan. Hamma narsada emas, sen uni hamma narsada tasdiqlaysan demoqchi emasman; axir sen baribir men uchun yordamchilarni haydab yubormadingmi? Eh, qaniydi bilsang, men qilayotgan va aytayotgan har bir ishingda, hatto u meni qiynasa ham, men uchun yaxshi bo'lgan mag'izni qanday ishtiyoq bilan izlashimni.» «Avvalo, Frida, — dedi K., — men sendan zarracha ham narsani yashirmayman. Beka mendan qanchalik nafratlanishini, seni mendan tortib olish uchun qanchalik urinishini, buni qanday jirkanch vositalar bilan qilishini va sen unga qanday yon berishingni — Frida, qanday yon berishingni! Ayt-chi, men sendan nimani yashiraman?

paras.en: That I want to get to Klamm you know; that you can't help me to do it and that I must therefore achieve it on my own you know too; that I haven't yet succeeded you can see. Should I now humiliate myself doubly by recounting the useless attempts that already humiliate me amply in reality? Should I boast, perhaps, of having waited in vain a whole long afternoon, freezing at the door of Klamm's sledge? Happy not to have to think of such things any more, I hurry to you, and now all of it comes at me again, threateningly, from you. And Barnabas? Certainly, I'm expecting him. He is Klamm's messenger; it wasn't I who made him that.' 'Barnabas again!' cried Frieda. 'I can't believe he's a good messenger.' 'Perhaps you're right,' said K., 'but he is the only messenger sent to me.' 'All the worse,' said Frieda, 'all the more you should beware of him.' 'Unfortunately he hasn't given me any cause for that so far,' said K., smiling. 'He comes seldom, and what he brings is trivial; only the fact that it comes straight from Klamm makes it valuable.' 'But just look,' said Frieda, 'it isn't even Klamm who's your goal any more; perhaps that's what worries me most.
paras.uz: Klammga yetib bormoqchi ekanimni bilasan, bunda menga yordam bera olmasligingni va shuning uchun bunga o'z kuchim bilan erishishim kerakligini ham bilasan, hozirgacha uddalay olmaganimni ko'rib turibsan. Endi meni haqiqatda ham yetarlicha xo'rlaydigan befoyda urinishlarni hikoya qilib, o'zimni ikki baravar xo'rlashim kerakmi? Klammning chanasi eshigi oldida muzlab, uzun bir tushdan keyingi vaqtni behuda kutganim bilan maqtanishim kerakmi? Bunday narsalar haqida endi o'ylamasligimdan baxtiyor bo'lib, senga shoshilaman, endi esa bularning hammasi sendan yana tahdid bilan menga qarab keladi. Barnabas-chi? Albatta, men uni kutyapman. U Klammning choparidir; uni men chopar qilmaganman.» «Yana Barnabas! — qichqirdi Frida. — Uning yaxshi chopar ekaniga ishona olmayman.» «Balki haqdirsan, — dedi K., — lekin u menga yuboriladigan yagona chopar.» «Undan ham yomon, — dedi Frida, — undan shunchalik ko'proq ehtiyot bo'lishing kerak.» «Afsuski, u hozirgacha menga bunga sabab bermadi», dedi K. jilmayib. «U kam keladi, olib keladigani esa arzimas narsa; faqat to'g'ridan-to'g'ri Klammdan kelgani uni qimmatli qiladi.» «Lekin qara-ya, — dedi Frida, — endi hatto Klamm ham sening maqsading emas, balki meni eng ko'p shu bezovta qilayotgandir.

paras.en: That you always pushed past me towards Klamm was bad; that you now seem to be drifting away from Klamm is much worse; it's something not even the landlady foresaw. According to the landlady, my happiness — questionable and yet very real happiness — would end on the day you finally saw that your hope of Klamm was in vain. But now you're not even waiting for that day any more; suddenly a little boy comes in, and you start fighting with him over his mother as though you were fighting for the air you breathe.' 'You've understood my conversation with Hans correctly,' said K. 'That's really how it was. But has your whole former life sunk so far away for you (except for the landlady, of course, who won't let herself be pushed down with it) that you no longer know how one must fight to get on, especially when one comes from far below? How one must use everything that gives any hope at all? And this woman comes from the Castle — she told me so herself when I strayed into Lasemann's on the first day. What could be more natural than to ask her for advice or even for help? If the landlady knows exactly all the obstacles that keep one from Klamm, then this woman probably knows the way; after all, she came down it herself.' 'The way to Klamm?' asked Frieda. 'To Klamm, certainly — where else?' said K.
paras.uz: Sen doim mening ustimdan oshib Klammga intilganing yomon edi, endi Klammdan uzoqlashayotgandek ko'rinishing esa undan ham ancha yomon, bu hatto beka ham oldindan ko'rmagan narsa. Bekaning aytishicha, mening baxtim — shubhali, lekin juda haqiqiy baxt — sen Klammga bo'lgan umiding behuda ekanini nihoyat anglagan kuni tugashi kerak edi. Endi esa sen hatto o'sha kunni ham kutmayapsan; to'satdan kichkina bola kirib keladi va sen u bilan uning onasi uchun go'yo nafas oladigan havo uchun kurashgandek kurasha boshlaysan.» «Sen mening Hans bilan suhbatimni to'g'ri tushunding, — dedi K. — Haqiqatan ham shunday edi. Lekin nahotki butun avvalgi hayoting sen uchun shunchalik cho'kib ketgan bo'lsa (albatta, birga pastga itarib bo'lmaydigan bekadan tashqari), oldinga intilish uchun, ayniqsa juda pastdan kelgan bo'lsang, qanday kurashish kerakligini endi bilmasang? Qandaydir umid beradigan hamma narsadan qanday foydalanish kerakligini? Bu ayol esa Qasrdan keladi, buni birinchi kuni Lazemannikiga adashib kirganimda menga o'zi aytgan. Undan maslahat yoki hatto yordam so'rashdan tabiiyroq nima bo'lishi mumkin edi; agar beka Klammdan uzoqlashtiradigan barcha to'siqlarnigina aniq bilsa, bu ayol, ehtimol, yo'lni biladi, axir u o'sha yo'ldan o'zi tushib kelgan.» «Klammga olib boradigan yo'lnimi?» — so'radi Frida. «Klammga, albatta, yana qayerga», dedi K.

paras.en: Then he jumped up: 'But now it's high time to fetch the snack.' Urgently, far beyond what the occasion warranted, Frieda begged him to stay, as though only his staying would confirm all the comforting things he had said to her. But K. reminded her of the teacher, pointed to the door, which might burst open at any moment with a thunderclap, promised to come back at once; she needn't even light the stove, he would see to it himself. Finally Frieda gave in silently. When K. was tramping outside through the snow — the path should long since have been shovelled clear; strange how slowly the work was getting on — he saw one of the assistants at the railings, holding on, dead tired. Only one — where was the other? Had K. broken the endurance of at least one of them, then? The one who remained was still keen enough on the business, of course; that could be seen when, revived by the sight of K., he at once began more wildly stretching out his arms and rolling his eyes longingly. 'His unyieldingness is exemplary,' K. said to himself, and had to add, admittedly, 'one freezes to death with it at the railings.' Outwardly, however, K. had nothing for the assistant but a threatening fist, which ruled out any approach; indeed, the assistant anxiously moved back a considerable distance. Just then Frieda opened a window to air the room before lighting the stove, as had been agreed with K. At once the assistant left K. and crept, irresistibly drawn, towards the window.
paras.uz: Keyin u sakrab turdi: «Endi esa gazakni olib kelish vaqti allaqachon keldi.» Frida undan sababdan ancha ortiq darajada qolishini qattiq iltimos qildi, go'yo faqat uning qolishi unga aytgan barcha yupatuvchi gaplarini tasdiqlaydigandek. Lekin K. o'qituvchini eslatdi, har lahzada momaqaldiroq gumburlashi bilan ochilib ketishi mumkin bo'lgan eshikni ko'rsatdi, darhol qaytib kelishga ham va'da berdi, hatto pech yoqishi ham shart emas, buni uning o'zi qiladi. Nihoyat Frida indamay yon berdi. K. tashqarida qor kechib ketayotganida — yo'l allaqachon kurab tozalangan bo'lishi kerak edi, ish qanchalik sekin ketayotgani g'alati edi — panjara yonida yordamchilardan birining o'lguday charchab yopishib turganini ko'rdi. Faqat bittasi, ikkinchisi qayerda? Demak, K. hech bo'lmaganda bittasining chidamini sindirgan ekanmi? Qolgani, albatta, hali ham ishga yetarlicha g'ayratli edi; bu u K.ni ko'rib jonlanib, darhol qo'llarini yanada vahshiyona cho'zib, ko'zlarini sog'inch bilan aylantira boshlaganida ko'rindi. «Uning bo'ysunmasligi namunali», dedi o'ziga o'zi K. va, to'g'ri, qo'shib qo'yishga majbur bo'ldi: «u bilan panjara yonida muzlab o'lasan.» Lekin tashqi tomondan K.da yordamchi uchun har qanday yaqinlashishni istisno qiladigan musht bilan tahdid qilishdan boshqa hech narsa yo'q edi; ha, yordamchi qo'rqib, yana ancha joyga orqaga chekindi. Aynan shu payt Frida, K. bilan kelishilganidek, pech yoqishdan oldin shamollatish uchun derazani ochdi. Darhol yordamchi K.dan voz kechib, qarshi turib bo'lmas darajada tortilib, deraza tomon sudralib bordi.

paras.en: Her face distorted by friendliness towards the assistant and imploring helplessness towards K., she waved her hand a little from up at the window — it wasn't even clear whether it was a rebuff or a greeting — and the assistant wasn't deterred by it from coming closer. Then Frieda hastily shut the outer window, but stayed behind it, her hand on the catch, her head tilted to one side, with big eyes and a fixed smile. Did she know that she was attracting the assistant more than she was deterring him? But K. no longer looked back; he would rather hurry as much as possible and come back soon. At last — it was already dark, late afternoon — K. had cleared the garden path, piled the snow high on both sides of the path and beaten it firm, and was now finished with the day's work. He stood at the garden gate, alone for a wide distance around. He had driven the assistant away hours ago, chased him a long way; then the assistant had hidden somewhere between little gardens and huts and couldn't be found any more, and hadn't come out again since. Frieda was at home, and was either already washing the laundry or still washing Gisa's cat. It had been a sign of great trust on Gisa's part that she had handed this work over to Frieda — an unappetising and unsuitable job, admittedly, whose acceptance K. would certainly not have tolerated had it not been very advisable, after their various failures in duty, to use every opportunity of putting Gisa under an obligation to them.
paras.uz: Yordamchiga nisbatan iltifot va K.ga nisbatan iltijoli ojizlikdan yuzi buzilgan holda Frida derazadan qo'lini biroz silkitdi — bu rad etishmi yoki salommi, hatto aniq emas edi — yordamchi esa bundan yaqinlashishda chalg'imadi. Shunda Frida tashqi derazani shoshib yopdi, lekin uning orqasida qoldi — qo'li tutqichda, boshi bir tomonga egilgan, ko'zlari katta, qotib qolgan tabassum bilan. U bu bilan yordamchini cho'chitishdan ko'ra ko'proq jalb qilayotganini bilarmidi? Lekin K. endi orqasiga qaramadi, u iloji boricha shoshilib, tezroq qaytishni afzal ko'rdi. Nihoyat — allaqachon qorong'i, kech tushdan keyingi payt edi — K. bog' yo'lini tozalab, yo'lning ikki tomoniga qorni baland uyib, zichlab bosib bo'ldi va endi kunlik ishni tugatdi. U bog' darvozasi oldida, keng atrofda yolg'iz turardi. Yordamchini u soatlar oldin haydab, uzoq quvlagan edi; keyin yordamchi kichik bog'lar va kulbalar orasida qayergadir yashiringan, endi topib bo'lmagan va shundan beri qayta chiqmagan edi. Frida uyda edi va yo allaqachon kir yuvayotgan, yo hali ham Gizaning mushugini yuvayotgan edi; Giza bu ishni Fridaga topshirgani uning katta ishonchining belgisi edi — to'g'ri, bu ko'ngil aynitadigan va nomunosib ish edi; agar turli xizmat kamchiliklaridan keyin Gizani o'zlariga minnatdor qilish mumkin bo'lgan har bir imkoniyatdan foydalanish juda maqsadga muvofiq bo'lmaganida, K. bunga albatta yo'l qo'ymasdi.

paras.en: Gisa had watched with satisfaction as K. brought the little children's bathtub down from the attic, as water was warmed, and as finally the cat was carefully lifted into the tub. Then Gisa had even left the cat entirely to Frieda, for Schwarzer, K.'s acquaintance from the first evening, had come, had greeted K. with a mixture of shyness — the grounds for which had been laid that evening — and boundless contempt, such as was due to a caretaker, and had then gone off with Gisa into the other schoolroom. The two of them were still there. As K. had been told at the Bridge Inn, Schwarzer, though he was the son of a castellan, had long been living in the village for love of Gisa; through his connections he had got himself appointed assistant teacher by the community, but he exercised this office mainly by missing hardly a single one of Gisa's lessons, sitting either on a school bench among the children or, preferably, on the platform at Gisa's feet. It no longer bothered anyone; the children had long since got used to it, and perhaps all the more easily since Schwarzer had neither affection for nor understanding of children, hardly spoke to them, had taken over only the gymnastics lessons from Gisa and otherwise was content to live near Gisa, in her air, in her warmth. His greatest pleasure was to sit beside Gisa and correct exercise books.
paras.uz: Giza K. chordoqdan kichkina bolalar cho'milish tog'orasini olib tushganini, suv isitilganini va nihoyat mushukni ehtiyotkorlik bilan tog'oraga qanday ko'tarib qo'yishganini mamnuniyat bilan kuzatgan edi. Keyin Giza mushukni hatto butunlay Fridaga topshirib qo'ydi, chunki K.ning birinchi kechadagi tanishi Shvarser kelgan, K. bilan o'sha kechada asosi solingan tortinchoqlik va maktab qorovuliga munosib cheksiz nafrat aralash salomlashgan va keyin Giza bilan boshqa sinf xonasiga o'tib ketgan edi. Ular ikkalasi hamon o'sha yerda edi. «Ko'prik yonidagi» mehmonxonada K.ga aytib berishganidek, Shvarser, garchi kastelyanning o'g'li bo'lsa ham, Gizaga bo'lgan sevgisi tufayli allaqachon uzoq vaqtdan beri qishloqda yashardi; u o'z aloqalari orqali jamoa tomonidan yordamchi o'qituvchi etib tayinlanishiga erishgan, lekin bu lavozimni asosan Gizaning deyarli birorta darsini qoldirmaslik, yo bolalar orasida partada, yo — bunisini afzal ko'rardi — minbarda Gizaning oyoqlari ostida o'tirish tarzida bajarardi. Bu endi hech kimga xalaqit bermasdi, bolalar bunga allaqachon o'rganib qolishgan edi; ehtimol, bu yanada osonroq bo'lgandir, chunki Shvarserda bolalarga nisbatan na mehr, na tushunish bor edi, u ular bilan deyarli gaplashmas, Gizadan faqat gimnastika darsini olgan edi, qolgan jihatdan esa Gizaning yaqinida, uning havosida, uning iliqligida yashash bilan qanoatlanardi. Uning eng katta zavqi Gizaning yonida o'tirib, daftarlarni tekshirish edi.

paras.en: Today too they were busy with this; Schwarzer had brought a big pile of exercise books — the teacher always gave them his too — and as long as it had still been light K. had seen the two of them working at a little table by the window, head to head, motionless; now only two candles could be seen flickering there. It was a serious, silent love that bound the two; it was Gisa who set the tone, whose ponderous nature sometimes, it was true, grew wild and broke through all bounds, but who would never have tolerated anything similar in others at other times; so the lively Schwarzer too had to adapt himself, walk slowly, speak slowly, be silent a great deal; but he was richly rewarded for everything, one could see, by Gisa's simple, quiet presence. Yet perhaps Gisa didn't love him at all; at any rate her round grey eyes, which positively never blinked and seemed rather to rotate in their pupils, gave no answer to such questions; one saw only that she tolerated Schwarzer without objection, but she certainly didn't know how to appreciate the honour of being loved by a castellan's son, and she carried her full, opulent body along with unchanging calm, whether Schwarzer followed her with his eyes or not. Schwarzer, on the other hand, made her the constant sacrifice of staying in the village; messengers from his father, who often came to fetch him, he dismissed as indignantly as though even the brief reminder of the Castle and his duty as a son that they caused were a sensitive, irreparable disturbance of his happiness.
paras.uz: Bugun ham ular shu bilan band edilar; Shvarser katta bir dasta daftar olib kelgan edi — o'qituvchi ham ularga doim o'z daftarlarini berardi — va hali yorug' bo'lganida K. ikkalasining deraza yonidagi kichkina stolda bosh-boshga qo'yib, qimirlamay ishlayotganini ko'rgan edi; endi u yerda faqat ikkita sham lipillayotgani ko'rinardi. Ikkalasini bog'lab turgan bu jiddiy, jim sevgi edi; ohangni aynan Giza belgilardi — uning og'ir-vazmin tabiati, to'g'ri, ba'zan yovvoyilashib, barcha chegaralarni buzib o'tardi, lekin u boshqa paytda boshqalardagi shunga o'xshash narsaga hech qachon chidamasdi; shuning uchun jonli Shvarser ham bo'ysunishga — sekin yurishga, sekin gapirishga, ko'p jim turishga majbur edi; lekin buning hammasi uchun, ko'rinib turardiki, u Gizaning oddiy, jim borligi bilan mo'l-ko'l mukofotlanardi. Shu bilan birga, Giza uni umuman sevmasligi ham mumkin edi; har holda uning yumaloq, kulrang, rosmana hech qachon pirpiramaydigan, aksincha, qorachiqlarida aylanayotgandek ko'rinadigan ko'zlari bunday savollarga javob bermasdi; faqat u Shvarserga e'tirozsiz toqat qilishi ko'rinardi, lekin kastelyan o'g'li tomonidan sevilish sharafini u, albatta, qadrlay olmasdi va Shvarser uni nigohi bilan kuzatadimi-yo'qmi, o'zining to'la, barq urgan tanasini o'zgarmas xotirjamlik bilan olib yurardi. Shvarser esa aksincha, unga qishloqda qolishdek doimiy qurbonlik keltirardi; uni olib ketish uchun tez-tez keladigan otasining choparlarini u shunchalik g'azab bilan jo'natib yuborardiki, go'yo ular sabab bo'lgan Qasr va o'g'illik burchi haqidagi qisqa eslatmaning o'zi ham uning baxtiga sezilarli, o'rnini to'ldirib bo'lmaydigan xalaqitdek.

quiz.why_uz: Indinga, otasi Herrenhofga ketganda.

quiz.why_uz: Beka: K. Fridani Klamm bilan savdolashish uchun garov sifatida olgan.
