quiz.why_uz: Shvarser — kastelyan o'g'li, Gizani sevgani uchun qishloqda qolgan.

chapters.title: 13. Olga's secrets
chapters.recap_uz: K. Shvarser birinchi kechada uni idoralar e'tiboriga tushirganini o'ylaydi. Barnabas kelmagani uchun K. uning uyiga boradi. Amaliya K.ga Olga uni sevishini aytadi. Olga Barnabasning xizmati haqida gapirib beradi: unga rasmiy kiyim berilmagan, u idoralarda to'siqlardan o'ta olmaydi, unga Klamm deb ko'rsatilgan amaldor rostdan Klammmi — bunga ham shubha qiladi. Klammning qiyofasi har kim uchun turlicha ekan. Xatlarni Barnabas kotibdan oladi; ular eski va kechikkan xatlar.

paras.en: And yet he actually had plenty of free time, for Gisa generally showed herself to him only during lessons and when correcting exercise books — not out of calculation, of course, but because she loved comfort, and therefore solitude, above everything, and was probably happiest when she could stretch out at home on the sofa in complete freedom, the cat beside her, which didn't disturb her because it could hardly move any more. So Schwarzer loafed about for a large part of the day with nothing to do; but he liked that too, for it always gave him the opportunity — which he very often took — of going to Lion Lane, where Gisa lived, climbing up to her little attic room, listening at the always locked door and then hurrying away again, having established without exception the most perfect, incomprehensible silence in the room. All the same, the consequences of this way of life showed themselves in him too at times — but never in Gisa's presence — in ridiculous outbursts of an official arrogance momentarily reawakened, which suited his present position badly enough; it usually didn't end very well, as K. too had experienced.
paras.uz: Shunga qaramay, aslida uning bo'sh vaqti mo'l edi, chunki Giza unga umuman faqat dars paytida va daftar tekshirayotganda ko'rinardi — bu, albatta, hisob-kitobdan emas, balki u hamma narsadan ko'ra qulaylikni, shuning uchun yolg'izlikni sevgani uchun edi va, ehtimol, uyda, butunlay erkin holda kanapeda cho'zilib yotganida, yonida deyarli qimirlay olmagani uchun xalaqit bermaydigan mushuk bilan eng baxtiyor bo'lardi. Shunday qilib, Shvarser kunning katta qismini ishsiz daydib o'tkazardi, lekin bu ham unga yoqardi, chunki bunda doim — undan juda tez-tez foydalanardi ham — Giza yashaydigan Arslon ko'chasiga borib, uning chordoqdagi kichkina xonasiga ko'tarilib, doim qulflangan eshikka quloq solish, keyin xonada istisnosiz eng mukammal, tushunib bo'lmas sukunatni aniqlagach, shoshib yana ketib qolish imkoniyati bor edi. Shunday bo'lsa ham, bu turmush tarzining oqibatlari unda ham ba'zan — lekin hech qachon Giza huzurida emas — bir lahzaga qayta uyg'ongan rasmiy kibrning kulgili portlashlarida namoyon bo'lardi; bu, albatta, uning hozirgi mavqeiga yetarlicha yomon mos kelardi; odatda bu unchalik yaxshi tugamasdi, K. ham buni boshidan kechirganidek.

paras.en: The only astonishing thing was that people — at the Bridge Inn at least — nevertheless spoke of Schwarzer with a certain respect, even when it concerned things more ridiculous than respectable; Gisa too was included in this respect. Yet Schwarzer was wrong if, as assistant teacher, he believed himself extraordinarily superior to K.; this superiority did not exist. For the teaching staff, and especially for a teacher of Schwarzer's sort, a caretaker is a very important person, whom one may not disregard with impunity, and whose disregard, if one cannot give it up for reasons of rank, one must at least make bearable with a suitable return. K. meant to remember this when the occasion arose; besides, Schwarzer was still in his debt from the first evening, and the debt had not become smaller because the following days had in fact proved Schwarzer's reception right. For one must not forget that this reception had perhaps set the direction for everything that followed. Through Schwarzer, quite absurdly, the full attention of the authorities had been directed at K. in the very first hour, when he, still a complete stranger in the village, without acquaintances, without refuge, exhausted from the march, quite helpless as he lay there on the straw mattress, was at the mercy of any official intervention.
paras.uz: Hayratlanarli tomoni faqat shunda ediki, hech bo'lmaganda «Ko'prik yonidagi» mehmonxonada Shvarser haqida, hatto gap hurmatga loyiqdan ko'ra kulgiliroq narsalar haqida bo'lsa ham, baribir qandaydir hurmat bilan gapirishardi; bu hurmatga Giza ham kirardi. Lekin Shvarser yordamchi o'qituvchi sifatida K.dan nihoyatda ustun deb hisoblasa, bu noto'g'ri edi, bunday ustunlik yo'q edi; o'qituvchilar uchun, ayniqsa Shvarser kabi o'qituvchi uchun maktab qorovuli juda muhim shaxs — uni jazosiz mensimaslik mumkin emas, agar mavqe manfaatlari tufayli mensimaslikdan voz kecha olmasang, hech bo'lmaganda unga munosib javob qaytarish bilan buni chidasa bo'ladigan qilish kerak. K. fursat kelganda buni yodda tutmoqchi edi; bundan tashqari, Shvarser birinchi kechadan beri unga qarzdor edi va keyingi kunlar Shvarserning o'shandagi qarshi olishiga aslida haq bergani bilan bu qarz kamaymagan edi. Chunki bunda unutmaslik kerak ediki, o'sha qarshi olish, ehtimol, keyingi hamma narsaga yo'nalish bergan edi. Shvarser tufayli mutlaqo bema'ni ravishda birinchi soatdayoq idoralarning to'liq e'tibori K.ga qaratilgan edi — u hali qishloqda butunlay begona, tanishsiz, boshpanasiz, yo'ldan holdan toygan, somon to'shakda butunlay ojiz yotgan holda har qanday rasmiy aralashuvga qaram edi.

paras.en: Only one night later everything might have gone differently, quietly, half in concealment; at any rate nobody would have known anything about him or had any suspicion; at least they wouldn't have hesitated to let him stay a day as a journeyman; people would have seen how useful and reliable he was, word would have gone round the neighbourhood, and he would probably soon have found a place somewhere as a farmhand. Of course the authorities would have found out. But there was an essential difference between the central office, or whoever had been at the telephone, being shaken awake in the middle of the night on his account and an immediate decision being demanded — demanded with apparent humility but with tiresome relentlessness, and moreover by Schwarzer, who was probably disliked up there — and, instead of all that, K. knocking on the mayor's door the next day during office hours and, as was proper, reporting himself as a travelling journeyman who already had a place to sleep with a particular member of the community and would probably move on again tomorrow — unless the quite improbable case occurred and he found work here, only for a few days, of course, for he certainly didn't want to stay longer. That, or something like it, is how it would have been without Schwarzer. The authorities would still have concerned themselves with the matter, but calmly, through official channels, undisturbed by the impatience of the party concerned, which they probably particularly hated.
paras.uz: Faqat bir kecha keyin hammasi boshqacha, tinch, yarim yashirin o'tishi mumkin edi; har holda hech kim u haqda hech narsa bilmagan, shubha qilmagan, hech bo'lmaganda uni sargardon hunarmand sifatida bir kun o'zinikida qoldirishdan ikkilanmagan bo'lardi; uning foydali va ishonchli ekanini ko'rishardi, bu qo'ni-qo'shnilar orasida tarqalardi, ehtimol, u tez orada qayerdadir xizmatkor sifatida joy topgan bo'lardi. Albatta, idora buni payqamay qolmasdi. Lekin uning tufayli yarim tunda markaziy idora yoki telefon yonida kim bo'lsa, o'shani uyg'otib, zudlik bilan qaror talab qilinishi — zohiran kamtarlik bilan, lekin baribir zerikarli qat'iylik bilan, buning ustiga, ehtimol, tepada yoqtirilmaydigan Shvarser tomonidan talab qilinishi — bilan, buning o'rniga K. ertasi kuni ish soatlarida oqsoqolning eshigini taqillatib, munosib tarzda, ma'lum bir jamoa a'zosinikida allaqachon yotoq joyi bor va, ehtimol, ertaga yana yo'lga tushadigan begona sargardon hunarmand sifatida o'zini ro'yxatdan o'tkazishi o'rtasida muhim farq bor edi — agar mutlaqo ehtimoldan yiroq holat yuz berib, u bu yerda ish topmasa, albatta, faqat bir necha kunga, chunki u bundan ortiq qolishni aslo istamaydi. Shvarsersiz shunday yoki shunga o'xshash bo'lardi. Idora ham bu ish bilan baribir shug'ullanardi, lekin xotirjam, rasmiy yo'l bilan, ariza beruvchining unga, ehtimol, ayniqsa yoqmaydigan sabrsizligidan xalaqitsiz.

paras.en: Now K. was innocent of all this; the fault lay with Schwarzer; but Schwarzer was the son of a castellan, and outwardly he had behaved correctly, so it could only be made to recoil on K. And the ridiculous cause of it all? Perhaps an ungracious mood of Gisa's that day, because of which Schwarzer had roamed about sleepless in the night, and had then compensated himself for his sorrow at K.'s expense. From another side, of course, one could also say that K. owed a great deal to this behaviour of Schwarzer's. Only through it had something become possible which K. alone would never have achieved, never have dared to achieve, and which the authorities for their part would hardly ever have admitted: namely, that from the very beginning, without subterfuge, openly, eye to eye, he had confronted the authorities, as far as that was possible with them at all. But it was a bad gift; it spared K. much lying and secrecy, but it also made him almost defenceless, at any rate put him at a disadvantage in the fight, and might have driven him to despair in view of that, had he not had to tell himself that the difference in power between the authorities and himself was so monstrous that all the lies and cunning he might have been capable of could not have reduced the difference significantly in his favour.
paras.uz: Bularning hech birida K. aybdor emas edi, ayb Shvarserda edi, lekin Shvarser kastelyanning o'g'li edi va tashqi tomondan to'g'ri yo'l tutgan edi, demak, buning javobini faqat K.ga to'latish mumkin edi. Bularning hammasining kulgili sababi-chi? Balki o'sha kuni Gizaning noxush kayfiyati bo'lgandir, shu tufayli Shvarser tunda uyqusiz kezib yurib, keyin o'z dardining alamini K.dan olgandir. To'g'ri, boshqa tomondan, K. Shvarserning bu xatti-harakatiga ko'p narsa uchun qarzdor, deb ham aytish mumkin edi. Faqat shu tufayli K. yolg'iz o'zi hech qachon erisha olmaydigan, erishishga hech qachon jur'at etmaydigan va idora ham o'z navbatida deyarli hech qachon tan olmaydigan narsa mumkin bo'ldi: ya'ni u boshidanoq, hiyla-nayrangsiz, ochiq, ko'zma-ko'z — bu idora bilan umuman mumkin bo'lgan darajada — idoraga qarshi chiqdi. Lekin bu yomon sovg'a edi: u K.ni ko'p yolg'on va yashirinlikdan qutqardi, lekin uni deyarli himoyasiz ham qildi, har holda kurashda noqulay ahvolga soldi va agar u idora bilan o'zi o'rtasidagi kuch farqi shunchalik dahshatli ekanini, qodir bo'lgan barcha yolg'on va hiylalar bu farqni uning foydasiga sezilarli kamaytira olmasligini o'ziga aytishga majbur bo'lmaganida, uni bu jihatdan umidsizlikka solishi mumkin edi.

paras.en: But this was only a thought with which K. comforted himself; Schwarzer remained in his debt nevertheless. If he had harmed K. then, perhaps he could help next time; K. would go on needing help in the very smallest things, in the very first preconditions — so, for example, Barnabas seemed to be failing again.
paras.uz: Lekin bu K. o'zini yupatgan fikrgina edi; Shvarser baribir unga qarzdor bo'lib qolaverdi; agar o'shanda K.ga zarar yetkazgan bo'lsa, balki keyingi safar yordam bera olar; K.ga bundan keyin ham eng arzimas narsalarda, eng dastlabki shart-sharoitlarda yordam kerak bo'lardi — masalan, Barnabas ham yana muvaffaqiyatsizlikka uchrayotgandek edi.

paras.en: Because of Frieda K. had hesitated all day to go and ask at Barnabas's home; so as not to have to receive him in front of Frieda, he had now worked outside and had stayed on here after work, waiting for Barnabas; but Barnabas did not come. Now there was nothing for it but to go to the sisters — only for a short while; he would ask only from the threshold and would soon be back. And he rammed the shovel into the snow and ran. He arrived breathless at Barnabas's house, flung open the door after a short knock and asked, without noticing what the room looked like: 'Hasn't Barnabas come yet?' Only now did he notice that Olga wasn't there, that the two old people were again sitting at the distant table in a twilight state, had not yet grasped what had happened at the door and were only slowly turning their faces round, and finally that Amalia was lying under blankets on the stove bench and, in her first fright at K.'s appearance, had started up and was holding her hand to her forehead to collect herself. Had Olga been here she would have answered at once and K. could have left again; as it was, he had at least to take the few steps to Amalia, give her his hand, which she pressed in silence, and ask her to keep the startled parents from any wanderings about — which she did with a few words.
paras.uz: Frida tufayli K. kun bo'yi Barnabasning uyiga borib so'rashdan ikkilangan edi; uni Fridaning oldida qabul qilishga majbur bo'lmaslik uchun hozir tashqarida ishlagan va ishdan keyin ham Barnabasni kutib shu yerda qolgan edi, lekin Barnabas kelmadi. Endi opa-singillarnikiga borishdan boshqa chora qolmadi — faqat bir oz muddatga, faqat ostonadan so'ramoqchi edi, tez orada qaytib keladi. U kurakni qorga sanchdi va yugurdi. Nafasi bo'g'zida Barnabasning uyiga yetib keldi, qisqa taqillatgandan keyin eshikni lang ochib, xonaning ko'rinishiga e'tibor bermay so'radi: «Barnabas hali ham kelmadimi?» Faqat endi u Olga yo'qligini, ikki qariya yana uzoqdagi stol yonida g'ira-shira holatda o'tirganini, eshikda nima bo'lganini hali tushunib yetmay, yuzlarini endigina sekin burayotganini va nihoyat Amaliya pech yonidagi supada adyollar ostida yotganini, K. paydo bo'lganidan dastlabki qo'rquvda sapchib turib, o'zini yig'ish uchun qo'lini peshonasiga tutganini payqadi. Agar Olga shu yerda bo'lganida, darhol javob bergan bo'lardi va K. yana ketishi mumkin edi; endi esa u hech bo'lmaganda Amaliyaga qarab bir necha qadam tashlab, unga qo'l berishi — u indamay siqdi — va cho'chib ketgan ota-onani har qanday kezishdan to'xtatishini so'rashi kerak edi; u buni bir necha so'z bilan qildi ham.

paras.en: K. learned that Olga was chopping wood in the yard, that Amalia, exhausted — she gave no reason — had had to lie down a little while ago, and that Barnabas had not yet come, it was true, but must come very soon, for he never stayed overnight at the Castle. K. thanked her for the information; he could now go again; but Amalia asked whether he didn't want to wait for Olga; but unfortunately he had no more time. Then Amalia asked whether he had already spoken to Olga today; he said no, surprised, and asked whether Olga had wanted to tell him something in particular. Amalia twisted her mouth as if slightly annoyed, nodded to K. in silence — it was clearly a dismissal — and lay back again. From her reclining position she scrutinised him, as though surprised that he was still there. Her gaze was cold, clear, motionless as always; it was not directed precisely at what she was observing but went — and this was disconcerting — a little, hardly noticeably, but unmistakably, past it; it seemed to be caused not by weakness, not by embarrassment, not by insincerity, but by a constant longing for solitude, superior to every other feeling, which perhaps came to her own consciousness only in this way.
paras.uz: K. Olga hovlida o'tin yorayotganini, Amaliya holdan toyib — sababini aytmadi — yaqinda yotib olishga majbur bo'lganini, Barnabas esa hali kelmagan, lekin juda tez orada kelishi kerakligini bilib oldi, chunki u hech qachon Qasrda tunab qolmasdi. K. ma'lumot uchun minnatdorchilik bildirdi, endi yana ketishi mumkin edi, lekin Amaliya Olgani kutmoqchi emasmi, deb so'radi; lekin afsuski, uning vaqti qolmagan edi. Keyin Amaliya u bugun Olga bilan gaplashganmi, deb so'radi; u hayron bo'lib, yo'q dedi va Olga unga biror alohida narsa aytmoqchimidi, deb so'radi. Amaliya go'yo biroz g'ashlangandek og'zini qiyshaytirdi, K.ga indamay bosh irg'adi — bu aniq xayrlashuv edi — va yana yotdi. U yotgan joyidan uni go'yo hali ham shu yerdaligidan hayron bo'lgandek ko'zdan kechirdi. Uning nigohi doimgidek sovuq, tiniq, qimirlamas edi; u kuzatayotgan narsaga to'ppa-to'g'ri qaratilmagan, balki — bu bezovta qiladigan edi — biroz, deyarli sezilmas, lekin shubhasiz uning yonidan o'tib ketardi; bunga zaiflik ham, xijolat ham, nosamimiylik ham sabab emasdek, balki har qanday boshqa tuyg'udan ustun turuvchi doimiy yolg'izlik istagi sababdek edi — balki uning o'zi ham buni faqat shu tarzda anglardi.

paras.en: K. thought he remembered that this gaze had already occupied him on the first evening; indeed, that probably the whole ugly impression this family had made on him at once went back to this gaze, which in itself was not ugly, but proud, and sincere in its reserve. 'You're always so sad, Amalia,' said K. 'Is something tormenting you? Can't you say it? I've never seen a country girl like you. Only today, only now, has it really struck me. Do you come from the village here? Were you born here?' Amalia said yes, as though K. had asked only the last question; then she said: 'So you'll wait for Olga after all?' 'I don't know why you keep asking the same thing,' said K. 'I can't stay longer, because my fiancée is waiting at home.'
paras.uz: K.ga bu nigoh birinchi kechadayoq uni o'ylantirgandek, ha, ehtimol, bu oila unda darhol qoldirgan butun xunuk taassurot o'z-o'zidan xunuk emas, balki mag'rur va yopiqligida samimiy bo'lgan shu nigohga borib taqalgandek tuyuldi. «Sen doim shunchalik g'amginsan, Amaliya, — dedi K., — seni biror narsa qiynayaptimi? Aytib bera olmaysanmi? Men senga o'xshagan qishloq qizini hali ko'rmaganman. Faqat bugun, faqat hozir buni aslida payqadim. Sen shu qishloqdanmisan? Shu yerda tug'ilganmisan?» Amaliya go'yo K. faqat oxirgi savolni bergandek ha, dedi, keyin dedi: «Demak, baribir Olgani kutasanmi?» «Nega doim bir narsani so'rayotganingni bilmayman, — dedi K. — Men uzoqroq qola olmayman, chunki uyda qallig'im kutyapti.»

paras.en: Amalia propped herself on her elbow; she knew of no fiancée. K. named the name. Amalia didn't know her. She asked whether Olga knew of the engagement; K. thought she probably did — Olga had seen him with Frieda, after all, and such news spreads quickly in the village. But Amalia assured him that Olga didn't know, and that it would make her very unhappy, for she seemed to love K. She hadn't spoken of it openly, for she was very reserved, but love betrays itself involuntarily. K. was convinced that Amalia was mistaken. Amalia smiled, and this smile, though it was sad, lit up the gloomily contracted face, made the muteness speak, made the strangeness familiar; it was the yielding up of a secret, the yielding up of a possession guarded until now, which could indeed be taken back again, but never entirely. Amalia said she was certainly not mistaken; indeed, she knew more: she knew that K. too had a liking for Olga, and that his visits, which had some message or other from Barnabas as their pretext, were in reality meant only for Olga. But now that Amalia knew all about it, he needn't be so strict about it any more and might come more often. That was all she had wanted to tell him. K. shook his head and reminded her of his engagement.
paras.uz: Amaliya tirsagiga tayandi, u hech qanday qallig'dan bexabar edi. K. ismini aytdi. Amaliya uni tanimasdi. U Olga unashtiruv haqida biladimi, deb so'radi; K. bilsa kerak, deb o'yladi, axir Olga uni Frida bilan ko'rgan, qishloqda bunday xabarlar tez tarqaladi. Lekin Amaliya uni Olga bilmasligiga va bu uni juda baxtsiz qilishiga ishontirdi, chunki u K.ni sevadiganga o'xshaydi. U bu haqda ochiq gapirmagan, chunki u juda o'zini tutadi, lekin sevgi beixtiyor o'zini oshkor qiladi. K. Amaliya adashayotganiga amin edi. Amaliya jilmaydi va bu tabassum g'amgin bo'lsa ham, qovog'i solingan yuzni yoritdi, sukutni gapirtirdi, begonalikni yaqin qildi; bu sirni oshkor qilish, hozirgacha qo'riqlab kelingan boylikni oshkor qilish edi — uni, to'g'ri, yana qaytarib olish mumkin edi, lekin hech qachon butunlay emas. Amaliya albatta adashmayotganini aytdi; ha, u bundan ham ko'proq narsani biladi: K. ham Olgaga moyil ekanini va Barnabasning qandaydir xabarlarini bahona qilgan tashriflari aslida faqat Olgaga qaratilganini biladi. Lekin endi Amaliya hammasidan xabardor bo'lgani uchun, u buni bunchalik qattiq olmasligi va tez-tez kelishi mumkin. U unga faqat shuni aytmoqchi edi. K. bosh chayqadi va unashtiruvini eslatdi.

paras.en: Amalia didn't seem to waste many thoughts on this engagement; the immediate impression of K., who alone was standing before her, was decisive for her. She only asked when K. had got to know that girl; after all, he had been in the village only a few days. K. told her about the evening at the Herrenhof, whereupon Amalia only said shortly that she had been very much against his being taken to the Herrenhof. She called Olga as a witness to this too, who was just coming in with an armful of wood, fresh and stung by the cold air, lively and strong, as if transformed by the work compared with her usual heavy way of standing about in the room. She threw down the wood, greeted K. without embarrassment and asked at once after Frieda. K. exchanged a glance with Amalia, but she did not seem to consider herself refuted. A little irritated by this, K. talked about Frieda in more detail than he otherwise would have, described under what difficult conditions she was nevertheless keeping house of a sort at the school, and in the haste of his telling — he did want to go home at once — so forgot himself that, by way of farewell, he invited the sisters to visit him some time. Now, of course, he took fright and stopped short, while Amalia at once, without leaving him time for another word, declared that she accepted the invitation; now Olga had to join in too, and did so.
paras.uz: Amaliya bu unashtiruvga ko'p fikr sarflamayotgandek edi; uning oldida yolg'iz turgan K.ning bevosita taassuroti u uchun hal qiluvchi edi; u faqat K. o'sha qiz bilan qachon tanishganini so'radi, axir u qishloqda bor-yo'g'i bir necha kundan beri. K. Herrenhofdagi kechani aytib berdi, shunda Amaliya qisqagina: uni Herrenhofga olib borishlariga juda qarshi bo'lganini aytdi. Buning guvohi sifatida u endigina bir quchoq o'tin bilan kirib kelgan Olgani ham chaqirdi — u sovuq havodan tetik va yuzi qizargan, jonli va baquvvat, xonada odatdagidek og'ir turishiga nisbatan ish tufayli go'yo o'zgarib qolgan edi. U o'tinni tashladi, K. bilan tortinmay salomlashdi va darhol Fridani so'radi. K. Amaliya bilan nigoh almashdi, lekin u o'zini rad etilgan deb hisoblamayotgandek edi. Bundan biroz g'ashlangan K. Frida haqida odatdagidan batafsilroq gapirib berdi, u maktabda qanday og'ir sharoitda baribir qandaydir xo'jalik yuritayotganini tasvirladi va hikoya qilish shoshilinchida — axir u darhol uyga ketmoqchi edi — o'zini shunchalik unutdiki, xayrlashuv tariqasida opa-singillarni bir kun mehmonga kelishga taklif qildi. Endi, albatta, u cho'chib, to'xtab qoldi, Amaliya esa unga boshqa bir so'z aytishga vaqt qoldirmay, darhol taklifni qabul qilishini aytdi; endi Olga ham qo'shilishi kerak edi va qo'shildi.

paras.en: But K., constantly pressed by thoughts of the need for a hasty leave-taking, and feeling uneasy under Amalia's gaze, didn't hesitate to admit without further ornament that the invitation had been completely unconsidered and prompted only by his personal feeling, but that unfortunately he couldn't uphold it, since there was a great enmity — to him, admittedly, quite incomprehensible — between Frieda and the Barnabas household. 'It isn't enmity,' said Amalia, getting up from the bench and throwing the blanket behind her, 'it isn't such a great thing as that; it's merely parroting public opinion. And now go, go to your fiancée — I can see how you're in a hurry. And don't be afraid that we'll come; I only said it at first as a joke, out of malice. But you can come to us more often; there's no obstacle to that, I should think; you can always use Barnabas's messages as a pretext. I'll make it easier for you still by saying that Barnabas, even if he brings a message from the Castle for you, can't go all the way to the school again to deliver it to you. He can't run about so much, the poor boy; he's wearing himself out in the service; you'll have to come yourself to fetch the news.' K. had never heard Amalia say so much at a stretch; it sounded different from her usual speech, too; there was a kind of loftiness in it, which not only K. felt but evidently also Olga, the sister who was used to her.
paras.uz: Lekin tez xayrlashish zarurligi haqidagi o'ylar to'xtovsiz qistayotgan va Amaliyaning nigohi ostida o'zini noqulay his qilgan K. hech qanday bezaksiz taklif mutlaqo o'ylanmagan va faqat shaxsiy tuyg'usidan kelib chiqqanini, lekin afsuski, uni saqlab qola olmasligini tan olishdan ikkilanmadi, chunki Frida bilan Barnabas xonadoni o'rtasida katta — to'g'ri, unga butunlay tushunarsiz — adovat bor. «Bu adovat emas, — dedi Amaliya, supadan turib, adyolni orqasiga tashlab, — bu unchalik katta narsa emas, bu shunchaki umumiy fikrni to'tidek takrorlash. Endi esa ket, qallig'ingning oldiga ket, qanday shoshilayotganingni ko'ryapman. Biz kelamiz deb qo'rqma ham, men buni boshida faqat hazil, yomonlik bilan aytdim. Sen esa bizga tez-tez kelishing mumkin, bunga hech qanday to'siq bo'lmasa kerak, axir har doim Barnabasning xabarlarini bahona qilishing mumkin. Men buni senga yana ham osonlashtiraman: aytamanki, Barnabas senga Qasrdan xabar olib kelsa ham, uni senga yetkazish uchun yana maktabgacha bora olmaydi. U bunchalik ko'p yugura olmaydi, bechora bola, xizmatda o'zini yeb bitiryapti, xabarni olish uchun o'zing kelishingga to'g'ri keladi.» K. Amaliyaning hech qachon bunchalik ko'p gapni bir yo'la aytganini eshitmagan edi, bu uning odatdagi nutqidan boshqacha ham eshitildi, unda qandaydir ulug'vorlik bor edi — buni nafaqat K., balki, aftidan, unga o'rganib qolgan singlisi Olga ham his qildi.

paras.en: She stood a little apart, hands in her lap, again in her usual broad-legged, slightly stooping posture; her eyes were turned on Amalia, while Amalia looked only at K. 'It's a mistake,' said K., 'a great mistake, if you believe I'm not serious about waiting for Barnabas. To put my affairs with the authorities in order is my highest, really my only wish. And Barnabas is to help me with it; much of my hope rests on him. True, he has already disappointed me very much once; but that was more my own fault than his; it happened in the confusion of the first hours; I believed then that I could achieve everything through a little evening walk, and then I held it against him that the impossible had proved impossible. It even influenced my judgement of your family, of you. That's over; I think I understand you better now; you are even …' K. searched for the right word, didn't find it at once and contented himself with a casual — 'you are perhaps more good-natured than anyone else among the village people, as far as I know them so far. But now, Amalia, you confuse me again by belittling — if not your brother's service, then at least the importance it has for me.
paras.uz: U biroz chetroqda, qo'llarini tizzasiga qo'yib, yana odatdagi oyoqlarini kerib, biroz engashgan holatida turardi; ko'zlari Amaliyaga qaratilgan edi, Amaliya esa faqat K.ga qarardi. «Bu xato, — dedi K., — agar men Barnabasni kutishga jiddiy qaramayman deb o'ylasang, bu katta xato. Idoralar bilan ishlarimni tartibga keltirish — mening eng oliy, aslida yagona istagim. Barnabas esa bunda menga yordam berishi kerak, umidimning ko'p qismi unga bog'liq. To'g'ri, u bir marta meni qattiq hafsalamni pir qilgan; lekin bu uning aybidan ko'ra ko'proq mening aybim edi, bu dastlabki soatlarning sarosimasida bo'lgan edi; o'shanda men hamma narsaga kichik bir kechki sayr bilan erisha olaman deb o'ylagan edim va keyin imkonsiz narsa imkonsiz bo'lib chiqqani uchun undan xafa bo'ldim. Bu hatto sizlarning oilangiz, sizlar haqidagi fikrimga ham ta'sir qildi. Bu o'tib ketdi, endi sizlarni yaxshiroq tushunaman deb o'ylayman, sizlar hatto…» K. to'g'ri so'zni izladi, darhol topa olmadi va o'tkinchi: «sizlar, balki, men hozirgacha bilgan qishloq odamlari orasida hammadan ko'ra mehribonroqdirsizlar», degan so'z bilan qanoatlandi. «Lekin endi, Amaliya, sen meni yana chalg'ityapsan — akangning xizmatini bo'lmasa ham, uning men uchun ahamiyatini kamsityapsan.

paras.en: Perhaps you're not initiated into Barnabas's affairs — then all is well, and I'll let the matter rest; but perhaps you are initiated — and that's rather my impression — and then it's bad, for that would mean that your brother is deceiving me.' 'Don't worry,' said Amalia, 'I'm not initiated; nothing could induce me to let myself be initiated, nothing could induce me — not even consideration for you, for whom I'd do a good deal, for, as you said, we are good-natured. But my brother's affairs belong to him; I know nothing of them except what I happen to hear here and there against my will. Olga, on the other hand, can give you full information, for she is his confidante.' And Amalia went away, first to her parents, with whom she whispered, then into the kitchen; she had gone without saying goodbye to K., as though she knew he would stay a long time yet and no farewell was needed. K. stayed behind with a somewhat astonished face; Olga laughed at him and drew him to the stove bench; she really seemed happy that she could now sit here alone with him, but it was a peaceful happiness, certainly not clouded by jealousy. And precisely this absence of jealousy, and hence of any severity, did K. good; he liked looking into these blue eyes, not alluring, not domineering, but shyly resting, shyly holding firm.
paras.uz: Balki sen Barnabasning ishlaridan voqif emassan — unda yaxshi, men bu ishni o'z holiga qo'yaman; lekin balki voqifsan — menda ko'proq shunday taassurot bor — unda yomon, chunki bu akang meni aldayapti, degani bo'lardi.» «Xotirjam bo'l, — dedi Amaliya, — men voqif emasman, hech narsa meni voqif bo'lishga undashi mumkin emas, hech narsa — hatto senga bo'lgan e'tibor ham, garchi sen uchun ko'p narsa qilgan bo'lsam ham, chunki o'zing aytganingdek, biz mehribonmiz. Lekin akamning ishlari unga tegishli, men ular haqida faqat istamagan holda tasodifan u yerda-bu yerda eshitganlarimnigina bilaman. Olga esa senga to'liq ma'lumot bera oladi, chunki u uning sirdoshi.» Va Amaliya ketdi — avval ota-onasining oldiga borib, ular bilan pichirlashdi, keyin oshxonaga; u K. bilan xayrlashmay ketdi, go'yo u hali uzoq qolishini va xayrlashuvga hojat yo'qligini bilgandek. K. biroz hayron yuz bilan qoldi, Olga uning ustidan kulib, uni pech yonidagi supaga tortdi; u endi K. bilan shu yerda yolg'iz o'tira olganidan rostdan ham baxtiyordek edi, lekin bu osoyishta baxt edi, rashk bilan, albatta, xiralashmagan edi. Aynan shu rashkdan, demak, har qanday qattiqlikdan yiroqlik K.ga yoqdi; u bu zangori, jalb qilmaydigan, hukmronlik qilmaydigan, balki uyalib tinch turadigan, uyalib bardosh beradigan ko'zlarga bajonidil qaradi.

paras.en: It was as though the warnings of Frieda and the landlady had made him not more susceptible to all this, but more attentive and more resourceful. And he laughed with Olga when she wondered why he had called Amalia, of all people, good-natured; Amalia was many things, but good-natured she really wasn't. Whereupon K. explained that the praise had of course been meant for her, Olga, but Amalia was so domineering that she not only appropriated everything said in her presence, but that people also voluntarily allotted everything to her. 'That's true,' said Olga, growing more serious, 'truer than you think. Amalia is younger than I, younger than Barnabas too, but it's she who decides in the family, for good and for ill; of course, she also bears it more than all of us, the good as well as the ill.' K. thought this exaggerated; Amalia had just said, after all, that she didn't concern herself with her brother's affairs, for instance, whereas Olga knew everything about them. 'How shall I explain it?' said Olga. 'Amalia doesn't concern herself either with Barnabas or with me; she really doesn't concern herself with anyone except our parents; she looks after them day and night; just now she asked again what they wanted and has gone into the kitchen to cook for them; she forced herself to get up for their sake, for she's been ill since midday and was lying here on the bench.
paras.uz: Go'yo Frida va bekaning ogohlantirishlari uni bularning hammasiga moyilroq emas, balki diqqatliroq va topqirroq qilgandek edi. Va Olga nega u aynan Amaliyani mehribon deb ataganidan hayron bo'lganida, u Olga bilan birga kuldi: Amaliya ko'p narsa, lekin mehribon emas. Shunda K. maqtov, albatta, unga — Olgaga qaratilganini, lekin Amaliya shunchalik hukmronki, nafaqat uning huzurida aytilgan hamma narsani o'ziga oladi, balki unga hamma narsani o'z ixtiyori bilan ham beradilar, deb tushuntirdi. «Bu to'g'ri, — dedi Olga jiddiylashib, — sen o'ylagandan ham to'g'riroq. Amaliya mendan kichik, Barnabasdan ham kichik, lekin oilada yaxshilikda ham, yomonlikda ham u hal qiladi; to'g'ri, u buni hammadan ko'proq ko'taradi ham — yaxshisini ham, yomonini ham.» K. buni mubolag'a deb hisobladi, axir Amaliya hozirgina u, masalan, akasining ishlari bilan qiziqmasligini, Olga esa ular haqida hamma narsani bilishini aytdi-ku. «Buni qanday tushuntirsam ekan? — dedi Olga. — Amaliya na Barnabas, na men bilan qiziqadi, u aslida ota-onamizdan boshqa hech kim bilan qiziqmaydi, ularni kecha-kunduz parvarish qiladi, hozir ham yana ularning istaklarini so'rab, ular uchun ovqat pishirgani oshxonaga ketdi, ular uchun o'zini majburlab o'rnidan turdi, chunki u tushdan beri kasal va shu yerda, supada yotgan edi.

paras.en: But although she doesn't concern herself with us, we depend on her as though she were the eldest, and if she advised us in our affairs we'd certainly follow her; but she doesn't, we're strangers to her. You have a lot of experience of people, after all; you come from abroad; doesn't she seem especially clever to you too?' 'She seems especially unhappy to me,' said K. 'But how does it square with your respect for her that Barnabas, for example, does this messenger's service that Amalia disapproves of, perhaps even despises?' 'If he knew what else he could do, he'd leave the messenger's service at once — it doesn't satisfy him at all.' 'Isn't he a fully trained shoemaker, then?' asked K. 'Certainly,' said Olga, 'he works for Brunswick on the side, too, and if he wanted he'd have work day and night and good earnings.' 'Well, then,' said K., 'he'd have a substitute for the messenger's service.' 'For the messenger's service?' asked Olga, astonished. 'Did he take it on for the sake of the earnings, then?' 'Maybe,' said K., 'but you did mention that it doesn't satisfy him.' 'It doesn't satisfy him, for various reasons,' said Olga, 'but it is Castle service, after all, a kind of Castle service at any rate — at least so one ought to believe.' 'What,' said K., 'you're in doubt even about that?'
paras.uz: Lekin u biz bilan qiziqmasa ham, biz unga go'yo u eng kattamizdek qaramiz; agar u bizga ishlarimizda maslahat bersa, albatta, unga amal qilardik, lekin u bunday qilmaydi, biz unga begonamiz. Sening odamlar haqida tajribang ko'p-ku, sen begona yurtdan kelgansan; senga ham u ayniqsa aqlli bo'lib ko'rinmaydimi?» «Menga u ayniqsa baxtsiz bo'lib ko'rinadi, — dedi K., — lekin unga bo'lgan hurmatingiz bilan, masalan, Barnabasning Amaliya ma'qullamaydigan, balki hatto mensimaydigan bu choparlik xizmatini qilishi qanday mos keladi?» «Agar boshqa nima qilishni bilganida, uni umuman qoniqtirmaydigan choparlik xizmatini darhol tashlab ketardi.» «Axir u o'qib bo'lgan etikdo'z emasmi?» — so'radi K. «Albatta, — dedi Olga, — u qo'shimcha ravishda Brunsvik uchun ham ishlaydi, agar xohlasa, kecha-kunduz ishi va mo'l daromadi bo'lardi.» «Xo'sh, unda, — dedi K., — choparlik xizmatining o'rnini bosadigan narsa bor ekan-ku.» «Choparlik xizmatininmi? — so'radi Olga hayron bo'lib. — Nahotki u uni daromad uchun olgan bo'lsa?» «Bo'lishi mumkin, — dedi K., — lekin sen axir u uni qoniqtirmasligini aytding-ku.» «U uni qoniqtirmaydi, turli sabablarga ko'ra, — dedi Olga, — lekin bu baribir Qasr xizmati, har holda Qasr xizmatining bir turi — hech bo'lmaganda shunday deb ishonish kerak.» «Qanday, — dedi K., — hatto bunda ham shubhadamisizlar?»

paras.en: 'Well,' said Olga, 'not really; Barnabas goes into the offices, mixes with the servants as one of them, sees individual officials from a distance, is given comparatively important letters, even messages to deliver by word of mouth — that's quite a lot, after all, and we can be proud of how much he has already achieved at so young an age.' K. nodded; he wasn't thinking of going home now. 'He has his own livery too?' he asked. 'You mean the jacket?' said Olga. 'No, Amalia made that for him, even before he was a messenger. But you're coming close to the sore point. He ought long ago to have been given — not a livery, there's no such thing at the Castle — but a suit from the office; he was promised it, too, but in this respect they are very slow at the Castle, and the bad thing is that one never knows what this slowness means. It can mean that the matter is going through official channels; but it can also mean that the official process hasn't even begun — that, for instance, they still want to test Barnabas first; and finally it can also mean that the official process is already finished, that for some reason the promise has been withdrawn and Barnabas will never get the suit. Nothing more precise can be found out about it, or only after a long time. There's a saying here — perhaps you know it: official decisions are as shy as young girls.'
paras.uz: «Xo'sh, — dedi Olga, — aslida yo'q; Barnabas idoralarga boradi, xizmatkorlar bilan ularning tengidek muomala qiladi, ayrim amaldorlarni uzoqdan ko'radi, unga nisbatan muhim xatlar, hatto og'zaki yetkaziladigan xabarlar ham ishonib topshiriladi — bu axir ancha ko'p va biz u shunchalik yosh bo'lib, allaqachon qanchalik ko'p narsaga erishgani bilan faxrlanishimiz mumkin.» K. bosh irg'adi, u endi uyga qaytishni o'ylamayotgan edi. «Uning o'z xizmat libosi ham bormi?» — so'radi u. «Kamzulni nazarda tutyapsanmi? — dedi Olga. — Yo'q, uni unga hali chopar bo'lmasidan oldin Amaliya tikib bergan. Lekin sen og'riqli nuqtaga yaqinlashyapsan. Unga allaqachon — xizmat libosi emas, Qasrda bunday narsa yo'q — idoradan kiyim berilishi kerak edi, bu unga va'da ham qilingan, lekin bu borada Qasrda juda sekin ishlashadi, eng yomoni esa, bu sekinlik nimani anglatishini hech qachon bilmaysan; bu ish rasmiy yo'lda ekanini anglatishi mumkin, lekin rasmiy yo'l hali umuman boshlanmaganini ham, ya'ni, masalan, Barnabasni hali ham avval sinab ko'rmoqchi ekanlarini ham anglatishi mumkin; nihoyat, bu rasmiy yo'l allaqachon tugaganini, qandaydir sabablarga ko'ra va'da qaytarib olinganini va Barnabas kiyimni hech qachon olmasligini ham anglatishi mumkin. Bu haqda aniqroq narsani bilib bo'lmaydi yoki faqat uzoq vaqtdan keyin bilinadi. Bu yerda bir maqol bor, balki sen uni bilarsan: Rasmiy qarorlar yosh qizlardek uyatchan.»

paras.en: 'That's a good observation,' said K. — he took it even more seriously than Olga — 'a good observation; the decisions may have still other qualities in common with girls.' 'Perhaps,' said Olga. 'I don't know, of course, how you mean it. Perhaps you even mean it as praise. But as regards the official clothes, that's just one of Barnabas's worries, and since we share our worries, mine too. Why doesn't he get official clothes, we ask ourselves in vain. But this whole matter isn't so simple. The officials, for example, don't seem to have official clothes at all; as far as we know here, and as far as Barnabas tells us, the officials go about in ordinary clothes — fine ones, admittedly. Besides, you've seen Klamm. Now, Barnabas is of course not an official, not even an official of the lowest category, and doesn't presume to want to be one. But even the higher servants — whom, of course, one never gets to see here in the village at all — have no official suits, according to Barnabas's account. That's a certain comfort, one might think at first, but it's deceptive, for is Barnabas a higher servant?
paras.uz: «Bu yaxshi kuzatish, — dedi K. — u buni Olgadan ham jiddiyroq qabul qildi, — yaxshi kuzatish, qarorlarning qizlar bilan yana boshqa umumiy xususiyatlari ham bo'lishi mumkin.» «Balki, — dedi Olga. — To'g'ri, buni qanday ma'noda aytayotganingni bilmayman. Balki hatto maqtov ma'nosida aytayotgandirsan. Lekin rasmiy kiyimga kelsak, bu Barnabasning tashvishlaridan biri, biz tashvishlarimizni baham ko'rganimiz uchun, meniki ham. Nega unga rasmiy kiyim berilmaydi, deb o'zimizdan behuda so'raymiz. Lekin bu butun ish unchalik oddiy emas. Masalan, amaldorlarning umuman rasmiy kiyimi yo'qqa o'xshaydi; biz bu yerda bilganimizcha va Barnabas aytib berganicha, amaldorlar oddiy, to'g'ri, chiroyli kiyimlarda yurishadi. Aytgancha, sen Klammni ko'rgansan-ku. Xo'sh, Barnabas, albatta, amaldor emas, hatto eng past toifadagi amaldor ham emas va shunday bo'lishni istashga jur'at etmaydi. Lekin Barnabasning hikoyasiga ko'ra, yuqoriroq xizmatkorlarning ham — ularni bu yerda, qishloqda, albatta, umuman ko'rib bo'lmaydi — rasmiy kiyimlari yo'q; bu, boshida o'ylash mumkinki, qandaydir tasalli, lekin u aldamchi, chunki Barnabas yuqoriroq xizmatkormi?

paras.en: No — however well disposed one is towards him, one can't say that; he isn't a higher servant; the very fact that he comes to the village, even lives here, is proof to the contrary. The higher servants are even more reserved than the officials — perhaps rightly; perhaps they're even higher than some officials; there is something to be said for that: they work less, and according to Barnabas it's a wonderful sight to see these exceptionally tall, strong men walking slowly through the corridors; Barnabas always creeps about around them. In short, there can be no question of Barnabas's being a higher servant. So he could be one of the lower servants; but these have official suits, at least those who come down to the village; it isn't a livery in the proper sense, there are many variations too, but all the same one recognises a servant from the Castle at once by his clothes — you've seen such people at the Herrenhof. The most striking thing about the clothes is that they're mostly close-fitting; a peasant or a craftsman couldn't use such clothes. Well, Barnabas doesn't have these clothes; that isn't merely shaming or degrading — one could bear that — but it makes us, Barnabas and me, doubt everything, especially in gloomy hours, and we have such hours sometimes, not too seldom. Is it Castle service at all, what Barnabas does, we ask then; certainly he goes into the offices, but are the offices the real Castle?
paras.uz: Yo'q, unga qanchalik moyil bo'lmagin, buni aytib bo'lmaydi, u yuqoriroq xizmatkor emas; uning qishloqqa kelishi, hatto shu yerda yashashi buning teskarisini isbotlaydi; yuqoriroq xizmatkorlar amaldorlardan ham ko'proq o'zlarini chetda tutishadi, balki haqli ravishda, balki ular hatto ba'zi amaldorlardan ham yuqoriroqdir; buning foydasiga ba'zi dalillar bor: ular kamroq ishlashadi va Barnabasning aytishicha, bu tanlangan baland bo'yli, baquvvat erkaklarning yo'laklar bo'ylab sekin yurishini ko'rish ajoyib manzara ekan; Barnabas doim ularning atrofida aylanib yuradi. Qisqasi, Barnabas yuqoriroq xizmatkor ekani haqida gap bo'lishi ham mumkin emas. Demak, u quyi xizmatkorlardan biri bo'lishi mumkin, lekin ularning rasmiy kiyimlari bor, hech bo'lmaganda qishloqqa tushadiganlarining; bu haqiqiy xizmat libosi emas, ko'p farqlar ham bor, lekin har holda Qasrdan kelgan xizmatkorni kiyimidan darhol taniysan, sen bunday odamlarni Herrenhofda ko'rgansan. Kiyimlarning eng ko'zga tashlanadigan tomoni shundaki, ular asosan tanaga zich yopishib turadi, dehqon yoki hunarmand bunday kiyimni ishlata olmasdi. Xo'sh, bu kiyim Barnabasda yo'q; bu faqat uyatli yoki kamsituvchi emas — bunga chidash mumkin edi — balki bu, ayniqsa g'amgin soatlarda — bizda bunday soatlar ba'zan, unchalik kam emas, bo'lib turadi — Barnabas bilan meni hamma narsaga shubha qilishga majbur qiladi. Barnabas qilayotgan ish umuman Qasr xizmatimi, deb so'raymiz o'shanda; albatta, u idoralarga boradi, lekin idoralar haqiqiy Qasrmi?

paras.en: And even if offices belong to the Castle, are they the offices Barnabas is allowed to enter? He gets into offices; but it's only a part of all of them; then there are barriers, and behind them there are still other offices. He isn't exactly forbidden to go further, but he can't go further once he has found his superiors and they have dealt with him and sent him away. Besides, one is always watched there, or at least one believes so. And even if he went further, what use would it be, if he had no official work there and would be an intruder? Nor must you imagine these barriers as a definite boundary; Barnabas keeps drawing my attention to that. There are barriers in the offices he goes into, too; so there are barriers that he passes, and they look no different from those he has not yet got past, and so it can't be assumed from the start that behind these latter barriers there are offices essentially different from those Barnabas has already been in. Only in those gloomy hours does one believe that. And then the doubt goes further; one simply can't defend oneself. Barnabas speaks to officials, Barnabas receives messages. But what officials, what messages are they? Now, as he says, he is assigned to Klamm and gets his orders from him personally.
paras.uz: Hatto idoralar Qasrga tegishli bo'lsa ham, Barnabas kirishga ruxsat berilgan idoralar o'shalarmi? U idoralarga kiradi; lekin bu hammasining faqat bir qismi, keyin to'siqlar bor, ularning ortida esa yana boshqa idoralar bor. Unga oldinga borishni to'g'ridan-to'g'ri taqiqlashmaydi, lekin u o'z boshliqlarini topib, ular uning ishini bitirib, jo'natib yuborgandan keyin oldinga bora olmaydi. Bundan tashqari, u yerda doim kuzatib turishadi, hech bo'lmaganda shunday deb o'ylaysan. Hatto u oldinga borsa ham, agar u yerda uning rasmiy ishi bo'lmasa va u bostirib kirgan begona bo'lsa, bu nimaga yordam berardi? Bu to'siqlarni aniq bir chegara deb ham tasavvur qilmasliging kerak, Barnabas ham doim mening e'tiborimni shunga qaratadi. To'siqlar u kiradigan idoralarda ham bor; demak, u o'tadigan to'siqlar ham bor va ular u hali o'ta olmagan to'siqlardan farq qilmaydi, shuning uchun bu oxirgi to'siqlar ortida Barnabas allaqachon bo'lgan idoralardan tubdan farq qiladigan idoralar bor deb oldindan taxmin qilib bo'lmaydi. Faqat o'sha g'amgin soatlardagina shunday deb ishonasan. Keyin shubha davom etadi, undan umuman himoyalana olmaysan. Barnabas amaldorlar bilan gaplashadi, Barnabas xabarlar oladi. Lekin ular qanday amaldorlar, qanday xabarlar? Endi u, o'zi aytganidek, Klammga biriktirilgan va topshiriqlarni undan shaxsan oladi.

paras.en: Well, that would be a great deal; even higher servants don't get so far; it would almost be too much — that's what's frightening. Just think: to be assigned directly to Klamm, to speak with him mouth to mouth. But that's how it is, isn't it? Well, yes, it is; but then why does Barnabas doubt that the official who is called Klamm there is really Klamm?' 'Olga,' said K., 'you surely don't want to joke; how can there be any doubt about Klamm's appearance? It's known what he looks like; I've seen him myself.' 'Certainly not, K.,' said Olga. 'They're not jokes, but my most serious worries. But I'm not telling you this to relieve my heart and perhaps burden yours, but because you asked about Barnabas, because Amalia gave me the task of telling you, and because I believe it's useful for you too to know more exactly. I'm doing it for Barnabas's sake too, so that you won't set too great hopes on him, and he won't disappoint you and then suffer himself under your disappointment. He is very sensitive; for instance, he didn't sleep last night because you were dissatisfied with him yesterday evening; you're said to have said that it's very bad for you to have only such a messenger as Barnabas. Those words robbed him of his sleep. You yourself probably didn't notice much of his agitation; Castle messengers have to control themselves very much.
paras.uz: Xo'sh, bu axir juda ko'p bo'lardi, hatto yuqoriroq xizmatkorlar ham bunchalik uzoqqa yetib bormaydi, bu deyarli juda ko'p bo'lardi — qo'rqinchli tomoni ham shunda. O'ylab ko'r: to'g'ridan-to'g'ri Klammga biriktirilgan bo'lish, u bilan og'izma-og'iz gaplashish. Lekin axir shunday-ku? Xo'sh, ha, shunday, lekin unda nega Barnabas u yerda Klamm deb ataladigan amaldor rostdan ham Klamm ekaniga shubha qiladi?» «Olga, — dedi K., — hazillashmoqchi emassan-ku; Klammning tashqi ko'rinishi haqida qanday shubha bo'lishi mumkin, axir u qanday ko'rinishi ma'lum, uni o'zim ko'rganman.» «Albatta, hazil emas, K., — dedi Olga. — Bu hazil emas, balki mening eng jiddiy tashvishlarim. Lekin men buni senga yuragimni yengillashtirish va seni og'irlashtirish uchun emas, balki sen Barnabas haqida so'raganing, Amaliya menga aytib berishni topshirgani va buni aniqroq bilish sen uchun ham foydali deb o'ylaganim uchun aytyapman. Buni Barnabas uchun ham qilyapman, toki sen unga haddan tashqari katta umid bog'lamagin, u sening hafsalangni pir qilmasin va keyin o'zi sening hafsalasizliging ostida azob chekmasin. U juda sezgir; masalan, u bugun tunda uxlamadi, chunki kecha kechqurun sen undan norozi bo'lding; aytishlaricha, sen Barnabasdek choparing borligi sen uchun juda yomon, degan ekansan. Bu so'zlar uning uyqusini o'g'irladi. Sen o'zing uning hayajonlarini, ehtimol, unchalik payqamagansan, Qasr choparlari o'zlarini juda tutishlari kerak.

paras.en: But he doesn't have it easy, not even with you. In your own terms you certainly don't ask too much of him; you've brought certain ideas of a messenger's service with you, and you measure your demands by them. But at the Castle they have different ideas of a messenger's service; they can't be reconciled with yours, even if Barnabas sacrificed himself entirely to the service — which, unfortunately, he sometimes seems ready to do. One would have to submit, mustn't say anything against it — if only there weren't the question whether what he does is really a messenger's service. To you, of course, he mustn't express any doubt about it; for him it would mean undermining his own existence if he did, grossly violating laws he still believes himself to be under; and even to me he doesn't speak freely; I have to coax his doubts out of him, kiss them out of him, and even then he still resists admitting that the doubts are doubts. He has something of Amalia in his blood. And he certainly doesn't tell me everything, although I'm his only confidante. But we sometimes talk about Klamm. I haven't seen Klamm yet — you know Frieda doesn't love me much and would never have granted me the sight — but of course his appearance is known in the village; some have seen him, all have heard of him, and out of eyewitness, rumours and some false ulterior motives too, a picture of Klamm has formed that is probably correct in its basic features. But only in its basic features.
paras.uz: Lekin uning ishi oson emas, hatto sen bilan ham. Sen o'z tushunchangda undan, albatta, ortiqcha narsa talab qilmaysan, sen choparlik xizmati haqida ma'lum tasavvurlar olib kelgansan va talablaringni ularga qarab o'lchaysan. Lekin Qasrda choparlik xizmati haqida boshqa tasavvurlar bor, ularni seniki bilan birlashtirib bo'lmaydi — hatto Barnabas o'zini butunlay xizmatga qurbon qilsa ham; u, afsuski, ba'zan bunga tayyordek ko'rinadi. Bo'ysunish, bunga qarshi hech narsa demaslik kerak bo'lardi, faqat u qilayotgan ish haqiqatan ham choparlik xizmatimi degan savol bo'lmasa. Senga, albatta, u bu haqda hech qanday shubha bildirmasligi kerak; agar buni qilsa, bu u uchun o'z mavjudligini kovlash, o'zi hali ham bo'ysunaman deb hisoblaydigan qonunlarni qo'pol buzish bo'lardi; hatto menga ham u erkin gapirmaydi, uning shubhalarini erkalab, o'pib undan sug'urib olishim kerak, shunda ham u shubhalar shubha ekanini tan olishdan bosh tortadi. Uning qonida Amaliyadan nimadir bor. U menga hammasini, albatta, aytmaydi, garchi men uning yagona sirdoshi bo'lsam ham. Lekin Klamm haqida biz ba'zan gaplashamiz; men Klammni hali ko'rmaganman — bilasan, Frida meni unchalik yaxshi ko'rmaydi va bu manzarani menga hech qachon ravo ko'rmasdi — lekin, albatta, uning ko'rinishi qishloqda ma'lum, ba'zilar uni ko'rgan, hammasi u haqda eshitgan va ko'rganlardan, mish-mishlardan, ba'zi g'arazli niyatlardan ham Klammning asosiy chiziqlarda to'g'ri bo'lsa kerak bo'lgan qiyofasi shakllangan. Lekin faqat asosiy chiziqlarda.

paras.en: Otherwise it's changeable — and perhaps not even as changeable as Klamm's real appearance. He's said to look quite different when he comes into the village and different when he leaves it, different before he has drunk beer, different afterwards, different awake, different asleep, different alone, different in conversation, and — what is understandable after all this — almost fundamentally different up at the Castle. And even within the village quite big differences are reported — differences of height, of bearing, of stoutness, of beard; only as regards his clothes are the reports fortunately uniform: he always wears the same clothes, a black jacket-suit with long tails. Now of course all these differences aren't due to any magic, but are very understandable; they arise from the momentary mood, the degree of excitement, the countless gradations of hope or despair in which the onlooker finds himself — who, besides, is mostly allowed to see Klamm only for a moment. I'm telling you all this again just as Barnabas has often explained it to me, and in general, if one isn't personally and directly involved in the matter, one can set one's mind at rest with it. We can't; for Barnabas it's a question of life whether he really speaks to Klamm or not.' 'For me no less,' said K., and they moved still closer together on the stove bench.
paras.uz: Qolgan jihatdan u o'zgaruvchan — balki Klammning haqiqiy tashqi ko'rinishichalik o'zgaruvchan ham emasdir. Aytishlaricha, u qishloqqa kelganda butunlay boshqacha, ketayotganda boshqacha, pivo ichishdan oldin boshqacha, keyin boshqacha, uyg'oqlikda boshqacha, uyquda boshqacha, yolg'iz bo'lganda boshqacha, suhbatda boshqacha va — bulardan keyin tushunarli — tepada, Qasrda deyarli tubdan boshqacha ko'rinarmish. Hatto qishloq ichida ham ancha katta farqlar aytiladi — bo'y, qomat, semizlik, soqol farqlari; faqat kiyim borasida, baxtimizga, hikoyalar bir xil: u doim bir xil kiyimda — uzun etakli qora kostyumda yuradi. Albatta, bu farqlarning hech biri sehrgarlikka borib taqalmaydi, balki juda tushunarli; ular tomoshabinning — u ham odatda Klammni faqat bir lahzagina ko'rishi mumkin — o'sha paytdagi kayfiyati, hayajon darajasi, umid yoki umidsizlikning son-sanoqsiz pog'onalaridan kelib chiqadi. Men bularning hammasini senga Barnabas menga ko'p marta tushuntirganidek yana aytib beryapman va umuman, agar o'zing shaxsan va bevosita ishtirok etmasang, bu bilan tinchlanish mumkin. Biz tinchlana olmaymiz; Barnabas uchun u rostdan ham Klamm bilan gaplashadimi-yo'qmi — bu hayot-mamot masalasi.» «Men uchun ham bundan kam emas», dedi K. va ular pech yonidagi supada yana bir-biriga yaqinroq surilishdi.

paras.en: K. was struck, it is true, by all Olga's unfavourable news, but he saw a compensation in large part in the fact that here he found people who, outwardly at least, were in a very similar position to himself, whom he could therefore join, with whom he could come to an understanding in many things — not only in some, as with Frieda. True, he was gradually losing hope of any success from Barnabas's message; but the worse things went for Barnabas, the closer he came to him down here; K. would never have thought that out of the village itself such an unhappy striving could arise as that of Barnabas and his sister. Of course it was still far from sufficiently explained, and might in the end turn into its opposite; one mustn't let oneself be seduced at once by a certain innocent quality in Olga into believing in Barnabas's sincerity too. 'Barnabas knows the reports of Klamm's appearance very well,' Olga went on; 'he has collected and compared many of them, perhaps too many; he once saw Klamm himself in the village through a carriage window, or believed he saw him; so he was sufficiently prepared to recognise him; and yet — how do you explain it? — when he came into an office at the Castle and they pointed out one official among several and said that this was Klamm, he didn't recognise him, and for a long time afterwards he couldn't get used to the idea that this was supposed to be Klamm.
paras.uz: Olganing barcha noxush yangiliklari K.ni, to'g'ri, larzaga soldi, lekin u buning o'rnini ko'p jihatdan shunda ko'rdiki, bu yerda u hech bo'lmaganda tashqi tomondan o'zinikiga juda o'xshash ahvoldagi odamlarni topdi; demak, ularga qo'shilishi, ular bilan ko'p narsada — Frida bilan bo'lganidek faqat ba'zi narsalarda emas — til topishishi mumkin edi. To'g'ri, u Barnabasning xabaridan muvaffaqiyat kutish umidini asta-sekin yo'qotayotgan edi, lekin Barnabasning ahvoli qanchalik yomon bo'lsa, u bu yerda, pastda unga shunchalik yaqinlashardi; K. hech qachon qishloqning o'zidan Barnabas va uning singlisinikidek baxtsiz intilish chiqishi mumkinligini o'ylamagan edi. To'g'ri, bu hali yetarlicha tushuntirilganidan juda uzoq edi va oxir-oqibat teskarisiga ham aylanib ketishi mumkin edi; Olganing qandaydir beg'ubor tabiatiga aldanib, darhol Barnabasning samimiyligiga ham ishonib qolmaslik kerak edi. «Klammning ko'rinishi haqidagi hikoyalarni, — davom etdi Olga, — Barnabas juda yaxshi biladi, ko'plarini to'plab, solishtirgan, balki juda ko'plarini; bir marta o'zi ham qishloqda Klammni arava derazasidan ko'rgan yoki ko'rdim deb o'ylagan; demak, uni tanishga yetarlicha tayyor edi; shunga qaramay — buni qanday tushuntirasan? — u Qasrda bir idoraga kirganida va unga bir necha amaldor orasidan birini ko'rsatib, bu Klamm deyishganida, u uni tanimadi va keyin ham uzoq vaqt bu Klamm bo'lishi kerakligiga ko'nika olmadi.

paras.en: But if you ask Barnabas in what way that man differs from the usual idea people have of Klamm, he can't answer; or rather, he does answer and describes the official at the Castle, but the description corresponds exactly to the description of Klamm as we know it. Well then, Barnabas, I say, why do you doubt, why do you torment yourself? Whereupon he, in visible distress, begins to list peculiarities of the official at the Castle, which, however, he seems to invent rather than report, and which besides are so trivial — they concern, for example, a particular nod of the head or even just the unbuttoned waistcoat — that one can't possibly take them seriously. Even more important seems to me the way Klamm deals with Barnabas. Barnabas has often described it to me, even drawn it. Usually Barnabas is taken into a large office room, but it isn't Klamm's office, not the office of any single person at all. Lengthwise, this room is divided into two parts by a single standing desk reaching from side wall to side wall: a narrow part, where two people can only just squeeze past each other — that is the officials' space — and a broad part, the space for the parties, the onlookers, the servants, the messengers. On the desk lie big books, opened, one beside the other, and at most of them stand officials reading.
paras.uz: Lekin agar Barnabasdan o'sha odam Klamm haqidagi odatiy tasavvurdan nimasi bilan farq qilishini so'rasang, u javob bera olmaydi; to'g'rirog'i, javob beradi va Qasrdagi amaldorni tasvirlaydi, lekin bu tasvir biz bilgan Klammning tasviriga aynan mos keladi. Xo'sh, Barnabas, deyman men, nega shubhalanasan, nega o'zingni qiynaysan? Shunda u ko'rinib turgan iztirob bilan Qasrdagi amaldorning o'ziga xos xususiyatlarini sanay boshlaydi — lekin u ularni hikoya qilishdan ko'ra ko'proq to'qib chiqarayotgandek ko'rinadi, bundan tashqari, ular shunchalik arzimaski — masalan, boshning o'ziga xos irg'ashi yoki shunchaki tugmasi yechilgan nimcha — ularni jiddiy qabul qilib bo'lmaydi. Menga Klammning Barnabas bilan muomalasi bundan ham muhimroq tuyuladi. Barnabas buni menga ko'p marta tasvirlab bergan, hatto chizib ham bergan. Odatda Barnabasni katta idora xonasiga olib kirishadi, lekin bu Klammning idorasi emas, umuman biror kishining idorasi emas. Bu xona uzunasiga bir yon devordan ikkinchisigacha cho'zilgan yagona tik turib yoziladigan stol bilan ikki qismga bo'lingan: tor qismi — u yerda ikki kishi bir-birining yonidan zo'rg'a o'ta oladi — amaldorlarning joyi, keng qismi esa ariza beruvchilar, tomoshabinlar, xizmatkorlar, choparlarning joyi. Stolda yonma-yon ochiq katta kitoblar yotadi va ko'pchiligi yonida amaldorlar turib o'qishadi.

paras.en: But they don't always stay at the same book; they don't exchange the books, though, but their places; what astonishes Barnabas most is how they have to squeeze past each other in changing places, precisely because of the narrowness of the space. In front, close to the standing desk, are low little tables at which clerks sit, who, when the officials wish it, write from their dictation. Barnabas always wonders how this happens. There is no express order from the official, nor is anything dictated aloud; one hardly notices that dictation is going on; rather, the official seems to be reading as before, only that he is also whispering, and the clerk hears it. Often the official dictates so softly that the clerk can't hear it at all sitting down; then he has to keep jumping up, catch what is dictated, quickly sit down and write it down, then jump up again, and so on. How strange that is! It's almost incomprehensible. Barnabas, of course, has enough time to observe all this, for he stands there in the onlookers' space for hours and sometimes days before Klamm's glance falls on him. And even when Klamm has seen him and Barnabas draws himself up to attention, nothing has been decided yet, for Klamm may turn away from him to the book again and forget him; that often happens. But what kind of a messenger's service is it that is so unimportant? I feel melancholy when Barnabas says in the morning that he is going to the Castle.
paras.uz: Lekin ular doim bir kitob yonida qolishmaydi; kitoblarni emas, joylarni almashtirishadi; Barnabasni eng ko'p hayratga soladigan narsa — joy almashtirganda aynan joyning torligi tufayli bir-birining yonidan qanday siqilib o'tishlari. Oldinda, tik stolga zich qilib past kichik stolchalar qo'yilgan, ularda kotiblar o'tirishadi va amaldorlar xohlaganda ularning aytib turishi bo'yicha yozishadi. Barnabas bu qanday sodir bo'lishiga doim hayron qoladi. Amaldordan hech qanday aniq buyruq bo'lmaydi, baland ovozda ham aytib turilmaydi, aytib turilayotganini deyarli sezmaysan; aksincha, amaldor avvalgidek o'qiyotgandek ko'rinadi, faqat bunda yana pichirlaydi va kotib buni eshitadi. Ko'pincha amaldor shunchalik sekin aytib turadiki, kotib o'tirgan holda umuman eshita olmaydi; shunda u doim sakrab turib, aytilganni ilib olishi, tez o'tirib, uni yozishi, keyin yana sakrab turishi va hokazo kerak bo'ladi. Bu qanchalik g'alati! Bu deyarli tushunarsiz. Barnabasning, albatta, bularning hammasini kuzatishga yetarlicha vaqti bor, chunki u yerda, tomoshabinlar joyida u Klammning nigohi unga tushguncha soatlab, ba'zan kunlab turadi. Hatto Klamm uni ko'rib, Barnabas «hushyor» holatida qaddini rostlagandan keyin ham hali hech narsa hal bo'lmagan, chunki Klamm undan yana kitobga o'girilib, uni unutishi mumkin; bu tez-tez bo'lib turadi. Lekin bunchalik ahamiyatsiz choparlik xizmati qanday xizmat? Barnabas ertalab Qasrga ketyapman desa, ko'nglim g'ash bo'ladi.

paras.en: That probably quite useless walk, that probably lost day, that probably vain hope. What's the point of it all? And here shoemaking work is piling up that nobody does, and Brunswick is pressing for it to be done.' 'Very well,' said K. 'Barnabas has to wait a long time before he gets an errand. That's understandable; there seems to be a superabundance of employees here; not everyone can get an errand every day; you mustn't complain about that; it probably happens to everyone. But in the end Barnabas does get errands, surely; he's already brought me two letters himself.' 'It's possible,' said Olga, 'that we're wrong to complain, especially I, who know everything only by hearsay and, as a girl, can't understand it as well as Barnabas, who also holds back a good deal. But now listen to how it is with the letters — with the letters to you, for example. He doesn't get these letters directly from Klamm, but from the clerk. On any day, at any hour — that's why the service, easy as it seems, is very tiring, for Barnabas has to be on the alert all the time — the clerk remembers him and beckons to him.
paras.uz: Bu, ehtimol, butunlay befoyda yo'l, bu, ehtimol, yo'qotilgan kun, bu, ehtimol, behuda umid. Bularning hammasi nima uchun? Bu yerda esa hech kim qilmaydigan va Brunsvik bajarilishini qistayotgan etikdo'zlik ishi to'planib yotibdi.» «Xo'sh, yaxshi, — dedi K. — Barnabas topshiriq olguncha uzoq kutishi kerak. Bu tushunarli, bu yerda xizmatchilar haddan ziyod ko'pga o'xshaydi, hamma har kuni topshiriq ola olmaydi, bundan shikoyat qilmasligingiz kerak, bu, ehtimol, hammaning boshida bor. Lekin oxir-oqibat Barnabas ham topshiriqlar oladi-ku, menga o'zi allaqachon ikkita xat olib kelgan.» «Bo'lishi mumkin, — dedi Olga, — shikoyat qilishga haqqimiz yo'qdir, ayniqsa men — hamma narsani faqat eshitganimdan bilaman va qiz bola sifatida buni yana ko'p narsani yashiradigan Barnabaschalik yaxshi tushuna olmayman. Lekin endi eshit, xatlar bilan qanday — masalan, senga yozilgan xatlar bilan. Bu xatlarni u to'g'ridan-to'g'ri Klammdan emas, kotibdan oladi. Istalgan kuni, istalgan soatda — shuning uchun xizmat qanchalik yengil ko'rinmasin, juda charchatadi, chunki Barnabas doim hushyor turishi kerak — kotib uni eslab qolib, unga imo qiladi.

paras.en: Klamm doesn't seem to have prompted it at all; he goes on reading quietly in his book; sometimes, it's true — but he does that often at other times too — he happens to be cleaning his pince-nez when Barnabas comes, and perhaps looks at him while doing so — assuming that he can see at all without his pince-nez; Barnabas doubts it; Klamm then has his eyes almost closed; he seems to be asleep and cleaning his pince-nez only in a dream. Meanwhile the clerk searches out a letter for you from among the many files and papers he has under the table; so it isn't a letter he has just written; rather, to judge by the look of the envelope, it's a very old letter that has been lying there a long time. But if it's an old letter, why did they make Barnabas wait so long? And probably you too? And finally the letter too, for it is probably out of date by now. And Barnabas thereby gets the reputation of being a bad, slow messenger. The clerk, of course, makes it easy for himself: he gives Barnabas the letter, says: From Klamm for K., and with that Barnabas is dismissed.
paras.uz: Bunga Klamm sabab bo'lganga umuman o'xshamaydi, u kitobini xotirjam o'qiyveradi; ba'zan, to'g'ri — lekin u buni boshqa paytlarda ham tez-tez qiladi — Barnabas kelganda u aynan ko'zoynagini artayotgan bo'ladi va bunda, balki, unga qarab qo'yar; agar u umuman ko'zoynaksiz ko'ra olsa — Barnabas bunga shubha qiladi — shunda Klammning ko'zlari deyarli yumuq bo'ladi, u go'yo uxlayotgandek va ko'zoynagini faqat tushida artayotgandek ko'rinadi. Bu orada kotib stol ostidagi ko'plab hujjatlar va xat-xabarlar orasidan sen uchun bir xatni izlab topadi; demak, bu u endigina yozgan xat emas, aksincha, konvertining ko'rinishiga qaraganda, bu allaqachon uzoq vaqtdan beri u yerda yotgan juda eski xat. Lekin agar bu eski xat bo'lsa, nega Barnabasni bunchalik uzoq kuttirishdi? Va, ehtimol, seni ham? Nihoyat xatni ham, chunki u endi, ehtimol, allaqachon eskirgan. Bu bilan esa Barnabasga yomon, sekin chopar degan nom chiqariladi. Kotib esa, albatta, ishni o'ziga oson qiladi: Barnabasga xatni berib: Klammdan K. uchun, deydi va shu bilan Barnabasni jo'natib yuboradi.

paras.en: Well, and then Barnabas comes home, breathless, the letter he has finally got hold of under his shirt against his bare skin, and then we sit down here on the bench as now, and he tells his story, and we examine everything in detail and estimate what he has achieved, and finally find that it's very little, and the little questionable; and Barnabas puts the letter aside and has no desire to deliver it, but has no desire to go to sleep either; he takes up the shoemaking and sits out the night there on the stool. That's how it is, K., and those are my secrets, and now you probably won't be surprised any more that Amalia does without them.' 'And the letter?' asked K. 'The letter?' said Olga. 'Well, after a while, when I've pressed Barnabas enough — days and weeks may have passed in the meantime — he does take the letter and go to deliver it. In such outward things he depends on me very much. For once I've got over the first impression of his story, I can pull myself together again — which he probably can't, precisely because he knows more. And so I can then say to him again and again something like: What do you really want, Barnabas? What career, what goal are you dreaming of? Do you perhaps want to get so far that you'll have to leave us — leave me — entirely? Is that your goal?
paras.uz: Xo'sh, keyin Barnabas nafasi bo'g'zida, nihoyat qo'lga kiritgan xatni ko'ylagi ostida, yalang'och tanasiga bosib uyga keladi, biz esa hozirgidek shu supaga o'tiramiz, u hikoya qiladi, biz hamma narsani birma-bir tekshirib, u nimaga erishganini baholaymiz va nihoyat bu juda oz va o'sha ozgina ham shubhali ekanini topamiz; Barnabas xatni chetga qo'yadi va uni yetkazishga xohishi bo'lmaydi, lekin uxlashga yotishga ham xohishi bo'lmaydi, etikdo'zlik ishini olib, o'sha yerda kursichada tunni o'tkazadi. Mana shunday, K., bular mening sirlarim, endi Amaliya ulardan voz kechishiga, ehtimol, hayron bo'lmaysan.» «Xat-chi?» — so'radi K. «Xatmi? — dedi Olga. — Xo'sh; biroz vaqt o'tgach, men Barnabasni yetarlicha qistaganimdan keyin — bu orada kunlar va haftalar o'tib ketishi mumkin — u baribir xatni olib, yetkazishga ketadi. Bunday tashqi ishlarda u mendan juda qaram. Gap shundaki, men uning hikoyasining birinchi taassurotini yengib o'tgach, o'zimni yana qo'lga ola olaman; u esa, ehtimol, aynan ko'proq bilgani uchun bunga qodir emas. Shuning uchun men unga qayta-qayta taxminan shunday deyishim mumkin: Aslida nima istaysan, Barnabas? Qanday martaba, qanday maqsad haqida orzu qilasan? Balki shunchalik uzoqqa bormoqchisanki, bizni, meni butunlay tashlab ketishing kerak bo'ladi? Balki maqsading shudir?

gloss.ex: …ge.' K. nodded; he wasn't thinking of going home now. 'He has his own livery too?' he asked. 'You mean the jacket?' said Olga. 'No, Amalia made that for him, ev…
…ets into offices; but it's only a part of all of them; then there are barriers, and behind them there are still other offices. He isn't exactly forbidden to go…
