quiz.q: What does Amalia tell K. about Olga?
quiz.why_uz: Amaliya: Olga K.ni sevadiganga o'xshaydi.

quiz.q: Why does Barnabas doubt his service?
o: He has no official suit, cannot pass the barriers, and doubts that 'Klamm' is really Klamm
quiz.why_uz: Rasmiy kiyim yo'q, to'siqlar, va Klammning o'zi ekaniga shubha.

quiz.q: Where does Barnabas get K.'s letters from?
o: From a clerk, out of old papers under the table
quiz.why_uz: Kotib stol ostidagi eski hujjatlar orasidan xatni chiqarib beradi.

chapters.title: 14. Amalia's secret
chapters.recap_uz: K. Olgaga Barnabas juda yosh va qo'rqoq ekanini, lekin unga baribir nimadir in'om etilganini aytadi: dahliz, to'siqlar, kotib — bularning hammasi yo'l bo'lishi mumkin. Olga oilaning sirini ochadi: uch yil oldin o't o'chiruvchilar bayramida Qasr amaldori Sortini Amaliyani ko'rib qoladi. Ertasi tongda u Amaliyaga uni darhol Herrenhofga chaqiruvchi tuban xat yuboradi. Amaliya xatni yirtib, choparning yuziga otadi. K. bu hokimiyatni suiiste'mol qilish ekanini aytadi.

paras.en: Mustn't I believe that, since otherwise it would be incomprehensible why you're so terribly dissatisfied with what you've already achieved? Just look around and see whether anyone among our neighbours has got so far already. Of course their situation is different from ours, and they have no reason to strive beyond their farms; but even without comparing, one must see that with you everything is going as well as possible. There are obstacles, questionable things, disappointments; but that only means what we knew beforehand — that nothing will be given you, that you must fight for every single little thing yourself; one more reason to be proud, not downcast. And then, you're fighting for us too, aren't you? Does that mean nothing to you? Doesn't it give you new strength? And that I'm happy and almost arrogant to have such a brother — doesn't that give you confidence? Truly, it isn't in what you've achieved at the Castle that you disappoint me, but in what I've achieved with you.
paras.uz: Bunga ishonmasligim kerakmi, axir aks holda nega allaqachon erishgan narsangdan bunchalik dahshatli norozi ekaning tushunarsiz bo'lardi? Atrofga qara-chi, qo'shnilarimiz orasida birortasi bunchalik uzoqqa yetib borganmi? To'g'ri, ularning ahvoli biznikidan boshqacha va ularda o'z xo'jaliklaridan tashqariga intilish uchun sabab yo'q, lekin solishtirmasdan ham tushunish kerakki, senda hammasi eng yaxshi yo'lda. To'siqlar bor, shubhali narsalar, hafsalasizliklar bor, lekin bu faqat biz oldindan bilgan narsani anglatadi: senga hech narsa tekin berilmaydi, aksincha, har bir mayda narsa uchun o'zing kurashishing kerak; bu tushkunlikka emas, faxrlanishga yana bir sabab. Keyin, axir sen biz uchun ham kurashyapsan-ku? Bu sen uchun hech narsani anglatmaydimi? Bu senga yangi kuch bermaydimi? Shunday akam borligidan baxtiyor va deyarli mag'rur ekanim senga ishonch bermaydimi? Rostini aytsam, sen meni Qasrda erishgan narsang bilan emas, men sendan erishgan narsam bilan hafsalamni pir qilyapsan.

paras.en: You're allowed into the Castle, you're a regular visitor to the offices, you spend whole days in the same room as Klamm, you're a publicly recognised messenger, you have a claim to official clothes, you're given important letters to carry; you are all that, you're allowed all that, and you come down, and instead of our lying in each other's arms weeping with happiness, all your courage seems to leave you at the sight of me; you doubt everything; only the shoemaker's last attracts you, and the letter, this guarantee of our future, you leave lying there. That's how I talk to him, and after I've repeated it for days, he takes the letter with a sigh one day and goes. But it probably isn't the effect of my words at all; it's only that he's driven to the Castle again, and he wouldn't dare go there without having carried out the errand.' 'But you're right in everything you say to him,' said K. 'You've summed everything up admirably. How astonishingly clearly you think!' 'No,' said Olga, 'it deceives you, and so perhaps I deceive him too. What has he achieved, then? He's allowed into an office, but it doesn't even seem to be an office — rather an antechamber of the offices, perhaps not even that, perhaps a room where everyone is to be held back who isn't allowed into the real offices. He speaks to Klamm — but is it Klamm? Isn't it rather someone who resembles Klamm a little?
paras.uz: Senga Qasrga kirishga ruxsat bor, idoralarning doimiy mehmonisan, butun kunlarni Klamm bilan bir xonada o'tkazasan, ommaviy tan olingan choparsan, rasmiy kiyimga haqqing bor, muhim xatlarni yetkazish senga topshiriladi; sen bularning hammasisan, bularning hammasiga ruxsating bor, pastga tushasan va biz baxtdan yig'lab bir-birimizning quchog'ida yotish o'rniga, meni ko'rganda butun jasorating seni tark etgandek bo'ladi; hamma narsaga shubha qilasan, seni faqat etikdo'z qolipi o'ziga tortadi, kelajagimizning kafolati bo'lgan xatni esa tashlab qo'yasan. Men unga shunday gapiraman, buni kunlab takrorlaganimdan keyin u bir kuni xo'rsinib xatni oladi va ketadi. Lekin bu, ehtimol, umuman mening so'zlarimning ta'siri emas, balki uni yana Qasrga undayotgan narsa, topshiriqni bajarmay turib u yerga borishga esa jur'at etmaydi.» «Lekin unga aytgan hamma gaplaringda haqsan-ku, — dedi K. — Hammasini hayratlanarli darajada to'g'ri jamlading. Qanchalik ajoyib aniq fikrlaysan!» «Yo'q, — dedi Olga, — bu seni aldayapti, shuning uchun balki men ham uni aldayotgandirman. U nimaga erishdi o'zi? Unga idoraga kirishga ruxsat bor, lekin bu hatto idoraga ham o'xshamaydi, ko'proq idoralarning dahliziga, balki hatto unga ham emas, balki haqiqiy idoralarga kirishga ruxsat berilmaganlarning hammasi ushlab turiladigan xonadir. U Klamm bilan gaplashadi, lekin bu Klammmi? Bu ko'proq Klammga biroz o'xshaydigan kimdir emasmi?

paras.en: A secretary perhaps, at the very most, who resembles Klamm a little and makes an effort to resemble him still more, and then gives himself airs in Klamm's sleepy, dreamy manner. That part of his nature is the easiest to imitate; a good many try their hand at it; of the rest of his nature, of course, they wisely keep their fingers off. And a man so often longed for and so seldom reached as Klamm easily takes on different shapes in people's imagination. Klamm has a village secretary here, for instance, called Momus. So? You know him? He keeps himself very much to himself too, but I've seen him a few times. A young, strong gentleman, isn't he? And so he probably doesn't look like Klamm at all. And yet you can find people in the village who would swear that Momus is Klamm and nobody else. That's how people work at their own confusion. And must it be different at the Castle? Someone told Barnabas that that official is Klamm, and there really is a resemblance between the two, but a resemblance Barnabas constantly doubts. And everything speaks for his doubts. Klamm, here in a common room, among other officials, a pencil behind his ear, having to squeeze his way about? That's surely most improbable.
paras.uz: Ko'pi bilan, balki, Klammga biroz o'xshaydigan va unga yanada o'xshashga harakat qiladigan, keyin Klammning uyqusiragan, xayolparast uslubida o'zini katta tutadigan kotibdir. Uning tabiatining bu qismiga taqlid qilish eng oson, ko'pchilik buni sinab ko'radi, uning qolgan tabiatiga esa, albatta, oqilona ravishda qo'l tekkizishmaydi. Klamm kabi shunchalik tez-tez orzu qilinadigan va shunchalik kam yetib boriladigan odam esa odamlarning tasavvurida osongina turli qiyofalarga kiradi. Masalan, Klammning bu yerda Momus degan qishloq kotibi bor. Shundaymi? Uni taniysanmi? U ham o'zini juda chetda tutadi, lekin men uni bir necha marta ko'rganman. Yosh, baquvvat janob, shundaymi? Demak, u Klammga, ehtimol, umuman o'xshamaydi. Shunga qaramay, qishloqda Momus Klammning o'zi, boshqa hech kim emas, deb qasam ichadigan odamlarni topishing mumkin. Odamlar o'z chalkashliklari ustida shunday ishlashadi. Qasrda boshqacha bo'lishi shartmi? Kimdir Barnabasga o'sha amaldor Klamm ekanini aytgan va haqiqatan ham ikkalasi o'rtasida o'xshashlik bor, lekin Barnabas doim shubha qiladigan o'xshashlik. Hamma narsa uning shubhalari foydasiga gapiradi. Klamm bu yerda umumiy xonada, boshqa amaldorlar orasida, qalami qulog'i orqasida, tiqilib yurishi kerakmi? Bu axir juda ehtimoldan yiroq.

paras.en: Barnabas sometimes says, a little childishly — but this is already a confident mood — The official does look very like Klamm; if he sat in an office of his own, at his own desk, and his name were on the door, I'd have no doubts left. That's childish, but sensible too. It would be much more sensible still, of course, if Barnabas, when he's up there, asked several people at once how things really stand; according to him there are enough people standing about in the room. And even if their statements weren't much more reliable than the statement of the man who showed him Klamm unasked, at least some clues, some points of comparison would have to emerge from their variety. That isn't my idea, it's Barnabas's, but he doesn't dare carry it out; for fear that by some unintended violation of unknown regulations he might lose his post, he doesn't dare speak to anyone, so insecure does he feel; this really pitiful insecurity illuminates his position for me more sharply than all descriptions. How doubtful and threatening everything must seem to him there, if he doesn't even dare to open his mouth for an innocent question. When I think of that, I accuse myself of leaving him alone in those unknown rooms, where things go on in such a way that even he, who is more reckless than cowardly, probably trembles with fear there.' 'Here, I think, you're coming to the decisive point,' said K. 'That's it.
paras.uz: Barnabas ba'zan biroz bolalarcha — lekin bu allaqachon ishonchli kayfiyat — deydi: Amaldor axir Klammga juda o'xshaydi; agar u o'z idorasida, o'z yozuv stolida o'tirganida va eshigida uning ismi bo'lganida, menda boshqa shubha qolmasdi. Bu bolalarcha, lekin baribir oqilona ham. To'g'ri, agar Barnabas tepada bo'lganida darhol bir necha kishidan ishlar aslida qanday ekanini so'rasa, bundan ham ancha oqilonaroq bo'lardi; uning aytishicha, xonada yetarlicha odam turibdi-ku. Ularning gaplari unga so'ramasdan Klammni ko'rsatgan odamning gapidan unchalik ishonchliroq bo'lmasa ham, ularning xilma-xilligidan hech bo'lmaganda qandaydir tayanch nuqtalar, solishtirish nuqtalari chiqishi kerak edi. Bu mening g'oyam emas, Barnabasning g'oyasi, lekin u uni amalga oshirishga jur'at etmaydi; noma'lum qoidalarni qandaydir beixtiyor buzib, lavozimini yo'qotishdan qo'rqib, u hech kimga gapirishga jur'at etmaydi — o'zini shunchalik ishonchsiz his qiladi; bu aslida ayanchli ishonchsizlik menga uning mavqeini barcha tasvirlardan ko'ra o'tkirroq yoritib beradi. Agar u hatto beg'ubor savol uchun ham og'iz ochishga jur'at etmasa, u yerda unga hamma narsa qanchalik shubhali va tahdidli ko'rinishi kerak. Buni o'ylasam, uni o'sha noma'lum xonalarda yolg'iz qoldirganim uchun o'zimni ayblayman — u yerda ishlar shunday ketadiki, hatto qo'rqoqdan ko'ra ko'proq tavakkalchi bo'lgan u ham, ehtimol, qo'rquvdan titraydi.» «Menimcha, bu yerda sen hal qiluvchi nuqtaga kelyapsan, — dedi K. — Gap shunda.

paras.en: After all you've told me, I believe I now see clearly. Barnabas is too young for this task. Nothing he tells can be taken seriously just like that. Since he's dying of fear up there, he can't observe there, and if you force him to report here all the same, you get confused fairy tales. I'm not surprised at it. Reverence for the authorities is inborn in you here; it's further instilled in you throughout your whole lives in the most varied ways and from all sides, and you yourselves help with it as much as you can. But basically I'm not saying anything against that; if an authority is good, why shouldn't one revere it? Only, then one mustn't suddenly send an untaught youth like Barnabas, who has never been beyond the village bounds, into the Castle, and then want to demand truthful reports from him, and examine each of his words like a word of revelation, and make one's own happiness in life depend on the interpretation. Nothing could be more mistaken. Of course I too, no differently from you, let myself be misled by him, and both set hopes on him and suffered disappointments through him, both of which were founded only on his words — that is, on almost nothing.' Olga was silent. 'It isn't easy for me,' said K., 'to shake your trust in your brother, when I can see how you love him and what you expect of him.
paras.uz: Aytib berganlaringning hammasidan keyin endi aniq ko'ryapman deb o'ylayman. Barnabas bu vazifa uchun juda yosh. U aytgan narsalarning hech birini shunchaki jiddiy qabul qilib bo'lmaydi. U tepada qo'rquvdan halok bo'layotgani uchun u yerda kuzata olmaydi, agar uni bu yerda baribir hikoya qilishga majbur qilsang, chalkash ertaklar olasan. Bunga hayron emasman. Idoraga nisbatan ehtirom sizlarda bu yerda tug'ma, keyin butun hayotingiz davomida turli yo'llar bilan va har tomondan sizga singdiriladi, sizlarning o'zingiz ham bunga qo'lingizdan kelganicha yordam berasizlar. Lekin aslida men bunga qarshi hech narsa demayman; agar idora yaxshi bo'lsa, nega unga ehtirom ko'rsatmaslik kerak. Faqat unda qishloq doirasidan tashqariga chiqmagan Barnabas kabi o'qimagan yigitni to'satdan Qasrga yuborib, keyin undan haqqoniy hisobotlar talab qilmoqchi bo'lish, uning har bir so'zini vahiy so'zidek tekshirish va o'z hayotiy baxtingni talqinga bog'lab qo'yish kerak emas. Bundan ham xato narsa bo'lishi mumkin emas. To'g'ri, men ham xuddi sendek undan chalg'idim, unga umid ham bog'ladim, u tufayli hafsalasizliklar ham chekdim — ikkalasi ham faqat uning so'zlariga, ya'ni deyarli hech narsaga asoslangan edi.» Olga jim qoldi. «Menga oson emas, — dedi K., — seni akangga bo'lgan ishonchingda chalg'itish, chunki uni qanchalik sevishingni va undan nima kutayotganingni ko'rib turibman.

paras.en: But it must be done, and not least for the sake of your love and your expectations. For look: again and again something — I don't know what it is — prevents you from fully recognising, not what Barnabas has achieved, but what has been given to him. He's allowed into the offices — or, if you like, into an antechamber; well, then it's an antechamber; but there are doors there that lead further, barriers one can pass through if one has the skill. To me, for instance, this antechamber is completely inaccessible, at least for the time being. Who Barnabas talks to there I don't know; perhaps that clerk is the lowest servant; but even if he is the lowest, he can lead to the next higher one, and if he can't lead to him, he can at least name him, and if he can't name him, he can at least refer one to someone who will be able to name him.
paras.uz: Lekin buni qilish kerak, eng avvalo sevging va umidlaring uchun. Chunki qara, seni doim nimadir — bu nima ekanini bilmayman — Barnabas nimaga erishganini emas, balki unga nima in'om etilganini to'liq anglashdan to'sadi. Unga idoralarga yoki, xohlasang, dahlizga kirishga ruxsat bor; xo'sh, demak, bu dahliz, lekin u yerda oldinga olib boradigan eshiklar, mahorating bo'lsa, o'tish mumkin bo'lgan to'siqlar bor. Masalan, men uchun bu dahliz, hech bo'lmaganda hozircha, butunlay yopiq. Barnabas u yerda kim bilan gaplashishini bilmayman, balki o'sha kotib eng past xizmatkordir, lekin u eng past bo'lsa ham, keyingi yuqoriroqqa olib borishi mumkin; agar unga olib bora olmasa, hech bo'lmaganda uning ismini aytishi mumkin; agar ismini ayta olmasa, hech bo'lmaganda ismini ayta oladigan kishiga yo'naltirishi mumkin.

paras.en: The supposed Klamm may have not the slightest thing in common with the real one; the resemblance may exist only for Barnabas's eyes, blind with excitement; he may be the lowest of the officials, he may not even be an official at all; but he has some task or other at that desk; he reads something in his big book, whispers something to the clerk, thinks something when once in a long while his glance falls on Barnabas; and even if none of that is true and he and his actions mean nothing at all, someone has nevertheless put him there and did so with some intention. By all this I mean that something is there, something is offered to Barnabas, at least something, and that it's only Barnabas's fault if he can achieve nothing with it but doubt, fear and hopelessness. And in saying this I've still been starting from the most unfavourable case, which is even very improbable. For we have the letters in our hands, which I don't trust much, it's true, but much more than Barnabas's words.
paras.uz: Go'yoki Klammning haqiqiysi bilan zarracha ham umumiyligi bo'lmasligi mumkin, o'xshashlik faqat Barnabasning hayajondan ko'r bo'lgan ko'zlari uchun mavjud bo'lishi mumkin, u amaldorlarning eng pasti bo'lishi, hatto umuman amaldor bo'lmasligi ham mumkin, lekin o'sha stol yonida uning qandaydir vazifasi bor, o'sha katta kitobida nimanidir o'qiydi, kotibga nimanidir pichirlaydi, uzoq vaqtda bir marta nigohi Barnabasga tushganda nimanidir o'ylaydi; agar bularning hech biri to'g'ri bo'lmasa va u va uning harakatlari hech narsani anglatmasa ham, uni u yerga baribir kimdir qo'ygan va buni qandaydir niyat bilan qilgan. Bularning hammasi bilan men aytmoqchimanki, u yerda nimadir bor, Barnabasga nimadir taklif qilinyapti, hech bo'lmaganda nimadir; agar u bu bilan shubha, qo'rquv va umidsizlikdan boshqa hech narsaga erisha olmasa, bu faqat Barnabasning aybi. Shu bilan birga, men hali ham eng noqulay holatdan kelib chiqdim, u esa hatto juda ehtimoldan yiroq. Chunki qo'limizda xatlar bor — ularga, to'g'ri, unchalik ishonmayman, lekin Barnabasning so'zlaridan ancha ko'proq ishonaman.

paras.en: They may be old, worthless letters, pulled out at random from a pile of equally worthless letters — at random and with no more sense than the canaries at fairs use to peck out anyone's fortune from a pile — and let that be so; still, these letters at least have some bearing on my work; they are plainly meant for me, even if perhaps not for my benefit; they were, as the mayor and his wife testified, written by Klamm's own hand, and, again according to the mayor, they have only a private and not very transparent significance, it's true, but a great one all the same.' 'Did the mayor say that?' asked Olga. 'Yes, he said that,' K. answered. 'I'll tell Barnabas,' Olga said quickly, 'it will cheer him up a lot.' 'But he doesn't need cheering up,' said K. 'To cheer him up means telling him he's right, that he should only carry on in his previous way; but in precisely that way he'll never achieve anything. You can encourage someone whose eyes are blindfolded as much as you like to stare through the cloth; he'll still never see anything; only when the cloth is taken off can he see. Barnabas needs help, not encouragement.
paras.uz: Ular eski, qadrsiz xatlar bo'lishi, xuddi shunday qadrsiz xatlar uyumidan tasodifan — tasodifan va yarmarkalardagi to'tiqushlar har qanday odamning taqdir qog'ozini uyumdan cho'qib olish uchun sarflaganidan ortiq aql bilan emas — sug'urib olingan bo'lishi mumkin; mayli, shunday bo'lsin, lekin bu xatlar hech bo'lmaganda mening ishimga qandaydir aloqador; ular ko'rinib turibdiki, men uchun mo'ljallangan, garchi balki mening foydam uchun bo'lmasa ham; oqsoqol va uning xotini guvohlik berganidek, ularni Klamm o'z qo'li bilan yozgan va yana oqsoqolning aytishicha, ularning ahamiyati faqat shaxsiy va unchalik shaffof bo'lmasa ham, baribir katta.» «Buni oqsoqol aytdimi?» — so'radi Olga. «Ha, shunday dedi», javob berdi K. «Buni Barnabasga aytaman, — dedi Olga tezda, — bu uni juda ruhlantiradi.» «Lekin unga ruhlantirish kerak emas, — dedi K., — uni ruhlantirish unga haqsan, faqat avvalgi yo'lingda davom etaver, deyish demakdir, lekin aynan shu yo'l bilan u hech qachon hech narsaga erisha olmaydi. Ko'zlari bog'langan odamni mato orqali tikilishga qanchalik ruhlantirmagin, u baribir hech qachon hech narsani ko'rmaydi; faqat undan matoni olsang, ko'ra oladi. Barnabasga ruhlantirish emas, yordam kerak.

paras.en: Just think: up there are the authorities in their inextricable vastness — I believed I had approximate ideas of them before I came here; how childish all that was! — there, then, are the authorities, and Barnabas confronts them, nobody else, only he, pitiably alone; too much honour still for him if he doesn't stay crouched all his life, lost, in a dark corner of the offices.' 'Don't believe, K.,' said Olga, 'that we underestimate the difficulty of the task Barnabas has taken on. We don't lack reverence for the authorities — you said so yourself.' 'But it's misguided reverence,' said K. 'Reverence in the wrong place; such reverence degrades its object. Can it still be called reverence when Barnabas misuses the gift of admission to that room to spend his days there idly, or when he comes down and suspects and belittles those before whom he has just been trembling, or when out of despair or tiredness he doesn't deliver letters at once and doesn't pass on messages entrusted to him at once? That surely isn't reverence any more. But the reproach goes further; it goes against you too, Olga; I can't spare you it. Although you believe you revere the authorities, you sent Barnabas into the Castle in all his youth and weakness and forlornness — or at least you didn't hold him back.'
paras.uz: O'ylab ko'r: u yerda, tepada o'zining chigal ulug'vorligi bilan idora — men bu yerga kelishdan oldin u haqida taxminiy tasavvurga egaman deb o'ylagan edim, bularning hammasi qanchalik bolalarcha edi — demak, u yerda idora va unga qarshi Barnabas chiqadi, boshqa hech kim emas, faqat u, achinarli darajada yolg'iz; agar u butun umr idoralarning qorong'i burchagida bedarak yo'qolib, bukchayib qolmasa, bu ham uning uchun ortiqcha sharaf.» «Ishonma, K., — dedi Olga, — Barnabas o'z zimmasiga olgan vazifaning og'irligini biz yengil baholaymiz deb. Bizda idoraga nisbatan ehtirom yetishmaydi deb bo'lmaydi, buni o'zing aytding.» «Lekin bu adashgan ehtirom, — dedi K., — noto'g'ri joydagi ehtirom, bunday ehtirom o'z obyektini kamsitadi. Agar Barnabas o'sha xonaga kirish in'omini u yerda kunlarni bekor o'tkazish uchun suiiste'mol qilsa, yoki pastga tushib, hozirgina oldida titragan odamlarni gumon qilib, kamsitsa, yoki umidsizlik yoki charchoqdan xatlarni darhol yetkazmasa va unga ishonib topshirilgan xabarlarni darhol aytmasa, buni hali ham ehtirom deb atash mumkinmi? Bu, ehtimol, endi ehtirom emas. Lekin ta'na bundan ham uzoqqa boradi, senga ham qaratilgan, Olga; uni sendan ayay olmayman. Sen idoraga ehtiromim bor deb ishonsang ham, Barnabasni butun yoshligi, zaifligi va yolg'izligi bilan Qasrga yubording yoki hech bo'lmaganda ushlab qolmading.»

paras.en: 'The reproach you make me,' said Olga, 'I've made myself too, always. Not, admittedly, that I sent Barnabas into the Castle — I didn't send him, he went himself; but I ought to have held him back by every means — by force, by cunning, by persuasion. I ought to have held him back; but if today were that day, that day of decision, and I felt Barnabas's need, our family's need, as I did then and do today, and if Barnabas again, clearly conscious of all the responsibility and danger, freed himself from me smiling and gently in order to go — I wouldn't hold him back today either, despite all the experiences of the time since; and I believe that you too, in my place, could do no other. You don't know our need; that's why you do us an injustice, and above all Barnabas. We had more hope then than today, but our hope wasn't great even then; only our need was great, and has remained so. Hasn't Frieda told you anything about us, then?' 'Only hints,' said K., 'nothing definite; but even your name upsets her.' 'And the landlady hasn't told you anything either?' 'No, nothing.' 'And nobody else?' 'Nobody.' 'Of course — how could anyone tell anything? Everyone knows something about us — either the truth, as far as it's accessible to people, or at least some rumour, taken over or mostly made up themselves — and everyone thinks of us more than necessary, but nobody will tell it straight out; they're afraid to take these things into their mouths. And they're right in that. It's hard to bring it out, even to you, K.; and isn't it possible, too, that once you've heard it you'll go away and want to know nothing more of us, however little it seems to concern you?
paras.uz: «Sen menga qilayotgan ta'nani, — dedi Olga, — men ham azaldan o'zimga qilib kelaman. To'g'ri, Barnabasni Qasrga yuborganim uchun meni ayblash mumkin emas, men uni yubormaganman, u o'zi ketgan; lekin uni har qanday yo'l bilan — kuch bilan, hiyla bilan, ko'ndirish bilan — ushlab qolishim kerak edi. Uni ushlab qolishim kerak edi, lekin agar bugun o'sha kun, o'sha hal qiluvchi kun bo'lganida va men Barnabasning muhtojligini, oilamizning muhtojligini o'shandagidek va bugungidek his qilganimda va agar Barnabas yana barcha mas'uliyat va xavfni aniq anglagan holda jilmayib va muloyimlik bilan ketish uchun mendan ajralganida, oradan o'tgan barcha tajribalarga qaramay, men uni bugun ham ushlab qolmasdim va menimcha, sen ham mening o'rnimda boshqacha qila olmasding. Sen bizning muhtojligimizni bilmaysan, shuning uchun bizga, ayniqsa Barnabasga nohaqlik qilyapsan. O'shanda bizda bugungidan ko'ra ko'proq umid bor edi, lekin o'shanda ham umidimiz katta emas edi, faqat muhtojligimiz katta edi va shundayligicha qoldi. Nahotki Frida senga biz haqimizda hech narsa aytmagan bo'lsa?» «Faqat ishoralar, — dedi K., — aniq hech narsa; lekin sizlarning ismingizning o'zi ham uni hayajonga soladi.» «Beka ham hech narsa aytmadimi?» «Yo'q, hech narsa.» «Boshqa hech kim ham?» «Hech kim.» «Albatta, kim ham aytib bera olardi. Har kim biz haqimizda nimanidir biladi — yo odamlarga ochiq bo'lgan darajadagi haqiqatni, yo hech bo'lmaganda boshqalardan olingan yoki ko'pincha o'zi to'qib chiqargan qandaydir mish-mishni; har kim biz haqimizda kerak bo'lganidan ko'proq o'ylaydi, lekin to'g'ridan-to'g'ri hech kim aytmaydi, bu narsalarni tilga olishdan tortinishadi. Bunda ular haq. Buni aytish qiyin, hatto senga ham, K.; axir uni eshitgach, u seni qanchalik kam qiziqtirgandek ko'rinmasin, ketib qolishing va biz haqimizda boshqa hech narsa bilishni istamasliging ham mumkin emasmi?

paras.en: Then we'll have lost you — you, who now, I confess, mean almost more to me than Barnabas's Castle service so far. And yet — this contradiction has been tormenting me all evening — you must learn it, for otherwise you'll get no overall view of our situation, and you would remain unjust to Barnabas, which would especially pain me; the complete unity that is necessary would be lacking, and you could neither help us nor accept our help — the extraordinary help. But there's still one question: do you want to know it at all?' 'Why do you ask that?' said K. 'If it's necessary I want to know it; but why do you ask like that?' 'Out of superstition,' said Olga. 'You'll be drawn into our affairs — innocently, not much more guilty than Barnabas.' 'Tell me quickly,' said K. 'I'm not afraid. And you're making it worse than it is with a woman's timidity.' 'Judge for yourself,' said Olga. 'Besides, it sounds very simple; one doesn't understand at once how it can have great significance. There's an important official at the Castle called Sortini.' 'I've already heard of him,' said K. 'He was involved in my appointment.' 'I don't think so,' said Olga. 'Sortini hardly appears in public. Aren't you confusing him with Sordini, with a d?' 'You're right,' said K. 'It was Sordini.' 'Yes,' said Olga, 'Sordini is very well known, one of the most industrious officials, much talked about; Sortini, on the other hand, is very retiring and a stranger to most people.
paras.uz: Unda biz seni yo'qotamiz — tan olaman, hozir sen men uchun Barnabasning hozirgacha bo'lgan Qasr xizmatidan ham deyarli ko'proq narsani anglatasan. Shunga qaramay — bu qarama-qarshilik meni butun kech qiynayapti — sen buni bilishing kerak, aks holda bizning ahvolimiz haqida umumiy tasavvur hosil qilmaysan, Barnabasga nisbatan nohaq bo'lib qolasan — bu menga ayniqsa og'ir botardi; bizda zarur bo'lgan to'liq hamjihatlik bo'lmasdi va sen na bizga yordam bera olarding, na bizning yordamimizni — favqulodda yordamni — qabul qila olarding. Lekin yana bir savol qoladi: sen umuman buni bilishni istaysanmi?» «Nega buni so'rayapsan? — dedi K. — Agar zarur bo'lsa, bilishni istayman; lekin nega bunday so'rayapsan?» «Xurofot tufayli, — dedi Olga. — Sen bizning ishlarimizga tortilasan, aybsiz, Barnabasdan unchalik ko'p aybli emas.» «Tezroq aytib ber, — dedi K., — men qo'rqmayman. Sen ayollarcha qo'rqoqlik bilan uni bo'lganidan ham yomonroq qilyapsan.» «O'zing hukm qil, — dedi Olga, — aytgancha, bu juda oddiy eshitiladi, uning qanday qilib katta ahamiyatga ega bo'lishi mumkinligini darhol tushunmaysan. Qasrda Sortini degan katta amaldor bor.» «Men u haqda allaqachon eshitganman, — dedi K., — u mening chaqirilishimda ishtirok etgan.» «Menimcha, unday emas, — dedi Olga, — Sortini omma oldida deyarli ko'rinmaydi. Sen uni «d» harfi bilan yoziladigan Sordini bilan adashtirmayapsanmi?» «Haqsan, — dedi K., — Sordini edi.» «Ha, — dedi Olga, — Sordini juda mashhur, eng tirishqoq amaldorlardan biri, u haqda ko'p gapirishadi; Sortini esa aksincha, juda odamovi va ko'pchilikka notanish.

paras.en: More than three years ago I saw him for the first and last time. It was on the third of July, at a festival of the fire brigade association; the Castle had taken part too and had donated a new fire engine. Sortini, who is said to deal partly with fire brigade matters (but perhaps he was only there as a deputy — the officials mostly deputise for each other, and so it's hard to recognise the competence of this official or that), took part in the handing over of the engine. Of course others had come from the Castle too, officials and servants, and Sortini, as befits his character, was right in the background. He's a small, frail, thoughtful gentleman; one thing that struck everyone who noticed him at all was the way his forehead creased: all the creases — and there were a lot of them, although he's certainly not more than forty — ran fan-like straight across his forehead to the bridge of his nose; I've never seen anything like it. Well, that was the festival. We, Amalia and I, had been looking forward to it for weeks; our Sunday clothes had partly been newly made over; Amalia's dress especially was beautiful, the white blouse puffed up high in front, one row of lace above another — mother had lent all her lace for it. I was envious then and cried half the night before the festival. Only when in the morning the landlady of the Bridge Inn came to look us over …' 'The landlady of the Bridge Inn?' asked K.
paras.uz: Uch yildan ko'proq vaqt oldin men uni birinchi va oxirgi marta ko'rdim. Bu uchinchi iyulda, o't o'chiruvchilar jamiyatining bayramida edi; Qasr ham ishtirok etib, yangi o't o'chirish nasosini sovg'a qilgan edi. Qisman o't o'chirish ishlari bilan shug'ullanadi deyiladigan Sortini (lekin balki u faqat birovning o'rnida kelgandir — amaldorlar ko'pincha bir-birining o'rnini bosishadi, shuning uchun u yoki bu amaldorning vakolatini bilish qiyin) nasosni topshirishda ishtirok etdi; albatta, Qasrdan boshqalar ham — amaldorlar va xizmatkorlar kelgan edi, Sortini esa o'z xarakteriga mos ravishda butunlay orqa tomonda edi. U pakana, nimjon, o'ychan janob; uni umuman payqagan hammaning e'tiborini tortgan narsa — uning peshonasi qanday ajinlanishi edi: barcha ajinlar — ular juda ko'p edi, garchi u, albatta, qirq yoshdan oshmagan bo'lsa ham — peshonasi bo'ylab to'g'ri yelpig'ichdek burun tepasiga qarab cho'zilgan edi, men bunday narsani hech qachon ko'rmaganman. Xo'sh, mana o'sha bayram. Biz, Amaliya va men, unga haftalar davomida intiqib kutgan edik, bayram kiyimlarimiz qisman yangidan tikib tuzatilgan edi, ayniqsa Amaliyaning ko'ylagi chiroyli edi: oq bluzkasining oldi baland ko'pchigan, bir qator to'r ikkinchisining ustida — onamiz buning uchun barcha to'rlarini qarz bergan edi; men o'shanda hasad qildim va bayramdan oldin tunning yarmini yig'lab o'tkazdim. Faqat ertalab «Ko'prik yonidagi» mehmonxonaning bekasi bizni ko'rgani kelganida…» «Ko'prik yonidagi mehmonxonaning bekasimi?» — so'radi K.

paras.en: 'Yes,' said Olga, 'she was very friendly with us. So she came, had to admit that Amalia had the advantage, and therefore, to calm me, lent me her own necklace of Bohemian garnets. But then, when we were ready to go out and Amalia stood in front of me, and we all admired her, and father said, "Today, mark my words, Amalia will get a fiancé," then — I don't know why — I took off the necklace, my pride, and hung it round Amalia's neck, not envious any more at all. I simply bowed before her victory, and I believed everyone must bow before her; perhaps what surprised us then was that she looked different from usual, for she wasn't really beautiful; but her gloomy gaze, which she has kept in this way ever since, went high over our heads, and one almost actually, involuntarily, bowed before her. Everyone noticed it, Lasemann and his wife too, who came to fetch us.' 'Lasemann?' asked K. 'Yes, Lasemann,' said Olga. 'We were very highly respected, after all, and the festival couldn't well have begun without us, for example, because father was third drill instructor of the fire brigade.' 'Father was still so vigorous?' asked K. 'Father?' asked Olga, as though she didn't quite understand. 'Three years ago he was still, in a way, a young man; once at a fire in the Herrenhof, for instance, he carried an official, the heavy Galater, out on his back at a run.
paras.uz: «Ha, — dedi Olga, — u biz bilan juda do'st edi; xullas, u keldi, Amaliya ustun ekanini tan olishga majbur bo'ldi va shuning uchun meni tinchlantirish maqsadida menga o'zining bogemiya granatidan qilingan marjonini qarz berdi. Lekin keyin biz chiqishga tayyor bo'lganimizda, Amaliya oldimda turganda, biz hammamiz unga hayratlanib qaraganimizda va otamiz: «Esingizda bo'lsin, bugun Amaliya kuyovli bo'ladi», deganida, men — nega ekanini bilmayman — faxrim bo'lgan marjonni yechib, uni Amaliyaning bo'yniga taqdim, endi umuman hasad qilmay. Men shunchaki uning g'alabasi oldida bosh egdim va hamma uning oldida bosh egishi kerak deb ishondim; balki o'shanda u odatdagidan boshqacha ko'ringani bizni hayratga solgandir, chunki aslida u chiroyli emas edi; lekin o'shandan beri shu tarzda saqlab qolgan g'amgin nigohi bizning boshimiz ustidan baland o'tib ketardi va uning oldida deyarli rostdan ham, beixtiyor bosh egarding. Buni hamma payqadi, bizni olib ketgani kelgan Lazemann va uning xotini ham.» «Lazemannmi?» — so'radi K. «Ha, Lazemann, — dedi Olga. — Biz axir juda obro'li edik, masalan, bayram bizsiz yaxshi boshlana olmasdi, chunki otamiz o't o'chiruvchilarning uchinchi mashq rahbari edi.» «Otang hali shunchalik baquvvatmidi?» — so'radi K. «Otammi? — so'radi Olga go'yo yaxshi tushunmagandek. — Uch yil oldin u hali qaysidir ma'noda yosh odam edi; masalan, Herrenhofdagi yong'inda u bir amaldorni — og'ir Galaterni orqasiga ortib, yugurib olib chiqqan.

paras.en: I was there myself; there wasn't really any danger of fire, only the dry wood beside a stove began to smoke, but Galater got frightened, called for help from the window, the fire brigade came, and my father had to carry him out, although the fire had already been put out. Well, Galater is a man who moves with difficulty and has to be careful in such cases. I'm only telling it because of father; not much more than three years have passed since then, and now look how he sits there.' Only now did K. see that Amalia was already back in the room, but she was far away at their parents' table; she was feeding their mother, who couldn't move her rheumatic arms, and at the same time telling their father to be patient a little longer about his food; she would come to him at once to feed him too. But her admonition had no success, for their father, very greedy to get at his soup, overcame his physical weakness and tried now to suck the soup from the spoon, now to drink it straight from the plate, and growled angrily when neither worked: the spoon was long since empty before it reached his mouth, and it was never his mouth but always only his drooping moustache that dipped into the soup, and it dripped and sprayed in all directions except into his mouth.
paras.uz: Men o'zim u yerda edim; aslida yong'in xavfi yo'q edi, faqat pech yonidagi quruq o'tin tutay boshlagan edi, lekin Galater qo'rqib ketib, derazadan yordam so'rab qichqirdi, o't o'chiruvchilar keldi va olov allaqachon o'chirilgan bo'lsa ham, otam uni olib chiqishga majbur bo'ldi. Xo'sh, Galater qiyin qimirlaydigan odam va bunday hollarda ehtiyot bo'lishi kerak. Men buni faqat otam uchun aytyapman, o'shandan beri uch yildan unchalik ko'p vaqt o'tmadi, endi qara, u yerda qanday o'tiribdi.» Faqat endi K. Amaliya allaqachon yana xonada ekanini ko'rdi, lekin u ancha uzoqda, ota-onasining stoli yonida edi; u u yerda revmatizmdan qo'llarini qimirlata olmaydigan onasini ovqatlantirar va ayni paytda otasiga ovqat borasida yana biroz sabr qilishni, hozir uni ham ovqatlantirish uchun yoniga kelishini aytardi. Lekin uning nasihati natija bermadi, chunki sho'rvasiga yetishga juda ochko'z bo'lgan otasi jismoniy zaifligini yengib, sho'rvani goh qoshiqdan ho'plashga, goh to'g'ridan-to'g'ri likopchadan ichishga urinar va ikkalasi ham muvaffaqiyatsiz bo'lganda jahl bilan to'ng'illardi: qoshiq og'ziga yetmasdanoq allaqachon bo'shab qolardi va sho'rvaga hech qachon og'zi emas, doim faqat osilib turgan mo'ylovi botardi va sho'rva og'zidan boshqa hamma tomonga tomchilab, sachrardi.

paras.en: 'Three years have made that of him?' asked K.; but he still felt no pity for the old people and for that whole corner of the family table, only repugnance. 'Three years,' said Olga slowly, 'or, more exactly, a few hours of a festival. The festival was in a meadow outside the village by the stream; there was already a great crowd when we arrived; lots of people had come from the neighbouring villages too; one was quite bewildered by the noise. First, of course, father led us to the fire engine; he laughed with joy when he saw it; a new engine made him happy; he began to feel it and explain it to us; he tolerated no contradiction and no reserve from the others; if there was something to look at under the engine, we all had to bend down and almost crawl under it; Barnabas, who resisted at the time, got a beating for it. Only Amalia paid no attention to the engine; she stood upright beside it in her beautiful dress, and nobody dared say anything to her; I sometimes ran to her and took her arm, but she said nothing. I still can't explain to myself today how it came about that we stood in front of the engine so long and only noticed Sortini when father tore himself away from it — Sortini, who had evidently been leaning against one of the engine's levers behind it all the time. There was a terrible noise then, of course, not just as usual at festivals.
paras.uz: «Uch yil uni shunday qilib qo'ydimi?» — so'radi K., lekin u hamon qariyalarga va u yerdagi oila stolining butun burchagiga nisbatan achinish emas, faqat jirkanish his qilardi. «Uch yil, — dedi Olga sekin, — yoki aniqrog'i, bayramning bir necha soati. Bayram qishloq oldidagi soy bo'yidagi o'tloqda edi; biz yetib kelganimizda allaqachon katta olomon bor edi, qo'shni qishloqlardan ham ko'p xalq kelgan edi, shovqindan butunlay gangib qolarding. Avvaliga, albatta, otamiz bizni o't o'chirish nasosi oldiga olib bordi; uni ko'rib quvonchdan kuldi, yangi nasos uni baxtiyor qildi; u uni paypaslab, bizga tushuntira boshladi, boshqalarning e'tirozi va tortinishiga chidamadi; agar nasos ostida ko'radigan narsa bo'lsa, hammamiz engashib, deyarli nasos ostiga emaklab kirishimiz kerak edi; o'shanda qarshilik ko'rsatgan Barnabas shuning uchun kaltak yedi. Faqat Amaliya nasos bilan qiziqmadi, chiroyli ko'ylagida yonida tik turdi va hech kim unga biror narsa deyishga jur'at etmadi; men ba'zan uning oldiga yugurib, qo'ltig'idan oldim, lekin u jim turdi. Bugun ham qanday qilib nasos oldida shunchalik uzoq turib qolganimizni va faqat otamiz undan ajralgandagina, aftidan, butun vaqt davomida nasos orqasida uning dastagiga suyanib turgan Sortinini payqaganimizni tushuntira olmayman. To'g'ri, o'shanda dahshatli shovqin edi, bayramlarda odatdagidek emas.

paras.en: For the Castle had also given the fire brigade some trumpets, special instruments on which with the slightest effort — a child could do it — one could produce the wildest sounds; when you heard them you thought the Turks were already here, and you couldn't get used to it; at every fresh blast you started again. And because they were new trumpets everyone wanted to try them, and because it was a popular festival, after all, it was allowed. Right around us — perhaps Amalia had attracted them — there were several such trumpeters; it was hard to keep one's senses together, and if on top of that, at father's command, one was supposed to pay attention to the engine, that was the utmost one could manage; and so Sortini, whom we hadn't known before at all, escaped us for an unusually long time. "There's Sortini," Lasemann at last whispered to father — I was standing beside him. Father bowed deeply and excitedly signalled to us to bow too. Without knowing him until then, father had always revered Sortini as an expert in fire brigade matters and had often spoken of him at home; so it was very surprising and significant for us too to see Sortini now in reality.
paras.uz: Gap shundaki, Qasr o't o'chiruvchilarga yana bir nechta karnay ham sovg'a qilgan edi — maxsus asboblar, ularda eng kichik kuch bilan — buni bola ham qila olardi — eng vahshiy tovushlarni chiqarish mumkin edi; buni eshitganingda turklar allaqachon kelib qolgandek tuyulardi va bunga ko'nika olmasding, har yangi chalinishda yana cho'chib tushardingi. Yangi karnaylar bo'lgani uchun hamma ularni sinab ko'rishni istardi, xalq bayrami bo'lgani uchun esa bunga ruxsat berishdi. Aynan bizning atrofimizda — balki ularni Amaliya jalb qilgandir — bir nechta shunday karnaychilar bor edi; bunda hushni yig'ib turish qiyin edi, agar buning ustiga otamizning buyrug'iga ko'ra nasosga ham e'tibor berish kerak bo'lsa, bu qo'lingdan keladigan eng oxirgi narsa edi; shuning uchun avval umuman tanimagan Sortini bizning ko'zimizdan g'ayrioddiy uzoq vaqt chetda qoldi. «Ana Sortini», — deb pichirladi nihoyat Lazemann otamizga — men yonida turgan edim. Otamiz chuqur ta'zim qildi va hayajon bilan bizga ham ta'zim qilishga ishora berdi. Uni hozirgacha tanimasa ham, otamiz azaldan Sortinini o't o'chirish ishlarining mutaxassisi sifatida hurmat qilar va uyda u haqda tez-tez gapirardi, shuning uchun endi Sortinini haqiqatda ko'rish biz uchun ham juda kutilmagan va ahamiyatli edi.

paras.en: But Sortini paid no attention to us — that wasn't a peculiarity of Sortini's; most officials seem indifferent in public — and besides he was tired; only his official duty kept him down here; it isn't the worst officials who find precisely such representative duties particularly oppressive. Other officials and servants, since they were there anyway, mingled with the people; but he stayed by the engine, and anyone who tried to approach him with some request or flattery he drove away with his silence. So it came about that he noticed us even later than we noticed him. Only when we bowed respectfully and father tried to apologise for us did he look over at us, looked from one to the other in turn, tiredly; it was as though he sighed that beside one there was always yet another, until he stopped at Amalia, to whom he had to look up, for she was much taller than he. Then he started, jumped over the shaft to be nearer to Amalia; we misunderstood it at first and all wanted to approach him, led by father, but he held us back with raised hand and then waved to us to go. That was all. We teased Amalia a lot afterwards about having now really found a fiancé; in our foolishness we were very merry the whole afternoon; but Amalia was more silent than ever.
paras.uz: Lekin Sortini biz bilan qiziqmadi — bu Sortinining o'ziga xos xususiyati emas edi, ko'pchilik amaldorlar omma oldida befarqdek ko'rinadi — bundan tashqari, u charchagan edi, uni bu yerda, pastda faqat xizmat burchi ushlab turardi; aynan bunday vakillik burchlarini ayniqsa og'ir his qiladigan amaldorlar eng yomonlari emas. Boshqa amaldorlar va xizmatkorlar, baribir kelib qolishganidan keyin, xalq orasiga aralashib ketishdi; u esa nasos yonida qoldi va qandaydir iltimos yoki xushomad bilan unga yaqinlashmoqchi bo'lgan har kimni sukuti bilan haydab yubordi. Shunday qilib, u bizni biz uni payqaganimizdan ham kechroq payqadi. Faqat biz ehtirom bilan ta'zim qilganimizda va otamiz bizni uzrli qilishga urinanida, u bizga qaradi, birma-bir, charchoq bilan birimizdan ikkinchimizga ko'z yugurtirdi; go'yo u birining yonida doim yana ikkinchisi borligidan xo'rsinayotgandek edi; toki u Amaliyada to'xtadi — unga tepaga qarab qarashi kerak edi, chunki u undan ancha baland edi. Shunda u seskanib, Amaliyaga yaqinroq bo'lish uchun aravaning shotisi ustidan sakrab o'tdi; biz avval buni noto'g'ri tushunib, otamiz boshchiligida hammamiz unga yaqinlashmoqchi bo'ldik, lekin u qo'lini ko'tarib bizni to'xtatdi va keyin ketishimizga ishora qildi. Hammasi shu. Keyin biz Amaliyani endi rostdan ham kuyov topding deb ko'p mazax qildik; nodonligimizda butun tushdan keyingi vaqt juda quvnoq edik; Amaliya esa har qachongidan ham jimroq edi.

paras.en: "She's fallen head over heels in love with Sortini," said Brunswick, who is always a bit coarse and has no understanding for natures like Amalia's; but this time his remark seemed to us almost right. We were altogether crazy that day, and all of us except Amalia were as if stunned by the sweet Castle wine when we came home after midnight.' 'And Sortini?' asked K. 'Yes, Sortini,' said Olga. 'I saw Sortini several more times in passing during the festival; he sat on the shaft with his arms crossed over his chest and stayed like that until the Castle carriage came to fetch him. He didn't even go to the fire brigade drills, in which father — precisely in the hope that Sortini was watching — distinguished himself above all the men of his age.' 'And did you hear nothing more of him?' asked K. 'You seem to have great reverence for Sortini.' 'Yes, reverence,' said Olga, 'yes; and we did hear of him again. The next morning we were woken from our wine-sleep by a cry from Amalia; the others fell back into bed at once, but I was wide awake and ran to Amalia. She was standing at the window holding a letter in her hand that a man had just handed to her through the window; the man was still waiting for an answer.
paras.uz: «U Sortiniga telbalarcha oshiq bo'lib qolibdi», dedi har doim biroz qo'pol va Amaliya kabi tabiatlarni tushunmaydigan Brunsvik; lekin bu safar uning gapi bizga deyarli to'g'ri tuyuldi; o'sha kuni biz umuman telba edik va yarim tundan keyin uyga qaytganimizda, Amaliyadan tashqari hammamiz Qasrning shirin sharobidan go'yo bexush edik.» «Sortini-chi?» — so'radi K. «Ha, Sortini, — dedi Olga, — bayram davomida Sortinini yo'l-yo'lakay yana bir necha marta ko'rdim; u qo'llarini ko'kragida chalishtirib, aravaning shotisida o'tirar va Qasr aravasi uni olib ketgani kelguncha shunday qoldi. U hatto o't o'chirish mashqlariga ham bormadi — o'shanda otamiz aynan Sortini tomosha qilyapti degan umidda o'z tengdoshlari orasida hammadan ajralib turgan edi.» «U haqda boshqa hech narsa eshitmadingizmi? — so'radi K. — Sening Sortiniga katta ehtiroming borga o'xshaydi.» «Ha, ehtirom, — dedi Olga, — ha, u haqda yana eshitdik ham. Ertasi kuni ertalab bizni sharob uyqusidan Amaliyaning qichqirig'i uyg'otdi; boshqalar darhol yana to'shaklariga yiqilishdi, men esa butunlay uyg'oq edim va Amaliyaning oldiga yugurdim. U deraza oldida turib, qo'lida bir odam hozirgina derazadan uzatgan xatni ushlab turardi; o'sha odam hali ham javob kutib turardi.

paras.en: Amalia had already read the letter — it was short — and was holding it in her limply hanging hand; how I loved her whenever she was so tired! I knelt down beside her and read the letter like that. Hardly had I finished when Amalia, after a short glance at me, took it up again, but couldn't bring herself to read it any more; she tore it up, threw the scraps in the face of the man outside and shut the window. That was that decisive morning. I call it decisive, but every moment of the previous afternoon was just as decisive.' 'And what was in the letter?' asked K. 'Yes, I haven't told you that yet,' said Olga. 'The letter was from Sortini; it was addressed to the girl with the garnet necklace. I can't repeat its content. It was a summons to come to him at the Herrenhof, and Amalia was to come at once, for Sortini had to leave in half an hour. The letter was couched in the vilest expressions, which I had never heard before and only half guessed from the context. Anyone who didn't know Amalia and had read only this letter would have had to consider the girl to whom someone had dared to write like that dishonoured, even if she had never been touched at all. And it was no love letter; there was not one tender word in it; rather, Sortini was evidently angry that the sight of Amalia had seized him and kept him from his business.
paras.uz: Amaliya xatni — u qisqa edi — allaqachon o'qib bo'lgan va uni bo'shashib osilib turgan qo'lida ushlab turardi; u har doim shunchalik charchaganda men uni qanchalik sevardim. Men uning yonida tiz cho'kdim va xatni shunday o'qidim. Men tugatishim bilan Amaliya menga bir zum qarab, uni yana oldi, lekin endi uni o'qishga o'zini majbur qila olmadi, yirtib tashladi, parchalarini tashqaridagi odamning yuziga otdi va derazani yopdi. Bu o'sha hal qiluvchi tong edi. Men uni hal qiluvchi deyman, lekin oldingi tushdan keyingi vaqtning har bir lahzasi ham xuddi shunday hal qiluvchi edi.» «Xatda nima yozilgan edi?» — so'radi K. «Ha, buni hali aytmadim, — dedi Olga. — Xat Sortinidan edi, u granat marjonli qizga atalgan edi. Mazmunini takrorlay olmayman. Bu Herrenhofga uning oldiga kelishga chaqiriq edi, Amaliya darhol kelishi kerak edi, chunki yarim soatdan keyin Sortini jo'nab ketishi kerak edi. Xat men hech qachon eshitmagan va faqat kontekstdan yarim-yorti taxmin qilgan eng tuban iboralar bilan yozilgan edi. Amaliyani tanimaydigan va faqat shu xatni o'qigan har kim kimdir shunday yozishga jur'at etgan qizni, unga umuman tegilmagan bo'lsa ham, nomusi toptalgan deb hisoblashi kerak edi. Bu sevgi xati ham emas edi, unda birorta erkalovchi so'z yo'q edi, aksincha, Sortini Amaliyani ko'rish uni larzaga solib, ishlaridan chalg'itgani uchun jahli chiqqan ekani ko'rinib turardi.

paras.en: We worked it out later that Sortini had probably wanted to drive back to the Castle that very evening, had stayed in the village only because of Amalia, and in the morning, full of anger that even in the night he had not managed to forget Amalia, had written the letter. Faced with the letter, anyone — even the most cold-blooded — would have been outraged at first; but then, with anyone other than Amalia, fear of the wicked, threatening tone would probably have prevailed; with Amalia it remained outrage; she knows no fear, not for herself, not for others. And while I crept back into bed and kept repeating to myself the broken-off final sentence — "So you'll come at once, or —!" — Amalia stayed on the window seat and looked out, as though she were expecting further messengers and was ready to treat each of them like the first.' 'So that's what the officials are like,' said K. hesitantly. 'One finds such specimens among them. What did your father do? I hope he complained vigorously about Sortini to the proper authority, if he didn't prefer the shorter and surer way to the Herrenhof.
paras.uz: Keyin biz buni shunday tushundikki, Sortini, ehtimol, o'sha kechqurunoq Qasrga qaytmoqchi bo'lgan, faqat Amaliya tufayli qishloqda qolgan va ertalab, tunda ham Amaliyani unutolmaganidan g'azablanib, xatni yozgan. Xatga duch kelgan har kim, hatto eng sovuqqoni ham, avval g'azablanishi kerak edi; lekin keyin Amaliyadan boshqa har qanday qizda, ehtimol, yovuz, tahdidli ohangdan qo'rquv ustun kelardi; Amaliyada esa g'azab qoldi, u qo'rquvni bilmaydi — na o'zi uchun, na boshqalar uchun. Men yana to'shakka sudralib kirib, uzilib qolgan oxirgi jumlani o'zimga takrorlab yotganimda: «Demak, darhol kelasan, aks holda…!» — Amaliya deraza tokchasida qolib, tashqariga qaradi, go'yo yana boshqa choparlarni kutayotgandek va har birini birinchisidek kutib olishga tayyordek.» «Demak, amaldorlar shunday ekan, — dedi K. ikkilanib, — ular orasida bunday nusxalar ham uchraydi. Otang nima qildi? Umid qilamanki, agar Herrenhofga qisqaroq va ishonchliroq yo'lni afzal ko'rmagan bo'lsa, tegishli joyga Sortini ustidan qattiq shikoyat qilgandir.

paras.en: The very ugliest thing about the story isn't the insult to Amalia — that could easily have been made good; I don't know why you lay such excessive weight precisely on that. Why should Sortini have exposed Amalia for ever with such a letter? From your account one might believe so, but that's surely not possible; satisfaction could easily have been obtained for Amalia, and in a few days the incident would have been forgotten; Sortini didn't expose Amalia, he exposed himself. So it's Sortini I recoil from — from the possibility that such abuse of power exists. What failed in this case, because it was said plainly and was completely transparent and found in Amalia a superior opponent, may succeed completely in a thousand other cases, in only slightly less favourable circumstances, and may escape every eye — even the eye of the one abused.'
paras.uz: Hikoyaning eng xunuk tomoni axir Amaliyaning haqoratlanishi emas — buni osongina tuzatish mumkin edi; nega sen aynan bunga haddan tashqari katta ahamiyat berayotganingni bilmayman; nega Sortini bunday xat bilan Amaliyani abadiy sharmanda qilgan bo'lishi kerak; sening hikoyangdan shunday deb o'ylash mumkin, lekin aynan bu mumkin emas-ku; Amaliyaga qoniqish berish oson edi va bir necha kundan keyin voqea unutilardi; Sortini Amaliyani emas, o'zini sharmanda qildi. Demak, men Sortinidan, hokimiyatning bunday suiiste'mol qilinishi mumkinligidan cho'chiyman. Bu holatda ochiq-oydin aytilgani, butunlay shaffof bo'lgani va Amaliyada o'zidan ustun raqibni topgani uchun barbod bo'lgan narsa boshqa ming holatda, biroz noqulayroq sharoitlarda butunlay muvaffaqiyatli bo'lishi va har qanday nigohdan, hatto suiiste'mol qilinganning nigohidan ham yashirin qolishi mumkin.»
