chapters.title: 15. The curse
chapters.recap_uz: Olga hal qiluvchi narsa Amaliya Herrenhofga bormagani ekanini aytadi: shu bilan oilaga la'nat tushdi. U Fridani Klamm bilan solishtiradi, K. esa Fridani himoya qiladi va unga ko'p narsa uchun qarzdor ekanini aytadi. Olga voqeadan keyingi kunni eslaydi: do'stlar, mijozlar, shogird Brunsvik oiladan yuz o'giradi; o't o'chiruvchilar boshlig'i Zeeman otadan diplomini qaytarib oladi. Qasr esa jim; hech qanday jazo yo'q, faqat jimlik — va aynan shu eng og'ir jazo bo'ladi.

paras.en: 'Quiet,' said Olga, 'Amalia's looking over.' Amalia had finished feeding their parents and was now undressing their mother; she had just untied her skirt, hung her mother's arms round her own neck, lifted her a little like this, slipped the skirt off and then set her down again gently. Their father, always dissatisfied that their mother was attended to first — which evidently happened only because their mother was even more helpless than he — tried, perhaps also to punish his daughter for her supposed slowness, to undress himself; but although he began with the most unnecessary and easiest thing, the oversized slippers in which his feet were only loosely stuck, he could by no means manage to get them off; with a hoarse rattling he soon had to give up and leaned back stiffly in his chair again.
paras.uz: «Jim, — dedi Olga, — Amaliya bu yoqqa qarayapti.» Amaliya ota-onasini ovqatlantirib bo'lgan va endi onasini yechintirayotgan edi; u endigina uning yubkasini yechgan, onasining qo'llarini o'z bo'yniga osib, uni shu tarzda biroz ko'tarib, yubkasini sirg'atib olgan va keyin uni yana muloyimlik bilan o'tqazib qo'ygan edi. Doim onasiga birinchi xizmat qilinishidan norozi bo'lgan otasi — bu esa, aftidan, faqat onasi undan ham ojizroq bo'lgani uchun shunday bo'lardi — balki qizini go'yoki sekinligi uchun jazolash maqsadida ham o'zi yechinishga urindi; lekin u eng keraksiz va eng oson narsadan — oyoqlari bo'sh tiqilib turgan haddan tashqari katta shippaklardan boshlagan bo'lsa ham, ularni hech qanday yo'l bilan yecha olmadi; u xirillagan ovoz bilan tez orada bundan voz kechishga majbur bo'ldi va yana kursisiga qotib suyandi.

paras.en: 'You don't see the decisive thing,' said Olga. 'You may be right in everything, but the decisive thing was that Amalia didn't go to the Herrenhof. How she had treated the messenger might have passed in itself; that could have been hushed up; but by not going she pronounced the curse on our family, and then, of course, the treatment of the messenger also became something unforgivable — indeed, it was even pushed into the foreground for the public.' 'What!' cried K., and lowered his voice at once, as Olga raised her hands imploringly. 'You, her sister, surely aren't saying that Amalia should have obeyed Sortini and run to the Herrenhof?' 'No,' said Olga, 'may I be protected from such a suspicion; how can you believe that? I know nobody who is so firmly in the right as Amalia in everything she does. If she had gone to the Herrenhof, I'd of course have said she was right just the same; but that she didn't go was heroic. As for me — I confess it to you openly — if I'd got such a letter, I'd have gone. I couldn't have borne the fear of what was to come; only Amalia could do that.
paras.uz: «Sen hal qiluvchi narsani ko'rmayapsan, — dedi Olga, — hamma narsada haq bo'lishing mumkin, lekin hal qiluvchi narsa shu ediki, Amaliya Herrenhofga bormadi; u chopar bilan qanday muomala qilgani o'z-o'zidan o'tib ketishi, uni bosdi-bosdi qilish mumkin edi; lekin bormagani bilan oilamizga la'nat aytildi, endi esa, albatta, chopar bilan muomala ham kechirib bo'lmaydigan narsaga aylandi, ha, hatto omma uchun oldingi o'ringa surildi.» «Qanday! — qichqirdi K. va Olga iltijo bilan qo'llarini ko'targani uchun darhol ovozini pasaytirdi. — Sen, uning singlisi, nahotki Amaliya Sortiniga bo'ysunib, Herrenhofga yugurishi kerak edi demoqchi bo'lsang?» «Yo'q, — dedi Olga, — meni bunday gumondan Xudo asrasin; qanday qilib bunga ishonasan? Men qilgan hamma ishida Amaliyadek shunchalik qat'iy haq bo'lgan hech kimni bilmayman. Agar u Herrenhofga borganida, men, albatta, unga xuddi shunday haq bergan bo'lardim; lekin bormagani — qahramonlik edi. Menga kelsak, ochiq tan olaman: agar men shunday xat olganimda, borgan bo'lardim. Kelajakdagi narsadan qo'rquvga chiday olmasdim, buni faqat Amaliya qila olardi.

paras.en: There were some ways out, after all; another girl, for instance, would have dressed herself up very prettily, and a while would have passed over it, and then she'd have come to the Herrenhof and found that Sortini had already gone — perhaps that he'd driven off right after sending the messenger, something that is even very likely, for the gentlemen's whims are fleeting. But Amalia did nothing of the kind, nothing like it; she was too deeply insulted and answered without reservation. If only she'd obeyed somehow for appearance's sake, only just crossed the threshold of the Herrenhof at the time, the doom could have been averted; we have very clever advocates here, who know how to make anything you like out of nothing; but in this case there wasn't even the favourable nothing; on the contrary, there was the degradation of Sortini's letter and the insult to the messenger.' 'But what doom, then,' said K., 'what advocates? Surely Amalia couldn't be accused, or even punished, because of Sortini's criminal conduct?' 'Yes, she could,' said Olga, 'though not, of course, after a regular trial, and they didn't punish her directly either; but they did punish her in another way, her and our whole family; and how heavy this punishment is you're probably beginning to see.
paras.uz: Axir ba'zi chiqish yo'llari bor edi: boshqa qiz, masalan, chiroyli yasanib olardi, buning ustida biroz vaqt o'tardi, keyin Herrenhofga kelib, Sortini allaqachon ketganini — balki choparni yuborgandan keyin darhol jo'nab ketganini — bilib olardi; bu hatto juda ehtimoldan, chunki janoblarning injiqliklari o'tkinchi. Lekin Amaliya bunday qilmadi, shunga o'xshash hech narsa qilmadi, u juda chuqur haqoratlangan edi va hech bir shartsiz javob berdi. Qaniydi u qandaydir ko'rinish uchun bo'ysunsa, faqat o'sha paytda Herrenhof ostonasidan o'tsa, falokatning oldini olish mumkin edi; bizda bu yerda hech narsadan xohlagan narsani yasashni biladigan juda aqlli advokatlar bor; lekin bu holatda hatto qulay «hech narsa» ham yo'q edi; aksincha, Sortini xatining tubanligi va chopar haqorati bor edi.» «Lekin qanday falokat, — dedi K., — qanday advokatlar; Sortinining jinoiy xatti-harakati uchun Amaliyani ayblash yoki hatto jazolash mumkin emas edi-ku?» «Mumkin edi, — dedi Olga, — to'g'ri, qonuniy sud jarayonidan keyin emas, uni to'g'ridan-to'g'ri jazolashmadi ham, lekin uni boshqa yo'l bilan jazolashdi — uni va butun oilamizni; bu jazo qanchalik og'ir ekanini sen endi, ehtimol, tushuna boshlayapsan.

paras.en: To you it seems unjust and monstrous; that's an opinion quite isolated in the village; it's very favourable to us and ought to comfort us, and so it would, if it didn't plainly go back to errors. I can easily prove that to you. Forgive me if I speak of Frieda in doing so, but between Frieda and Klamm — apart from how it turned out in the end — something quite similar went on as between Amalia and Sortini; and yet, though you may have been shocked at first, you now find it right. And that isn't habit; one can't become so blunted by habit when it's a question of simple judgement; it's merely the casting off of errors.' 'No, Olga,' said K., 'I don't know why you drag Frieda into the matter; the case would be quite different; don't mix up such fundamentally different things, and go on with your story.' 'Please,' said Olga, 'don't hold it against me if I insist on the comparison; it's a remnant of errors, concerning Frieda too, if you believe you have to defend her against a comparison. She doesn't need defending at all, only praising. If I compare the cases, I'm not saying they're the same; they're related to each other like white and black, and white is Frieda.
paras.uz: Senga bu adolatsiz va dahshatli tuyuladi; bu qishloqda butunlay yolg'iz fikr, u biz uchun juda qulay va bizni yupatishi kerak edi; agar u aniq xatolarga asoslanmaganida, shunday bo'lardi ham. Buni senga osongina isbotlay olaman; bunda Frida haqida gapirsam, kechir, lekin Frida bilan Klamm o'rtasida — oxir-oqibat qanday bo'lganidan tashqari — Amaliya bilan Sortini o'rtasidagiga juda o'xshash narsa bo'lgan; shunga qaramay, avvaliga cho'chigan bo'lsang ham, endi buni to'g'ri deb hisoblaysan. Bu ko'nikish emas, oddiy baho berish haqida gap ketganda ko'nikish bilan bunchalik o'tmaslashib bo'lmaydi; bu shunchaki xatolardan voz kechish.» «Yo'q, Olga, — dedi K., — nega Fridani bu ishga aralashtirayotganingni bilmayman, uning holati butunlay boshqacha bo'lardi; tubdan farq qiladigan narsalarni bunday aralashtirma va hikoyangni davom ettir.» «Iltimos, — dedi Olga, — agar solishtirishda turib olsam, xafa bo'lma; agar sen Fridani solishtirishdan himoya qilishing kerak deb hisoblasang, bu ham Frida borasidagi xatolarning qoldig'i. Uni umuman himoya qilish kerak emas, faqat maqtash kerak. Agar holatlarni solishtirsam, ular bir xil demayman; ular bir-biriga oq va qora kabi munosabatda, oq esa — Frida.

paras.en: At worst one can laugh at Frieda, as I — naughtily; I very much regretted it later — did in the bar; but even whoever laughs here is already malicious or envious; still, one can laugh. Amalia, though, if one isn't bound to her by blood, one can only despise. That's why they're fundamentally different cases, as you say, but still similar too.' 'They're not similar either,' said K., shaking his head reluctantly. 'Leave Frieda aside; Frieda didn't get such a fine letter from Klamm as Amalia did from Sortini, and Frieda really loved Klamm, and whoever doubts it can ask her; she loves him still today.' 'But are those great differences?' asked Olga. 'Do you think Klamm couldn't have written to Frieda just the same? When the gentlemen get up from their desks they're like that; they can't find their way about in the world; then in their absent-mindedness they say the very coarsest things — not all of them, but many. The letter to Amalia may have been thrown onto the paper absent-mindedly, in complete disregard of what was actually written. What do we know of the gentlemen's thoughts? Haven't you yourself heard, or heard it told, in what tone Klamm dealt with Frieda? It's well known that Klamm is very coarse; he supposedly doesn't speak for hours, and then suddenly he says something so coarse that it makes you shudder. That isn't known of Sortini, as indeed he is very little known at all.
paras.uz: Eng yomon holatda Frida ustidan kulish mumkin, men bufetda odobsizlik qilib shunday qilganimdek — keyin buning uchun juda afsuslandim — lekin bu yerda kulgan odam ham allaqachon yovuz yoki hasadgo'y; har holda kulish mumkin. Amaliyani esa, agar u bilan qon orqali bog'lanmagan bo'lsang, faqat mensimaslik mumkin. Shuning uchun ular, sen aytganingdek, tubdan farq qiladigan holatlar, lekin baribir o'xshash ham.» «Ular o'xshash ham emas, — dedi K. va norozilik bilan bosh chayqadi, — Fridani chetga qo'y; Frida Klammdan Amaliya Sortinidan olgandek bunday «toza» xat olmagan, Frida esa Klammni haqiqatan sevgan; kim shubha qilsa, undan so'rashi mumkin, u uni bugun ham sevadi.» «Lekin bu katta farqlarmi? — so'radi Olga. — Klamm Fridaga xuddi shunday yoza olmasdi deb o'ylaysanmi? Janoblar yozuv stolidan turganda shunday bo'lishadi: dunyoda yo'lni topa olmaydilar, o'shanda parishonlikda eng qo'pol gaplarni aytishadi — hammasi emas, lekin ko'pchiligi. Amaliyaga xat o'ylanib turib, aslida yozilgan narsaga butunlay e'tibor bermay qog'ozga tushirilgan bo'lishi mumkin. Biz janoblarning fikrlari haqida nimani bilamiz? Klamm Frida bilan qanday ohangda muomala qilganini o'zing eshitmadingmi yoki aytib berishganini eshitmadingmi? Klamm juda qo'pol ekani ma'lum; u go'yoki soatlab gapirmaydi, keyin to'satdan shunday qo'pollik qiladiki, seskanib ketasan. Sortini haqida bu ma'lum emas, u umuman juda noma'lum.

paras.en: Really, all that's known of him is that his name is like Sordini's; if it weren't for this similarity of name, he probably wouldn't be known at all. Even as a fire brigade expert he's probably confused with Sordini, who is the real expert and exploits the similarity of name to shift representative duties especially onto Sortini and so remain undisturbed in his work. Now when such a man, as little at home in the world as Sortini, is suddenly seized with love for a village girl, it naturally takes other forms than when the carpenter's apprentice next door falls in love. And one must also consider that between an official and a shoemaker's daughter there is a great distance, which must somehow be bridged; Sortini tried it in this way; another may do it differently. True, it's said that we all belong to the Castle and there's no distance at all and nothing to be bridged, and that may be true ordinarily; but we have unfortunately had occasion to see that, precisely when it matters, it isn't true at all. At any rate, after all this, Sortini's conduct will have become more understandable to you, less monstrous; and it really is, compared with Klamm's, much more understandable and, even if one is very closely involved, much more bearable. When Klamm writes a tender letter, it's more embarrassing than Sortini's coarsest letter. Understand me rightly: I don't dare judge Klamm; I'm only comparing, because you resist the comparison.
paras.uz: Aslida u haqda faqat ismi Sordinining ismiga o'xshashligi ma'lum; agar bu ism o'xshashligi bo'lmaganida, ehtimol, uni umuman bilishmasdi. Hatto o't o'chirish mutaxassisi sifatida ham uni, ehtimol, haqiqiy mutaxassis bo'lgan Sordini bilan adashtirishadi; Sordini esa ism o'xshashligidan foydalanib, ayniqsa vakillik burchlarini Sortinining bo'yniga ag'darib, o'z ishida xalaqitsiz qoladi. Endi Sortini kabi dunyoni bilmaydigan odamni to'satdan qishloq qiziga sevgi bossa, bu, albatta, qo'shni duradgor shogirdi oshiq bo'lgandagidan boshqacha shakllarga kiradi. Shuni ham hisobga olish kerakki, amaldor bilan etikdo'zning qizi o'rtasida katta masofa bor, uni qandaydir yo'l bilan kesib o'tish kerak; Sortini buni shu tarzda sinab ko'rdi, boshqasi boshqacha qilishi mumkin. To'g'ri, hammamiz Qasrga tegishlimiz, hech qanday masofa yo'q va kesib o'tadigan hech narsa yo'q, deyishadi; bu odatda to'g'ri ham bo'lishi mumkin, lekin biz afsuski, aynan muhim bo'lganda bu umuman to'g'ri emasligini ko'rish imkoniga ega bo'ldik. Har holda bularning hammasidan keyin Sortinining xatti-harakati senga tushunarliroq, kamroq dahshatli bo'lib qolgandir; u haqiqatan ham Klammnikiga nisbatan ancha tushunarliroq va hatto juda yaqindan ishtirok etsang ham, ancha chidasa bo'ladigan. Klamm nozik xat yozsa, bu Sortinining eng qo'pol xatidan ham noqulayroq. Meni to'g'ri tushun, men Klamm haqida hukm chiqarishga jur'at etmayman, faqat solishtiryapman, chunki sen solishtirishga qarshilik qilyapsan.

paras.en: Klamm is like a commander over the women; he orders now this one, now that one, to come to him, tolerates none for long, and just as he orders them to come, he orders them to go. Oh, Klamm wouldn't even take the trouble to write a letter first. And compared with that, is it still monstrous if Sortini, who lives quite withdrawn and whose relations with women are at least unknown, sits down once and writes in his fine official hand a letter — an abominable one, admittedly? And if no difference in Klamm's favour results here, but the opposite, is Frieda's love supposed to bring it about? The relationship of women to officials is, believe me, very hard — or rather, always very easy — to judge. Love is never lacking here. There is no such thing as unhappy love for an official. In this respect it's no praise to say of a girl — and I'm by no means speaking only of Frieda here — that she gave herself to the official only because she loved him. She loved him and gave herself to him; that's how it was; but there's nothing to praise in it. But Amalia didn't love Sortini, you object. Well, yes, she didn't love him; but perhaps she did love him after all — who can decide? Not even she herself.
paras.uz: Klamm axir ayollar ustidan qo'mondondek: goh bunisiga, goh unisiga oldiga kelishni buyuradi, hech birini uzoq ushlab turmaydi, kelishni qanday buyursa, ketishni ham shunday buyuradi. Eh, Klamm avval xat yozishga ham ovora bo'lmasdi. Bunga nisbatan butunlay odamovi yashaydigan, ayollar bilan munosabatlari hech bo'lmaganda noma'lum bo'lgan Sortini bir marta o'tirib, o'zining chiroyli amaldorlik xatida, to'g'ri, jirkanch xat yozsa, bu hali ham dahshatlimi? Agar bu yerda Klamm foydasiga farq emas, aksincha bo'lsa, uni Fridaning sevgisi yuzaga keltirishi kerakmi? Ishon menga, ayollarning amaldorlarga munosabatiga baho berish juda qiyin, to'g'rirog'i, har doim juda oson. Bu yerda sevgi hech qachon yetishmaydi. Amaldorga baxtsiz sevgi degan narsa yo'q. Bu borada qiz haqida — men bu yerda faqat Frida haqida gapirayotganim yo'q — u amaldorga faqat uni sevgani uchun o'zini bag'ishladi, deyish maqtov emas. U uni sevdi va o'zini unga bag'ishladi, shunday bo'ldi, lekin bunda maqtaydigan hech narsa yo'q. Lekin Amaliya Sortinini sevmagan, deb e'tiroz bildirasan. Xo'sh, ha, u uni sevmagan, lekin balki baribir sevgandir — buni kim hal qila oladi? Hatto uning o'zi ham emas.

paras.en: How can she believe she didn't love him, when she rejected him so forcefully, as probably no official has ever been rejected before? Barnabas says she still sometimes trembles even now from the movement with which she slammed the window three years ago. That's true too, and that's why one mustn't ask her; she has finished with Sortini and knows nothing more than that; whether she loves him or not, she doesn't know. But we know that women can't help loving officials once these turn to them; indeed, they love the officials even beforehand, however much they want to deny it; and Sortini didn't only turn to Amalia, he jumped over the shaft when he saw Amalia — with legs stiff from desk work he jumped over the shaft. But Amalia is an exception, you'll say. Yes, she is; she proved it when she refused to go to Sortini; that's exception enough; but that on top of that she shouldn't have loved Sortini either — that would almost be too much of an exception; that would be beyond grasping. We were certainly struck with blindness that afternoon; but that we thought, through all the fog, that we noticed something of Amalia's being in love showed, after all, some sense still. But if one puts all this together, what difference is left between Frieda and Amalia?
paras.uz: Agar u uni hech qachon biror amaldor rad etilmaganchalik qattiq rad etgan bo'lsa, qanday qilib uni sevmagan deb ishona oladi? Barnabasning aytishicha, u uch yil oldin derazani qarsillatib yopgan harakatidan hali ham ba'zan titraydi. Bu to'g'ri ham, shuning uchun undan so'rash mumkin emas; u Sortini bilan hisobni yopgan va bundan ortiq hech narsani bilmaydi; uni sevadimi-yo'qmi — bilmaydi. Biz esa bilamizki, amaldorlar bir marta ayollarga yuz o'girsa, ayollar ularni sevmay qola olmaydi; ha, ular amaldorlarni hatto undan oldin ham sevishadi, qanchalik inkor qilishni istamasinlar; Sortini esa Amaliyaga faqat yuz o'girmadi, balki Amaliyani ko'rganda aravaning shotisi ustidan sakrab o'tdi — yozuv stoli ishidan qotib qolgan oyoqlari bilan shotidan sakrab o'tdi. Lekin Amaliya istisno-da, deysan. Ha, u shunday, buni Sortinining oldiga borishdan bosh tortganida isbotladi, bu istisno uchun yetarli; lekin buning ustiga u Sortinini sevmagan ham bo'lsa — bu istisno uchun deyarli ortiqcha bo'lardi, buni umuman tushunib bo'lmasdi. To'g'ri, o'sha tushdan keyin biz ko'r bo'lib qolgan edik, lekin o'shanda butun tuman orasidan Amaliyaning oshiqligidan nimanidir payqagandek bo'lganimiz baribir qandaydir hushyorlikni ko'rsatardi. Lekin bularning hammasini birlashtirsang, Frida bilan Amaliya o'rtasida qanday farq qoladi?

paras.en: Only this: that Frieda did what Amalia refused.' 'Maybe,' said K., 'but for me the main difference is that Frieda is my fiancée, whereas Amalia basically concerns me only in so far as she is the sister of Barnabas, the Castle messenger, and her fate is perhaps interwoven with Barnabas's service. If an official had done her such a crying wrong as it seemed to me at first from your story, it would have concerned me very much — but much more as a public matter than as Amalia's personal suffering. But now, from your story, the picture changes in a way I don't quite understand, it's true, but which, since it's you telling it, is credible enough; and so I'll very gladly disregard the matter entirely; I'm not a fireman — what do I care about Sortini? But I do care about Frieda; and there it's strange to me how you, whom I trusted completely and want always to trust, keep trying to attack Frieda by way of Amalia and make her suspect to me. I don't suppose you do it intentionally, let alone with bad intentions; otherwise I'd have had to leave long ago.
paras.uz: Faqat shuki, Frida Amaliya rad etgan narsani qildi.» «Bo'lishi mumkin, — dedi K., — lekin men uchun asosiy farq shundaki, Frida mening qallig'im, Amaliya esa meni aslida faqat Qasr choparining — Barnabasning singlisi ekani va uning taqdiri Barnabasning xizmati bilan chirmashib ketgan bo'lishi mumkinligi darajasidagina qiziqtiradi. Agar biror amaldor unga hikoyangdan dastlab menga tuyulgandek shunchalik ochiq nohaqlik qilganida, bu meni juda qiziqtirgan bo'lardi, lekin bu ham Amaliyaning shaxsiy dardidan ko'ra ko'proq ijtimoiy ish sifatida. Endi esa hikoyangga ko'ra manzara menga, to'g'ri, unchalik tushunarli bo'lmagan, lekin aytayotgan sen bo'lganing uchun yetarlicha ishonarli tarzda o'zgaryapti, shuning uchun bu ishni butunlay e'tiborsiz qoldirishni juda istayman; men o't o'chiruvchi emasman, Sortini menga nima? Lekin Frida meni qiziqtiradi va bu yerda men uchun g'alati: men butunlay ishongan va doim ishonishni istaydigan sen qanday qilib Amaliya orqali aylanma yo'l bilan Fridaga doim hujum qilib, uni menga shubhali qilishga urinayapsan. Buni ataylab, ayniqsa yomon niyat bilan qilayotganingni taxmin qilmayman; aks holda allaqachon ketishim kerak bo'lardi.

paras.en: You don't do it intentionally; circumstances lead you to it. Out of love for Amalia you want to set her up high above all women, and since you don't find enough that is praiseworthy in Amalia herself for this purpose, you help yourself by belittling other women. Amalia's deed is strange; but the more you tell of this deed, the less it can be decided whether it was great or small, clever or foolish, heroic or cowardly; Amalia keeps her motives locked in her breast; nobody will tear them from her. Frieda, on the other hand, did nothing strange at all, but only followed her heart; for anyone who looks at it in good will, that's clear; anyone can check it; there's no room for gossip. But I want neither to run down Amalia nor to defend Frieda, only to make clear to you how I stand towards Frieda and how every attack on Frieda is at the same time an attack on my existence. I came here of my own will, and of my own will I've dug myself in here; but everything that has happened since, and above all my prospects for the future — gloomy as they may be, still, they exist — all this I owe to Frieda; that can't be argued away.
paras.uz: Sen buni ataylab qilmayapsan, sharoitlar seni bunga undaydi; Amaliyaga bo'lgan sevging tufayli uni barcha ayollardan baland qo'ymoqchisan, buning uchun Amaliyaning o'zida yetarlicha maqtovga loyiq narsa topa olmaganing uchun boshqa ayollarni kamsitish bilan o'zingga yordam berasan. Amaliyaning qilmishi g'alati, lekin sen bu qilmish haqida qanchalik ko'p gapirsang, u buyukmi yoki kichikmi, aqllimi yoki ahmoqonami, qahramonlikmi yoki qo'rqoqlikmi — buni hal qilish shunchalik qiyinlashadi; Amaliya o'z sabablarini ko'ksida qulflab saqlaydi, ularni undan hech kim tortib ololmaydi. Frida esa aksincha, umuman g'alati hech narsa qilmagan, faqat yuragining ortidan ergashgan; bu bilan yaxshi niyatda shug'ullangan har kim uchun bu aniq, har kim buni tekshirishi mumkin, g'iybat uchun joy yo'q. Lekin men na Amaliyani kamsitmoqchiman, na Fridani himoya qilmoqchiman, balki senga faqat Fridaga qanday munosabatda ekanimni va Fridaga qarshi har qanday hujum ayni paytda mening mavjudligimga qarshi hujum ekanini tushuntirmoqchiman. Men bu yerga o'z xohishim bilan keldim va o'z xohishim bilan bu yerda o'rnashib oldim, lekin o'shandan beri sodir bo'lgan hamma narsa, eng avvalo kelajakdagi istiqbollarim — ular qanchalik xira bo'lmasin, har holda ular bor — bularning hammasi uchun Fridaga qarzdorman, buni bahs bilan yo'qqa chiqarib bo'lmaydi.

paras.en: I was taken on here as a land surveyor, it's true, but that was only in appearance; they were playing with me, they drove me out of every house; they're still playing with me today, but how much more elaborate it is; I've gained in size, so to speak, and that already means something. I have — however insignificant it all is — a home, a post and real work; I have a fiancée who, when I have other business, takes my professional work off my hands; I'll marry her and become a member of the community; besides the official relationship, I also have a personal one with Klamm — admittedly one I haven't been able to make use of so far. That's surely not little? And when I come to you, whom do you greet? Whom do you confide your family's story to? From whom do you hope for the possibility — be it only the tiny, improbable possibility — of some help? Surely not from me, the land surveyor, whom, for instance, Lasemann and Brunswick pushed out of their house by force only a week ago; no, you hope for it from the man who already has some means of power; but these means of power I owe to Frieda — Frieda, who is so modest that if you try to ask her about anything of the kind, she certainly won't want to know the slightest thing about it. And yet after all this it seems that Frieda in her innocence has done more than Amalia in all her pride; for look, I have the impression that you're seeking help for Amalia. And from whom?
paras.uz: To'g'ri, bu yerda meni yer o'lchovchi sifatida qabul qilishdi, lekin bu faqat zohiran edi, men bilan o'ynashdi, meni har uydan haydashdi, bugun ham men bilan o'ynashyapti, lekin bu qanchalik murakkabroq; men qandaydir hajm jihatdan o'sdim, bu esa allaqachon nimanidir anglatadi; bularning hammasi qanchalik arzimas bo'lmasin, menda uy, lavozim va haqiqiy ish bor, menda boshqa ishlarim bo'lganda kasbiy ishimni o'z zimmasiga oladigan qallig'im bor, men unga uylanaman va jamoa a'zosi bo'laman, menda rasmiy munosabatlardan tashqari Klamm bilan shaxsiy munosabat ham bor — to'g'ri, hozircha undan foydalana olmadim. Bu axir oz emas-ku? Men sizlarnikiga kelganimda, kim bilan salomlashasiz? Oilangiz tarixini kimga ishonib aytasan? Qandaydir yordam imkoniyatini — hatto eng kichik, ehtimoldan yiroq imkoniyatni ham — kimdan umid qilasan? Albatta, mendan — bir hafta oldin Lazemann va Brunsvik uylaridan kuch bilan itarib chiqargan yer o'lchovchidan emas, balki allaqachon qandaydir kuch vositalariga ega bo'lgan odamdan umid qilasan; bu kuch vositalari uchun esa Fridaga qarzdorman — shunchalik kamtar Fridaga ki, agar undan shunga o'xshash narsa haqida so'rashga urinsang, u albatta bu haqda zarracha ham bilishni istamaydi. Shunga qaramay, bularning hammasidan keyin Frida o'zining beg'uborligida Amaliya butun mag'rurligi bilan qilganidan ko'proq narsa qilganga o'xshaydi; chunki qara, menda shunday taassurot borki, sen Amaliya uchun yordam izlayapsan. Kimdan?

paras.en: From nobody, really, but Frieda?' 'Have I really spoken so badly of Frieda?' said Olga. 'I certainly didn't mean to, and I don't believe I did; but it's possible; our situation is such that we've fallen out with the whole world, and once we start complaining, it carries us away, we don't know where. You're right too: there's a great difference now between us and Frieda, and it's good to stress it for once. Three years ago we were respectable townsfolk's daughters, and Frieda, the orphan, was a maid at the Bridge Inn; we walked past her without so much as brushing her with a glance; we were certainly too proud, but we'd been brought up like that. But on that evening at the Herrenhof you may have recognised how things stand now: Frieda with the whip in her hand, and I in the crowd of farmhands. But it's even worse. Frieda may despise us; it suits her position; the actual circumstances compel it. But who doesn't despise us! Whoever decides to despise us at once comes into the very best company. Do you know Frieda's successor? Pepi, she's called. I only got to know her the evening before last; until then she was a chambermaid. She certainly surpasses Frieda in her contempt for me.
paras.uz: Aslida Fridadan boshqa hech kimdan emasmi?» «Nahotki Frida haqida shunchalik yomon gapirgan bo'lsam? — dedi Olga. — Men buni albatta istamadim va shunday qilganimga ishonmayman ham, lekin bo'lishi mumkin; bizning ahvolimiz shundayki, butun dunyo bilan aloqamiz uzilgan va shikoyat qila boshlasak, bizni qayergadir olib ketadi, qayerga — bilmaymiz. Sen haqsan ham, hozir biz bilan Frida o'rtasida katta farq bor va buni bir marta ta'kidlash yaxshi. Uch yil oldin biz obro'li xonadon qizlari edik, yetim Frida esa «Ko'prik yonidagi» mehmonxonada xizmatkor edi; biz uning yonidan nigohimizni ham tashlamay o'tib ketardik; biz, albatta, juda mag'rur edik, lekin bizni shunday tarbiyalashgan edi. Lekin Herrenhofdagi o'sha kechada hozirgi holatni ko'rgandirsan: qo'lida qamchi bilan Frida va xizmatkorlar to'dasida men. Lekin bundan ham yomoni bor. Frida bizni mensimasligi mumkin, bu uning mavqeiga mos, haqiqiy sharoitlar buni majbur qiladi. Lekin bizni kim mensimaydi deysan! Kim bizni mensimaslikka qaror qilsa, darhol eng katta jamiyatga tushadi. Fridaning o'rinbosarini taniysanmi? Uning ismi Pepi. Men u bilan faqat o'tgan kuni kechqurun tanishdim, hozirgacha u xona xizmatkori edi. U menga nisbatan nafratda, albatta, Fridadan ham o'zib ketadi.

paras.en: She saw me from the window as I came to fetch beer, ran to the door and locked it; I had to plead for a long time and promise her the ribbon I was wearing in my hair before she opened. But when I gave it to her, she threw it into the corner. Well, she may despise me; I'm partly dependent on her goodwill, and she's barmaid at the Herrenhof — only provisionally, of course, and she certainly doesn't have the qualities needed to be employed there permanently. Just listen to how the landlord talks to Pepi and compare it with how he talked to Frieda. But that doesn't stop Pepi from despising Amalia too — Amalia, whose glance alone would be enough to get little Pepi, with all her plaits and bows, out of the room faster than she could ever manage relying only on her own fat little legs. What outrageous chatter about Amalia I had to listen to from her again yesterday, until at last the guests took charge of me — in the way you've already seen once.' 'How frightened you are,' said K. 'I only put Frieda in her proper place; I didn't want to belittle you, as you now take it.
paras.uz: U meni pivo olgani kelayotganimda derazadan ko'rib, eshikka yugurdi va uni qulflab oldi; u eshikni ochishidan oldin men uzoq yolvorishim va sochimga taqib yurgan lentani va'da qilishim kerak bo'ldi. Lekin keyin uni berganimda, u lentani burchakka uloqtirdi. Xo'sh, u meni mensimasligi mumkin, qisman men uning iltifotiga muhtojman, u Herrenhofda bufetchi qiz; to'g'ri, u faqat vaqtincha shunday va u yerda doimiy ishlash uchun zarur bo'lgan fazilatlar unda, albatta, yo'q. Mehmonxona egasining Pepi bilan qanday gaplashishini tinglab, uning Frida bilan qanday gaplashganiga solishtirib ko'rish kifoya. Lekin bu Pepiga Amaliyani ham mensimaslikka xalaqit bermaydi — Amaliyani, uning bir nigohi butun kichkina Pepini barcha o'rimlari va bantlari bilan faqat o'zining semiz oyoqchalariga tayanib hech qachon uddalay olmaydigan tezlikda xonadan chiqarib yuborishga yetarli bo'lardi. Kecha yana undan Amaliya haqida qanday g'azablantiruvchi valdirashni tinglashim kerak bo'ldi, toki nihoyat mehmonlar meni o'z qaramog'iga olishdi — to'g'ri, sen bir marta ko'rgan usulda.» «Qanchalik qo'rqib ketgansan, — dedi K., — men faqat Fridani o'ziga munosib joyga qo'ydim, lekin sen hozir tushunayotganingdek sizlarni kamsitmoqchi emas edim.

paras.en: Your family has something special for me too; I haven't kept quiet about that; but how this specialness could give cause for contempt I don't understand.' 'Oh, K.,' said Olga, 'you'll understand it too, I'm afraid. Can't you understand at all that Amalia's conduct towards Sortini was the first cause of this contempt?' 'That would really be too strange,' said K. 'One might admire Amalia for it, or condemn her — but despise her? And if, out of some feeling I don't understand, people really do despise Amalia, why do they extend the contempt to you, to the innocent family? That Pepi, for example, despises you is a bit much, and when I come to the Herrenhof again I'll pay her back for it.' 'If you wanted, K.,' said Olga, 'to change the minds of all those who've betrayed us, that would be hard work, for everything comes from the Castle. I still remember exactly the morning that followed that early morning.
paras.uz: Sizlarning oilangizda men uchun ham qandaydir alohida narsa bor, buni yashirmadim; lekin bu alohidalik qanday qilib nafratga sabab bo'lishi mumkinligini tushunmayman.» «Eh, K., — dedi Olga, — qo'rqamanki, sen ham buni hali tushunasan; Amaliyaning Sortiniga nisbatan xatti-harakati bu nafratning birinchi sababi bo'lganini hech qanday yo'l bilan tushuna olmaysanmi?» «Bu juda g'alati bo'lardi, — dedi K., — buning uchun Amaliyaga hayratlanish yoki uni qoralash mumkin edi, lekin mensimaslik? Agar menga tushunarsiz tuyg'u tufayli Amaliyani haqiqatan mensimasalar, nega bu nafratni sizlarga, aybsiz oilaga yoyishadi? Masalan, Pepi seni mensimasligi — bu haddan oshish, men yana Herrenhofga borganimda, buning javobini unga qaytaraman.» «Agar sen, K., — dedi Olga, — bizga xiyonat qilganlarning hammasining fikrini o'zgartirmoqchi bo'lsang, bu og'ir ish bo'lardi, chunki hammasi Qasrdan chiqadi. O'sha tongdan keyingi ertalabni hali ham aniq eslayman.

paras.en: Brunswick, who was our assistant then, had come as he did every day; father had given him work and sent him home; then we sat at breakfast; everyone except Amalia and me was very lively; father kept talking about the festival; he had various plans concerning the fire brigade. For there is a fire brigade of its own at the Castle, which had also sent a delegation to the festival, and various things had been discussed with it; the gentlemen from the Castle who were present had seen what our fire brigade could do, had spoken very favourably of it, had compared it with what the Castle fire brigade could do, and the result was favourable to us; there had been talk of the need to reorganise the Castle fire brigade; for that, instructors from the village were needed; several men came into consideration, but father did have hope that the choice would fall on him. That's what he was talking about now, and, as was his dear way of spreading himself out at table, he sat there with his arms embracing half the table, and as he looked up at the sky through the open window his face was so young and full of hopeful joy; I was never to see him like that again.
paras.uz: O'shanda bizning yordamchimiz bo'lgan Brunsvik har kungidek kelgan edi, otamiz unga ish taqsimlab, uyiga jo'natgan edi; keyin biz nonushtada o'tirdik; Amaliya va mendan tashqari hamma juda jonli edi; otamiz to'xtovsiz bayram haqida gapirardi, o't o'chiruvchilar borasida uning turli rejalari bor edi: gap shundaki, Qasrda o'zining o't o'chirish xizmati bor, u ham bayramga vakillar yuborgan edi, ular bilan ko'p narsa muhokama qilingan edi; u yerda bo'lgan Qasr janoblari bizning o't o'chiruvchilarimiz nimaga qodir ekanini ko'rib, ular haqida juda ijobiy fikr bildirishgan, Qasr o't o'chiruvchilarining imkoniyatlari bilan solishtirishgan, natija bizning foydamizga bo'lgan edi; Qasr o't o'chirish xizmatini qayta tashkil etish zarurligi haqida gap bo'lgan, buning uchun qishloqdan yo'riqchilar kerak edi; bir nechta odam ko'rib chiqilayotgan edi, lekin otamiz tanlov unga tushishiga umid qilardi. U endi shu haqda gapirardi va stol atrofida keng yoyilib o'tirishni yoqtiradigan sevimli odatiga ko'ra, qo'llari bilan stolning yarmini quchoqlab o'tirardi; ochiq derazadan osmonga qaraganida, uning yuzi shunchalik yosh va umidli quvonchga to'la edi; men uni boshqa hech qachon bunday ko'rmasligim kerak edi.

paras.en: Then Amalia said, with a superiority we didn't know in her, that one mustn't trust such speeches of the gentlemen very much; on such occasions the gentlemen liked to say something pleasing, but it had little or no significance; hardly spoken, it was already forgotten for ever — though of course on the next occasion one fell for it again. Mother rebuked her for such talk; father only laughed at her precociousness and worldly wisdom; but then he stopped short, seemed to be looking for something whose absence he only now noticed — but nothing was missing — and said that Brunswick had told him something about a messenger and a torn-up letter, and he asked whether we knew anything about it, whom it concerned and what it was about. We were silent; Barnabas, still young as a little lamb then, said something particularly stupid or cheeky; they talked of other things, and the matter was forgotten. But shortly afterwards we were already being showered with questions from all sides about the letter story; friends and enemies came, acquaintances and strangers; but nobody stayed long; the best friends took leave most hastily of all.
paras.uz: Shunda Amaliya biz unda tanimagan ustunlik bilan janoblarning bunday gaplariga unchalik ishonmaslik kerakligini, janoblar bunday paytlarda yoqimli gap aytishni yaxshi ko'rishini, lekin buning ahamiyati kam yoki umuman yo'qligini, aytilishi bilan abadiy unutilishini — to'g'ri, keyingi fursatda yana ularning to'riga ilinishini aytdi. Onamiz unga bunday gaplar uchun tanbeh berdi, otamiz esa faqat uning oqsoqollarcha aqlliligi va ko'p tajribaliligidan kuldi; lekin keyin u to'xtab qoldi, go'yo endigina yo'qligini payqagan nimanidir izlayotgandek bo'ldi — lekin hech narsa yo'qolmagan edi — va Brunsvik qandaydir chopar va yirtilgan xat haqida nimadir aytganini, biz bu haqda biror narsa bilamizmi, bu kimga tegishli va qanday ish ekanini so'radi. Biz jim qoldik; o'shanda hali qo'zichoqdek yosh Barnabas ayniqsa ahmoqona yoki surbet bir narsa dedi, boshqa narsalar haqida gapirishdi va bu ish unutildi.» «Lekin ko'p o'tmay bizni xat voqeasi haqidagi savollarga har tomondan ko'mib tashlashdi; do'stlar va dushmanlar, tanishlar va begonalar kelishdi; lekin hech kim uzoq qolmadi, eng yaxshi do'stlar hammadan shoshilib xayrlashishdi.

paras.en: Lasemann, usually always slow and dignified, came in as though he only wanted to check the size of the room; one glance round, and he was done; it looked like a terrible children's game when Lasemann fled and father freed himself from other people and hurried after him to the threshold of the house and then gave up. Brunswick came and gave father notice; he wanted to set up on his own, he said quite honestly — a clever head who knew how to use the moment. Customers came and searched out from father's storeroom the boots they'd left with us for repair; at first father tried to make the customers change their minds — and we all supported him as best we could — later father gave up and silently helped the people search; in the order book line after line was crossed out; the stocks of leather people had with us were handed back; debts were paid; everything went without the slightest quarrel; people were content if they managed to sever the connection with us quickly and completely, even if they had losses by it — that didn't come into consideration.
paras.uz: Odatda doim sekin va salobatli Lazemann go'yo faqat xonaning o'lchamini tekshirmoqchidek kirdi: atrofga bir qarash — va u ishini bitirdi; Lazemann qochib ketayotganda va otamiz boshqa odamlardan ajralib, uning ortidan uy ostonasigacha shoshilib, keyin voz kechganida, bu dahshatli bolalar o'yiniga o'xshardi; Brunsvik kelib, otamizga ishdan ketishini aytdi; u mustaqil ishlamoqchi ekanini juda halol aytdi — fursatdan foydalanishni biladigan aqlli bosh; mijozlar kelib, otamizning omboridan ta'mirlash uchun qoldirgan etiklarini izlab topishdi; avval otamiz mijozlarning fikrini o'zgartirishga urindi — biz hammamiz uni qo'limizdan kelganicha qo'llab-quvvatladik — keyin otamiz voz kechdi va indamay odamlarga izlashda yordam berdi; buyurtmalar daftarida qatorma-qator o'chirildi, odamlarning bizda bo'lgan charm zaxiralari qaytarib berildi, qarzlar to'landi; hammasi zarracha janjalsiz o'tdi; odamlar biz bilan aloqani tez va butunlay uzishga muvaffaq bo'lishsa, mamnun edilar; bunda zarar ko'rishsa ham — bu hisobga olinmasdi.

paras.en: And finally — as was only to be expected — Seemann appeared, the chief of the fire brigade. I can still see the scene before me: Seemann, tall and strong, but a little stooped and consumptive, always serious — he can't laugh at all — stands before my father, whom he has admired, to whom in confidential hours he has held out the prospect of the post of deputy chief, and is now supposed to tell him that the association is dismissing him and requests the return of his diploma. The people who happened to be with us left their business and crowded in a circle round the two men. Seemann can't say anything; he only keeps patting father on the shoulder, as though he wanted to tap out of father the words he himself is supposed to say and can't find. And all the while he keeps laughing, by which he probably wants to calm himself and everyone a little; but since he can't laugh and nobody has ever heard him laugh, it occurs to nobody to believe that it's a laugh. But father is already too tired and desperate from that day to be able to help anyone; indeed, he seems too tired even to think about what it's all about. We were all equally desperate, of course, but since we were young we couldn't believe in such a complete collapse; we kept thinking that in the series of many visitors someone would come at last who would order a halt and force everything back into reverse.
paras.uz: Nihoyat, oldindan ko'rish mumkin bo'lganidek, o't o'chiruvchilar boshlig'i Zeeman paydo bo'ldi; bu manzarani hali ham ko'z oldimda ko'raman: baland bo'yli va baquvvat, lekin biroz bukchaygan va o'pka kasali, doim jiddiy — u umuman kula olmaydi — Zeeman o'zi hayratlangan, samimiy soatlarda boshliq o'rinbosari lavozimini va'da qilgan otamning oldida turibdi va endi unga jamiyat uni bo'shatayotganini va diplomini qaytarishni so'rayotganini aytishi kerak. Ayni paytda bizda bo'lgan odamlar ishlarini qoldirib, ikki erkak atrofida doira bo'lib tiqilishdi. Zeeman hech narsa deya olmaydi, faqat to'xtovsiz otamning yelkasiga qoqadi, go'yo o'zi aytishi kerak bo'lgan va topa olmayotgan so'zlarni otamdan qoqib chiqarmoqchidek. Shu bilan birga u to'xtovsiz kuladi — bu bilan, ehtimol, o'zini va hammani biroz tinchlantirmoqchi; lekin u kula olmagani va hech kim uning kulganini hech qachon eshitmagani uchun, hech kimning xayoliga bu kulgi ekanligiga ishonish kelmaydi. Otam esa o'sha kundan beri allaqachon hech kimga yordam bera olmaydigan darajada charchagan va umidsiz; ha, u gap nima haqida ekanini umuman o'ylashga ham juda charchagandek ko'rinadi. To'g'ri, biz hammamiz bir xil umidsiz edik, lekin yosh bo'lganimiz uchun bunday to'liq qulashga ishona olmasdik; ko'plab tashrif buyuruvchilar qatorida nihoyat «To'xta!» deb buyuradigan va hamma narsani orqaga qaytishga majbur qiladigan kimdir keladi deb doim o'ylardik.

paras.en: In our foolishness, Seemann seemed to us especially suited for that. We waited eagerly for the clear word to break loose at last from this constant laughter. What was there to laugh at now except the stupid injustice being done to us? Chief, chief, do tell the people at last, we thought, and pressed close to him, which only made him perform strange turning movements. At last he did begin to speak — not, of course, to fulfil our secret wishes, but in response to the encouraging or annoyed calls of the people. We still had hope. He began with great praise of father. Called him an ornament of the association, an unattainable model for the young, an indispensable member whose departure must almost destroy the association. That was all very fine; if only he'd ended there! But he went on. If the association had nevertheless decided to ask father — only provisionally, admittedly — to resign, people would recognise the seriousness of the reasons that forced the association to do so. Perhaps without father's brilliant achievements at yesterday's festival it need never have come to this; but precisely these achievements had particularly aroused official attention; the association now stood in the full light and must be even more mindful of its purity than before.
paras.uz: Nodonligimizda Zeeman bizga buning uchun ayniqsa mos tuyuldi. Bu to'xtovsiz kulgidan nihoyat aniq so'z ajralib chiqishini hayajon bilan kutardik. Endi nimaga kulish kerak edi — faqat bizga qilinayotgan ahmoqona nohaqlikka. Janob boshliq, janob boshliq, nihoyat odamlarga ayting-da, deb o'ylardik va unga yaqinroq tiqilardik, lekin bu uni faqat g'alati aylanma harakatlarga undardi. Nihoyat u gapira boshladi — to'g'ri, bizning yashirin istaklarimizni bajarish uchun emas, balki odamlarning ruhlantiruvchi yoki jahlli chaqiriqlariga javob berish uchun. Bizda hali ham umid bor edi. U otamni qattiq maqtashdan boshladi. Uni jamiyatning ziynati, yosh avlod uchun yetib bo'lmas namuna, ketishi jamiyatni deyarli yemirishi kerak bo'lgan almashtirib bo'lmas a'zo deb atadi. Bularning hammasi juda chiroyli edi; qaniydi shu yerda to'xtasa! Lekin u davom etdi. Agar shunga qaramay jamiyat otamdan — to'g'ri, hozircha — iste'foga chiqishni so'rashga qaror qilgan bo'lsa, jamiyatni bunga majbur qilgan sabablarning jiddiyligi tushunilar. Balki otamning kechagi bayramdagi ajoyib yutuqlari bo'lmaganida, ish bunchalik uzoqqa bormasligi kerak edi, lekin aynan shu yutuqlar rasmiy e'tiborni ayniqsa uyg'otgan; jamiyat endi to'liq yorug'likda turibdi va o'z pokligi haqida avvalgidan ham ko'proq qayg'urishi kerak.

paras.en: And now the insult to the messenger had happened; the association had found no other way out, and he, Seemann, had taken on the heavy office of announcing it. Father should not make it even harder for him. How glad Seemann was to have got that out! In his confidence about it he wasn't even excessively considerate any more; he pointed to the diploma hanging on the wall and beckoned with his finger. Father nodded and went to fetch it, but couldn't get it off the hook with his trembling hands; I climbed on a chair and helped him. And from that moment on everything was over; he didn't even take the diploma out of its frame any more, but gave Seemann everything as it was. Then he sat down in a corner, didn't move and spoke to nobody any more; we had to deal with the people alone as best we could.' 'And where do you see the influence of the Castle in this?' asked K. 'So far it doesn't seem to have intervened yet. What you've told so far was only the thoughtless timidity of people, pleasure in their neighbour's misfortune, unreliable friendship — things to be found everywhere; and on your father's side, too — at least so it seems to me — a certain pettiness; for that diploma, what was it?
paras.uz: Endi esa chopar haqorat qilindi, jamiyat boshqa chiqish yo'lini topmadi va u — Zeeman buni e'lon qilishdek og'ir vazifani o'z zimmasiga oldi. Otam buni unga yanada qiyinlashtirmasin. Zeeman buni aytib bera olganidan qanchalik xursand edi; bundan ishonch hosil qilib, u endi hatto haddan tashqari andishali ham emas edi: devorda osilib turgan diplomni ko'rsatib, barmog'i bilan imo qildi. Otam bosh irg'adi va uni olgani bordi, lekin titroq qo'llari bilan uni ilgakdan ola olmadi; men kursiga chiqib, unga yordam berdim. Shu lahzadan boshlab hammasi tugadi; u diplomni hatto ramkadan ham chiqarmadi, hammasini Zeemanga shundayligicha berdi. Keyin u burchakka o'tirib oldi, qimirlamadi va boshqa hech kim bilan gaplashmadi; biz odamlar bilan qo'limizdan kelganicha yolg'iz o'zimiz muomala qilishga majbur bo'ldik.» «Bunda Qasrning ta'sirini qayerda ko'ryapsan? — so'radi K. — Hozircha u aralashmaganga o'xshaydi. Hozirgacha aytib berganlaring faqat odamlarning o'ylamasdan qo'rqoqligi, yaqinining baxtsizligidan quvonish, ishonchsiz do'stlik edi — hamma joyda uchraydigan narsalar; otang tomonidan esa — hech bo'lmaganda menga shunday tuyuladi — qandaydir maydakashlik; chunki o'sha diplom nima edi?

paras.en: Confirmation of his abilities; and those he kept, after all; if they made him indispensable, so much the better; and he would really only have made things hard for the chief by throwing the diploma at his feet at the second word. But what seems especially telling to me is that you don't mention Amalia at all; Amalia, who was to blame for everything, was probably standing quietly in the background watching the devastation.' 'No,' said Olga, 'nobody is to be reproached; nobody could act otherwise; all that was already the influence of the Castle.' 'The influence of the Castle,' repeated Amalia, who had come in unnoticed from the yard; the parents had long been in bed. 'Castle stories are being told? You're still sitting together? And you wanted to leave at once, K., and now it's getting on for ten. Do such stories concern you at all, then? There are people here who feed on such stories; they sit together as you're sitting here and regale each other; but you don't seem to me to belong to those people.' 'Yes, I do,' said K., 'I belong exactly to them; on the other hand, people who don't concern themselves with such stories and only let others concern themselves don't make much impression on me.'
paras.uz: Uning qobiliyatlarining tasdig'i; ular esa axir unda qoldi, agar ular uni almashtirib bo'lmas qilsa — shunchalik yaxshi; u boshliqqa ishni faqat ikkinchi so'zdayoq diplomni oyoqlari ostiga otib qiyinlashtirgan bo'lardi. Lekin menga ayniqsa xarakterli tuyuladigan narsa — sen Amaliyani umuman tilga olmayapsan; hamma narsaga aybdor bo'lgan Amaliya, ehtimol, orqa tomonda xotirjam turib, vayronagarchilikni kuzatgandir.» «Yo'q, — dedi Olga, — hech kimni ayblab bo'lmaydi, hech kim boshqacha harakat qila olmasdi, bularning hammasi allaqachon Qasrning ta'siri edi.» «Qasrning ta'siri», takrorladi hovlidan sezdirmay kirib kelgan Amaliya; ota-onasi allaqachon to'shakda yotishardi. «Qasr hikoyalari aytilyaptimi? Hali ham birga o'tiribsizlarmi? Sen esa darhol xayrlashmoqchi eding, K., endi esa soat o'nga yaqinlashyapti. Bunday hikoyalar seni umuman qiziqtiradimi? Bu yerda bunday hikoyalar bilan oziqlanadigan odamlar bor, ular sizlar o'tirgandek birga o'tirib, bir-birini siylashadi; lekin sen menga bunday odamlar qatoriga kirmaydigandek ko'rinasan.» «Kiraman, — dedi K., — men aynan ular qatoriga kiraman; aksincha, bunday hikoyalar bilan qiziqmaydigan va faqat boshqalarni qiziqtiradigan odamlar menda unchalik taassurot qoldirmaydi.»

paras.en: 'Well, yes,' said Amalia, 'but people's interest varies a great deal. I once heard of a young man who occupied himself with thoughts of the Castle day and night; he neglected everything else; people feared for his everyday reason, because all his reason was up at the Castle. But in the end it turned out that it wasn't really the Castle he had meant, but only the daughter of a washerwoman in the offices; he got her, then, and after that everything was all right again.' 'I think I'd like that man,' said K. 'That you'd like the man,' said Amalia, 'I doubt; but perhaps his wife. Now don't let me disturb you; I'm going to bed, though, and I'll have to put out the light because of our parents; they fall fast asleep at once, it's true, but after an hour the real sleep is already over, and then the slightest light disturbs them. Good night.' And indeed it at once grew dark. Amalia was probably making up her bed somewhere on the floor by her parents' bed. 'Who is this young man she was talking about?' asked K. 'I don't know,' said Olga. 'Perhaps Brunswick, although it doesn't quite fit him; perhaps someone else, though. It isn't easy to understand her exactly, because one often doesn't know whether she's speaking ironically or seriously. Mostly it's serious, but it sounds ironic.' 'Never mind the interpretations!' said K.
paras.uz: «Xo'sh, ha, — dedi Amaliya, — lekin odamlarning qiziqishi juda xilma-xil; men bir marta kecha-kunduz Qasr haqidagi o'ylar bilan band bo'lgan bir yigit haqida eshitgan edim; u boshqa hamma narsani tashlab qo'ygan edi, uning kundalik aqli uchun qo'rqishardi, chunki uning butun aqli tepada, Qasrda edi. Lekin oxir-oqibat ma'lum bo'ldiki, u aslida Qasrni emas, balki idoralardagi bir farrosh ayolning qizini nazarda tutgan ekan; u esa uni oldi va keyin hammasi yana yaxshi bo'ldi.» «Menimcha, o'sha odam menga yoqardi», dedi K. «O'sha odam senga yoqishiga, — dedi Amaliya, — shubha qilaman, lekin balki uning xotini yoqar. Endi esa sizlarga xalaqit bermay; men, to'g'ri, uxlagani ketaman va ota-onam tufayli chiroqni o'chirishim kerak bo'ladi; ular, to'g'ri, darhol qattiq uxlab qolishadi, lekin bir soatdan keyin haqiqiy uyqu allaqachon tugaydi va keyin ularni eng kichik yorug'lik ham bezovta qiladi. Xayrli tun.» Va haqiqatan ham darhol qorong'i bo'ldi. Amaliya, ehtimol, qayerdadir polda, ota-onasining to'shagi yonida o'ziga joy hozirlayotgan edi. «U gapirgan bu yigit kim?» — so'radi K. «Bilmayman, — dedi Olga. — Balki Brunsvikdir, garchi bu unga unchalik mos kelmasa ham, balki boshqa birovdir. Uni aniq tushunish oson emas, chunki ko'pincha u kinoya bilan gapiryaptimi yoki jiddiymi, bilmaysan. Ko'pincha jiddiy, lekin kinoyali eshitiladi.» «Talqinlarni qo'y!» — dedi K.

paras.en: 'How did you come to be so very dependent on her? Was it like that even before the great misfortune? Or only afterwards? And do you never wish to become independent of her? And is this dependence reasonably founded in any way? She's the youngest and as such ought to obey. Guilty or innocent, she brought misfortune on the family. Instead of asking each of you afresh every new day for forgiveness for it, she holds her head higher than all of you, concerns herself with nothing except, barely, as a favour, her parents, wants to be initiated into nothing, as she puts it, and when at last she does speak to you, it's mostly serious but sounds ironic. Or does she rule perhaps through her beauty, which you sometimes mention? Well, you're all three very alike; but what distinguishes her from you two is decidedly to her disadvantage; even when I first saw her, her dull, loveless gaze put me off. And then, though she's the youngest, you notice nothing of that in her appearance; she has the ageless look of women who hardly age but have hardly ever really been young either. You see her every day; you don't notice the hardness of her face at all. That's why, when I think it over, I can't even take Sortini's inclination very seriously; perhaps he only wanted to punish her with the letter, not to summon her.'
paras.uz: «Sen qanday qilib unga bunchalik qaram bo'lib qolding? Bu katta baxtsizlikdan oldin ham shunday edimi? Yoki faqat keyinmi? Undan mustaqil bo'lish istagi senda hech qachon bo'lmaydimi? Bu qaramlik qandaydir oqilona asoslanganmi? U eng kichigi va shunday sifatida bo'ysunishi kerak. U aybli bo'ladimi yoki aybsiz, oilaga baxtsizlik keltirdi. Buning uchun har yangi kunda har biringizdan qaytadan kechirim so'rash o'rniga, u boshini hammadan baland tutadi, ota-onasidan boshqa hech narsa bilan qiziqmaydi, ular bilan ham zo'rg'a, marhamat yuzasidan; o'zi aytganidek, hech narsadan voqif bo'lishni istamaydi; nihoyat sizlar bilan gaplashsa ham, bu ko'pincha jiddiy, lekin kinoyali eshitiladi. Yoki u sen ba'zan tilga oladigan go'zalligi bilan hukmronlik qiladimi? Xo'sh, sizlar uchalangiz bir-biringizga juda o'xshaysiz, lekin uni sizlar ikkalangizdan ajratib turadigan narsa butunlay uning zarariga; uni birinchi marta ko'rganimdayoq uning xira, mehrsiz nigohi meni cho'chitgan edi. Keyin u, to'g'ri, eng kichigi, lekin bu uning tashqi ko'rinishida umuman sezilmaydi, unda deyarli qarimaydigan, lekin deyarli hech qachon haqiqatan yosh ham bo'lmagan ayollarning yoshsiz qiyofasi bor. Sen uni har kuni ko'rasan, yuzining qattiqligini umuman payqamaysan. Shuning uchun o'ylab ko'rsam, Sortinining moyilligini ham unchalik jiddiy qabul qila olmayman, balki u xat bilan uni chaqirmoqchi emas, faqat jazolamoqchi bo'lgandir.»

paras.en: 'I don't want to talk about Sortini,' said Olga. 'With the gentlemen at the Castle anything is possible, whether it's the most beautiful or the ugliest girl. But otherwise you're completely wrong about Amalia. Look, I have no reason to win you over to Amalia especially, and if I try nevertheless, I do it only for your sake. Amalia was in some way the cause of our misfortune, that's certain; but even father, who was hit hardest by the misfortune and could never control himself much in what he said, least of all at home — even father never said a word of reproach to Amalia, even in the worst times. And not because he approved of Amalia's action; how could he, an admirer of Sortini, have approved of it? He couldn't understand it even remotely; he would gladly have sacrificed himself and everything he had to Sortini — though not as it actually happened now, under Sortini's probable anger. Probable anger, for we heard nothing more of Sortini; if he had been withdrawn before, from now on he was so as though he no longer existed at all. And you should have seen Amalia at that time. We all knew that no express punishment would come. People only withdrew from us. The people here, and the Castle too. But while one naturally noticed the people's withdrawal, nothing at all could be noticed of the Castle.
paras.uz: «Sortini haqida gapirmoqchi emasman, — dedi Olga. — Qasr janoblarida hamma narsa mumkin, gap eng go'zal qiz haqidami yoki eng xunuk qiz haqidami — farqi yo'q. Lekin qolgan jihatdan sen Amaliya borasida butunlay adashyapsan. Qara, menda seni Amaliya tomoniga alohida og'dirish uchun sabab yo'q, agar shunga qaramay urinsam, buni faqat sen uchun qilaman. Amaliya qandaydir tarzda baxtsizligimizning sababi bo'ldi, bu aniq, lekin hatto baxtsizlikdan eng og'ir zarba olgan va so'zlarida o'zini hech qachon unchalik tuta olmagan — ayniqsa uyda — otam ham eng og'ir paytlarda ham Amaliyaga birorta ta'na so'zi aytmagan. Bu u Amaliyaning harakatini ma'qullagani uchun emas edi; Sortinining muxlisi bo'lgan u buni qanday ma'qullay olardi; u buni hatto uzoqdan ham tushuna olmasdi; u o'zini va bor narsasini Sortiniga bajonidil qurbon qilgan bo'lardi, lekin, albatta, hozir haqiqatan sodir bo'lgandek, Sortinining ehtimoliy g'azabi ostida emas. Ehtimoliy g'azab, chunki biz Sortini haqida boshqa hech narsa eshitmadik; agar u hozirgacha odamovi bo'lgan bo'lsa, endi go'yo umuman mavjud emasdek bo'lib qoldi. O'sha paytda Amaliyani ko'rsang edi. Biz hammamiz hech qanday aniq jazo kelmasligini bilardik. Bizdan faqat chekinishdi. Bu yerdagi odamlar ham, Qasr ham. Lekin odamlarning chekinishini, albatta, payqardik, Qasrdan esa hech narsa payqash mumkin emas edi.

paras.en: We hadn't noticed any care from the Castle before either; how could we have noticed a change now? This calm was the worst thing. By far — not the people's withdrawal; they hadn't done it out of any conviction, perhaps didn't have anything serious against us at all; today's contempt didn't yet exist; they'd done it only out of fear, and now they were waiting to see how it would turn out. Nor did we yet have any want to fear; all our debtors had paid us, the settlements had been advantageous, what we lacked in food relatives helped us out with in secret; it was easy, it was harvest time after all — we had no fields, admittedly, and nobody would let us work with them anywhere; for the first time in our lives we were condemned almost to idleness. And so we sat together with the windows shut, in the heat of July and August. Nothing happened. No summons, no news, no report, no visit, nothing.' 'Well,' said K., 'since nothing happened and no express punishment was to be expected either, what were you afraid of? What people you are!' 'How shall I explain it to you?' said Olga. 'We weren't afraid of anything to come; we were already suffering only from the present; we were in the very midst of the punishment.
paras.uz: Biz avval ham Qasrning g'amxo'rligini payqamagan edik, endi qanday qilib burilishni payqay olardik. Bu jimlik eng yomoni edi. Odamlarning chekinishi emas, aslo — ular buni qandaydir e'tiqod tufayli qilmagan edi, balki bizga qarshi umuman jiddiy hech narsalari yo'q edi, bugungi nafrat hali mavjud emas edi, ular buni faqat qo'rquvdan qilishgan edi va endi ish qanday tugashini kutishardi. Muhtojlikdan ham hali qo'rqmasdik: barcha qarzdorlar bizga to'lagan edi, hisob-kitoblar foydali bo'lgan edi, oziq-ovqatdan nima yetishmasa, qarindoshlarimiz yashirincha yordam berishardi; bu oson edi, axir hosil yig'im-terimi payti edi; to'g'ri, dalalarimiz yo'q edi va hech qayerda birga ishlashimizga yo'l qo'yishmasdi; hayotimizda birinchi marta biz deyarli bekorchilikka mahkum bo'ldik. Endi esa iyul va avgust jaziramasida derazalarni yopib birga o'tirardik. Hech narsa sodir bo'lmadi. Na chaqiruv, na xabar, na hisobot, na tashrif — hech narsa.» «Xo'sh, — dedi K., — hech narsa sodir bo'lmagan va hech qanday aniq jazo ham kutilmagan bo'lsa, nimadan qo'rqdingiz? Qanday odamlarsizlar o'zi!» «Buni senga qanday tushuntirsam ekan? — dedi Olga. — Biz kelajakdagi hech narsadan qo'rqmasdik, biz allaqachon faqat hozirgisidan azob chekardik, biz jazoning qoq o'rtasida edik.

paras.en: The people in the village were only waiting for us to come to them, for father to open his workshop again, for Amalia — who knew how to sew very beautiful dresses, though only for the most distinguished people — to take orders again; everyone was sorry for what they had done. When a respected family in the village is suddenly cut off completely, everyone suffers some disadvantage from it; in breaking with us they had only believed they were doing their duty; in their place we wouldn't have acted differently either. They hadn't even known exactly what it had all been about; only the messenger had come back to the Herrenhof with his hand full of scraps of paper. Frieda had seen him go out and come back, had exchanged a few words with him and spread what she had learned at once — but again not at all out of hostility towards us, simply out of duty, as it would have been anyone else's duty in the same case. And now, as I said, a happy solution of the whole thing would have been most welcome to people.
paras.uz: Qishloqdagi odamlar faqat biz ularning oldiga borishimizni, otamiz ustaxonasini yana ochishini, juda chiroyli ko'ylaklar tikishni biladigan — to'g'ri, faqat eng obro'li odamlar uchun — Amaliya yana buyurtmalar olishini kutishardi; qilgan ishlaridan hammasi afsuslanardi; agar qishloqda obro'li oila to'satdan butunlay chetga chiqarilsa, bundan har kim qandaydir zarar ko'radi; ular bizdan yuz o'girganda faqat o'z burchlarini bajaryapmiz deb o'ylashgan edi, ularning o'rnida biz ham boshqacha qilmagan bo'lardik. Ular gap nima haqida ekanini aniq bilishmagan ham edi, faqat chopar qo'li to'la qog'oz parchalari bilan Herrenhofga qaytib kelgan edi. Frida uning chiqib ketganini va keyin qaytib kelganini ko'rgan, u bilan bir necha og'iz gaplashgan va bilib olgan narsasini darhol tarqatgan edi; lekin bu ham bizga nisbatan dushmanlikdan emas, balki shunchaki burch tufayli edi — xuddi shunday holatda boshqa har kimning burchi bo'lganidek. Endi esa, aytganimdek, butun ishning baxtli hal bo'lishi odamlar uchun eng xush bo'lardi.

paras.en: If we had suddenly come one day with the news that everything was already in order — that, for instance, it had only been a misunderstanding, completely cleared up in the meantime, or that it had indeed been an offence but had already been made good by deeds, or — even that would have been enough for people — that through our connections at the Castle we had succeeded in having the matter quashed — we would most certainly have been welcomed back with open arms; there would have been kisses, embraces, celebrations; I've seen such things happen to others a few times. But not even such news would have been necessary; if only we had come out freely and offered ourselves and taken up the old connections again, without wasting even a word on the letter story, it would have been enough; everyone would gladly have done without discussing the matter. For besides fear, it was above all the embarrassment of the matter that had made people separate from us — simply so as not to have to hear anything of it, speak of it, think of it, be touched by it in any way. If Frieda had betrayed the matter, she hadn't done it to gloat over it, but to protect herself and everyone from it, to draw the community's attention to the fact that something had happened here from which one had to keep away most carefully.
paras.uz: Agar biz bir kun to'satdan hammasi allaqachon joyida, masalan, bu faqat bu orada butunlay oydinlashgan tushunmovchilik bo'lgan, yoki bu, to'g'ri, gunoh bo'lgan, lekin amalda allaqachon tuzatilgan, yoki — odamlar uchun hatto shu ham yetarli bo'lardi — Qasrdagi aloqalarimiz orqali ishni bosdi-bosdi qilishga muvaffaq bo'ldik, degan xabar bilan kelganimizda, bizni, albatta, yana quchoq ochib qabul qilishardi, o'pishlar, quchoqlashlar, bayramlar bo'lardi; men boshqalarda bunday narsani bir necha marta ko'rganman. Lekin hatto bunday xabar ham kerak emas edi; agar biz shunchaki erkin chiqib, o'zimizni taklif qilib, xat voqeasi haqida bir og'iz ham gapirmay eski aloqalarni qayta tiklaganimizda, bu yetarli bo'lardi, hamma bajonidil bu ishni muhokama qilishdan voz kechardi; axir qo'rquvdan tashqari, eng avvalo ishning noqulayligi tufayli odamlar bizdan ajralishgan edi — shunchaki bu haqda hech narsa eshitmaslik, u haqda gapirmaslik, u haqda o'ylamaslik, hech qanday tarzda unga tegib ketmaslik uchun. Agar Frida ishni oshkor qilgan bo'lsa, u buni undan quvonish uchun emas, balki o'zini va hammani undan saqlash uchun, jamoaning e'tiborini bu yerda eng ehtiyotkorlik bilan uzoq turish kerak bo'lgan narsa sodir bo'lganiga qaratish uchun qilgan edi.
